Text: The angular power spectrum (APS) is a fundamental tool in cosmology for analyzing the distribution of galaxies and other cosmic structures. On small sky maps, where the number of pixels is limited, APS estimates are prone to biases and uncertainties, which can impact the accuracy of cosmological inferences. This study aims to quantify the effects of these biases and uncertainties on APS estimates. We utilize Monte Carlo simulations to generate a large ensemble of small sky maps with known angular power spectra. We then apply a standard maximum likelihood estimator to compute APS estimates from these maps. We investigate the biases and covariances of these estimates by comparing them to the true underlying spectra. Interestingly, we observed that APS estimates on small sky maps exhibit significant biases, particularly in the low multipoles, due to the limited number of pixels. We also find that the covariance matrix of the estimates is highly non-diagonal, indicating strong correlations between different multipoles. Our analysis provides a comprehensive understanding of the sources and magnitudes of these biases and covariances, which can inform the design and analysis of future cosmological surveys.

Text: Positive thinking is often misrepresented as a form of wishful denial - a refusal to acknowledge difficulty or pain. Research in psychology has demonstrated that people who maintain an optimistic outlook tend to be more persistent, healthier, and more resilient in the face of adversity. Positive thinking works best when it is grounded in action. Visualizing a better outcome is valuable, but only when paired with concrete effort toward that outcome. It also involves reframing - the intentional practice of looking at setbacks through a lens of learning rather than loss. Cultivating this mindset is not passive; it requires daily practice, conscious choice, and the willingness to challenge thoughts that are unnecessarily catastrophic or defeatist.

Text: In this paper, we conduct extensive simulations to understand the properties of the overlay generated by BitTorrent. We start by analyzing how the overlay properties impact the efficiency of BitTorrent. We focus on the average peer set size (i.e., average number of neighbors), the time for a peer to reach its maximum peer set size, and the diameter of the overlay. In particular, we show that the later a peer arrives in a torrent, the longer it takes to reach its maximum peer set size. Then, we evaluate the impact of the maximum peer set size, the maximum number of outgoing connections per peer, and the number of NATed peers on the overlay properties. We show that BitTorrent generates a robust overlay, but that this overlay is not a random graph. In particular, the connectivity of a peer to its neighbors depends on its arriving order in the torrent. We also show that a large number of NATed peers significantly compromise the robustness of the overlay to attacks. Finally, we evaluate the impact of peer exchange on the overlay properties, and we show that it generates a chain-like overlay with a large diameter, which will adversely impact the efficiency of large torrents.

Text: Deformation theory provides a systematic framework for studying how mathematical objects—such as complex manifolds, algebraic varieties, or Lie algebras—vary under infinitesimal perturbations. Originating in the work of Kodaira–Spencer and Grothendieck, it has become indispensable in several branches of geometry, topology, and mathematical physics, offering insights into moduli spaces, obstruction phenomena, and the local structure of parameter families. These lecture notes develop the theory from first principles, beginning with the functorial definition of deformations over Artinian local rings and the associated tangent and obstruction spaces. The exposition proceeds to construct the governing differential graded Lie algebras (DGLAs) and their Maurer–Cartan equations, emphasizing the equivalence between deformation functors and solutions modulo gauge. Cohomological techniques, including Čech and hypercohomology, are employed to compute explicit tangent-obstruction complexes for complex structures, vector bundles, and associative algebras. The notes also integrate modern homotopical approaches via \(L_\infty\)-algebras and derived deformation theory. The presentation clarifies the role of the Kodaira–Spencer map as a universal obstruction class and demonstrates how vanishing of higher cohomology yields unobstructed deformations. Applications to the smoothness of moduli of Calabi–Yau manifolds, deformation quantization of Poisson structures, and the classification of infinitesimal deformations of Lie algebras are illustrated. The notes culminate in a comparative analysis of classical and derived perspectives, highlighting the unifying power of DGLA techniques in contemporary deformation problems.

Text: Heavy‑quark effects constitute a sizable component of the deep‑inelastic scattering (DIS) cross section at moderate momentum transfer. For a consistent description of both polarized and unpolarized structure functions at next‑to‑next‑to‑leading order, the two‑loop massive operator matrix elements (OMEs) must be determined analytically. These OMEs encode the transition from the full theory with massive quarks to the mass‑less factorization scheme used in parton distribution function (PDF) analyses. We compute the complete set of two‑loop massive OMEs for twist‑2 operators in the Mellin‑\(N\) space using dimensional regularization (\(D=4-2\varepsilon\)). Integration‑by‑parts identities are solved with the Laporta algorithm, and the resulting master integrals are expressed in terms of nested harmonic sums and generalized polylogarithms. Renormalization is performed in the \(\overline{\text{MS}}\) scheme, including mass, coupling‑constant, and operator renormalization, and the transition to the variable‑flavor‑number scheme is carried out. Independent checks are provided by reproducing known massless limits and by verifying the Ward identities for the polarized case. Explicit analytic expressions for all required OMEs are obtained for arbitrary Mellin moment \(N\). The exhibit the expected logarithmic mass dependence \(\ln^k(m^2/Q^2)\) (\(k=1,2\)) and correctly reduce to the massless two‑loop Wilson coefficients. Numerical implementation shows a 1–3 % shift in the charm‑induced contributions to \(F_2\) and \(g_1\) at \(Q^2\sim 10\) GeV\(^2\), thereby improving the precision of global PDF fits and the extraction of the polarized gluon distribution.

Text: This study examines the autonomous enhancement characteristics of Sobolev-Poincaré inequalities via methodologies encompassing domain restriction and geometric rearrangement, thereby advancing the theoretical framework for functional inequalities in both analytic and geometric domains. The demonstrate that such symmetrization not only facilitates the simplification of function representation but also catalyzes self-reinforcing mechanisms within the inequalities, culminating in optimal embedding theorems for Sobolev spaces characterized by minimal differentiability requirements. These theoretical advancements are leveraged to establish conditions governing the emergence and smoothness of solutions to elliptic and parabolic partial differential equations, particularly within domains exhibiting irregular boundaries where conventional analytical tools are inapplicable. Moreover, the framework extends to metric spaces equipped with measures, underscoring the adaptability of the proposed techniques across diverse geometric configurations. The integration of domain restriction and geometric rearrangement strategies presents a cohesive paradigm for addressing challenges in non-smooth analytic settings, with theoretical applications spanning variational calculus, continuum mechanics, and geometric measure theory. This synthesis of methodologies not only clarifies the interplay between symmetry-informed approaches and functional inequality self-improvement but also provides a robust foundation for analyzing the qualitative attributes of nonlinear PDE solutions in complex geometric environments.

Text: Cloud Computing has fundamentally transformed how businesses and individuals access, store, and process information by delivering computational resources, including servers, storage systems, databases, networking infrastructure, and software applications, via the internet on a consumption-based pricing model. Rather than investing capital in expensive on-premises hardware and physical infrastructure, organizations can dynamically scale their IT resources upward or downward in response to demand fluctuations. Principal service models include Infrastructure as a Service, Platform as a Service, and Software as a Service, each offering distinct levels of operational control and configurational flexibility. Leading cloud service providers such as Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform offer extensive ecosystems of services supporting everything from machine learning workloads to enterprise resource planning systems. Data security, sovereignty considerations, and vendor dependency concerns remain important factors that organizations must carefully evaluate when formulating cloud computing adoption strategies.

Text: This investigation introduces a pioneering K-minus estimator for elucidating the extensive large-scale structure of the cosmos, thereby providing a formidable analytical tool for comprehending the spatial distribution of matter on cosmological scales. Our approach entails the utilization of a Gaussian random field as a surrogate for the true density field, thereby facilitating the establishment of a statistical framework for scrutinizing the large-scale structure. The K-minus estimator is derived from the intrinsic properties of the Gaussian random field, thereby enabling the estimation of the density field's variance and covariance, which are crucial for understanding the distribution of matter on large scales. Consequently, our empirical demonstrate the efficacy of the K-minus estimator approach, yielding accurate reconstructions of the density field and providing a novel paradigm for comprehending the large-scale structure of the universe. The far-reaching implications of this research are multifaceted, empowering the extraction of valuable insights into the evolution of the universe, the spatial distribution of matter, and the properties of dark matter.

Text: This study investigates the spin-polarization characteristics of diffusive and ballistic current in magnetron-sputtered L10-ordered epitaxial FePt thin films. Through a combination of density functional theory (DFT) calculations, scanning tunneling microscopy (STM), and magneto-transport measurements, we elucidate the spin-dependent transport properties of FePt. Our reveal that the L10-ordered FePt structure exhibits a high degree of spin-polarization at the Fermi level, with a calculated spin-polarization ratio of 0.85. The diffusive current component exhibits a higher spin-polarization ratio compared to the ballistic current component, with values of 0.92 and 0.79, respectively. The observed differences in spin-polarization ratio are attributed to the varying scattering mechanisms and electron-phonon interactions in the diffusive and ballistic current components. Our demonstrate the potential of magnetron-sputtered L10-ordered FePt thin films as high-performance spintronic materials, with applications in spin-polarized current injection and detection devices. The of this study provide valuable insights into the spin-dependent transport properties of FePt and highlight the importance of considering the interplay between diffusive and ballistic current components in the design of efficient spintronic devices.

We find that the choice of boundary conditions significantly influences the black hole entropy, with certain conditions yielding a discrete, quantized entropy that is stable with the principles of loop quantum gravity. Our outcomes have important implications for the understanding of black hole thermodynamics and the holographic principle, and shed new light on the long-standing question of black hole information paradox.

Text: This study investigates the occurrence of non-CKM (Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa) induced flavor violation in minimal supersymmetric SU(5) models. The minimal supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM) is a well-established framework for extending the Standard Model to include supersymmetry, and SU(5) is a popular grand unified theory that provides a natural explanation for the unification of the strong, weak, and electromagnetic forces. Within this framework, we analyze the constraints imposed by experimental searches for flavor-violating processes, particularly those involving supersymmetric particles and their subsequent decay products. Our analysis focuses on the minimal SU(5) model, which assumes a minimal set of supersymmetric particles and a specific pattern of symmetry breaking. We find that this model can accommodate non-CKM induced flavor violation, leading to intriguing predictions for supersymmetric particle searches at current and future colliders. Notably, we identify certain regions of parameter space that could potentially be probed by ongoing and future experimental searches, offering a novel opportunity to test the underlying supersymmetry and grand unification theories.

Text: This study provides a comprehensive examination of the Manin conjecture, which forecasts the asymptotic expansion of rational points of bounded height on Fano varieties, determined by the Picard number and anticanonical volume. Specifically, in two-dimensional cases, this conjecture yields a detailed description of the distribution of rational points on del Pezzo surfaces over number fields. By leveraging a combination of techniques, including universal torsor parametrizations, adelic group harmonic analysis, and a nuanced lattice point counting method in weighted projective cones, we derive the anticipated asymptotic formula, complete with an explicit Peyre constant, for a wide range of singular del Pezzo surfaces with a degree of at least 4. Notably, this encompasses all del Pezzo surfaces featuring at most Du Val singularities that possess a toric or almost-toric structure. Our findings not only validate the conjecture's predictions but also elucidate the intricate relationships between arithmetic geometry, toric geometry, and analytic number theory, ultimately reinforcing the conjecture's robustness and providing a thorough verification of its claims in two-dimensional scenarios.

Text: Image and video quality in Long Range Observation Systems (LOROS) suffer from atmospheric turbulence that causes small neighbourhoods in image frames to chaotically move in different directions and substantially hampers visual analysis of such image and video sequences. The paper presents a real-time algorithm for perfecting turbulence degraded videos by means of stabilization and resolution enhancement. The latter is achieved by exploiting the turbulent motion. The algorithm involves generation of a reference frame and estimation, for each incoming video frame, of a local image displacement map with respect to the reference frame; segmentation of the displacement map into two classes: stationary and moving objects and resolution enhancement of stationary objects, while preserving real motion. Experiments with synthetic and real-life sequences have shown that the enhanced videos, generated in real time, exhibit substantially better resolution and complete stabilization for stationary objects while retaining real motion.

Text: In this work, we focus on the theoretical underpinnings of graph rubbling, a process wherein a graph is subjected to a series of edge deletions resulting in a graph with the minimum number of edges, while ensuring that no isolated vertices are created. We introduce the concept of optimal rubbling, which seeks to identify the minimum number of edge deletions required to achieve the most reduced graph structure. A novel algorithm we propose to calculate the optimal rubbling of a given graph, leveraging a combination of breadth-first search and depth-first search techniques to efficiently identify essential vertices and minimize edge deletions — theoretical bounds are established for the time complexity of the proposed algorithm, demonstrating its scalability to large graph inputs. Empirical evaluations are conducted on a range of graph datasets, showcasing the algorithm's effectiveness in achieving near-optimal rubbling results. More broadly, the findings have pronounced implications for the analysis and optimization of complex networks, particularly in the context of network resilience and graph compression. Theoretical and practical applications of optimal rubbling are explored, highlighting its potential to inform graph-based decision-making and problem-solving strategies.

Text: This paper investigates the capacity of a class of modulo-sum relay channels, a type of wireless communication network where a source communicates with a destination through the assistance of a relay node. The modulo-sum relay channel is characterized by a modulo-sum operation at the relay node, which limits the range of the received signal. We derive an achievable rate region for this channel using a combination of the modulo-sum property and the concept of superposition coding. Our show that the capacity region of the modulo-sum relay channel is strictly smaller than that of the classical relay channel, indicating the loss of information due to the modulo-sum operation at the relay node. We further analyze the impact of the modulo-sum operation on the capacity-achieving distribution and demonstrate that it leads to a non-trivial distortion in the received signal. Our provide valuable insights into the design of wireless communication systems and highlight the importance of considering the modulo-sum operation in the analysis of relay channels. Our have implications for the development of efficient coding and modulation schemes for wireless communication networks.

Text: Swimming with a friend at low Reynolds number is a new, interdisciplinary work that explores the collective dynamics of two swimming organisms in a viscous fluid environment, characterized by low Reynolds number. Our research combines experimental observations and quantitative simulations to study the effects of hydrodynamic interactions on the swimming patterns and efficiency of two swimmers. We consider a simplified model of two coupled swimmers, each propelled by a flagellar motion, and use a low-Reynolds-number fluid dynamics code to simulate their motion in a two-dimensional plane. Our results demonstrate that the swimming patterns of the two organisms are significantly influenced by their hydrodynamic interactions, with the leading swimmer experiencing a drag reduction and the lagging swimmer experiencing an enhanced propulsion force. We also find that the swimming efficiency of the pair is significantly higher than that of a single swimmer, indicating that swimming with a friend can be a viable strategy for propulsion in low-Reynolds-number environments. Our findings have implications for the study of collective behavior in biological systems and the development of bio-inspired swimming robots.

Text: The local Universe is a complex, dynamically evolving system where stars, gas, and dark matter interact to shape the cosmic web. Accurate census of metals and baryons within stars is essential to understand the chemical enrichment history, galaxy evolution, and the formation of heavy elements in the Universe. However, current estimates of metal enrichment and baryonic mass budgets in local galaxies remain incomplete and inconsistent. We conducted a systematic photometric and spectroscopic survey of 10,000 stars in 50 nearby galaxies (d < 20 Mpc) using state-of-the-art telescopes and spectrographs. We leveraged machine learning algorithms to classify stars by spectral type, luminosity class, and chemical composition. Additionally, we employed advanced stellar models to derive metallicities and baryonic masses from observed spectral features. Our census reveals a significant increase in metal enrichment with cosmic time, consistent with expectations from Big Bang nucleosynthesis and stellar nucleosynthesis. We find that the baryonic mass budget in local galaxies is dominated by stars, with a mean metal mass fraction of 0.015. Our provide a crucial benchmark for future galaxy evolution models and shed new light on the complex interplay between star formation, chemical enrichment, and galaxy growth in the local Universe.

Text: The Mn_(2)NiGa alloy is a fascinating system exhibiting complex magnetic and structural properties, while recent studies have revealed its potential for displaying unique magnetic ordering phenomena, including ferrimagnetism. This necessitates a comprehensive investigation to elucidate the interplay between martensitic transition, magnetic ordering, and Fermi surface nesting in Mn_(2)NiGa. We employed a combination of experimental techniques, including X-ray diffraction, magnetization measurements, and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), to probe the structural and magnetic properties of Mn_(2)NiGa. Our experiments were conducted on high-quality single crystals of the alloy, allowing for a precise analysis of the martensitic transition and its impact on magnetic ordering. Contrary to expectations, we observed that Mn_(2)NiGa undergoes a martensitic transition at T_M = 210 K, accompanied by a change in magnetic ordering from antiferromagnetism to ferrimagnetism. ARPES measurements indicate that the Fermi surface nesting plays a crucial role in driving the magnetic ordering transition, with the emergence of a nested Fermi surface pocket at the transition temperature. Our provide new insights into the complex interplay between structural, magnetic, and electronic properties in Mn_(2)NiGa, shedding light on the underlying mechanisms governing its magnetic behavior.

Text: He is brilliant and wonderful and charismatic and loving when he's not using, but like every addict I have ever heard of, he becomes a stranger when he is, distant and foolish and self-destructive and broken and dangerous. I have struggled to reconcile these two people. Whatever the cause-a genetic predisposition, the divorce, my drug history, my overprotectiveness, my failure to protect him, my leniency, my harshness, my immaturity, all of these-Nic's addiction seemed to have had a life of its own. I have tried to reveal how insidiously addiction creeps into a family and takes over. So many times in the last decade I made mistakes out of ignorance, hope, or fear. I've tried to recount them all as and when they happened, in the hope that readers will recognize a wrong path before they take it. When they don't, however, I hope that they may realize that it is a path they can't blame themselves for having taken. When my child was born, it was impossible to imagine that he would suffer in the ways that Nic has suffered. Parents want only good things for their children. I was a typical parent who felt that this could not happen to us-not to my son. But though Nic is unique, he is every child. He could be yours. Finally, the reader should know that I have changed a few names and details in the book to obscure the identities of some of the people herein. I begin when Nic was born. The birth of a child is, for many if not every family, a transformative event of joy and optimism. It was for us.

Text: Here, we present a comprehensive theoretical framework for color superconductivity, a phenomenon predicted to occur in the high-density, high-temperature quark-gluon plasma that is thought to have existed in the early universe and may be present in the cores of neutron stars. Our effective theory combines the essential features of quantum chromodynamics (QCD) with the principles of superconductivity, providing a quantitative structure for insight into the emergence of color superconducting phases in dense quark matter. We derive the efficient Lagrangian for the color-superconducting state, incorporating both the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio (NJL) and the Polyakov-NJL models, and demonstrate that the resulting theory exhibits a rich phase structure, including the formation of Cooper pairs, the onset of color superconductivity, and the transition to a color-flavor locked (CFL) phase. Our outcomes indicate that color superconductivity can occur at temperatures and densities relevant to astrophysical environments, with implications for our understanding of the behavior of matter under extreme conditions. The reliable theory developed here offers a powerful tool for investigating the properties of color superconducting matter and its potential applications in astrophysics and cosmology.

Text: This paper establishes a connection between vertex algebras, simple modules for the Lie algebra of vector fields on a torus, and differential equations on complex tori. We consider a vertex algebra associated with a lattice and demonstrate that the simple modules for the Lie algebra of vector fields on a torus can be constructed as modules over this vertex algebra. Furthermore, we provide a bijective correspondence between the simple modules for the Lie algebra of vector fields on a torus and the solutions of certain differential equations on the complex torus, thus establishing a direct relationship between the representation theory of the Lie algebra and the solutions of differential equations on the torus. The differential equations in question are linear partial differential equations of finite type, and we show that the classification of simple modules for the Lie algebra is equivalent to the classification of solution spaces for these differential equations. Our provide new insights into the representation theory of the Lie algebra of vector fields on a torus and shed light on the interplay between vertex algebras, simple modules, and differential equations on complex tori.

Text: Theoretical analysis of own and literature investigations of sexual motivation with the use of the partition test [Kudryavtseva, 1987, 1994] in male mice was carried out. It has been shown that appearance of a receptive female in the neighboring compartment of common cage separated by perforated transparent partition produces the enhancement of testosterone level in blood and stimulates the behavioral activity near partition as a reaction to the receptive female in naive males. In many studies this behavioral activity is considered as sexual motivation, arising in this experimental context in male mice. The lack of correlation between behavioral parameters and gonad reaction of males on receptive female, uninterconnected changes of these two parameters as well as the lack of sexual behavior between naive male and female when partition is removed cast doubt on this data interpretation. It has been supposed that in naive males behavioral reaction to a receptive female is induced by positive incentive - odor of the female associated with nursing and warmth from mother and other females which look after posterity. Short-term increase of the level of testosterone (possessing rewarding properties) is innate stimulus-response reaction which stimulates and prolongs behavioral interest of male to receptive female. It has been supposed that after sexual experience female odor is associated in experienced males with sexual behavior directed to the sexual partner and resulted in the formation of sexual motivation. The data are considered also in the light of the theory of motivated behavior including "liking", "wanting" and "learning" [Robinson and Berridge, 1993, 2000].

The structural and morphological attributes of the deposited films were thoroughly analyzed using X-ray diffractometry (XRD) and atomic force microscopy (AFM), which collectively demonstrated that the high-resolution XRD measurements revealed a preferred (001) orientation while showcasing a remarkably low lattice mismatch with the substrate, a hallmark of epitaxial growth. Concurrently, AFM measurements revealed a smoothly textured film surface, characterized by an RMS roughness of approximately 1.5 nm. Further probing using high-energy X-ray diffraction (HEXRD) and Rutherford backscattering spectrometry (RBS) disclosed the stoichiometric makeup and elemental composition of the films, although the did expose the presence of Pb-rich and Ti-poor interfaces, a phenomenon ascribed to the Pb adatoms' diffusion during the post-annealing process. The presence of ferroelectric properties was subsequently confirmed using capacitance-voltage measurements, which unveiled a spontaneous polarization of approximately 100 μC/cm². This comprehensive assessment collectively underscores the successful growth of high-quality PbTiO3 films via MBE. The suggest that these materials may be judiciously employed in the creation of novel piezoelectric devices and sensing applications, with ongoing research focused on refining the growth conditions to further enhance film quality and properties.

Text: Carrier mobility is a pivotal parameter governing the performance of semiconductor nanostructure devices, yet it is often limited by surface‑related scattering and dielectric mismatch with the surrounding medium. Recent advances in dielectric engineering suggest that tailoring the local dielectric environment can suppress Coulombic impurity scattering and phonon coupling, thereby unlocking higher mobilities in low‑dimensional systems. We fabricated silicon and III‑V nanowires (diameters 10–30 nm) and two‑dimensional quantum wells encapsulated in a series of high‑κ dielectrics (HfO₂, Al₂O₃) and low‑κ polymers (CYTOP). Systematic variation of dielectric constant (κ = 2–25) was combined with temperature‑dependent Hall measurements and low‑frequency noise spectroscopy. Complementary first‑principles density‑functional calculations and Boltzmann transport simulations were employed to quantify the impact of dielectric screening on ionized‑impurity and surface‑optical phonon scattering rates. Dielectric environments with κ ≥ 15 reduced the effective impurity scattering potential by up to 70 % and suppressed surface‑optical phonon emission, yielding a 3.2‑fold increase in room‑temperature electron mobility (from 150 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ to 480 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹) in 15‑nm Si nanowires. Similar trends were observed in InAs quantum wells, where mobility rose from 4 800 to 9 200 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹. The demonstrate that dielectric engineering offers a scalable route to overcome intrinsic mobility limits in semiconductor nanostructures, informing the design of next‑generation high‑speed nanoelectronic and optoelectronic devices.

Text: The ratio of shear viscosity to entropy density (η/s) provides a stringent probe of the microscopic dynamics of strongly interacting matter. In the context of compact stars, strange quark matter (SQM) – a deconfined phase of up, down, and strange quarks – may constitute the core or entire star. Establishing theoretical limits on η/s for SQM is essential for interpreting gravitational‑wave damping, thermal evolution, and rotational stability of such objects, and for testing the conjectured Kovtun‑Son‑Starinets (KSS) bound (η/s ≥ 1/4π). We employed a combined approach: (i) perturbative quantum chromodynamics (pQCD) at next‑to‑leading order to compute the shear viscosity from quark–quark scattering amplitudes, incorporating finite quark masses and running coupling at baryon chemical potentials μ_B = 0.5–1.5 GeV; (ii) a Nambu–Jona‑Lasinio (NJL) model calibrated to lattice QCD thermodynamics to obtain the entropy density s(T,μ_B); and (iii) gauge‑gravity duality techniques to derive an analytic lower bound on η/s for a class of holographic SQM analogues. Consistency checks were performed against existing neutron‑star cooling data. Our analysis yields a density‑dependent lower bound η/s ≥ (0.28 ± 0.03) /4π for SQM, modestly tighter than the universal KSS value. At μ_B ≈ 1 GeV the computed η/s approaches this bound, indicating near‑perfect fluidity, whereas at lower densities the ratio rises by up to a factor of three. The suggest that SQM cores can sustain rapid differential rotation without excessive viscous damping, offering a discriminant for future multimessenger observations of compact stars.

We consider a model of multiple scattering of a photon among superradiant pairs and calculate the elastic mean free path and the group velocity. The decrease in dark matter clustering strength is, however, almost entirely offset by an increase in halo bias, so predictions for galaxy clustering are barely altered. Models which fit observed luminosity functions predict projected 2-point correlation functions which scatter by about 10-20 per cent on large scale and by larger factors on small scale, depending both on cosmology and on details of galaxy formation. Measurements of the pairwise velocity distribution prefer the WMAP1 cosmology, but careful treatment of the systematics is needed. Given current modelling uncertainties, it is not easy to distinguish the WMAP1 and WMAP3 cosmologies on the basis of low-redshift galaxy properties. Text: Family values are the shared beliefs, principles, and behavioral norms that define how a family unit understands itself and relates both internally and to the broader world. These values - whether explicitly articulated or absorbed through observation - shape children's fundamental understanding of what is important: how to treat others, what to prioritize, how to handle conflict, and what constitutes a meaningful life. In healthy families, values like honesty, respect, generosity, and accountability are not just stated principles but lived realities, modeled consistently by the adults in the home. When family values align with ethical principles and are communicated with love rather than fear, they provide children with a moral compass that guides them through complexity and temptation. However, family values can also be limiting or harmful when they prioritize conformity over individuality, when they exclude those who are different, or when they are used to justify control rather than to nurture growth. The best family values are those that are grounded in genuine care and that prepare individuals to live with integrity in a diverse and complex world.

Text: In computing, a compiler is a computer program that translates computer code written in one programming language (the source language) into another language (the target language). The name "compiler" is primarily used for programs that translate source code from a high-level programming language to a lower level language (assembly language, object code, or machine code) to create an executable program.There are many different types of compilers which produce output in different useful forms. A cross-compiler produces code for a different CPU or operating system than the one on which the cross-compiler itself runs. A bootstrap compiler is written in the language that it intends to compile. A program that translates from a low-level language to a higher level one is a decompiler. A program that translates between high-level languages is usually called a source-to-source compiler or transpiler.

Text: The coupling between accretion inflows and relativistic outflows in Galactic black hole binaries remains a central problem in high-energy astrophysics. Cygnus X-1, the archetypal persistent black-hole candidate, offers a unique laboratory to investigate rapid, correlated variability across the radio and X-ray bands. We performed a coordinated multi-wavelength campaign using the Karl G, while jansky Very Large Array (5 GHz) and the *NICER* X-ray Timing Instrument (0.2-12 keV). Over a 48-hour interval, continuous radio monitoring (1 s cadence) was paired with high-time-resolution X-ray light curves (0.1 s). Cross-correlation analysis employed the Z-transformed Discrete Correlation Function (ZDCF) to quantify lag signatures, while spectral evolution was tracked via time-resolved hardness ratios and radio spectral indices derived from simultaneous dual-frequency observations. We detect a pronounced X-ray flare (peak increase ≈ 45 % above baseline) preceding a radio outburst by (τ = 5.2 pm 0.7) s, establishing a sub-minute lag consistent with internal shock propagation in a compact jet. The radio flare exhibits a flat-to-inverted spectrum (α = 0.12 ± 0.03), indicating freshly accelerated electrons. The X-ray hardness softens during the flare peak, suggesting a transient increase in coronal temperature. These provide the first direct measurement of a rapid radio-X-ray lag in Cygnus X-1, supporting models where X-ray variability seeds jet disturbances that evolve on light-travel timescales within the inner jet base.

Text: This study delves into the concept of ensemble averageability in network spectra, examining the conditions under which an ensemble of network spectra can be averaged to reveal a representative underlying structure. We propose a novel structure for assessing ensemble averageability based on the degree of spectral overlap and connectivity similarity between networks. Using a suite of synthetic and real-world network datasets, we validate our framework and establish its utility in identifying instances of ensemble averageability. Our outcomes indicate that while ensemble averageability is not a universal property of network spectra, it can be a valuable tool for identifying common structural features and patterns that underlie disparate networks. The findings of this study have implications for a range of applications, including network analysis, machine learning, and data-driven modeling of complex systems.

Text: The search for leptoquarks, hypothetical particles that exhibit both lepton and quark properties, is an active area of research in particle physics. Leptoquarks can be classified into scalar and gauge types, each with distinct implications for the Standard Model of fundamental interactions. The rare $K_L^0$ and $B^0$ decays to lepton pairs offer a unique opportunity to constrain leptoquark masses. We perform a statistical analysis of the branching fractions and decay rates for the $K_L^0 \to e^{\mp} \mu^{\pm}$ and $B^0 \to e^{\mp} \tau^{\pm}$ decays, incorporating the latest experimental and theoretical calculations. We use a global fit approach to determine the allowed mass ranges for scalar and gauge leptoquarks, while accounting for systematic uncertainties and correlations between the decays. Our analysis yields stringent mass limits for scalar leptoquarks, with $M_{\text{SQ}} > 3.2$ TeV at 95% confidence level, and for gauge leptoquarks, with $M_{\text{GQ}} > 2.5$ TeV. These provide valuable constraints on leptoquark models and offer a benchmark for future experimental searches.

Text: Previous molecular gas observations at arcsecond-scale resolution of the Seyfert 2 galaxy M51 suggest the presence of a dense circumnuclear rotating disk, which may be the reservoir for fueling the active nucleus and obscures it from direct view in the optical. However, our recent interferometric CO(3-2) observations show a hint of a velocity gradient perpendicular to the rotating disk, which suggests a more complex structure than previously thought. To image the putative circumnuclear molecular gas disk at sub-arcsecond resolution to better understand both the spatial distribution and kinematics of the molecular gas. We carried out CO(2-1) and CO(1-0) line observations of the nuclear region of M51 with the new A configuration of the IRAM Plateau de Bure Interferometer, yielding a spatial resolution lower than 15 pc. The high resolution images show no clear evidence of a disk, aligned nearly east-west and perpendicular to the radio jet axis, as suggested by previous observations, but show two separate features located on the eastern and western sides of the nucleus. The western feature shows an elongated structure along the jet and a good velocity correspondence with optical emission lines associated with the jet, suggesting that this feature is a jet-entrained gas. The eastern feature is elongated nearly east-west ending around the nucleus. A velocity gradient appears in the same direction with increasingly blueshifted velocities near the nucleus. This velocity gradient is in the opposite sense of that previously inferred for the putative circumnuclear disk. Possible explanations for the observed molecular gas distribution and kinematics are that a rotating gas disk disturbed by the jet, gas streaming toward the nucleus, or a ring with another smaller counter- or Keplarian-rotating gas disk inside.

Text: We report on the AAT-AAOmega LRG Pilot observing run to establish the feasibility of a large spectroscopic survey using the new AAOmega instrument. We have selected Luminous Red Galaxies (LRGs) using single epoch SDSS riz-photometry to i<20.5 and z<20.2. We have observed in 3 fields including the COSMOS field and the COMBO-17 S11 field, obtaining a sample of ~600 redshift z>=0.5 LRGs. Exposure times varied from 1 - 4 hours to determine the minimum exposure for AAOmega to make an essentially complete LRG redshift survey in average conditions. We show that LRG redshifts to i<20.5 can measured in approximately 1.5hr exposures and present comparisons with 2SLAQ and COMBO-17 (photo-)redshifts. Crucially, the riz selection coupled with the 3-4 times improved AAOmega throughput is shown to extend the LRG mean redshift from z=0.55 for 2SLAQ to z=0.681+/- 0.005 for riz-selected LRGs. This extended range is vital for maximising the S/N for the detection of the baryon acoustic oscillations (BAOs). Furthermore, we show that the amplitude of LRG clustering is s_0 = 9.9+/-0.7 h^-1 Mpc, as high as that seen in the 2SLAQ LRG Survey. Consistent for the real-space amplitude are found from projected and semi-projected correlation functions. This high clustering amplitude is consistent with a long-lived population whose bias evolves as predicted by a simple ``high-peaks'' model. We conclude that a redshift survey of 360 000 LRGs over 3000deg^2, with an effective volume some 4 times bigger than previously used to detect BAO with LRGs, is possible with AAOmega in 170 nights.

Text: A mesh is a graph that divides physical space into regularly-shaped regions. Meshes computations form the basis of many applications, e.g. finite-element , image rendering, and collision detection. In one important mesh primitive, called a mesh update, each mesh vertex stores a value and repeatedly updates this value based on the values stored in all neighboring vertices. The performance of a mesh update depends on the layout of the mesh in memory. This paper shows how to find a memory layout that guarantees that the mesh update has asymptotically optimal memory performance for any set of memory parameters. Such a memory layout is called cache-oblivious. Formally, for a $d$-dimensional mesh $G$, block size $B$, and cache size $M$ (where $M=\Omega(B^d)$), the mesh update of $G$ uses $O(1+|G|/B)$ memory transfers. The paper also shows how the mesh-update performance degrades for smaller caches, where $M=o(B^d)$. The paper then gives two algorithms for finding cache-oblivious mesh layouts. The first layout algorithm runs in time $O(|G|\log^2|G|)$ both in expectation and with high probability on a RAM. It uses $O(1+|G|\log^2(|G|/M)/B)$ memory transfers in expectation and $O(1+(|G|/B)(\log^2(|G|/M) + \log|G|))$ memory transfers with high probability in the cache-oblivious and disk-access machine (DAM) models. The layout is obtained by finding a fully balanced decomposition tree of $G$ and then performing an in-order traversal of the leaves of the tree. The second algorithm runs faster by almost a $\log|G|/\log\log|G|$ factor in all three memory models, both in expectation and with high probability. The layout obtained by finding a relax-balanced decomposition tree of $G$ and then performing an in-order traversal of the leaves of the tree.

Text: Studying the internal structure of extragalactic jets is crucial for understanding their physics. Our indicate that the jet is substantially stratified and different modes of the instability grow inside the jet at different distances to the jet axis. Twistor theory, by encoding space‑time geometry into holomorphic objects, has proved powerful for point particles and strings, suggesting that a twistor‑based approach could clarify the underlying symmetries and constraints of higher‑dimensional extended objects. Starting from the standard Nambu–Goto action, we introduce a pair of twistor variables \((Z^{A}_{\alpha},\bar Z_{A}^{\dot\alpha})\) for each world‑volume point, together with incidence relations that enforce the embedding coordinates as bilinears in the twistors. The resulting first‑order action incorporates Lagrange multipliers imposing the twistor reality conditions and the area‑preserving diffeomorphism constraints. Canonical analysis yields a closed set of second‑class constraints, which are solved by passing to Dirac brackets, thereby exhibiting an explicit \(SU(2,2)\) (or \(OSp(8|4)\) in the supersymmetric extension) symmetry. Quantization proceeds via the twistor Hilbert space, where the membrane’s physical states are identified with cohomology classes of a BRST operator built from the constraint algebra. The two‑twistor formulation reproduces the classical equations of motion of the Nambu–Goto membrane while rendering the world‑volume diffeomorphism invariance linear in twistor space. It reveals hidden conformal symmetries and simplifies the constraint structure, allowing a direct construction of membrane wavefunctions as twistor functions of homogeneity degree zero. Moreover, the approach naturally extends to supersymmetric membranes, where the twistor variables accommodate fermionic components and yield a manifestly super‑conformal action. These suggest that twistor provide a viable route toward a covariant quantization of membranes and may illuminate the geometric underpinnings of M‑theory.

Text: Microfluidic chips have revolutionized laboratory-scale fluid dynamics by enabling precise control over fluid flow and mixing. Acoustic resonances, however, can significantly affect fluid behavior in these devices, leading to undesired flow instabilities and decreased efficiency. A comprehensive understanding of acoustic resonances in microfluidic chips is essential for optimizing their performance. This study combines full-image micro-Particle Image Velocimetry (micro-PIV) experiments and numerical simulations to investigate acoustic resonances in microfluidic chips. A custom-designed microfluidic chip was fabricated to produce a resonant cavity, which was then subjected to a range of acoustic frequencies using a piezoelectric transducer. Simultaneously, micro-PIV experiments were performed to visualize and quantify the resulting fluid flow patterns. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations were also conducted using a finite element to model the acoustic- fluid interaction. Our study reveals that acoustic resonances induce complex flow patterns, including vortex shedding and flow recirculation, which can drastically affect fluid mixing and transport in microfluidic chips. Numerical simulations and micro-PIV experiments demonstrate excellent agreement, providing a detailed understanding of the acoustic-resonance-induced flow behavior. The of this study will contribute to the design and optimization of microfluidic chips, enabling their more efficient and reliable operation in various applications.

Text: We investigate the nonrelativistic phase in gamma-ray burst (GRB) afterglows, a transitional period preceding the eventual deceleration of the relativistic blast wave to nonrelativistic velocities. By comparing the observed afterglow properties to predictions from nonrelativistic hydrodynamics simulations, we identify distinct signatures of the transition from relativistic to nonrelativistic expansion, including the emergence of a synchrotron-dominated spectrum and the onset of significant deceleration of the blast wave. The results of our work point to that the nonrelativistic phase in GRB afterglows is characterized by a rapid evolution of the spectral index and a marked decline in the peak energy, which can be attributed to the interplay between the blast wave dynamics and the surrounding interstellar medium. Text: The Marcus-Lushnikov process is a finite stochastic particle system in which each particle is entirely characterized by its mass. Each pair of particles with masses $x$ and $y$ merges into a single particle at a given rate $K(x,y)$. We consider a {it strongly gelling} kernel behaving as $K(x,y)=xalpha y + x yalpha$ for some $alphain (0,1]$. In such a case, it is well-known that {it gelation} occurs, that is, giant particles emerge. Then two possible models for hydrodynamic limits of the Marcus-Lushnikov process arise: the Smoluchowski equation, in which the giant particles are inert, and the Flory equation, in which the giant particles interact with finite ones. We show that, when using a suitable cut-off coagulation kernel in the Marcus-Lushnikov process and letting the number of particles increase to infinity, the possible limits solve either the Smoluchowski equation or the Flory equation. We also study the asymptotic behaviour of the largest particle in the Marcus-Lushnikov process without cut-off and show that there is only one giant particle. This single giant particle represents, asymptotically, the lost mass of the solution to the Flory equation.

Text: Nuclear activity in late‑type galaxies provides a key diagnostic of black‑hole growth and star‑formation feedback within dense environments. The Virgo Cluster, as the nearest rich galaxy cluster, offers an unprecedented laboratory to assess how cluster processes modulate the incidence and nature of active galactic nuclei (AGN) in spirals and irregulars, yet a comprehensive, homogeneous census of their nuclear spectra remains lacking. We assembled a complete, magnitude‑limited sample of 312 late‑type Virgo members (Hubble types Sa–Im, \(M_{B}<-16\) mag) from the VCC catalog. Optical nuclear spectra were obtained from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (DR17) and supplemented with long‑slit observations at the ESO 3.6 m telescope for 48 galaxies lacking SDSS coverage. Emission‑line fluxes were measured and corrected for underlying stellar absorption using pPXF fits. Diagnostic diagrams (BPT, WHAN) were employed to classify nuclei as Seyfert, LINER, composite, or star‑forming, and X‑ray (Chandra) and radio (VLA) data were consulted to identify obscured AGN. Host properties (stellar mass, bulge‑to‑disk ratio, local density) were derived from multi‑band photometry. Nuclear activity is detected in 27 ± 3 % of the sample, with Seyfert/LINER fractions of 5 % and 9 % respectively, while 13 % show composite spectra. The AGN fraction rises steeply with stellar mass (\(>10^{10}\,M_{\odot}\)) and correlates with higher local galaxy density, indicating that both mass‑driven black‑hole fueling and cluster‑induced interactions enhance nuclear activity. Conversely, low‑mass dwarfs are overwhelmingly star‑forming (≈85 %). These establish a benchmark for environmental influences on black‑hole growth in late‑type galaxies.

We demonstrate that these flavour projections can be used to construct a consistent and predictive flavour theory, which provides a new perspective on the flavour puzzle in particle physics. Furthermore, our analysis shows that the geometric discretization can be used to derive a flavour-dependent mass matrix, which is in agreement with experimental observations and provides a possible solution to the hierarchy problem in the Standard Model. Text: Ultraluminous X-ray sources (ULXs) are extragalactic point sources whose apparent X-ray luminosities exceed the Eddington limit for typical stellar-mass black holes. Their inferred luminosities are pivotal for distinguishing between super-Eddington accretion onto stellar-mass compact objects and accretion onto intermediate-mass black holes. However, luminosity estimates are highly sensitive to the adopted spectral model, introducing a major systematic uncertainty that hampers population studies. We assembled a homogeneous sample of 84 ULXs observed with *XMM-Newton* and *Chandra* (0.3-10 keV) and performed simultaneous spectral fitting using three widely employed phenomenological models: (i) an absorbed power-law (PL), (ii) a multicolour disc blackbody (MCD), and (iii) a combined PL+MCD (PL+MCD). For each fit we derived the absorption-corrected 0.3-10 keV luminosity, propagated statistical errors, and evaluated model preference via the Akaike information criterion. Monte-Carlo simulations quantified the impact of model-induced bias on the luminosity distribution. The PL model systematically overestimates ULX luminosities by 30-45 % relative to the MCD model, while the PL+MCD yields intermediate values (≈15 % higher than MCD). The bias is most pronounced for sources with soft excesses (kT ≲ 0.3 keV) and for spectra with limited photon counts (<500). Consequently, classification of ∼20 % of the sample as candidate intermediate-mass black holes under PL fits collapses to <5 % under MCD fits. Crucially, our underscore the necessity of model-aware luminosity reporting for robust ULX population inferences.

Text: The concentration function, introduced by Lévy, quantifies the maximal probability that a real‑valued random variable \(X\) lies in an interval of prescribed length. Recent advances have highlighted deep connections between concentration phenomena and number‑theoretic properties of the underlying distribution, particularly through Diophantine approximation of the support points. However, a systematic quantitative framework linking the rate of approximation of irrational parameters to sharp bounds on the concentration function remains underdeveloped. We consider sums of independent, identically distributed random variables with lattice‑type and non‑lattice components determined by a real parameter \(\alpha\). Employing metric Diophantine approximation, we classify \(\alpha\) according to its irrationality exponent \(\mu(\alpha)\) and construct explicit majorants for the concentration function \(Q_X(\varepsilon)=\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\mathbb{P}\{X\in[x,x+\varepsilon]\}\). The analysis combines Fourier–analytic techniques, Esseen’s inequality, and recent bounds on exponential sums over well‑approximable numbers, yielding piecewise estimates that adapt to the Diophantine type of \(\alpha\). For any \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(\alpha\) with \(\mu(\alpha)=\kappa\), we prove \[ Q_X(\varepsilon)\le C\,\varepsilon^{1-1/\kappa}+o(1), \] where \(C\) depends only on the distribution’s variance. In particular, for badly approximable \(\alpha\) (\(\kappa=2\)) the concentration decays at the optimal rate \(\varepsilon^{1/2}\), while for Liouville numbers the bound deteriorates in accordance with \(\kappa\). These unify and extend previous ad‑hoc estimates, offering a comprehensive Diophantine‑based description of concentration behavior.

Text: An In-Depth Investigation of General Relativistic Flux Variations Induced by Accretion Disk Instabilities in Sagittarius A* Reveals a Complicated Interplay between Magnetohydrodynamic Phenomena and Gravitational Influences. A bespoke general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) code was custom-designed to model the emergence and saturation of MRI within the accretion disk encasing Sgr A*. Our meticulously executed computations demonstrate irrefutably that the advent of MRI is directly responsible for the creation of highly dynamic, turbulent structures within the accretion disk. These turbulent dynamics, in turn, give rise to marked fluctuations in the X-ray flux emitted by Sgr A*, thereby underscoring the intrinsic coupling between instability-driven dynamics and flux variations. Thorough analysis of the flux modulations obtained from our simulations, juxtaposed with observational data acquired by X-ray telescopes, reveals a striking correspondence between theoretical predictions and empirical observations. Notably, our computations indicate that the quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) exhibited in the X-ray flux are commensurate with observed frequencies, lending credence to the theory that disk instabilities are a primary generator of these phenomena. Ultimately, this comprehensive investigation affirms the crucial contribution of disk instabilities to the observed flux modulations in Sgr A*, providing profound insights into the intricate physics governing the accretion dynamics of supermassive black holes in galactic centers. Text: In this work, we present six novel conjectures that generalize or are related to Andrica's Conjecture, a well-known statement in number theory concerning consecutive prime numbers. Building on this, the first conjecture, known as the Generalized Andrica Conjecture, proposes that for any real number x greater than one, there exists a prime number p such that p and p+x are coprime, with the product of their prime factors exceeding x^2 — the second conjecture, the Andrica Conjecture for Twin Primes, posits that for any prime number p greater than 3, there exists another prime number q such that q-p is at most 2 and the product of their prime factors exceeds 2p. Three additional conjectures explore the relationship between Andrica's Conjecture and the distribution of prime numbers, particularly focusing on the distribution of prime gaps. Furthermore, we examine the possibility of extending Andrica's Conjecture to other types of numbers, such as the powers of 2 and the prime numbers of the form 2^k+1. As a result, lastly, we investigate the implications of these conjectures on the Riemann Hypothesis and the distribution of prime numbers, with the goal of shedding new light on the fundamental properties of prime numbers and their distribution.

Text: We investigate the phenomenon of birefringence, encompassing rotation of polarization plane and spin dichroism, in deuterons interacting with a carbon target. Furthermore, we observed a marked spin dichroism signal, indicating a strong dependence of the scattering cross-section on the spin orientation of the deuterons. These findings are consistent with theoretical predictions based on the relativistic Dirac equation and the Foldy-Wouthuysen transformation. The observed birefringence and spin dichroism effects are attributed to the interference between the Coulomb and spin-orbit interactions in the scattering process. Our results provide new understanding into the behavior of polarized deuterons in matter and have implications for applications in nuclear physics, materials science, and quantum information processing. Text: Recursive parameter estimation algorithms are central to adaptive signal processing, system identification, and online learning, yet rigorous characterizations of their asymptotic speed of convergence remain fragmented across disciplines. we develop a unified analytical framework for quantifying the rate of convergence of a broad class of stochastic recursive procedures defined by the update rule \(\theta_{n+1}= \theta_n + \gamma_n H(\theta_n,X_{n+1})\), where \(\{\gamma_n\}\) is a diminishing step‑size sequence and \(H\) satisfies mild regularity and martingale‑difference conditions, and by exploiting Lyapunov function techniques together with a refined martingale central limit theorem, we derive explicit non‑asymptotic bounds that capture the interplay between the step‑size schedule, the curvature of the underlying loss surface, and the noise moments of the observation process. Notably, in particular, for step‑sizes of the form \(\gamma_n = n^{-\alpha}\) with \(\alpha\in(0.5,1]\), we prove almost‑sure convergence rates of order \(O(n^{-\alpha/2})\) in mean‑square error, and establish optimality in the minimax sense under Gaussian noise; numerical simulations for adaptive linear regression and Kalman‑filter‑type models corroborate the theoretical predictions, highlighting the practical relevance of the derived rates for designing efficient online estimators.

Text: We consider the quadratic family of maps given by $f_{a}(x)=1-a x^2$ with $x\in [-1,1]$, where $a$ is a Benedicks-Carleson parameter. For each of these chaotic dynamical systems we study the extreme value distribution of the stationary stochastic processes $X_0,X_1,...$, given by $X_{n}=f_a^n$, for every integer $n\geq0$, where each random variable $X_n$ is distributed according to the unique absolutely continuous, invariant probability of $f_a$. Using techniques developed by Benedicks and Carleson, we show that the limiting distribution of $M_n=\max\{X_0,...,X_{n-1}\}$ is the same as that which would apply if the sequence $X_0,X_1,...$ was independent and identically distributed. Text: This paper contributes to the study of ring theory by establishing universal localisations of hereditary rings, a class of rings that has garnered significant attention in recent years due to its connections to homological algebra and module theory. Text: The proliferation of uncertain data in various fields has led to an increasing demand for efficient relational processing . We implemented FaSRPUD on top of a commercial relational database management system (RDBMS) and evaluated its performance using a suite of benchmark queries. Our experimental demonstrate that FaSRPUD significantly outperforms existing in terms of query execution time and memory usage, achieving a 3.5-fold improvement in processing uncertain queries. Text: We consider a brane world in an arbitrary number of dimensions without Z_2 symmetry and derive the effective Einstein equation on the brane, where its right-hand side is given by the matter on the brane and the curvature in the bulk. The latter corresponds to formulating an explicit junction condition on the mean of the extrinsic curvature, analogue to the Israel junction condition for the jump of the extrinsic curvature. Text: Strong coupling between excitons in semiconductor quantum wells and photons confined in photonic crystal (PhC) slabs enables the formation of exciton‑polariton quasiparticles with tailored dispersion and enhanced nonlinearities. While extensive work has addressed planar microcavities, a comprehensive quantum‑theoretical description of exciton‑photon interaction in PhC slabs—where the in‑plane periodicity and vertical confinement jointly shape the electromagnetic mode structure—is still lacking. We develop a second‑quantized Hamiltonian that treats the quantum‑well excitonic field and the Bloch‑mode photon field of a two‑dimensional PhC slab on equal footing. The photon modes are obtained from a rigorous plane‑wave expansion of Maxwell’s equations with realistic dielectric contrast, yielding complex eigenfrequencies and field profiles. Exciton operators are introduced for each quantum‑well subband, and the light‑matter coupling matrix elements are calculated by overlap integrals of the excitonic envelope functions with the transverse electric field of each Bloch mode. The resulting Hopfield‑type eigenvalue problem is solved numerically to extract polariton band structures, lifetimes, and Hopfield coefficients across the Brillouin zone. The model predicts the emergence of multiple polariton branches, including symmetry‑protected dark states and ultra‑slow‑light polaritons near band‑edge points. Strong coupling persists despite radiative losses, with Rabi splittings up to 15 meV for GaAs quantum wells embedded in a high‑index (Si) PhC slab. The dispersion can be engineered via lattice constant and slab thickness, enabling tunable group velocities and enhanced polariton‑polariton interactions. These provide a quantitative framework for designing PhC‑based polaritonic devices such as low‑threshold lasers, all‑optical switches, and quantum simulators.

Text: We report experiments on Fabry-Perot electron interferometers in the integer quantum Hall regime. The GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructure devices consist of two constrictions defined by etch trenches in 2D electron layer, enclosing an approximately circular island. The interferometer is formed by counterpropagating chiral edge channels coupled by tunneling in the two constrictions. Interference fringes are observed as conductance oscillations, similar to the Aharonov-Bohm effect. Front gates deposited in etch trenches allow to fine-tune the device and to change the constriction filling f relative to the bulk filling. Quantum-coherent conductance oscillations are observed on the f = 1 - 4 plateaus. On plateau f we observe f conductance oscillations per fundamental flux period h/e. This is attributed to the dominance of the electron-electron Coulomb interaction, effectively mixing Landau level occupation. On the other hand, the back-gate charge period is the same (one electron) on all plateaus, independent of filling. This is attributed to the self-consistent electrostatics in the large electron island. We also report dependence of the oscillation period on front-gate voltage for f = 1, 2 and 4 for three devices. Text: Numerous ongoing experiments aim at detecting WIMP dark matter particles from the galactic halo directly through WIMP-nucleon interactions. We estimate the sensitivity for various detector configurations using Monte Carlo and we show that the strongest signal is found in the relatively few high recoil energy events. Measuring beta to the precision of ~0.03 will require detecting more than 10^4 WIMP events with nuclear recoil energies greater than 100 keV for a WIMP mass of 100 GeV and a 32S target. This number corresponds to ~10^6 events at all energies. Furthermore, Theorem 2 posits that if $K_1$ and $K_2$ are compact, convex, and idempotent subsets of $E$ such that $K_1 \cap K_2 = \emptyset$, then a supporting hyperplane $H$ separates $K_1$ and $K_2$. Analytical tractability is achieved via a hierarchy of moment‑closure approximations and a variational inference scheme that minimizes the Kullback‑Leibler divergence between true and approximated posterior distributions. The theory is implemented in a modular computational toolbox and validated on benchmark problems including stochastic differential equations, fuzzy‑logic controllers, and hybrid dynamical systems. The proposed framework yields closed‑form expressions for propagated uncertainty moments and provides tight probabilistic bounds on system outputs. Comparative experiments demonstrate a 30‑45 % reduction in estimation error relative to conventional Monte‑Carlo and polynomial chaos , while requiring an order of magnitude fewer samples. Moreover, the information‑geometric perspective reveals intrinsic curvature metrics that predict sensitivity to model misspecification, offering a novel diagnostic for system reliability under uncertainty.

Text: This paper presents DOEF, a novel Dynamic Object Evaluation Framework designed to assess the performance and behavior of complex objects in various dynamic environments. Developed to address the limitations of traditional evaluation frameworks, DOEF integrates machine learning and computer vision techniques to provide a comprehensive and adaptive assessment of object properties and attributes. By leveraging a modular architecture, DOEF enables researchers to dynamically configure and extend the framework to accommodate diverse object categories and evaluation scenarios. The framework comprises a data preprocessing module, a feature extraction module, and a decision-making module, which collectively enable the evaluation of object properties such as shape, size, color, texture, and motion. DOEF has been successfully applied to a range of applications, including object recognition, tracking, and classification, demonstrating its potential to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of object evaluation tasks. Through its flexibility, scalability, and adaptability, DOEF offers a powerful tool for researchers and practitioners seeking to develop and evaluate complex object-based systems.

Text: Lithium niobate has emerged as a promising material for integrated photonics due to its exceptional electro-optic and nonlinear optical properties. Microring resonators, in particular, have shown great potential for applications in optical communication and sensing. In this study, we designed and fabricated electro-optically tunable microring resonators in lithium niobate using a combination of photolithography and dry etching techniques. The microring resonators were then characterized using a tapered fiber coupling system, allowing for precise control over the input wavelength and polarization. Our demonstrate a high-quality factor (Q) of over 10^5 and a resonance wavelength shift of up to 1.2 nm/V, indicating a strong electro-optic tuning effect. The devices exhibited a low power consumption and fast tuning speeds, making them suitable for various applications. These showcase the potential of lithium niobate microring resonators as compact, efficient, and highly tunable photonic devices, paving the way for their integration into next-generation optical systems. Further research is expected to optimize the device performance and explore their applications in optical communication, sensing, and quantum optics.

Text: We consider power allocation algorithms for fixed-rate transmission over Nakagami-m non-ergodic block-fading channels with perfect transmitter and receiver channel state information and discrete input signal constellations, under both short- and long-term power constraints. Optimal power allocation schemes are shown to be direct applications of previous in the literature. We show that the SNR exponent of the optimal short-term scheme is given by m times the Singleton bound. We also illustrate the significant gains available by employing long-term power constraints. In particular, we analyze the optimal long-term solution, showing that zero outage can be achieved provided that the corresponding short-term SNR exponent with the same system parameters is strictly greater than one. Conversely, if the short-term SNR exponent is smaller than one, we show that zero outage cannot be achieved. In this case, we derive the corresponding long-term SNR exponent as a function of the Singleton bound. Due to the nature of the expressions involved, the complexity of optimal schemes may be prohibitive for system implementation. We therefore propose simple sub-optimal power allocation schemes whose outage probability performance is very close to the minimum outage probability obtained by optimal schemes. We also show the applicability of these techniques to practical systems employing orthogonal frequency division multiplexing.

Text: This study presents a comprehensive analysis of the physical and spectral characteristics of T8 and later-type dwarfs, a subcategory of ultracool dwarfs that exhibit extremely low surface temperatures and unique atmospheric properties. Utilizing a combination of spectroscopic and photometric observations from the Hubble Space Telescope and the Very Large Telescope, we have gathered a vast dataset of 100 T8 and later-type dwarfs, spanning a temperature range of 500-700 K. Our results reveal a strong correlation between the spectral type and the physical properties of these objects, with T8 dwarfs exhibiting a mean surface gravity of 10^4.5 cm/s^2 and a mean radius of 0.1 R_sun. Furthermore, we have identified distinct spectral features in the near-infrared and optical regions, including the presence of methane and water absorption bands, which are indicative of the complex atmospheric chemistry of these objects. Our analysis also suggests that T8 and later-type dwarfs are characterized by a considerable level of chromospheric activity, with frequent bursts of intense emission in the H_alpha and He I lines. These outcomes provide new insights into the physical and spectral properties of T8 and later-type dwarfs, and highlight the importance of continued observational and theoretical research into these enigmatic objects.

Text: This study presents a comprehensive theoretical analysis of the effective CP-violating phase sin2(β/φ1)eff in b->s penguin-dominated modes within the Standard Model and its minimal extensions. By employing a Bayesian framework for parameter estimation, we derive predictions for sin2(β/φ1)eff based on a comprehensive set of b->s penguin-dominated processes, including B->K*μ+μ-, B->Kμ+μ-, B->Kπμ+μ-, and B->K*πμ+μ-, as well as the golden modes B->K+π- and B->K+π-. Our demonstrate that sin2(β/φ1)eff is highly sensitive to the CP-violating phases φ1 and φb, and exhibit distinct correlations with the penguin-dominated branching ratios. By incorporating the latest experimental constraints from the LHCb and Belle II experiments, our predictions provide valuable insights into the interplay between the CP-violating phases and the penguin-dominated decay channels. Furthermore, we investigate the potential impact of new physics contributions on sin2(β/φ1)eff, highlighting the importance of further experimental and theoretical explorations in this sector. Our emphasize the significance of sin2(β/φ1)eff as a sensitive probe of CP-violation in the B-meson sector.

Text: We report on our search for $B^- \to D^{(*)+}_s K^- \pi^-$, $\bar{B^0} \to D_s^{(*)+} K_S^0 \pi^-$, and $B^- \to D^{(*)+}_s K^- K^-$ decays in 383 million $\FourS \to B \Bbar$ events collected by the Babar detector at the PEP2 asymmetric-energy $B$-factory. The decays proceed via a tree-level $b\to c$ quark transition in which a gluon radiates into an $s\bar{s}$ pair. Their branching fractions are measured to be ${\cal B}(B^- \to D^+_s K^- \pi^-) = (2.02 \pm 0.13_{stat} \pm 0.38_{syst}) \times 10^{-4},$ ${\cal B}(B^- \to D^{*+}_s K^- \pi^-)= (1.67 \pm 0.16_{stat} \pm 0.35_{syst}) \times 10^{-4},$ ${\cal B}(\bar{B^0} \to D_s^{+} K_S^0 \pi^-)= (0.55 \pm 0.13_{stat} \pm 0.10_{syst}) \times 10^{-4},$ and ${\cal B}(B^- \to D_s^{+} K^- K^-) = (0.11 \pm 0.04_{stat} \pm 0.02_{syst}) \times 10^{-4}$. Upper limits at the 90% C.L. are set on ${\cal B}(\bar{B^0} \to D_s^{*+} K_S^0 \pi^-)< 0.55 \times 10^{-4}$ and ${\cal B}(B^- \to D_s^{*+} K^- K^-) < 0.15 \times 10^{-4}$. We present evidence that the invariant mass distributions of $D^{(*)+}_s K^-$ pairs from $B^- \to D^{(*)+}_s K^- \pi^-$ decays are inconsistent with the phase-space model, suggesting the presence of charm resonances lying below the $D^{(*)+}_s K^-$ threshold.

Text: Type Ic supernovae (SNe Ic) represent the core‑collapse endpoints of massive, stripped‑envelope stars, yet the degree to which their explosions deviate from spherical symmetry remains uncertain. SN 2002ap, a nearby, energetically intermediate SN Ic, offers a valuable test case because its late‑time (nebular) spectra preserve information on the geometry of the ejecta and the distribution of radioactive ^56Ni. We obtained a homogeneous set of high‑resolution nebular spectra of SN 2002ap spanning 200–400 days post‑explosion. The spectra were modeled with a three‑dimensional Monte‑Carlo radiative‑transfer code that simultaneously solves for ionisation balance, non‑local thermodynamic equilibrium level populations, and line formation in an expanding, aspherical ejecta. A suite of axisymmetric models with varying axial ratios, ^56Ni clumpiness, and viewing angles were fitted to the observed [O I] λλ6300,6364, [Ca II] λλ7291,7324, and Fe‑group emission features. Model selection employed Bayesian evidence to quantify the preference for non‑spherical geometries. The best‑fit configuration requires a prolate ejecta with an axial ratio of ≈1.6 ± 0.2, viewed ≈30° off the symmetry axis. The [O I] profile exhibits a pronounced double‑peaked structure reproduced only by a bipolar ^56Ni distribution, while the Fe‑group lines indicate modest mixing. These demonstrate that SN 2002ap possessed a significantly aspherical explosion, supporting the hypothesis that energetic SNe Ic commonly launch mildly collimated outflows, even in the absence of an associated gamma‑ray burst.

Text: we present an in-depth analysis of pion freeze-out properties in heavy ion collisions, leveraging HBT (Hanbury-Brown and Twiss) correlations from a detailed dataset spanning the entire energy range of available heavy ion colliders, including FAIR/AGS, SPS, and RHIC, and by employing a multi-phase transport model, we investigate the behavior of pion freeze-out conditions in a wide energy regime, from the intermediate energies of FAIR/AGS to the high-energy collisions at RHIC. Building on this, our results reveal a gradual reduction in the freeze-out radius with increasing energy, accompanied by a decrease in freeze-out temperature. Notably, the findings indicate a more pronounced effect of energy on the radial flow component of the pion freeze-out momentum, with a corresponding increase in the longitudinal component. The observed trends are consistent with expectations based on the expanding fireball scenario and the underlying dynamics of the QGP (quark-gluon plasma) formation. The comprehensive analysis of HBT correlations at various energies provides valuable insights into the pion freeze-out properties, ultimately shedding light on the physics processes governing the hadronization of the QGP.

Text: Multiple applications that execute concurrently on heterogeneous platforms compete for CPU and network resources. In this paper we analyze the behavior of $K$ non-cooperative schedulers using the optimal strategy that maximize their efficiency while fairness is ensured at a system level ignoring applications characteristics. We limit our study to simple single-level master-worker platforms and to the case where each scheduler is in charge of a single application consisting of a large number of independent tasks. The tasks of a given application all have the same computation and communication requirements, but these requirements can vary from one application to another. In this context, we assume that each scheduler aims at maximizing its throughput. We give closed-form formula of the equilibrium reached by such a system and study its performance. We characterize the situations where this Nash equilibrium is optimal (in the Pareto sense) and show that even though no catastrophic situation (Braess-like paradox) can occur, such an equilibrium can be arbitrarily bad for any classical performance measure.

Text: Sportsmanship is the quality of playing fairly, respecting opponents, officials, and the spirit of the game, and maintaining dignity in both victory and defeat. It is, at its core, the application of ethical values to competitive athletic contexts - a recognition that the way you compete matters as much as whether you win. Great sportsmanship is striking precisely because competition creates genuine incentives to win at all costs, making the choice to honor the rules, acknowledge superior performance, and support a fallen opponent a genuinely moral act. In an era of professional sport where the financial stakes are enormous and the pressure to win can distort ethical judgment, examples of genuine sportsmanship carry particular weight and can inspire far beyond the sporting arena. Coaches who model sportsmanship - who teach young athletes to compete fiercely within the rules, to handle both success and failure with grace, and to respect the humanity of their opponents - are contributing to character formation that has applications across every dimension of life.
