Text: A derivation of the equations of motion of general relativity is presented that does not invoke the Axiom of Choice, but requires the explicit construction of a choice function q for continuous three-space regions. The motivation for this (seemingly academic) endeavour is to take the independence intrinsic to Einstein gravity one step further, and to assure that both the equations of motion and the way in which those equations of motion are derived are as self-consistent as possible. That is, solutions to the equations of motion of general relativity endow a three-space region with a physical and distinguishing geometry in four-dimensional space-time. However, in order to derive these equations of motion one should first be able to choose a three-space region without having any prior knowledge of its physically appropriate geometry. The expression of this choice process requires a three-dimensional topological manifold Q, to which all considered three-space regions belong, and that generates an equation of motion whose solutions are q. These solutions relate the effects of curvature to the source term through the topology of Q and constitute Einstein gravity. Q is given by 2T^3+3S^1xS^2, and is embedded in four dimensions. This points toward a hidden topological content for general relativity, best phrased as: Q and q provide a structure for how to choose a three-space region irrespective of what geometric properties it has, while at the same time Q and q determine that only GR can endow a three-space with those geometric properties. In this sense, avoiding the Axiom of Choice allows one to gain physical insight into GR. Possible links with holography are pointed out.

Text: In this study, we implement a paradigmatic realization of chaotic inflation within the auspices of supergravity, capitalizing on the D-term potential engendered by a U(1) gauge symmetry, thereby establishing a supersymmetric framework that facilitates the emergence of a D-term driven inflationary scenario. Through the of a set of chiral superfields coupled to the gauge field and a Fayet-Iliopoulos term, we construct a supersymmetric model that exhibits a high degree of flexibility in accommodating a broad spectrum of inflationary dynamics, ranging from the slow-roll paradigm to the ultra-fast roll regime, contingent upon the selection of model parameters. By analytically solving the inflationary dynamics and computationally evaluating the spectral index, tensor-to-scalar ratio, and other relevant observables, we demonstrate that the proposed model is commensurate with current observational constraints. Furthermore, we investigate the predictions of the model for the primordial power spectrum and find that it conforms to a characteristic scale-invariant form, consonant with the theoretical expectations of chaotic inflation. Our present a novel avenue for elucidating the early universe, and we contend that the D-term chaotic inflation model in supergravity offers a compelling framework for probing the intricate interplay between supergravity and inflationary cosmology.

Text: This study presents an investigation into the non-Markovian dynamics that govern the atom-laser outcoupling process from a double-well Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC). By employing a combination of theoretical modeling and numerical simulations, we demonstrate that the outcoupling process is significantly influenced by non-Markovian effects, which arise due to the finite correlation time of the environment. Our show that the non-Markovian dynamics lead to the emergence of a non-exponential decay of the condensate population, accompanied by a characteristic oscillatory behavior in the outcoupling rate. Furthermore, we find that the interplay between the non-Markovian effects and the double-well potential geometry gives rise to a rich phenomenology, including the observation of transient and long-lived oscillations in the outcoupling rate. Our have implications for the understanding of non-equilibrium dynamics in BECs and suggest new avenues for the manipulation of matter-wave lasers. The of this study provide a comprehensive framework for the analysis of non-Markovian dynamics in outcoupling processes from double-well BECs.

Text: The Zeldovich approximation is a well-established framework for modeling the large-scale structure of the universe. Recently, there has been a resurgence of interest in using this dynamics to test various expansion schemes, including those that deviate from the standard ΛCDM paradigm. In this study, we employ the Zeldovich dynamics to investigate the viability of several expansion schemes, including the standard ΛCDM model, as well as alternative scenarios such as the Rh = ct and the emergent gravity models. We utilize a suite of N-body simulations to track the evolution of density fluctuations and compare the with theoretical predictions from each expansion scheme. Our show that the Zeldovich dynamics provides a robust framework for distinguishing between different expansion schemes. We find that the standard ΛCDM model provides an excellent fit to the simulated data, while alternative scenarios exhibit significant deviations. Notably, the Rh = ct model is ruled out at high confidence, whereas the emergent gravity model shows promise in reproducing certain features of the simulated data. These highlight the potential of the Zeldovich dynamics as a powerful tool for testing cosmological expansion schemes.

Text: We introduce a original flow equation method to the Kondo necklace model, a paradigmatic example of quantum many-body systems where a Luttinger liquid is coupled to a quantum spin bath. By utilizing the exact renormalization group (RG) flow equation technique, we derive a closed-form flow equation for the Kondo necklace model, allowing for the systematic integration of the RG flow of the Luttinger liquid parameters with the Kondo interaction. Our approach captures the essential low-energy physics of the system, including the emergence of a collective mode at the Kondo scale and the associated scaling behavior of the Luttinger liquid parameters. We show the validity and accuracy of our flow equation approach by comparing our results to existing perturbative calculations and quantitative simulations. Our work provides a powerful tool for studying the Kondo necklace model and related quantum many-body systems, enabling the systematic exploration of the RG flow in the presence of strong quantum fluctuations. This framework has the potential to shed new light on the physics of quantum spin baths and the interplay between Luttinger liquids and Kondo correlations.

Text: The dynamics of flexible polymers subject to inextensible bonds can be recast as a constrained stochastic process whose statistical description is naturally formulated within a path‑integral approach. In this work we develop a rigorous functional integral representation for a random chain whose elementary links are subject to rigid length constraints, thereby extending the conventional Wiener measure to a manifold of admissible configurations defined by a set of holonomic conditions. By introducing Lagrange multiplier fields that enforce the constraints at each infinitesimal time step, we derive an reliable action that incorporates both the kinetic term of the monomeric degrees of freedom and a non‑local term arising from the Jacobian of the constraint manifold. The resulting propagator admits a perturbative expansion in the strength of thermal fluctuations, and we reveal that the leading‑order contribution reproduces the well‑known Rouse dynamics projected onto the subspace of allowed motions. Numerical simulations based on a discretized version of the action support the analytical predictions for correlation functions and mean‑square displacement, while also revealing subtle renormalization effects at higher orders. The formalism offers a versatile tool for studying a broad class of polymeric systems with rigid constraints, including semiflexible filaments, knotted loops, and networks with topological restrictions.

Text: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) relies on free‑falling geodetic reference masses (GRMs) to serve as inertial sensors for gravitational‑wave detection. Residual forces arising from temperature gradients across the GRM housing generate spurious accelerations that can limit the mission’s low‑frequency sensitivity. Quantifying these thermal‑gradient‑induced forces is therefore essential for the design of thermal‑control hardware and the development of noise‑budget models. A combined analytical‑numerical approach was employed. First, a perturbative model of radiometric, outgassing, and radiation‑pressure forces was derived for a cubic GRM surrounded by a multilayer thermal shield. The model was implemented in a finite‑element thermal‑mechanical simulation to compute spatial temperature fields for realistic spacecraft heating scenarios. Complementary torsion‑pendulum experiments were performed on a ground‑based LISA Pathfinder‑type test mass assembly, wherein controlled temperature differentials (0.1–5 K) were imposed and the resulting torque was measured with sub‑nanonewton resolution. Data were fitted to the theoretical expressions to extract empirical coefficients. The simulations predict a net acceleration noise of \(1.2\times10^{-15}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}\,Hz^{-1/2}}\) at 0.1 mHz for a 1 K gradient, dominated by radiometric effects. Experimental confirm the model within 15 % and reveal a linear scaling of force with gradient up to 3 K, beyond which outgassing contributes a nonlinear term. Implementation of a high‑conductivity carbon‑fiber shield reduces the effective gradient by a factor of three, bringing the thermal‑gradient noise below the LISA requirement of \(3\times10^{-15}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}\,Hz^{-1/2}}\). These validate the thermal design strategy and provide calibrated parameters for the mission’s noise budget.

Text: Radiation pressure acceleration (RPA) is a novel method for generating high-energy electron beams, offering unprecedented acceleration rates and compactness. Recent advancements in high-power laser technology have sparked interest in leveraging circularly polarized (CP) laser pulses for RPA, potentially enhancing electron beam quality and stability. However, the complex interaction between CP laser pulses and thin foils remains poorly understood. In this study, we experimentally investigate the RPA of thin foils using CP laser pulses, while our setup consists of a high-power laser system, capable of delivering 100 J pulses at 800 nm, and a thin foil target. We employ a diagnostic suite, including spectrometers and imaging detectors, to characterize the electron beam and foil morphology. A range of foil thicknesses and laser intensities are explored to elucidate the effects of CP polarization on the acceleration process. Our demonstrate that CP laser pulses can significantly enhance the acceleration efficiency of thin foils, leading to higher electron beam energies and improved stability. We observe a direct correlation between the degree of CP polarization and the resulting electron beam quality, with optimal performance achieved at high polarization levels. Crucially, these have far-reaching implications for the development of compact, high-energy electron sources and highlight the potential of CP laser pulses in RPA applications.

Text: This investigation presents a novel route to electroweak symmetry breaking that eliminates the requirement of a fundamental Higgs boson at the Large Hadron Collider. Conventional wisdom within the Standard Model assigns a scalar field the role of breaking the electroweak gauge symmetry, which is then interpreted as the Higgs particle; yet the measured Higgs mass of 125 GeV and the absence of signals for additional scalar resonances hint that this picture may not be unique. Motivated by dynamical electroweak symmetry–breaking frameworks, we explore composite Higgs scenarios in which the underlying strong dynamics generate a pseudo‑Nambu‑Goldstone boson that behaves as the Higgs field. Employing an exhaustive scan of the theory’s parameter space and incorporating the latest LHC measurements, we identify a consistent configuration in which electroweak symmetry is broken without invoking a fundamental Higgs scalar. This outcome not only addresses the hierarchy problem but also opens a new experimental window into the electroweak sector at the LHC.

Text: The pervasive need for dependable wireless communication systems has catalyzed the proliferation of iterative decoding techniques, designed to mitigate the deleterious effects of error propagation in digital data transmission over fading channels. A critical determinant of these techniques' efficacy lies in the precise calculation of log-likelihood ratios (LLRs) at the receiver, necessitating the development of novel approaches that obviate the limitations inherent in prevailing . This study proposes an optimal linear LLR calculation paradigm, predicated on the maximum-likelihood principle and leveraging a Gaussian approximation of the channel state information, thereby yielding a closed-form formula that maximally mitigates the Mean Squared Error (MSE) between estimated and actual LLRs. Numerical simulations in Rayleigh fading channel scenarios substantiate the proposed method's superiority in terms of bit error rate (BER) performance and convergence rate, as compared to existing techniques. Notably, theoretical analysis and comprehensive simulations corroborate the efficacy of the proposed approach, underscoring its suitability for deployment in 5G and beyond wireless communication systems, as well as other domains requiring robust data transmission over fading channels.

Text: Tackling the Intractable Bound of Non-Zero Capacity in Pauli Channels via Rigorous Analytical Techniques Recent breakthroughs in the comprehension of channel capacity within the framework of Pauli noise models have precipitated a profound reappraisal of the fundamental limits governing decoherence and noise in quantum communication systems. This investigation seeks to push the bounds of our understanding by introducing novel lower bound derivations on the non-zero capacity of the Pauli Channel, a paradigmatic model that encapsulates the intricacies of quantum information theory. By synthesizing refined techniques from convex optimization, probability theory, and quantum mechanics, our analysis yields significantly tighter lower bounds than heretofore established . The Pauli Channel, characterized by a discrete-time noise structure facilitating a more amenable analysis, serves as the focal point of our inquiry. We leverages the unique properties inherent to this model to derive tight lower bounds on its non-zero capacity, thus bridging the erstwhile insurmountable gap between previously established bounds and the capacity of the Pauli Channel. This study contributes substantially to our comprehension of quantum channel capacity and has far-reaching implications for the design of robust communication systems capable of withstanding the ravages of decoherence and noise. Our are articulated in terms of the Holevo-Schumacher-West capacity criterion, and a detailed comparison is provided with existing encompassing both the Pauli Channel and more generalized scenarios. Notably, we establish that the non-zero capacity of Pauli Channels is at least a factor of $\sqrt{2}$ larger than previously established lower bounds, offering invaluable insights into the fundamental constraints governing quantum communication. The potential of our analysis extends to the advancement of understanding channel capacity in the quantum regime and informs the design of quantum error correction codes and communication strategies. In doing so, our investigation draws upon the interplay of Pauli Channels, quantum channel capacity, convex optimization, probability theory, and quantum information theory.

Text: We have developed an image restoration technique based on the Richardson-Lucy algorithm optimized for GLAST-LAT image analysis. Our algorithm is original since it utilizes the PSF (point spread function) that is calculated for each event. This is critical for EGRET and GLAST-LAT image analysis since the PSF depends on the energy and angle of incident gamma-rays and varies by more than one order of magnitude. EGRET and GLAST-LAT image analysis also faces Poisson noise due to low photon statistics. Our technique incorporates wavelet filtering to minimize noise effects. We present studies of EGRET sources using this novel image restoration technique for possible identification of extended gamma-ray sources.

Text: This study addresses the Calabi-Yau problem for maximal surfaces in the three-dimensional Lorentzian space L^3, where a maximal surface is defined as an immersion of a surface with zero mean curvature in a spacetime. We investigate the existence and properties of Calabi-Yau metrics, which are solutions to the Calabi-Yau equation, on these surfaces. Our research aims to generalize the Calabi-Yau problem from the Riemannian setting to the Lorentzian context, which is essential for understanding the geometric structure of spacetime in general relativity. We establish a rigorous framework for the problem, leveraging techniques from differential geometry, global analysis, and partial differential equations. Our main result is the proof of the existence of Calabi-Yau metrics on maximal surfaces in L^3 with specific topological and geometric properties. These provide new insights into the geometric properties of spacetime and shed light on the interplay between curvature, topology, and geometry in the context of general relativity. Our work opens up new avenues for exploring the relationship between the Calabi-Yau problem and the geometry of spacetime.

Text: This study presents an evaluation of the low-lying vertices $DDV$ and $D^*DV$ within the framework of light-cone QCD sum rules, a non-perturbative framework to Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD). Utilizing the factorization formula for the light-cone distribution amplitudes of the light mesons, we derive the sum rules for the above-mentioned vertices, which represent the fundamental building blocks for the description of strong interactions in the sector of charmed mesons. The obtained sum rules are expressed in terms of the vacuum condensates of QCD and are found to be sensitive to the non-perturbative dynamics of the QCD vacuum. We then perform a detailed assessment of the sum rules, taking into account the contributions from the lowest-order condensates and the perturbative corrections. The results are compared with available experimental data and theoretical predictions from other approaches, providing a comprehensive understanding of the underlying strong interaction dynamics governing the $DDV$ and $D^*DV$ vertices. Our observations are expected to shed new light on the structure of charmed mesons and contribute to the ongoing efforts in the pursuit of a unified theory of strong interactions.

Text: This study explores the application of elastic scattering theory in understanding transport phenomena in graphene, a two-dimensional material exhibiting exceptional electrical and thermal conductivity. We develop a comprehensive framework incorporating the Landau-Fermi liquid theory and the Boltzmann transport equation to describe the transport properties of graphene in the presence of elastic scattering events. Our analysis accounts for both phonon and impurity-mediated scattering mechanisms, providing a unified treatment of the respective contributions to the scattering rate. We demonstrate that the elastic scattering theory accurately captures the temperature-dependent behavior of the electrical conductivity and thermal conductivity in graphene, exhibiting excellent agreement with experimental data. Furthermore, our reveal a significant impact of the scattering mechanisms on the Fermi level and carrier mobility in graphene, highlighting the importance of elastic scattering theory in understanding the material's transport properties. This work provides a theoretical foundation for the design and optimization of graphene-based devices, leveraging the material's exceptional transport characteristics for a wide range of applications.

Text: Cosmological scenarios with k-essence are invoked in order to explain the observed late-time acceleration of the universe. These scenarios avoid the need for fine-tuned initial conditions (the "coincidence problem") because of the attractor-like dynamics of the k-essence field \phi. It was recently shown that all k-essence scenarios with Lagrangians p=L(X)/\phi^2, necessarily involve an epoch where perturbations of \phi propagate faster than light (the "no-go theorem"). We carry out a comprehensive study of attractor-like cosmological solutions ("trackers") involving a k-essence scalar field \phi and another matter component. The result of this study is a complete classification of k-essence Lagrangians that admit asymptotically stable tracking solutions, among all Lagrangians of the form p=K(\phi)L(X) . Using this classification, we select the class of models that describe the late-time acceleration and avoid the coincidence problem through the tracking mechanism. An analogous "no-go theorem" still holds for this class of models, indicating the existence of a superluminal epoch. In the context of k-essence cosmology, the superluminal epoch does not lead to causality violations. We discuss the implications of superluminal signal propagation for possible causality violations in Lorentz-invariant field theories.

Text: This study investigates the possibility of warm inflation in the context of the Dvali-Gabadadze-Porrati (DGP) brane-world model, a framework that postulates the existence of a four-dimensional brane embedded in a five-dimensional bulk space. We consider a scenario where the brane is tensionless and the bulk is described by a single scalar field, which is responsible for driving inflation. The warm inflation model, characterized by an additional dissipative term in the Friedmann equation, is incorporated into the DGP brane-world framework. Our analysis reveals that the DGP brane-world model can exhibit warm inflationary behavior, with the dissipative term playing a crucial role in stabilizing the inflationary epoch. We derive a set of equations that govern the evolution of the brane's scale factor and the scalar field during warm inflation, and solve them numerically to obtain the resulting power spectra of scalar and tensor perturbations. Our show that the warm inflation model in the DGP brane-world scenario can produce a realistic spectrum of cosmological perturbations, consistent with observations from the cosmic microwave radiation and large-scale structure surveys.

Text: This paper presents a novel approach to the computation of singular link Floer homology, a powerful invariant in low-dimensional topology that encodes rich information about the topology of knots and links in a three-dimensional manifold. Text: The fluctuation theorem (FT) is a fundamental concept in nonequilibrium statistical mechanics that describes the directional asymmetry of entropy production in stochastic processes. However, the application of FT to quantum systems remains an open question, with the Tasaki-Crooks quantum fluctuation theorem (TQFT) providing a theoretical framework for understanding quantum stochastic processes. We employed a combination of mathematical derivations and numerical simulations to investigate the TQFT. Specifically, we formulated a quantum master equation for a driven-dissipative system and derived the TQFT from the quantum Jarzynski equality. We then numerically simulated the TQFT for various quantum systems, including a harmonic oscillator and a quantum spin. Our demonstrate that the TQFT accurately describes the quantum stochastic processes, exhibiting a non-equilibrium entropy production that is consistent with the classical FT. Furthermore, we found that the TQFT provides a novel perspective on the role of quantum coherence in nonequilibrium systems, highlighting the importance of quantum fluctuations in driving entropy production. Our work provides a theoretical foundation for understanding the behavior of quantum systems far from equilibrium and sheds light on the fundamental laws governing quantum stochastic processes.

Text: We develop a systematic perturbative model for evaluating large‑deviation functionals governing the probability of atypical macroscopic trajectories in fluctuating hydrodynamics. Starting from the macroscopic fluctuation theory, we expand the action functional around the deterministic hydrodynamic solution in powers of a small parameter quantifying the strength of the noise or the deviation from equilibrium. The method combines a functional‑Taylor expansion with diagrammatic techniques to organize contributions from nonlinear transport coefficients and non‑Gaussian noise cumulants. At leading order we recover the Gaussian Onsager‑Machlup functional, while the next‑to‑leading corrections capture the influence of mode‑coupling and boundary‑driven fluxes, yielding explicit expressions for the rate functional up to second order in the perturbation. The framework is illustrated on driven diffusive systems with conserved density and on active matter models with non‑reciprocal currents, where analytical results agree with numerical rare‑event simulations. Our theory provides a versatile tool for quantifying fluctuation‑induced phenomena such as dynamical phase transitions, optimal paths, and response properties in a broad class of nonequilibrium fluids, thereby extending the reach of large‑deviation analysis beyond the linear regime.

Text: In the framework of instantaneous approximations to the Bethe-Salpeter formalism for the description of bound states within quantum field theories, depending on the Lorentz structure of the Bethe-Salpeter interaction kernel the solutions of the full Salpeter equation with some confining interaction may exhibit certain instabilities, which are possibly related to the Klein paradox and signal the decay of states assumed to be bound by the confining interactions. They are observed in numerical (variational) studies of the Salpeter equation. The presumably simplest scenario allowing for the fully analytic investigation of this problem is set by the reduced Salpeter equation with harmonic-oscillator interaction. In this case, Salpeter's integral equation simplifies to either an algebraic relation or a second-order homogeneous linear ordinary differential equation, immediately accessible to standard techniques. There one may hope to be able to decide unambiguously whether this setting poses a well-defined eigenvalue problem the solutions of which correspond to stable bound states associated to real energy eigenvalues bounded from below. Text: .** The nearby M-dwarf Gliese 581 hosts several super-Earth candidates (e.g., Gl 581d, g, f) that lie within or near the star's habitable zone. Determining their potential to support liquid water and life requires integrating dynamical, atmospheric, and geophysical constraints for planets with masses 5-10 M⊕. .** We combined high-precision radial-velocity measurements with transit-timing variations to refine orbital parameters and planetary masses. Using a 1-D radiative-convective climate model coupled to a photochemical network, we simulated surface temperature and atmospheric composition across a grid of stellar fluxes, surface gravities, and atmospheric pressures. We further incorporated tidal heating estimates and interior heat-flux calculations to assess tectonic activity. Monte-Carlo sampling of the parameter space provided probabilistic habitability metrics, quantified as the fraction of simulations yielding surface temperatures between 273 K and 373 K under Earth-like CO₂ inventories. .** Interestingly, we observed that Gl 581d and g can maintain temperate surface conditions if they possess substantial CO₂ atmospheres (≥ 0.1 bar) and active plate tectonics, whereas Gl 581f is unlikely to sustain liquid water due to excessive stellar insolation and limited greenhouse amplification. Tidal heating contributes ≤ 10 % of the surface energy budget for all three planets, insufficient to drive runaway greenhouse or global glaciation. Overall, the probability of habitable conditions is ≈ 35 % for Gl 581d and ≈ 20 % for Gl 581g, underscoring the importance of atmospheric characterization in future observations.

Text: Democracy is a system of governance in which political authority is vested in the people, who exercise that power either directly or through freely elected representatives who remain accountable to the citizenry. Democracy is widely regarded as the political system most compatible with human dignity and individual freedom, though democratic systems worldwide vary considerably in their institutional designs, representational quality, and practical performance outcomes. Liberal democracy, which combines majority governance with constitutional protections for individual rights and minority groups, is distinguished from illiberal forms of democracy that conduct elections while suppressing political opposition, restricting press freedom, or undermining institutional independence. Text: Randomness extraction is of fundamental importance for information-theoretic cryptography. It allows to transform a raw key about which an attacker has some limited knowledge into a fully secure random key, on which the attacker has essentially no information. Up to date, only very few randomness-extraction techniques are known to work against an attacker holding quantum information on the raw key. This is very much in contrast to the classical (non-quantum) setting, which is much better understood and for which a vast amount of different techniques are known and proven to work. We prove a new randomness-extraction technique, which is known to work in the classical setting, to be secure against a quantum attacker as well. Randomness extraction is done by XOR'ing a so-called delta-biased mask to the raw key. Our result allows to extend the classical applications of this extractor to the quantum setting. We discuss the following two applications. We show how to encrypt a long message with a short key, information-theoretically secure against a quantum attacker, provided that the attacker has enough quantum uncertainty on the message. This generalizes the concept of entropically-secure encryption to the case of a quantum attacker. As second application, we show how to do error-correction without leaking partial information to a quantum attacker. Such a technique is useful in settings where the raw key may contain errors, since standard error-correction techniques may provide the attacker with information on, say, a secret key that was used to obtain the raw key.

Text: This work proposes a thermodynamically consistent framework for modeling state-dependent diffusion processes, wherein the diffusion coefficient varies according to the system's state, thereby necessitating an extension of classical stochastic differential equations to ensure compliance with the second law of thermodynamics. The resulting generalized Fokker-Planck equation, derived via a modified continuity equation incorporating a metric tensor to account for spatially varying diffusivity, preserves entropy production and satisfies the fluctuation theorem, thus maintaining thermodynamic consistency. A corresponding path integral representation is formulated, demonstrating that the stochastic dynamics of state-dependent diffusion can be expressed through a time-ordered exponential of a non-local action functional, which bridges the gap between mesoscopic transport models and macroscopic thermodynamics, thereby enabling the analysis of systems with spatially heterogeneous mobilities, such as active matter, biological transport, or heterogeneous materials. By leveraging this unified theoretical foundation, numerical validation confirms that the proposed framework accurately captures non-equilibrium steady states and transient responses under external gradients, thereby providing insights into the thermodynamic costs of spatially modulated transport and guiding the design of energy-efficient nanoscale systems.

Text: We study the spontaneous breaking of non‑Abelian gauge symmetry induced by the Euclidean time component \(A_{0}\) of gauge fields in thermal Yang–Mills theories, elucidating its relation to the Hosotani mechanism and the Polyakov‑loop order parameter. Employing background‑field quantization on \(S^{1}\times\mathbb{R}^{3}\) with periodic boundary conditions for bosons, we derive the one‑loop effective potential for constant \(A_{0}\) configurations, incorporating both perturbative contributions and non‑perturbative caloron effects. The analysis reveals that, for gauge groups of rank greater than one, the minima of the potential can reside at non‑trivial holonomies, thereby reducing the original gauge group to a proper subgroup without invoking scalar Higgs fields. Lattice simulations of SU(3) at temperatures near the deconfinement transition corroborate the analytic predictions, displaying a clear alignment of the Polyakov loop with the symmetry‑breaking pattern inferred from the effective potential. Our results demonstrate that Euclidean temporal gauge fields provide a viable dynamical source of gauge symmetry breaking, offering a unified framework for understanding phase structure in finite‑temperature gauge theories and suggesting novel avenues for model building in beyond‑Standard‑Model physics.

Text: Branching Ratio Measurement of $K_S\to \gamma \gamma$ Decay using a Pure $\ks$ Beam in the KLOE Detector** The $K_S\to \gamma \gamma$ decay is a rare and intriguing process that has garnered significant attention in the field of particle physics. This decay is a prime example of the hadronic sector's sensitivity to new physics beyond the Standard Model. Despite its importance, the branching ratio of this decay has thus far been determined with limited precision, primarily due to the challenges associated with isolating the $K_L$ component in the $\ks$ beam. The KLOE detector, located at the Frascati National Laboratory, provides a unique opportunity to study this process with unprecedented accuracy. We employed a data-driven approach, utilizing a high-statistics sample of $\ks$ events collected with the KLOE detector. By exploiting the distinctive characteristics of the $\ks$ and $K_L$ decays, we were able to isolate the $K_S\to \gamma \gamma$ signal and measure its branching ratio with high precision. Our analysis yields a branching ratio of $(4.58 \pm 0.20) \times 10^{-5}$, which represents a significant improvement over previous measurements. The resulting value provides a crucial constraint on theoretical models aiming to describe the hadronic sector and its connection to new physics. Our demonstrate the KLOE detector's ability to deliver precise measurements in the field of hadron physics, paving the way for future studies of rare decays and beyond.

Text: The study of unique continuation properties for partial differential equations (PDEs) is a fundamental problem in the field of analysis and mathematical physics. In the context of parabolic equations with nonsmooth coefficients, unique continuation are essential for understanding the behavior of solutions and for developing numerical . The Carleman estimate, a powerful tool in the study of PDEs, has been widely used to establish unique continuation properties for second-order elliptic and hyperbolic equations. However, its application to parabolic equations with nonsmooth coefficients remains largely unexplored. In this paper, we employ a combination of Carleman estimates and techniques from nonsmooth analysis to investigate the unique continuation problem for second-order parabolic equations with nonsmooth coefficients. Our approach involves constructing a Carleman estimate for the parabolic equation, followed by a careful analysis of the resulting inequality to establish the desired unique continuation property. We establish a Carleman estimate for second-order parabolic equations with nonsmooth coefficients, and use this estimate to show that if the solution of the equation vanishes on a non-empty open subset of the spatial domain, then the solution must vanish everywhere. This result provides a unique continuation property for parabolic equations with nonsmooth coefficients, and has important implications for the study of PDEs in a wide range of applications.

Text: The photo‑electric response of Bernal‑stacked bi‑layer graphite is investigated through combined angle‑resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and time‑dependent density‑functional theory (TD‑DFT) to elucidate the influence of interlayer coupling on electron emission dynamics. Samples were exfoliated to achieve uniform bilayer regions and characterized by Raman spectroscopy to confirm AB stacking and minimal defect density. Ultraviolet photons with energies ranging from 3.5 eV to 6.5 eV were incident at variable angles, and the kinetic energy distribution of emitted electrons was recorded with sub‑10 meV resolution. The data reveal a pronounced threshold at 4.2 eV, corresponding to the transition from the low‑energy parabolic bands to the split Dirac cones induced by interlayer hybridization. Quantum efficiency exhibits a non‑monotonic dependence on photon energy, peaking at 5.1 eV where the joint density of states is maximized. TD‑DFT simulations reproduce the observed spectral features and attribute the enhanced emission to constructive interference between interlayer transition dipoles. These findings reveal that bi‑layer graphite possesses a tunable photo‑electric response distinct from monolayer graphene, offering a platform for engineered optoelectronic devices operating in the ultraviolet regime.

Text: Ethical Hacking, also designated as penetration testing or white-hat security assessment, is the authorized practice of systematically probing computer systems, networks, and software applications for exploitable security vulnerabilities, utilizing the same methodological approaches as malicious attackers, with the objective of identifying and remediating security weaknesses before they can be exploited by genuine adversaries. Ethical hackers operate under explicit contractual authorization from the organizations whose systems are being assessed and follow agreed-upon rules of engagement defining scope, boundaries, and acceptable testing methods. The ethical hacking process typically encompasses reconnaissance and information gathering, network and service scanning and enumeration, controlled exploitation of identified vulnerabilities, post-exploitation analysis, and the preparation of comprehensive reports detailing findings with prioritized remediation recommendations. Professional certifications including the Certified Ethical Hacker and Offensive Security Certified Professional are widely recognized credentials within the penetration testing field. As cyberattacks grow in sophistication and financial impact, demand for skilled ethical hackers and penetration testers has grown substantially.

Text: Short‑period extrasolar gas giants (hot Jupiters) experience intense stellar irradiation on their permanent day sides, producing strong longitudinal temperature gradients that drive atmospheric circulation. The efficiency of heat redistribution to the night side is thought to depend sensitively on the atmospheric opacity, yet quantitative predictions remain uncertain because opacity controls both radiative cooling rates and the depth of stellar energy deposition. We employed a suite of three‑dimensional general circulation models (GCMs) coupled to non‑grey radiative transfer to simulate tidally locked gas giants with orbital periods of 1–5 days. Atmospheric opacity was systematically varied by adjusting the abundances of key absorbers (H₂O, CO, TiO/VO) and by imposing gray opacity scalings spanning two orders of magnitude. Each simulation was integrated until a statistically steady state was achieved, and night‑side temperature fields were extracted for analysis of their dependence on the prescribed opacity spectrum. Night‑side temperatures increase monotonically with increasing opacity, following an approximate power‑law relation \(T_{\mathrm{night}} \propto \kappa^{0.25}\). High‑opacity atmospheres trap heat at deeper layers, enhancing vertical mixing and allowing more efficient advection of thermal energy to the anti‑stellar hemisphere. Conversely, low‑opacity cases exhibit rapid radiative cooling, yielding night‑side temperatures up to 400 K lower than their high‑opacity counterparts. These provide a predictive framework for interpreting phase‑curve observations and suggest that measured night‑side temperatures can constrain atmospheric composition and cloud opacity in hot Jupiters.

Text: It is known that the defining relations of the orthosymplectic Lie superalgebra osp(1|2n) are equivalent to the defining (triple) relations of n pairs of paraboson operators $b^\pm_i$. In particular, with the usual star conditions, this implies that the ``parabosons of order p'' correspond to a unitary irreducible (infinite-dimensional) lowest weight representation V(p) of osp(1|2n). Apart from the simple cases p=1 or n=1, these representations had never been constructed due to computational difficulties, despite their importance. In the present paper we give an explicit and elegant construction of these representations V(p), and we present explicit actions or matrix elements of the osp(1|2n) generators. The orthogonal basis vectors of V(p) are written in terms of Gelfand-Zetlin patterns, where the subalgebra u(n) of osp(1|2n) plays a crucial role. Our also lead to character formulas for these infinite-dimensional osp(1|2n) representations. Text: In this paper, we introduce the on-line Viterbi algorithm for decoding hidden Markov models (HMMs) in much smaller than linear space. Text: The Yangian is a quantum deformation of the universal enveloping algebra of a semisimple Lie algebra. In recent years, there has been a growing interest in studying Yangians for superalgebras of the $Q_{n-1}$ type. These superalgebras have a rich structure and have connections to representation theory and integrable systems. We employ Drinfel'd's approach to construct the Yangian of the strange Lie superalgebra of $Q_{n-1}$ type. This involves defining a Hopf superalgebra with a specific coproduct, counit, and antipode, and verifying that it satisfies the necessary properties to be a Yangian. We use a combination of mathematical software and manual calculations to derive the Yangian's generators and relations. We present a new class of Yangians for the $Q_{n-1}$ type, providing a complete set of generators and relations. Our demonstrate that the Yangian of the strange Lie superalgebra of $Q_{n-1}$ type has a particularly simple and elegant structure. The derived Yangian can be used to study representation theory, integrable systems, and other areas of mathematical physics. Text: Classical problems of sorting and searching assume an underlying linear ordering of the objects being compared. In this paper, we study a more general setting, in which some pairs of objects are incomparable. This generalization is relevant in applications related to rankings in sports, college admissions, or conference submissions. It also has potential applications in biology, such as comparing the evolutionary fitness of different strains of bacteria, or understanding input-output relations among a set of metabolic reactions or the causal influences among a set of interacting genes or proteins. Our improve and extend from two decades ago of Faigle and Tur'{a}n. A measure of complexity of a partially ordered set (poset) is its width. Our algorithms obtain information about a poset by queries that compare two elements. We present an algorithm that sorts, i.e. completely identifies, a width w poset of size n and has query complexity O(wn + nlog(n)), which is within a constant factor of the information-theoretic lower bound. We also show that a variant of Mergesort has query complexity O(wn(log(n/w))) and total complexity O((w2)nlog(n/w)). Faigle and Tur'{a}n have shown that the sorting problem has query complexity O(wn(log(n/w))) but did not address its total complexity. For the related problem of determining the minimal elements of a poset, we give efficient deterministic and randomized algorithms with O(wn) query and total complexity, along with matching lower bounds for the query complexity up to a factor of 2. We generalize these to the k-selection problem of determining the elements of height at most k. We also derive upper bounds on the total complexity of some other problems of a similar flavor.

Text: We present an in-depth analysis of the radio luminosity properties of the solitary millisecond pulsar PSR J1453+1902 in comparison to its binary counterparts. Through a comprehensive examination of the pulsar's broadband radio spectrum, we derive its intrinsic luminosity, allowing us to assess the implications of spin-down power and luminosity evolution on the observed radio emission. Specifically, we show that the Maurer-Cartan equations of a Lie algebroid encode the equations of motion for a wide class of classical field theories, encompassing both gauge and non-gauge systems. Our approach relies on the interpretation of the conformal Killing vector fields of the CFT as infinitesimal symmetries of the classical field equations, which in turn enables the derivation of the corresponding Maurer-Cartan equations. The resulting formal Maurer-Cartan structures provide a novel perspective on the interplay between quantum and classical descriptions of field theories, thereby offering a potential avenue for reconciling the two domains. Our have far-reaching implications for the understanding of the relationship between quantum field theories and their classical limits.

Our suggest that the Landauer bound no longer serves as a strict limit on information erasure in the quantum regime, and we propose a revised bound that takes into account the quantum mechanical uncertainties. Text: The advent of grazing-incidence X-ray telescopes (GI XRTs) has significantly advanced the field of X-ray astronomy by permitting high-resolution imaging of celestial sources, thereby facilitating unparalleled insights into the universe's hidden domains. Notwithstanding the GI XRT's superior performance, the grazing incidence angle, which enables minimal absorption of X-rays, also introduces inherent systematic errors stemming from the inherent optical properties of the telescope's configuration. This study seeks to elucidate the analytical evaluation of X-ray scattering contributions to the degradation of imaging quality in GI XRTs, a critical aspect that has not been thoroughly investigated. Through a comprehensive evaluation of ray tracing simulations and analytical models, we investigate the differential effects of Bragg scattering, Compton scattering, and refraction on the point spread function (PSF) of GI XRTs. Notably, our indicate that Bragg scattering, a phenomenon arising from the inelastic scattering of X-rays at the crystal facets, is responsible for the majority of the imaging degradation, resulting in appreciable broadening and elongation of the PSF. Furthermore, we develop an elaborate analytical model, which provides a lucid description of the scattering effects and facilitates their validation against the simulated data. Our indicate that the scattering-induced PSF broadening is positively correlated with energy, angle of incidence, and detector position, suggesting that these parameters play a crucial role in the degradation of imaging quality. In addition, a comparative analysis reveals that the effects of Compton scattering and refraction are relatively insignificant compared to Bragg scattering. This study provides a profound understanding of the imaging limitations of GI XRTs and highlights the pivotal role of scattering effects in high-energy astronomy, underscoring the need for accurate correction and calibration in future mission designs. The developed analytical model offers a powerful tool for correcting for scattering-induced imaging degradation, thereby enhancing angular resolution and sensitivity in GI XRT missions. Our study holds significant implications for the design, calibration, and data analysis of GI XRTs, and will contribute to the advancement of X-ray astronomy research by mitigating the challenges associated with imaging degradation, ultimately leading to groundbreaking discoveries in the field.

Text: We present evidence for the production of a color‑octet scalar in proton–proton interactions at the CERN Large Hadron Collider operating at a centre‑of‑mass energy of 13 TeV. A selection based on several kinematic observables—such as the invariant mass of the \(\eta\) system, the missing transverse momentum, and the jet multiplicity—has been employed to maximise the signal‑to‑background discrimination. The resulting invariant‑mass distribution of the \(\eta\) system exhibits a narrow excess that aligns with the expected mass and width of the color‑octet scalar, providing the first experimental indication of coloured scalar states at a hadron collider. This constitutes a notable advance in the exploration of physics beyond the Standard Model, and motivates additional measurements to characterise the scalar’s couplings and to deepen our understanding of quantum chromodynamics.

Text: This investigation probes the characteristics of supersymmetric heterotic string configurations, a theoretical construct that merges supersymmetry with heterotic string theory. The backgrounds examined here are ten‑dimensional manifolds in which supersymmetry is spontaneously broken along six dimensions while remaining partially intact in the residual four. By implementing the Green–Schwarz anomaly‑cancellation mechanism, we analyze the dynamical behavior of these strings and extract precise constraints governing the survival of supersymmetry. Our findings reveal that the supersymmetric heterotic backgrounds support a diverse array of geometric structures and field profiles, thereby offering fresh perspectives on the interplay between supersymmetry and string theory. Text: We identify satellites of isolated galaxies in SDSS and examine their angular distribution. Using mock catalogues generated from cosmological N-body simulations, we demonstrate that the selection criteria used to select isolated galaxies and their satellites must be very strict in order to correctly identify systems in which the primary galaxy dominates its environment. The criteria used in many previous studies instead select predominantly group members. We refine a set of selection criteria for which the group contamination is estimated to be less than 7% and present a catalogue of the resulting sample. The angular distribution of satellites about their host is biased towards the major axes for spheroidal galaxies and probably also for red disc galaxies, but is isotropic for blue disc galaxies, i.e. it is the colour of the host that determines the distribution of its satellites rather than its morphology. The similar anisotropy measured in this study as in studies that were dominated by groups implies that group-specific processes are not responsible for the angular distribution. Satellites that are most likely to have been recently accreted show a tendancy to lie along the same axis as the surrounding large scale structure. The orientations of isolated early and intermediate-type galaxies also align with the surrounding large scale structures. We discuss the origin of the anisotropic satellite distribution and consider the implications of our , critically assessing the respective roles played by the orientation of the visible galaxy within its dark matter halo; anisotropic accretion of satellites from the larger scale environment; and the biased nature of satellites as tracers of the underlying dark matter subhalo population. Text: Supersymmetry (SUSY) is a theoretically well-motivated extension of the Standard Model, providing a potential solution to the hierarchy problem. This scenario can be tested at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) and its gravity dual in AdS/CFT correspondence. In this study, we investigate single-sector SUSY breaking through a combination of theoretical and experimental approaches. We employ a 5-dimensional AdS/CFT correspondence to derive a gravity dual for a single-sector SUSY breaking scenario. We then analyze the LHC phenomenology of this scenario using the ATLAS and CMS detectors' data. Our analysis includes Monte Carlo simulations and a detailed study of SUSY signature events. Interestingly, we observed that a single-sector SUSY breaking scenario can be distinguished from the MSSM scenario at the LHC. The AdS/CFT correspondence allows us to derive a gravity dual that matches the LHC data. We find that the gluino and squark mass splittings are sensitive to the SUSY breaking scale and can be used to test this scenario at the LHC. Our study provides a new perspective on SUSY breaking and its implications for LHC physics.

This is the essence of decision fatigue, a phenomenon well-documented in psychology and behavioral economics. Studies have shown that judges are more likely to grant parole early in the day than late in the afternoon, suggesting that cognitive depletion leads to default or risk-averse choices. To protect your decision-making capacity, reduce the number of trivial choices you must make. Automate recurring decisions through routines and systems. Reserve your sharpest mental energy for decisions that truly matter. Simplifying your environment - your wardrobe, your meals, your schedule - is not a sign of laziness; it is a form of cognitive self-care that preserves your capacity for meaningful judgment.

Interestingly, we observed that directed networks exhibit distinct local structures, characterized by asymmetric degree distributions, high clustering coefficients, and community structures that are often hierarchical. Text: The Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM) with gravity-mediated supersymmetry breaking, also known as the mSUGRA model, provides a well-motivated framework for understanding supersymmetry at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). The mSUGRA model incorporates a set of universal boundary conditions, which include the trilinear coupling parameter A_0. While A_0 is often set to zero, recent studies suggest that non-zero values of A_0 may be necessary to reconcile the model with experimental constraints. We investigate the implications of a non-zero trilinear parameter A_0 in the mSUGRA model, focusing on its impact on dark matter and collider signals at the Tevatron and LHC. We employ a Monte Carlo simulation to generate a large sample of events, which are then analyzed using the MadGraph/MadEvent+Pythia framework. We find that non-zero values of A_0 can significantly modify the dark matter and collider signatures of the mSUGRA model. In particular, we observe enhanced production rates of gluinos and squarks, leading to an increase in the number of multi-jet events at the Tevatron and LHC. Furthermore, the non-zero A_0 parameter affects the properties of the dark matter candidate, leading to a range of possible signatures that may be distinguishable from the standard mSUGRA scenario.

Text: We establish a novel volume inequality for quantum Fisher information, which provides a lower bound on the quantum Fisher information in terms of the volume of a suitable convex body in the space of quantum states. This inequality has a direct connection to the uncertainty principle, as it implies that the precision of our ability to estimate a parameter of a quantum system is limited by the uncertainty principle. Furthermore, our result generalizes and improves upon existing inequalities for quantum Fisher information, offering new insights into the relationship between quantum information and the fundamental limits of measurement precision. Text: The Coma field has long served as a benchmark for studies of cluster‐scale synchrotron phenomena, yet the transition between the well‑characterized ∼1 Mpc radio halo and the surrounding Galactic foreground remains poorly sampled. Detecting faint, diffuse emission on angular scales ranging from several degrees down to a few arcminutes is essential for probing the magnetised inter‑galactic medium (IGM) and for disentangling Galactic cirrus from extragalactic structures. We combined deep, wide‑field observations from the Low‑Frequency Array (LOFAR) at 144 MHz with complementary 1.4 GHz data from the Westerbork Synthesis Radio Telescope (WSRT). Multi‑scale CLEAN imaging, direction‑dependent calibration, and wavelet‑based filtering were employed to recover emission on scales from 8° to 3′ while suppressing sidelobe artefacts. Spectral index maps were generated using matched‑resolution images, and the diffuse structures were cross‑checked against ROSAT X‑ray and Planck dust maps to assess Galactic contamination. We report the discovery of a network of faint (∼0.1 mJy beam⁻¹) synchrotron features extending up to 8° (∼13 Mpc at z = 0.023) from the Coma cluster core, with filamentary sub‑structures down to 3′ (∼70 kpc). The emission exhibits a steep spectral index (α ≈ −1.3) and aligns partially with known large‑scale filaments traced by galaxy density. A subset of the diffuse signal correlates with Galactic dust, indicating a mixed origin. These imply that low‑surface‑brightness radio synchrotron permeates the cosmic‑web filaments surrounding rich clusters, providing new constraints on IGM magnetic field strengths (∼0.1 µG) and the distribution of relativistic electrons beyond the cluster virial radius.

Text: We introduce a extensive characterization of all supersymmetric solutions of gauged N=1, d=5 supergravity, providing a systematic classification of the various configurations that preserve supersymmetry in this five-dimensional theory. Our analysis reveals that there are two distinct types of supersymmetric solutions: those with a non-trivial holonomy group, which are characterized by a non-zero graviphoton field strength, and those with a trivial holonomy group, which are described by a zero graviphoton field strength. Within the first class, we identify two subclasses of solutions: rotating black holes and warped AdS5 solutions, both of which preserve half of the original supersymmetry. For the second class, we find that the supersymmetric solutions are Minkowski spacetimes and warped AdS5 solutions, with the latter being further divided into two subclasses corresponding to different types of warp factors. Our results reveal a complete understanding of the supersymmetric solutions of gauged N=1, d=5 supergravity, with implications for the AdS/CFT correspondence and the analysis of supersymmetric field theories in five dimensions.

Text: Negative streamer discharges are fast-propagating ionisation fronts that play a crucial role in atmospheric electricity and high-voltage technology. Their dynamics are governed by a strong coupling between the electric field, space-charge layers and the ionisation reaction zone, which makes direct numerical simulation computationally demanding. A reduced description that captures the essential physics while allowing efficient large-scale calculations is therefore highly desirable. We derived a moving-boundary (sharp-interface) model in which the ionisation front is treated as a thin conductive sheath separating a non-ionised exterior from a weakly conducting interior. The model incorporates (i) a Laplace equation for the electric potential in the exterior, (ii) a curvature-dependent velocity law obtained from asymptotic analysis of the underlying fluid equations, and (iii) a charge-conservation condition at the interface. The governing equations were implemented in a level-set framework and solved using adaptive mesh refinement. Model predictions were benchmarked against fully resolved 2-D fluid simulations and against laboratory measurements of negative streamers in nitrogen at 1 bar. The moving-boundary model reproduces streamer velocities, branching thresholds and electric field enhancement within 5 % of the full fluid , while reducing computational cost by two orders of magnitude. Curvature effects are shown to dominate the branching dynamics, confirming theoretical expectations. The approach provides a robust tool for exploring streamer propagation in complex geometries and for coupling to larger-scale discharge phenomena.

Text: The Isobaric Multiplet Mass Equation (IMME) is a fundamental concept in nuclear physics that describes the relationship between the masses of nuclear isomers with the same isospin and seniority quantum numbers. Deviations from the IMME have been observed in several cases, indicating a breakdown of the equation. This study aims to investigate the A=35, T=3/2 isospin quartet, which has not been thoroughly examined. This study employed state-of-the-art nuclear mass measurement techniques, including Penning Trap Mass Spectrometry, to determine the masses of the members of the A=35, T=3/2 isospin quartet with high precision. The experimental data were compared to the predictions of the IMME. Our measurements reveal a significant deviation from the IMME for the A=35, T=3/2 isospin quartet, with a mean deviation of 0.23 MeV. This result indicates a breakdown of the IMME for this isospin quartet, which has implications for our understanding of nuclear shell model and the nuclear force. The observed deviation may be attributed to quenching of the isospin symmetry due to the presence of a proton-neutron interaction.

They became popular meeting places where men of learning often gathered to converse, play chess or backgammon-type games, sing and dance, listen to music, discuss politics and news of the day, and smoke and drink. They became known as "schools of wisdom" because of the clientele they attracted, and, though political and religious leaders feared the free and frank discourse common in such establishments, their frequent bans on coffeehouses were impossible to maintain. Text: We introduce a thorough investigation of the subgiant star bet Hyi, utilizing a multidisciplinary approach combining long-baseline optical interferometry and asteroseismology to determine its radius and mass. Our interferometric observations, obtained using the Very Extensive Telescope Interferometer (VLTI), enable us to accurately measure the angular diameter of bet Hyi, from which we derive a linear radius of 6.51 ± 0.14 solar radii (R). The seismic data, combined with a grid of stellar evolution models, allowed us to constrain the mass of bet Hyi to 1.73 ± 0.07 solar masses (M). Text: This investigation examines the thermal gradient-induced forces on geodetic reference masses for the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA), a forthcoming gravitational wave observatory that will consist of three spacecraft orbiting the Sun in a triangular formation. Our outcomes show that the thermal gradient-induced forces can be significant, with magnitudes comparable to or even exceeding the expected measurement noise floor of the LISA mission. We identified key parameters that influence the magnitude of these forces, including the thermal conductivity, specific heat capacity, and coefficient of thermal expansion of the reference mass materials. Text: In multipartite quantum information, Bell‑type constraints are traditionally expressed as inequalities that separate local‑hidden‑variable (LHV) predictions from quantum mechanics. Recent work has highlighted a complementary class of *equalities*—linear relations that must hold exactly for any LHV model. Their violation would provide a stringent, noise‑resilient signature of non‑classical correlations, especially in higher‑dimensional systems such as bipartite qutrits (3‑level particles), where the richer Hilbert space promises stronger departures from classical realism. We derived a complete set of LHV equalities for two‑party, three‑outcome measurements using the facet‑enumeration algorithm on the local polytope. The equalities were then tested against the maximally entangled qutrit state \(|\psi\rangle=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\sum_{k=0}^{2}|kk\rangle\) and a family of partially entangled states. Quantum predictions were obtained analytically via the Born rule and corroborated with high‑precision numerical optimization (semidefinite programming) over measurement bases. Robustness to white‑noise admixture was evaluated by introducing a depolarizing channel of varying strength. Several LHV equalities are violated by up to 12.3 % for the maximally entangled qutrit pair, exceeding the maximal violation of the standard CGLMP inequality (≈9 %). The violation persists for noise levels up to 23 % depolarization, demonstrating enhanced noise tolerance. Moreover, the equalities reveal a hierarchy of non‑locality that distinguishes between different entanglement classes. These establish equalities as powerful tools for certifying high‑dimensional quantum correlations and suggest new avenues for device‑independent protocols based on bipartite qutrit systems.

Text: This study examines the distribution of luminosity among satellite galaxies within galaxy groups, utilizing a comprehensive dataset that spans a redshift range of \(0.01<z<0.1\). By integrating spectroscopic and photometric data from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey's 16th data release with the Galaxy And Mass Assembly survey's high-resolution group catalogues, we compiled a robust sample of 12,345 groups with halo masses between \(10^{12.5}\) and \(10^{14.5} M_{\odot}\). To determine satellite luminosities, we employed extinction-corrected \(r\)-band absolute magnitudes, applying completeness corrections through a forward-modeling approach that considers fibre collisions and flux limits. Text: Active galactic nuclei, x-ray binaries, pulsars, and gamma-ray bursts are all believed to be powered by compact objects surrounded by relativistic plasma flows driving phenomena such as accretion, winds, and jets. We use a modified form of the WENO method to construct a finite-volume general relativistic hydrodynamics code called WHAM that converges at fifth order. We avoid (1) field-by-field decomposition by adaptively reducing down to 2-point stencils near discontinuities for a more accurate treatment of shocks, and (2) excessive reduction to low order stencils, as in the standard WENO formalism, by maintaining high order accuracy in smooth monotonic flows. Our scheme performs the proper surface integral of the fluxes, converts cell averaged conserved quantities to point conserved quantities before performing the reconstruction step, and correctly averages all source terms. Text: Quantum key distribution (QKD) offers an unconditionally secure means of communication based on the laws of quantum mechanics. Currently, a major challenge is to achieve a QKD system with a 40 dB channel loss, which is required if we are to realize global scale QKD networks using communication satellites. Here we report the first QKD experiment in which secure keys were distributed over 42 dB channel loss and 200 km of optical fibre. We employed the differential phase shift quantum key distribution (DPS-QKD) protocol implemented with a 10-GHz clock frequency, and superconducting single photon detectors (SSPD) based on NbN nanowire. The SSPD offers a very low dark count rate (a few Hz) and small timing jitter (60 ps full width at half maximum). These characteristics allowed us to construct a 10-GHz clock QKD system and thus distribute secure keys over channel loss of 42 dB. In addition, we achieved a 17 kbit/s secure key rate over 105 km of optical fibre, which is two orders of magnitude higher than the previous record, and a 12.1 bit/s secure key rate over 200 km of optical fibre, which is the longest terrestrial QKD yet demonstrated. The keys generated in our experiment are secure against both general collective attacks on individual photons and a specific collective attack on multi-photons, known as a sequential unambiguous state discrimination (USD) attack.

Text: We investigate the emergence of a Hall-like transverse response in a system of two closely spaced, parallel quantum wires fabricated from high‑mobility GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructures and subjected to a perpendicular magnetic field. The transverse voltage scales linearly with magnetic field up to 5 T, exhibits a non‑monotonic temperature dependence characteristic of the crossover from ballistic to interaction‑dominated regimes, and is strongly suppressed when the wires are electrically decoupled by gate‑controlled barriers. Our analysis uncovers that the Hall effect in this quasi‑one‑dimensional configuration originates from the interplay of chirality induced by the magnetic field and collective charge‑density excitations, providing a direct probe of spin‑charge separation and inter‑wire Luttinger parameters. Text: The QCD phase diagram at finite baryon density is expected to contain a critical endpoint separating a crossover from a first-order transition. However, lattice QCD simulations at real chemical potential suffer from the sign problem, rendering direct calculations infeasible. Earlier investigations employing Taylor expansion, reweighting, and imaginary-chemical-potential techniques have produced conflicting indications of the critical point's location. We performed large-scale lattice QCD simulations with 2+1 flavors of highly improved staggered quarks on (N_t=8text{-}12) lattices at imaginary chemical potential (mu_I). Observables were expanded in powers of ((mu/pi T)) and analytically continued to real (mu). Finite-size scaling of the chiral susceptibility and the Binder cumulant of the Polyakov loop were used to locate the critical point. Crucially, were cross-checked with a complex Langevin approach to assess systematic biases. Our analysis yields a critical endpoint at (T_E approx 147(4),text{MeV}) and (mu_BE approx 360(50),text{MeV}), consistent with a Z(_2) universality class. The continuum extrapolation shows mild lattice artefacts, and the extracted critical exponents agree within errors with the 3D Ising model. These provide the most stringent lattice constraints to date and support the existence of a finite-density critical point in QCD.

Text: This investigation delves into the intricate framework of superconformal nets, a class of algebraic structures that elegantly encode supersymmetric two-dimensional conformal field theories. Building upon the foundational concept of local nets of von Neumann algebras, we establish a rigorous definition of superconformal nets by incorporating supersymmetry generators that satisfy superconformal commutation relations, thereby providing a unified algebraic perspective on supersymmetric conformal field theories. Our systematic analysis reveals that superconformal nets exhibit a modular structure, admitting a grading by supersymmetry charges and decomposing into sectors invariant under spacetime symmetries. A key contribution of this work lies in the development of a classification scheme, which capitalizes on the interplay between superconformal invariance and the representation theory of the super-Virasoro algebra. By examining the fusion rules of superconformal defect nets and their equivalence under Morita-type transformations, we demonstrate that superconformal nets are classified up to isomorphism by their central charge and the topological data of their defect sectors. Furthermore, our elucidate the role of fermionic symmetry extensions in stabilizing superconformal structures, thereby establishing a connection to topological quantum field theories and string theory compactifications. Ultimately, this investigation provides a comprehensive algebraic framework for supersymmetric conformal field theories, offering novel tools for addressing open problems in mathematical physics and quantum gravity, and forging a bridge between operator algebraic and categorical approaches to supersymmetry.

Text: It has recently been suggested cite{Chang:2006bm} that a reliable and unambiguous definition of the non-perturbative massive quark condensate could be provided by considering a non positive-definite class of solutions to the Schwinger Dyson Equation for the quark propagator. Indeed, studying these three classes reveals a degeneracy of possible condensate definitions leading to a whole range of values. However, we show that the {it physical} condensate may in fact be extracted by simple fitting to the Operator Product Expansion, a procedure which is stabilised by considering the three classes of solution together. We find that for current quark masses in the range from zero to 25 MeV or so (defined at a scale of 2 GeV in the $bar{MS}$ scheme), the dynamically generated condensate increases from the chiral limit in a wide range of phenomenologically successful models of the confining QCD interaction. Text: .** Curvature line parametrizations are fundamental in differential geometry for visualizing and processing smooth surfaces. Using a system of integrable difference equations, we propagate these normals across the mesh, yielding a pair of conjugate coordinate functions. The analysis reveals a statistically robust linkage between metrics of accelerated expansion and amplified ecological degradation, a relationship that is mediated through escalated energy consumption and augmented material fluxes. Consequently, the very geometry of spacetime—by engendering conditions conducive to exponential resource exploitation—appears to indirectly foster systemic harm. These accentuate the imperative for interdisciplinary architectures that synthesize cosmological insights with sustainable development paradigms, and they advocate for policy measures aimed at attenuating the pernicious feedback loops connecting cosmic expansion with terrestrial wellbeing.

Text: We study the spectroscopic binary system Gl 375. We employ medium resolution echelle spectra obtained at the 2.15 m telescope at the Argentinian observatory CASLEO and photometric observations obtained from the ASAS database. We separate the composite spectra into those corresponding to both components. The separated spectra allow us to confirm that the spectral types of both components are similar (dMe3.5) and to obtain precise measurements of the orbital period (P = 1.87844 days), minimum masses (M_1 sin^3 i = 0.35 M_sun and M_2 sin^3 i =0.33 M_sun) and other orbital parameters. The photometric observations exhibit a sinusoidal variation with the same period as the orbital period. We interpret this as signs of active regions carried along with rotation in a tidally synchronized system, and study the evolution of the amplitude of the modulation in longer timescales. Together with the mean magnitude, the modulation exhibits a roughly cyclic variation with a period of around 800 days. This periodicity is also found in the flux of the Ca II K lines of both components, which seem to be in phase. The periodic changes in the three observables are interpreted as a sign of a stellar activity cycle. Both components appear to be in phase, which implies that they are magnetically connected. The measured cycle of approximately 2.2 years (800 days) is consistent with previous determinations of activity cycles in similar stars.

Text: This analysis studies the complex processes governing dust formation and survival in the ejecta of supernovae, a phenomenon critical to our insight into of the interstellar medium and the origins of life on Earth. We employ a combination of quantitative simulations and radiative transfer models to explore the nucleation and growth of dust grains within the hot, dense environments surrounding supernovae. Our results show that dust formation is facilitated by the rapid cooling and condensation of gas in the ejecta, with silicate and carbonaceous grains emerging as the dominant dust species. However, we also find that dust survival is severely compromised by the intense radiation fields and energetic particles present in the ejecta, leading to pronounced fragmentation and sputtering of grains. Our model predictions are compared to observations of dust in supernova remnants and progenitor stars, revealing a complex interplay between dust formation and destruction mechanisms. These findings have important implications for our insight into of the role of supernovae in shaping the interstellar medium and the global budget of dust in the universe.

Text: In this paper we suggest a theoretical method based on the statistical mechanics for treating the alpha-helix-random coil transition in alanine polypeptides. Text: Let $S$ be a surface of finite type which is not a sphere with at most four punctures, a torus with at most two punctures, or a closed surface of genus two. Let $\mathcal{MF}$ be the space of equivalence classes of measured foliations of compact support on $S$ and let $\mathcal{UMF}$ be the quotient space of $\mathcal{MF}$ obtained by identifying two equivalence classes whenever they can be represented by topologically equivalent foliations, that is, forgetting the transverse measure. The extended mapping class group $\Gamma^*$ of $S$ acts as by homeomorphisms of $\mathcal{UMF}$. We show that the restriction of the action of the whole homeomorphism group of $\mathcal{UMF}$ on some dense subset of $\mathcal{UMF}$ coincides with the action of $\Gamma^*$ on that subset. More precisely, let $\mathcal{D}$ be the natural image in $\mathcal{UMF}$ of the set of homotopy classes of not necessarily connected essential disjoint and pairwise nonhomotopic simple closed curves on $S$. The set $\mathcal{D}$ is dense in $\mathcal{UMF}$, it is invariant by the action of $\Gamma^*$ on $\mathcal{UMF}$ and the restriction of the action of $\Gamma^*$ on $\mathcal{D}$ is faithful. We prove that the restriction of the action on $\mathcal{D}$ of the group $\mathrm{Homeo}(\mathcal{UMF})$ coincides with the action of $\Gamma^*(S)$ on that subspace.

Text: Finite element method is one of powerful numerical to solve PDE. Usually, if a finite element solution to a Poisson equation based on a triangulation of the underlying domain is not accurate enough, one will discard the solution and then refine the triangulation uniformly and compute a new finite element solution over the refined triangulation. It is wasteful to discard the original finite element solution. We propose a prewavelet method to save the original solution by adding a prewavelet subsolution to obtain the refined level finite element solution. To increase the accuracy of numerical solution to Poisson equations, we can keep adding prewavelet subsolutions. Our prewavelets are orthogonal in the $H^1$ norm and they are compactly supported except for one globally supported basis function in a rectangular domain. We have implemented these prewavelet basis functions in MATLAB and used them for numerical solution of Poisson equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions. Numerical simulation demonstrates that our prewavelet solution is much more efficient than the standard finite element method.
