Text: We consider the classical and quantum dynamics of excitations in a system of two capacitively coupled Josephson junctions. In the classical case the equations of motion admit discrete breather solutions, which are time periodic and localized predominantly on one of the junctions. In the quantum case breather states are found in the central part of the energy spectrum of the confined nonescaping states of the system. We perform a systematic analysis of their tunneling frequency, site correlations, fluctuations of the number of quanta, and entanglement. Quantum breather states show strong site correlation of quanta and are characterized by a strong excitation of quanta on one junction which perform slow coherent tunneling motion from one junction to the other. They suppress fluctuations of the total number of excited quanta. Quantum breather states are the least entangled states among the group of eigenstates in the same range of the energy spectrum. We describe how quantum breather excitations could be experimentally observed by employing the already developed techniques for quantum information processing using Josephson junctions.

Text: Heavy quarkonia, bound states of quark-antiquark pairs, have long been a subject of interest in the field of nuclear physics. Their production and decay patterns can provide valuable insights into the properties of the quark-gluon plasma (QGP), a state of matter created in high-energy heavy-ion collisions. The STAR (Solenoidal Tracker at RHIC) experiment at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC) is uniquely positioned to study these phenomena. We present an analysis of heavy-quarkonia production in Au+Au collisions at √sNN = 200 GeV, utilizing a dataset of approximately 200 million events. The data were collected using the STAR detector, which provides excellent particle identification and tracking capabilities. We employed a template fit to extract the yields and nuclear modification factors (RCP) of J/ψ, ψ(2S), and Υ(1S) mesons. Our analysis reveals significant suppression of heavy-quarkonia yields in central Au+Au collisions, which is indicative of in-medium energy loss and interactions with the QGP. The are consistent with predictions from various transport models, which suggest that the QGP acts as a medium that suppresses the production of heavy quarkonia. The extracted RCP values are found to be in good agreement with previous STAR measurements, providing further evidence for the formation of a QGP in heavy-ion collisions.

Text: It was suggested that the two consecutive metamagnetic transitions and the large residual resistivity discovered in Sr$_3$Ru$_2$O$_7$ can be understood via the nematic order and its domains in a single layer system. However, a recently reported anisotropy between two longitudinal resistivities induced by tilting the magnetic field away from the c-axis cannot be explained within the single layer nematic picture. To fill the gap in our understanding within the nematic order scenario, we investigate the effects of bilayer coupling and in-plane magnetic field on the electronic nematic phases in a bilayer system. We propose that the in-plane magnetic field in the bilayer system modifies the energetics of the domain formation, since it breaks the degeneracy of two different nematic orientations. Thus the system reveals a pure nematic phase with a resistivity anisotropy in the presence of an in-plane magnetic field. In addition to the nematic phase, the bilayer coupling opens a novel route to a hidden nematic phase that preserves the x-y symmetry of the Fermi surfaces.

Text: Perfect, amicable, and sociable numbers have been extensively studied in number theory, with chains of such numbers exhibiting intriguing properties. Sociable chains extend this concept, comprising a sequence of numbers where each is the sum of the proper divisors of the previous number, ultimately returning to the starting number. We employed a computational approach, utilizing algorithms to generate and analyze perfect, amicable, and sociable chains. Our involved iterating through numbers to identify potential chains, verifying the sociable property, and characterizing the resulting sequences. Our research yielded several novel sociable chains, including a chain of length 28, the longest discovered to date. We also identified patterns and correlations between chain length and the properties of constituent numbers. The contribute to a deeper understanding of the complex relationships between perfect, amicable, and sociable numbers, shedding light on the underlying structural properties of these enigmatic chains.

Our analysis revealed that the standard Doppler shift equation can lead to systematic errors in the calculation of redshift for high-redshift Type Ia supernovae. Text: This study critically studies the non-standard definition of work as introduced in recent literature, which deviates from the traditional notion of work as a force applied to an object causing a displacement. The put forward definition, where work is defined as the product of force and displacement along the direction of the force, has garnered attention for its potential to simplify certain calculations in mechanics. However, this research reveals a fundamental inconsistency in the definition's application. By analyzing a series of cases involving friction, potential energy, and rotational motion, we show that the non-standard definition fails to account for the work done in scenarios where force and displacement are not aligned, leading to discrepancies in calculated energies and force requirements. Furthermore, we show that the definition's reliance on direction introduces unnecessary complexity and ambiguity in the analysis of mechanical systems. Our findings indicate that the non-standard definition of work, while seemingly intuitive, is not a viable replacement for the traditional definition and should be approached with caution in future applications. The findings of this study have meaningful implications for the field of mechanics and emphasize the need for a rigorous re-evaluation of the definition of work.

We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach by applying it to several illustrative examples, including the Ising model and the WZW model. By exploiting the orthogonal factorisation system (surjections, injections) on FinOrd, we construct a presentation of 𝖢𝖘𝖕(FinOrd, Surj) as the free symmetric monoidal bicategory generated by a single object equipped with a commutative comonoid structure satisfying a special Frobenius law and a compatible “order‑collapse’’ 2‑cell that encodes the linear ordering. This universal property unifies several existing constructions—such as the bicategory of spans of finite sets and the PROP for commutative bialgebras—and yields a robust algebraic framework for diagrammatic network models where both ordering and surjective connectivity are essential.

Text: We argue that the well known Dynes formula [Dynes R C {\it et al.} 1978 {\it Phys. Rev. Lett.} {\bf 41} 1509] for the superconducting quasiparticle density of states, which tries to incorporate the lifetime broadening in an approximate way, cannot be justified microscopically for conventional superconductors. Instead, we propose a new simple formula in which the energy gap has a finite imaginary part $-\Delta_2$ and the quasiparticle energy is real. We prove that in the quasiparticle approximation 2$\Delta_2$ gives the quasiparticle decay rate at the gap edge for conventional superconductors. This does not depend on the nature of interactions that cause the quasiparticle decay. The new formula is tested on the case of a strong coupling superconductor Pb$_{0.9}$Bi$_{0.1}$ and an excellent agreement with theoretical predictions is obtained. While both the Dynes formula and the one proposed in this work give good fits and fit parameters for Pb$_{0.9}$Bi$_{0.1}$, only the latter formula can be justified microscopically.

Text: Fitness challenges - structured programs that set participants a defined physical goal to accomplish within a specified timeframe - have become enormously popular as tools for motivation, habit formation, and community building around physical activity. The appeal is intuitive: a clear, bounded goal with defined parameters is easier to commit to than the open-ended aspiration of simply getting fitter. Whether it is a thirty-day push-up challenge, a couch-to-5K running program, or a hundred-day yoga journey, these structures provide accountability, measurable progress, and the community of fellow participants that makes sustained effort more enjoyable. The most effective fitness challenges are those that are appropriately challenging without being unrealistic, that build habits sustainable beyond the challenge period itself, and that prioritize consistency over intensity. Social challenges - in which participants share progress and provide encouragement to one another - consistently outperform solitary efforts in terms of completion rates and sustained behavior change. The psychological rewards of successfully completing a physical challenge can also have significant ripple effects, building a sense of capability and self-efficacy that extends beyond the fitness domain.

Text: The anomalously high flow rates observed in solid ⁴He confined within nanoscale channels have sparked intense debate over the existence of a supersolid phase and the role of surface morphology. While bulk experiments suggest a glassy supersolid component, the mechanisms enabling rapid mass transport through nanoconfinement remain unclear, particularly when the pore walls exhibit nanoscale waviness that can modify boundary slip and defect dynamics. We employed a combined theoretical–computational approach to model helium‑4 in wavy‑rough cylindrical nanpores of diameter 10–50 nm. The supersolid order parameter was described by a time‑dependent Ginzburg–Landau equation coupled to a viscoelastic glassy response. Wall roughness was introduced via a sinusoidal modulation (amplitude 0.5–2 nm, wavelength 5–20 nm) and incorporated through a Navier‑type slip boundary condition with a roughness‑enhanced slip length. Molecular dynamics simulations validated the continuum predictions and provided atomistic insight into defect nucleation at curvature extrema. The wavy‑rough geometry amplifies slip by up to an order of magnitude, producing a non‑linear increase in the effective superfluid fraction (Δρ_s/ρ≈0.03–0.07) and reducing the critical velocity threshold by 40 %. Defect‑mediated phase slips localize at troughs, enabling rapid, dissipation‑less transport consistent with experimental flow‑rate spikes. These suggest that surface waviness is a pivotal factor in realizing glassy supersolid helium flow in nanoporosity.

Text: Film criticism is the practice of analyzing, evaluating, and contextualizing films within broader aesthetic, cultural, historical, and theoretical frameworks — a discipline that, at its best, deepens understanding of cinema as an art form and serves as a vital intermediary between films and the audiences who might engage with them. Great film criticism does more than tell you whether a film is worth seeing; it illuminates what a film is doing and why, situates it within the director's body of work and the history of the medium, brings relevant historical and cultural knowledge to bear on its interpretation, and makes the experience of engaging with cinema richer and more rewarding. The digital transformation of media has dramatically changed the landscape of film criticism: the reduction of space for long-form critical writing in newspapers and magazines, the explosion of online voices ranging from the brilliant to the worthless, and the rise of audience aggregation platforms have all shifted the critical ecosystem in ways whose ultimate effects on film culture remain contested.

Text: The study of actions on compact groups has far-reaching implications in various fields of mathematics, particularly in the study of ergodic theory, geometric group theory, and representation theory. Compact groups are equipped with a natural measure, allowing for the study of ergodic properties of actions on these spaces. In this context, we explore the interplay between distal and ergodic actions, two fundamental concepts in ergodic theory. We employ a combination of topological and measure-theoretic techniques to analyze the behavior of actions on compact groups. Specifically, we utilize the notion of distal actions, which are characterized by the property that the orbits of nearby points are separated by a distance that grows without bound. We also examine ergodic actions, which are invariant under the action and have no invariant sets of positive measure. Our establish a dichotomy between distal and ergodic actions on compact groups. We show that if an action is ergodic, then it is also distal. Conversely, if an action is distal, then it has a finite number of ergodic components. Our have significant implications for the study of ergodic theory and geometric group theory, shedding new light on the interplay between these two fundamental concepts.

Text: Confined electron spins are preferred candidates for embodying quantum information in the solid state. A popular idea is the use of optical excitation to achieve the ``best of both worlds'', i.e. marrying the long spin decoherence times with rapid gating. Here we study an all-optical adiabatic approach to generating single qubit phase gates. We find that such a gate can be extremely robust against the combined effect of all principal sources of decoherence, with an achievable fidelity of 0.999 even at finite temperature. Crucially this performance can be obtained with only a small time cost: the adiabatic gate duration is within about an order of magnitude of a simple dynamic implementation. An experimental verification of these predictions is immediately feasible with only modest resources.

Text: We introduce a model of random interlacements made of a countable collection of doubly infinite paths on Z^d, d bigger or equal to 3. A non-negative parameter u measures how many trajectories enter the picture. This model describes in the large N limit the microscopic structure in the bulk, which arises when considering the disconnection time of a discrete cylinder with base a d-1-dimensional discrete torus of side-length N, or the set of points visited by simple random walk on the d-dimensional discrete torus of side-length N by times of order uN^d. We study the percolative properties of the vacant set left by the interlacement at level u, which is an infinite, connected, translation invariant random subset of Z^d. We introduce a critical value such that the vacant set percolates for u below the critical value, and does not percolate for u above the critical value. Our main show that the critical value is finite when d is bigger or equal to 3, and strictly positive when d is bigger or equal to 7.

The performance of each procedure was rigorously evaluated using metrics such as Mean Squared Error (MSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Kullback-Leibler Divergence (KLD). Findings indicate that the choice of density estimation procedure is significantly dependent on the underlying data characteristics, with GMM outperforming KDE in datasets with high-dimensional and multimodal distributions, whereas KDE excelled in cases with sparse and irregularly-distributed data. Conversely, BDE consistently demonstrated robustness in handling outliers and noisy data. These findings underscore the importance of dataset-specific evaluation and highlight the need for a tailored method to density estimation, thereby facilitating informed decision-making in various applications. Overall, this study contributes to the development of a comprehensive understanding of density estimation procedures and their relative strengths and limitations.

Our research reveal that the higher-order curvature corrections exert a notable influence on the deconfinement transition, in turn affecting the critical temperature $T_c$ and the behavior of the order parameter $\sigma$ in proximity to the transition. The present study holds significant implications for the investigation of the strong interaction at finite temperature and density. Our underscore the necessity of including higher-order curvature corrections in AdS/QCD models to accurately describe the hadron-quark transition. In contrast, heterogeneous nucleation is found to be significantly facilitated by the presence of defects and impurities, which can act as nucleation sites. The of our simulations also show that the effect of surface tension on heterogeneous nucleation is more pronounced than in homogeneous nucleation, highlighting the importance of surface energy in determining the nucleation behavior of Lennard-Jones liquids. Text: Quantum criticality refers to a phase transition that occurs in the zero-temperature limit, where quantum fluctuations dominate the behavior of the system. In these environments, entanglement plays a crucial role in shaping the phase diagram and influencing the emergence of novel phases. However, the interplay between quantum criticality and entanglement remains poorly understood, hindering our ability to predict and control the behavior of these systems. We performed a computational study of a two-dimensional Ising model at its quantum critical point, using a combination of density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) and entanglement spectrum analysis. Our simulations enabled us to probe the entanglement structure of the system in real space and momentum space, allowing us to identify the characteristic features of disentanglement in this environment. Our reveal a non-trivial entanglement structure in the quantum critical regime, characterized by a "sea" of non-local entangled pairs separated by regions of disentanglement. We find that the entanglement spectrum exhibits a clear signature of disentanglement, which is associated with the emergence of a topological phase. Crucially, our provide new insights into the interplay between quantum criticality and entanglement, and have implications for understanding the behavior of exotic phases in quantum materials.

Text: When two-photon interactions are induced by down-converted light with a bandwidth that exceeds the pump bandwidth, they can obtain a behavior that is pulse-like temporally, yet spectrally narrow. At low photon fluxes this behavior reflects the time and energy entanglement between the down-converted photons. However, two-photon interactions such as two-photon absorption (TPA) and sum-frequency generation (SFG) can exhibit such a behavior even at high power levels, as long as the final state (i.e. the atomic level in TPA, or the generated light in SFG) is narrowband enough. This behavior does not depend on the squeezing properties of the light, is insensitive to linear losses, and has potential applications. In this paper we describe analytically this behavior for travelling-wave down-conversion with continuous or pulsed pumping, both for high- and low-power regimes. For this we derive a quantum-mechanical expression for the down-converted amplitude generated by an arbitrary pump, and formulate operators that represent various two-photon interactions induced by broadband light. This model is in excellent agreement with experimental of TPA and SFG with high power down-converted light and with entangled photons [Dayan et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 93, 023005 (2004), Dayan et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 94, 043602, (2005), Pe'er et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 94, 073601 (2005)].

Furthermore, we show that the SU(3) family symmetry can resolve the long-standing CP problem in supersymmetric theories, providing a natural explanation for the observed pattern of CP-violating phases. Text: We use Spitzer Space Telescope observations from the Spitzer Survey of the Small Magellanic Cloud (S3MC) to study the young stellar content of N66, the largest and brightest HII region in the SMC. In addition to large numbers of normal stars, we detect a significant population of bright, red infrared sources that we identify as likely to be young stellar objects (YSOs). We use spectral energy distribution (SED) fits to classify objects as ordinary (main sequence or red giant) stars, asymptotic giant branch stars, galaxies, and YSOs. This represents the first large-scale attempt at blind source classification based on Spitzer SEDs in another galaxy. We firmly identify at least 61 YSOs, with another 50 probable YSOs; only one embedded protostar in the SMC was reported in the literature prior to the S3MC. We present color selection criteria that can be used to identify a relatively clean sample of YSOs with IRAC photometry. Our fitted SEDs indicate that the infrared-bright YSOs in N66 have stellar masses ranging from 2 Msun to 17 Msun, and that approximately half of the objects are Stage II protostars, with the remaining YSOs roughly evenly divided between Stage I and Stage III sources. We find evidence for primordial mass segregation in the HII region, with the most massive YSOs being preferentially closer to the center than lower-mass objects. Despite the low metallicity and dust content of the SMC, the observable properties of the YSOs appear consistent with those in the Milky Way. Although the YSOs are heavily concentrated within the optically bright central region of N66, there is ongoing star formation throughout the complex and we place a lower limit on the star formation rate of 3.2 x 10-3 Msun/yr over the last 1 Myr.

Text: The U(1) problem in quantum chromodynamics (QCD) refers to the difficulty of reconciling the chiral symmetry breaking and the conservation of the U(1)_A axial current within the framework of QCD. We utilize the holographic D-brane model to construct a 5D effective action, which includes the Eta meson field. Our indicate that the Eta meson plays a crucial role in resolving the U(1) problem within AdS/QCD. Text: We implement a standard Monte Carlo algorithm to study the slow, equilibrium dynamics of a silica melt in a wide temperature regime, from 6100 K down to 2750 K. By contrast, the strong thermal vibrations related to the Boson peak present at short times in molecular dynamics are efficiently suppressed by the Monte Carlo algorithm. This allows us to reconsider silica dynamics in the context of mode-coupling theory, because several shortcomings of the theory were previously attributed to thermal vibrations. A mode-coupling theory analysis of our data is qualitatively correct, but quantitative tests of the theory fail, raising doubts about the very existence of an avoided singularity in this system. We discuss the emergence of dynamic heterogeneity and report detailed measurements of a decoupling between translational diffusion and structural relaxation, and of a growing four-point dynamic susceptibility. Dynamic heterogeneity appears to be less pronounced than in more fragile glass-forming models, but not of a qualitatively different nature.

Text: R‑symmetry plays a pivotal role in the dynamics of O’Raifeartaigh‑type supersymmetry‑breaking models, governing the existence of metastable vacua and the emergence of runaway directions. Using the superspace formalism, we construct the most general superpotential consistent with a given R‑charge assignment and impose the conditions for F‑term supersymmetry breaking. The vacuum structure is analyzed through algebraic elimination of auxiliary fields and a detailed study of the resulting scalar potential, employing both analytic techniques (Groebner basis reduction) and numerical scans. Runaway directions are identified by examining the asymptotic behavior of the potential along flat directions, while the impact of explicit R‑symmetry‑violating terms is quantified via perturbative expansions. We demonstrate that (i) the presence of non‑trivial global symmetries constrains the allowed R‑charge assignments, often forbidding spontaneous R‑symmetry breaking; (ii) explicit R‑symmetry breaking generically induces runaway trajectories unless protected by discrete subgroups of the global symmetry; (iii) a subset of models admits stable, R‑symmetry‑breaking vacua without runaways, characterized by a residual Z₂ symmetry. These provide a comprehensive framework for engineering O’Raifeartaigh models with controlled R‑symmetry breaking and elucidate the conditions under which runaway directions can be avoided.

Text: The prevalence of marching bands, jazz bandwagon advertisements, and spasm bands performing in the streets of New Orleans meant that vernacular musical innovations such as jazz were available to everyone within listening range, regardless of laws that attempted to keep Black and white cultures mutually exclusive. In the period from 1895 to 1925, most jazz musicians came from these neighborhoods, where the outdoor music was taking place. The "hotter" and more expressive dance music that came to be known as jazz catalyzed the attraction of young people. Thus, this musical style, rooted in the good-time practices of the uptown African American community, spread rapidly throughout the metropolitan area, into the rural hinterland, and across the nation. The conventional wisdom about musical illiteracy as pervasive in early jazz does not accurately describe the variety of skill sets that musicians used to satisfy the demands of diverse clienteles. The trumpeter Louis Armstrong and trombonist Kid Ory both learned to read music when their careers required it; others, like the clarinetist Sidney Bechet, never did. Yet most New Orleans jazz bands drew upon varying skill levels among "readers" (who introduced the latest favorites from scores), "spellers" (who could not sight-read notes but could follow a written chord progression), and "fakers" in order to meet the functional requirements of a competitive market that required flexibility. "Faking" (or playing by ear) often led to further instruction, which could include solfège, musical literacy, theory, and arranging at the hands of teachers like Manuel Perez or Lorenzo Tio Jr.

The mass of the planet, HD171028b, was determined to be 2.43 M_Jup, placing it firmly in the category of a gas giant. The metallicity of the host star, [Fe/H] = -0.44 ± 0.09, is significantly lower than the Galactic average, making HD171028b a valuable addition to the growing sample of planets orbiting metal-poor stars. The planetary companion's orbital eccentricity was found to be 0.13 ± 0.02, suggesting a possible tidal interaction with the host star. Our contribute to a better understanding of the formation and evolution of planets in metal-poor environments, shedding light on the processes that govern the assembly of planetary systems. This discovery also underscores the importance of continuing radial velocity surveys for identifying additional planets in the southern hemisphere.

Text: This study presents a original Seedless Infrared-Safe Cone jet algorithm, designed to facilitate efficient and accurate particle-based simulations in a wide range of thermal and non-thermal applications. The proposed algorithm leverages a hybrid strategy, combining the benefits of a standard cone jet approach with the computational efficiency of a seedless technique. By eliminating the need for manual seeding, this modified algorithm significantly reduces the computational overhead associated with initialization and particle distribution. The cone jet model is further enhanced with an infrared-safe treatment, ensuring the algorithm's stability and accuracy in simulations involving high-temperature and high-speed flows. Theoretical analyses and numerical experiments show the introduced algorithm's robustness and performance, achieving a 30% reduction in computational time while maintaining equivalent accuracy compared to traditional seeding-based cone jet methods. The practical Seedless Infrared-Safe Cone jet algorithm holds pronounced promise for applications in fluid dynamics, aerodynamics, and combustion modeling, offering a valuable tool for researchers seeking to efficiently simulate complex, high-temperature phenomena.

Text: We present a comprehensive study of electric charge correlations in heavy-ion collisions at the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS) energies, focusing on the rapidity and energy dependence of these correlations. The measurements were performed using the NA49 and NA60 experiments, which provided high-statistics data on Au+Au and Pb+Pb collisions at beam energies ranging from 20 to 158 GeV per nucleon. Our analysis reveals a significant dependence of the electric charge correlations on the collision energy and rapidity interval, indicating a strong coupling between the spatial and momentum distributions of the produced particles. The are consistent with expectations from hydrodynamic models, which predict a strong correlation between the charge of particles and their relative rapidity. However, the data also show a significant deviation from the expected behavior at forward rapidities, suggesting the presence of non-hydrodynamic mechanisms that influence the final state particle correlations. These have important implications for our understanding of the hadronization process and the properties of the Quark-Gluon Plasma created in heavy-ion collisions.

Text: The comfort of routines in uncertain times is a paradox that warrants closer examination, especially for those who find solace in the predictability that structures like schedules, rituals, and daily habits bring. On the surface, routines seem like a mundane aspect of our lives, a necessary evil that we trudge through without much thought. Yet, for many, they serve as a lifeline that anchors us in moments of chaos and unpredictability. Research has shown that humans are wired to respond to patterns and rhythms, and that the absence of them can lead to feelings of disorientation and anxiety. This is precisely why routines become so essential during times of crisis or upheaval. They provide a sense of control, a reassuring sense that despite the turmoil swirling around us, we can still rely on ourselves to show up, perform, and navigate our daily tasks. The rituals of morning coffee, exercise, or meditation, for instance, offer a fleeting moment of reprieve from the uncertainty that lies ahead. Moreover, routines have a way of making us feel connected to our past selves, allowing us to hold onto memories and experiences that remind us of who we were before the storm hit. As such, routines become a vital component of resilience, a coping mechanism that reminds us that even in the darkest of times, there is still a semblance of continuity, and that it's precisely this continuity that keeps us going.

Our proposed has been successfully applied to design and implement a STA for a 5G wireless communication system. The show that the designed STA achieves a significant improvement in signal processing and transmission efficiency, resulting in a 30% reduction in latency and a 25% increase in throughput. The proposed provides a systematic and structured approach to designing STAs, enabling the efficient design of advanced communication systems.

Text: When an electric field is applied to an electrolyte-saturated polymer gel embedded with charged colloidal particles, the force that must be exerted by the hydrogel on each particle reflects a delicate balance of electrical, hydrodynamic and elastic stresses. This paper examines the displacement of a single charged spherical inclusion embedded in an uncharged hydrogel. We present numerically exact solutions of coupled electrokinetic transport and elastic-deformation equations, where the gel is treated as an incompressible, elastic Brinkman medium. This model problem demonstrates how the displacement depends on the particle size and charge, the electrolyte ionic strength, and Young's modulus of the polymer skeleton. The numerics are verified, in part, with an analytical (boundary-layer) theory valid when the Debye length is much smaller than the particle radius. Further, we identify a close connection between the displacement when a colloid is immobilized in a gel and its velocity when dispersed in a Newtonian electrolyte. Finally, we describe an experiment where nanometer-scale displacements might be accurately measured using back-focal-plane interferometry. The purpose of such an experiment is to probe physicochemical and rheological characteristics of hydrogel composites, possibly during gelation.

Text: We investigate the chemical evolution of the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC) based on abundance data of planetary nebulae (PNe). The main goal is to investigate the time evolution of the oxygen abundance in this galaxy by deriving an age-metallicity relation. Such a relation is of fundamental importance as an observational constraint of chemical evolution models of the SMC. We have used high quality PNe data in order to derive the properties of the progenitor stars, so that the stellar ages could be estimated. We collected a large number of measured spectral fluxes for each nebula, and derived accurate physical parameters and nebular abundances. New spectral data for a sample of SMC PNe obtained between 1999 and 2002 are also presented. These data are used together with data available in the literature to improve the accuracy of the fluxes for each spectral line. We obtained accurate chemical abundances for PNe in the Small Magellanic Cloud, which can be useful as tools in the study of the chemical evolution of this galaxy and of Local Group galaxies. We present the resulting oxygen versus age diagram and a similar relation involving the [Fe/H] metallicity based on a correlation with stellar data. We discuss the implications of the derived age-metallicity relation for the SMC formation, in particular by suggesting a star formation burst in the last 2-3 Gyr.

Text: Pr\"ufer's ideal numbers, introduced by Georg Pr\"ufer in 1901, are a type of ideal in the ring of algebraic integers that exhibit unique factorization properties. In a separate development, Gelfand's maximal ideals, named after Israel Gelfand, are a fundamental concept in the theory of commutative Banach algebras. This study explores the connection between these two distinct mathematical frameworks. We utilize a combination of algebraic and topological techniques to establish a correspondence between Pr\"ufer's ideal numbers and Gelfand's maximal ideals. Specifically, we employ the theory of local rings and the properties of maximal ideals in Banach algebras to construct a bijection between the set of Pr\"ufer's ideal numbers and the set of Gelfand's maximal ideals. Our demonstrate that Pr\"ufer's ideal numbers can be naturally identified with Gelfand's maximal ideals, providing a novel insight into the structure of algebraic integers. The correspondence established in this study has far-reaching implications for the development of algebraic number theory and the application of Banach algebra techniques to problems in algebraic geometry.

Our also shed light on the connection between the properness of a mapping and the geometry of the spectral unit ball, including its boundary and the properties of its associated Bergman metric. Text: We report on the Scanning Tunneling Microscope (STM) observation of linear fringes together with spatially varying super-lattice structures on (0001) graphite (HOPG) surface. It then changes into a one-dimensional (1-D) fringe-like pattern before relaxing into a pattern-free region. We attribute this surface structure to a shear strain giving rise to a spatially varying rotation of the affected graphite layer relative to the bulk substrate. We propose a simple method to understand these moire patterns by looking at the fixed and rotated lattices in the Fourier transformed k-space. Using this approach we can reproduce the spatially varying 2-D lattice as well as the 1-D fringes by simulation. The 1-D fringes are found to result from a particular spatial dependence of the rotation angle.

Text: This study investigates the phenomenon of stochastic resonance in subwavelength hole arrays, leading to enhanced energy coupling at the nanoscale. By introducing disorder in the form of subwavelength holes with varied diameters and periodic spacings, we observed a significant increase in the absorption of incident electromagnetic radiation. This phenomenon, known as stochastic resonance, arises from the interplay between the disorder-induced fluctuations and the resonant behavior of the subwavelength holes. Our experiments revealed that the stochastic resonance effect is maximized at a critical disorder strength, resulting in an enhancement of energy coupling by up to 300% compared to the ordered array configuration. Furthermore, we demonstrated that the stochastic resonance effect can be tailored by adjusting the disorder parameters, allowing for fine control over the energy absorption properties of the subwavelength hole arrays. These have important implications for the development of nanostructured materials and devices for applications in energy harvesting, sensing, and photonics.

Text: In a recent theoretical study, we have explored the modulating influence of externally applied magnetic fields on ultracold atomic interactions, with a particular focus on suppressing inelastic cross-sections near Feshbach resonances. These resonances occur when the energy level of the molecular state coincidentally intersects that of the colliding atoms, thereby inducing enhanced scattering lengths and, subsequently, inelastic processes. Notably, the deliberate manipulation of the magnetic field strength surrounding the ultracold gas enables the engineering of a resonance frequency shift, effectively diminishing inelastic cross-sections. Through the implementation of a coupled-channel model for numerical calculations, we have observed a substantial decrease in inelastic loss rates when the magnetic field strength approaches the Feshbach resonance condition from the low-field side. In doing so, we have demonstrated that the application of magnetic field tuning can efficiently reduce inelastic cross-sections by a factor of 3-5 in proximity to the Feshbach resonance, without jeopardizing the overall collisional stability. This novel approach has important implications for the study and fine-tuning of ultracold atomic interactions, particularly in the context of atomic fountain experiments and magnetic trapping applications. The presented here further contribute to a more profound comprehension of the intricate relationship between magnetic fields and ultracold collisional dynamics, thereby paving the way for the development of innovative experimental techniques and improved control over ultracold atomic interactions.

Text: This paper presents a new game-theoretic model to optimize energy-efficient modulation in Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA) networks subject to delay Quality of Service (QoS) constraints. We formulate a non-cooperative game between users, where each user seeks to maximize its own throughput while adhering to the imposed delay QoS constraints. The game is structured around a set of modulation and coding schemes, each associated with a specific transmission power and delay performance. By capitalizing on the concept of Nash Equilibrium, we derive a set of optimal modulation and power allocation strategies that balance the tradeoff between energy efficiency and delay QoS. Simulation results reveal the effectiveness of our put forward method in reducing energy consumption while meeting prescribed delay deadlines, thereby enhancing the overall network efficiency and user satisfaction. Our approach offers a practical solution for managing energy-efficient modulation in CDMA networks under stringent delay QoS requirements.

Text: The neutral species of chromium (Cr I) is indispensable for delineating the Galaxy’s chemical evolution, yet the prevailing uncertainty in spectroscopic abundance determinations stems from the laboratory transition probabilities associated with its optical transitions. In this work we furnish an exhaustive array of refined Cr I oscillator strengths obtained through a synergistic approach that couples time‑resolved laser‑induced fluorescence lifetime determinations with high‑resolution Fourier‑transform spectroscopic measurements of branching fractions. The resultant logarithmic oscillator strengths (log gf) achieve an internal accuracy of approximately 0.04 dex and effectively eliminate the systematic discrepancy that previously beset laboratory and astrophysical datasets. Employing these updated atomic parameters, we re‑evaluate chromium abundances in the solar spectrum and in three archetypal benchmark stars—HD 84937, HD 140283, and HD 76932—using both local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) and non‑LTE (NLTE) frameworks. The solar chromium abundance is thereby determined to be A(Cr) = 5.64 ± 0.04, which aligns closely with the meteoritic benchmark, while the stellar analyses reveal a uniform [Cr/Fe] ratio of approximately zero across the metallicity interval −2.5 < [Fe/H] < −1.0, thereby resolving the historically persistent chromium deficiency observed in metal‑poor stellar populations. These accentuate the paramount importance of precise laboratory measurements for credible stellar abundance investigations and furnish a definitive reference dataset for forthcoming studies of chromium nucleosynthesis.

Text: This study presents an innovative multi-criteria scheduling framework for pipeline workflows, designed to optimize the execution of complex data processing tasks in distributed computing environments. The PipeFlow framework is comprised of three primary components: a workflow decomposition module that breaks down complex pipelines into manageable sub-tasks; a scheduling module that employs a multi-objective genetic algorithm to explore the Pareto frontier of feasible solutions; and a post-processing module that evaluates and ranks the optimal schedules based on user-defined priorities. Our experimental , obtained through simulations on a range of benchmark datasets and workflows, demonstrate the effectiveness of PipeFlow in achieving significant improvements in processing time, resource efficiency, and energy savings, while also providing users with a high degree of flexibility and control over the scheduling process. The PipeFlow framework is anticipated to have a wide range of applications in fields such as scientific computing, data analytics, and high-performance computing.

Text: We consider optimal execution strategies for block market orders placed in a limit order book (LOB). We build on the resilience model proposed by Obizhaeva and Wang (2005) but allow for a general shape of the LOB defined via a given density function. Thus, we can allow for empirically observed LOB shapes and obtain a nonlinear price impact of market orders. We distinguish two possibilities for modeling the resilience of the LOB after a large market order: the exponential recovery of the number of limit orders, i.e., of the volume of the LOB, or the exponential recovery of the bid-ask spread. We consider both of these resilience modes and, in each case, derive explicit optimal execution strategies in discrete time. Applying our to a block-shaped LOB, we obtain a new closed-form representation for the optimal strategy, which explicitly solves the recursive scheme given in Obizhaeva and Wang (2005). We also provide some evidence for the robustness of optimal strategies with respect to the choice of the shape function and the resilience-type.

Text: This work examines the coherent dynamics of photoinduced nucleation processes in crystalline solids, shedding light on the underlying mechanisms governing the formation of atomic-scale defects and nucleation sites. Employing a combination of ultrafast pump-probe spectroscopy and first-principles simulations, we have elucidated the temporal evolution of coherent phonon modes and their role in facilitating the photoinduced nucleation of defects. Text: Deterministic generation of large‑scale atomic cluster states is a prerequisite for scalable measurement‑based quantum computation, yet current protocols rely on probabilistic entangling operations that require single‑photon detection and suffer from low success rates. The derivation employs a mixed Hodge structure on the relative cohomology \(H^{3}(X,\mathcal{L})\), where \(\mathcal{L}\) denotes the D‑brane locus, and utilizes the special geometry of the open‑closed moduli space. Crucially, the framework resolves holomorphic ambiguities via boundary conditions derived from large‑radius monodromy and open‑string mirror symmetry. The combination of simulation and experiment allowed for a detailed understanding of the self-diffusion and interdiffusion processes in Al80Ni20 melts, with implications for the development of advanced alloys and materials with tailored properties. This work highlights the utility of molecular dynamics simulations in predicting and grasp of the diffusion behavior of complex systems.

Text: We outline the findings of a comprehensive Spitzer IRAC (Infrared Array Camera) survey of newly-discovered planetary nebulae (PNe) from the Macquarie-AAO-Strasbourg H-alpha Planetary Nebula Project. Our work involves the observation of 43 previously uncatalogued PNe, selected based on their bright H-alpha emission and absence from existing infrared catalogs. Through the IRAC camera on board the Spitzer Space Telescope, we obtained 4-band (3.6, 4.5, 5.8, and 8.0 micron) imaging data for each PN, which were then analyzed to derive physical parameters, including dust temperature, mass, and spatial distribution. Our outcomes indicate that the observed PNe exhibit a wide range of morphologies, from spherical to irregular and bipolar, with some displaying complex, multi-component structures. We also find that the majority of the PNe in our sample have warmer dust temperatures (T > 100 K) than previously thought, suggesting the presence of marked thermal emission from dust grains in the nebulae. These results have important implications for our insight into of PN evolution and the role of dust in shaping the morphology and properties of these objects.

Text: This study presents a comprehensive and rigorous formulation of a general theory of electromagnetic fluctuations near a homogeneous surface, derived in terms of its reflection amplitudes. Our formulation explicitly takes into account the scattering amplitudes of the surface, thereby enabling a thorough investigation of the effects of surface properties on electromagnetic fluctuations. The resulting theory is capable of describing a wide range of physical phenomena, including thermal radiation, quantum fluctuations, and non-equilibrium effects, all of which are of paramount importance in fields such as quantum optics, surface science, and nanotechnology. Our provide a unified and quantitative understanding of electromagnetic fluctuations near a homogeneous surface, thereby laying the groundwork for further theoretical and experimental investigations into the fundamental nature of these fluctuations. Text: We report on the investigation of optically-induced nuclear spin orientation in semiconductor quantum dots via a combination of optical pumping and magnetic resonance techniques. Our results demonstrate the bistable behavior of nuclear spin polarization in quantum dots, whereby the system exhibits two stable states of nuclear spin orientation that are separated by a essential point. The lower energy state corresponds to a fully polarized nuclear spin, while the higher energy state corresponds to a partially polarized or unpolarized nuclear spin configuration. The bistability is found to be robust and insensitive to variations in the magnetic field strength and the optical pumping conditions. We attribute the bistability to the interplay between the nuclear spin-lattice relaxation and the nuclear spin-spin interactions, which lead to the emergence of a hysteretic behavior in the nuclear spin polarization. Our results have implications for the development of quantum information processing and spin-based quantum computing, where precise control over nuclear spin polarization is essential for the implementation of quantum gates and other quantum operations. The bistability of nuclear spin orientation in quantum dots outlines a new paradigm for the manipulation of quantum systems.

Text: The computation of integer powers in floating-point arithmetic presents significant challenges in domains such as scientific computing, machine learning, and cryptographic protocols, primarily due to the inherent rounding errors and precision constraints of IEEE 754 representations. While conventional approaches, such as sequential multiplicative accumulation or squaring-based exponentiation, frequently exhibit a trade-off between computational expediency and numerical robustness, thereby underscoring the lack of integrated solutions that harmonize these competing objectives. To address this, this study introduces an innovative algorithmic framework tailored for IEEE 754 floating-point arithmetic, synthesizing exponentiation via squaring techniques with adaptive error compensation mechanisms to suppress the propagation of accumulated rounding discrepancies. By strategically modulating the sequence of arithmetic operations to attenuate error accumulation, the proposed retains a logarithmic time complexity ($ O(\log n) $) for exponentiation, thereby achieving parity with conventional squaring-based approaches in computational efficiency. Through rigorous analytical proofs and empirical evaluations across diverse test cases, the algorithm demonstrates superior error containment relative to extant , with absolute error margins constrained within $ \epsilon \cdot |x|^n $—where $ \epsilon $ denotes machine epsilon—thereby guaranteeing numerical accuracy in precision-sensitive contexts. Benchmark assessments reveal that the proposed method maintains competitive execution times compared to squaring-based algorithms on contemporary architectures, while concurrently exhibiting enhanced precision for large exponents or ill-conditioned operands. Applications in polynomial evaluation frameworks and iterative solution algorithms further underscore the algorithm's efficacy in mitigating error accumulation, thereby elevating computational reliability. By resolving the inherent tension between computational efficiency and numerical precision, this research establishes a versatile paradigm for integer power computation in floating-point arithmetic, with far-reaching implications for scientific and engineering applications.

Text: We introduce a novel field-theoretical approach for MOND-like gravity, providing a well-defined and steady extension of the theory to the regime of strong gravitational fields. Our formulation is grounded in the TeVeS (Tensor-Vector-Scalar) theory, a known covariant approach to MOND, and incorporates a innovative field-theoretic representation of the MONDian force law. By introducing a dynamical vector field that couples to matter and a scalar field responsible for the MONDian acceleration scale, we derive a set of field equations that describe the dynamics of the gravitational field in the strong-field limit. Our formulation reproduces the MONDian force law in the weak-field limit, while providing a smooth transition to Newtonian gravity in the strong-field regime. Furthermore, we demonstrate that our field-theoretical framework is compatible with existing MOND-based models of galaxy rotation curves and galaxy clusters. The introduced formulation provides a new perspective on the MOND paradigm, offering a more stable and mathematically elegant framework for describing the gravitational dynamics of astronomical systems in the strong-field regime.

Text: We explore the internal space dependence of the static quark-antiquark potential within the framework of ${\cal N}=4$ Super Yang-Mills (SYM) plasma wind, a theoretical model of a strongly coupled quark-gluon plasma. By employing a combination of numerical lattice simulations and analytical calculations, we analyze the behavior of the potential as a function of the distance between the quark and antiquark, as well as the internal spatial separation of the quark and antiquark within the plasma. Our outcomes reveal a non-trivial dependence of the potential on the internal spatial separation, which we find to be characterized by a suppression of the potential at small internal separations. This suppression is attributed to the screening effects of the plasma, which become more pronounced as the internal separation decreases. We demonstrate that the internal space dependence of the potential has a meaningful impact on the phenomenology of quark-antiquark dissociation within the plasma, and provide a in-depth comparison with existing experimental and theoretical studies of quark-gluon plasma dynamics.

Text: This study delves into the fundamental concept of reparameterizations of continuous paths, a crucial aspect of modern mathematics with applications in various fields, including differential geometry, topology, and machine learning. We examine the reparameterization of curves, which involves transforming a curve given in one parameterization to another parameterization, resulting in a new curve with the same geometric properties. Our research focuses on the theoretical framework underlying this concept, leveraging the tools of differential geometry and functional analysis to derive necessary and sufficient conditions for reparameterization. Specifically, we investigate the relationship between the reparameterization of curves and the associated notion of isometry, exploring how reparameterization affects the geometric and topological properties of the underlying curve. Through a combination of theoretical analysis and numerical experimentation, we demonstrate the applicability of our to problems in computer vision and robotics, highlighting the potential of reparameterization as a powerful tool for curve analysis and manipulation. Text: In the paradigm of non-supersymmetric Grand Unified Theories (GUTs), wherein the electroweak and strong interactions are merged into a unified gauge structure, we embark on an in-depth examination of decoupling phenomena, particularly the Appelquist-Carazzone (AC) decoupling, a theoretical framework positing that heavy particles exhibit exponentially suppressed couplings with the light sector, thereby decoupling from low-energy physics. However, a comprehensive analysis of various non-supersymmetric GUT models reveals a significant deviation from this decoupling scenario, necessitating a reevaluation of the theoretical frameworks underpinning these theories. Our systematic investigation elucidates that the decoupling of heavy particles from light sectors is not solely dependent on the exponential suppression of their couplings, but is instead influenced by the residual interactions among the light fields, thereby inducing a persistent coupling between the heavy sector and the Standard Model (SM) particles. Using numerical simulations, we demonstrate that the AC decoupling condition is violated in models featuring multiple Higgs doublets, large Yukawa couplings, and extended gauge symmetry groups, which arises from the intricate interplay between the SM particles and the heavy sectors, generating non-negligible corrections to the AC decoupling condition. These prompt a reevaluation of the validity of the AC decoupling in non-supersymmetric GUTs and provide novel insights into the behavior of these theories at the interface between the electroweak and Grand Unified scales. Moreover, our have profound implications for the phenomenology of non-supersymmetric GUTs, underscoring the imperative need for refined theoretical models capable of accurately describing the decoupling of heavy particles from light sectors. Text: We present a novel nilpotent normal form for divergence-free vector fields and volume-preserving maps, which provides a unified framework for the study of these geometric objects. This nilpotent normal form reveals the hidden structure of the vector field and enables the computation of its topological invariants, including the Betti numbers and the Euler characteristic. Furthermore, we show that the nilpotent normal form can be used to classify volume-preserving maps, which are essential in the study of Hamiltonian systems and symplectic geometry. Text: We present a comprehensive time-dependent Dalitz plot analysis of the B0 --> Ks pi+ pi- decay mode, providing valuable insights into the underlying dynamics of this complex hadronic process. Our analysis yields a sample of approximately 3,200 signal events, allowing for a detailed examination of the decay dynamics. We find that the decay amplitude exhibits a significant variation with respect to the B0 lifetime, indicating a substantial contribution from rescattering effects in the hadronic final state. Our results are consistent with the predictions of the U-spin symmetry, which serves as a crucial guiding principle in our analysis. Furthermore, we report the determination of several key parameters governing the decay dynamics, including the strong phase difference and the amplitude fractions, which are essential for advancing our understanding of the strong interactions governing the B0 --> Ks pi+ pi- decay mode.

Text: We present bright-dark vector solitons in quasi-one-dimensional spinor (F=1) Bose-Einstein condensates. Using a multiscale expansion technique, we reduce the corresponding nonintegrable system of three coupled Gross-Pitaevskii equations (GPEs) to a completely integrable Yajima-Oikawa system. In this way, we obtain approximate solutions for small-amplitude vector solitons of dark-dark-bright and bright-bright-dark types, in terms of the $m_{F}=+1,-1,0$ spinor components, respectively. By means of numerical simulations of the full GPE system, we demonstrate that these states indeed feature soliton properties, i.e., they propagate undistorted and undergo quasi-elastic collisions. It is also shown that, in the presence of a parabolic trap of strength $omega $, the bright component(s) is (are) guided by the dark one(s), and, as a result, the small-amplitude vector soliton as a whole performs harmonic oscillations of frequency $omega/ sqrt{2}$ in the shallow soliton limit. Text: HIV-1 infection leads to the dysregulation of host cell apoptosis, a process critical for maintaining cellular homeostasis. Fas-induced apoptosis is a key mechanism by which infected cells can be eliminated, but this process is disrupted by HIV-1 proteins and virions. Understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying this disruption is essential for developing effective therapeutic strategies. We employed a systems biology approach, combining bioinformatics, mathematical modeling, and experimental validation to investigate the effects of HIV-1 virions and proteins on Fas-induced apoptosis. We constructed a dynamic model of the Fas signaling pathway in infected cells, incorporating experimentally validated data on the interactions between HIV-1 proteins and host cell factors. Our modeling indicate that HIV-1 virions and proteins induce a significant delay in Fas-induced apoptosis, primarily by modulating the activity of key signaling molecules. Specifically, we found that the HIV-1 protein Vpr interacts with the Fas-associated death domain protein (FADD), inhibiting its ability to recruit caspase-8. Crucially, these provide novel insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying HIV-1-induced apoptosis resistance and highlight potential targets for therapeutic intervention.

Text: Low‑dimensional quantum antiferromagnets with bond randomness exhibit unconventional ground states, such as random‑singlet phases and disorder‑induced gap closing. The mixed‑halide compound (CH₃)₂CHNH₃Cu(ClₓBr₁₋ₓ)₃ provides a tunable platform in which the superexchange pathways are modulated by the Cl/Br ratio, enabling a systematic investigation of the random‑bond effect on the spin‑½ Cu²⁺ chains. Single crystals with nominal compositions x = 0.0, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, and 1.0 were grown by the slow‑evaporation technique and characterized by X‑ray diffraction. ^1H‑NMR spectra were recorded in the temperature range 0.3–30 K under magnetic fields of 6–9 T. The Knight shift, full‑width at half‑maximum, and spin‑lattice relaxation rate (1/T₁) were extracted as functions of temperature and composition. Spectral deconvolution was performed to separate contributions from protons coupled to Cu²⁺ spins in distinct local environments, and the distribution of relaxation times was analyzed using stretched‑exponential fits. For intermediate halide concentrations (0.25 ≤ x ≤ 0.75) the ^1H line broadens dramatically and 1/T₁ follows a power‑law temperature dependence (1/T₁ ∝ T^α, α ≈ 0.6), indicative of a broad distribution of exchange couplings. The Knight shift deviates from the uniform‑chain Curie‑Weiss behavior, revealing a reduction of the average spin gap with increasing bond disorder. Scaling analysis demonstrates that the low‑energy excitations obey random‑singlet statistics, confirming that bond randomness drives the system toward a disorder‑controlled quantum critical regime.

Text: Recent halo star abundance observations exhibit an important feature of consequence to the r-process: the presence of a main r-process between the second and third peaks which is consistent among halo stars. We explore fission cycling and steady-beta flow as the driving mechanisms behind this feature. The presence of fission cycling during the r-process can account for nucleosynthesis yields between the second and third peaks, whereas the presence of steady-beta flow can account for consistent r-process patterns, robust under small variations in astrophysical conditions. We employ the neutrino-driven wind of the core-collapse supernova to examine fission cycling and steady-beta flow in the r-process. As the traditional neutrino-driven wind model does not produce the required very neutron-rich conditions for these mechanisms, we examine changes to the neutrino physics necessary for fission cycling to occur in the neutrino-driven wind environment, and we explore under what conditions steady-beta flow is obtained.

Text: This study investigates the thermal timescale mass transfer rates in intermediate-mass X-ray binaries, a class of stellar systems characterized by the transfer of material from a massive companion star to a compact accretor, such as a neutron star or black hole. Our analysis combines multi-wavelength observations and numerical simulations to derive self-consistent models of mass transfer rates in these systems. We find that the mass transfer rates in intermediate-mass X-ray binaries are significantly influenced by the thermal evolution of the companion star, particularly during the thermal timescale, where the star's interior and envelope evolve in a synchronized manner. Our indicate that the mass transfer rates in these systems can be accurately described by a thermal timescale mass transfer rate formula, which takes into account the companion star's mass, luminosity, and radius. We validate our model using a sample of intermediate-mass X-ray binaries and demonstrate its applicability to a wide range of system parameters. The derived thermal timescale mass transfer rates provide a critical input for modeling the evolution and accretion processes in these complex stellar systems.

Text: We investigate the compactness of the complex Green operator, a fundamental operator in the study of partial differential equations, particularly in the context of the Helmholtz equation. The complex Green operator is defined as the integral operator with a kernel involving the Green's function for the Helmholtz equation. By employing a combination of functional analysis and operator theory techniques, we derive a necessary and sufficient condition for the compactness of the complex Green operator in Hilbert spaces. Our analysis reveals that the compactness of the operator is intimately linked to the properties of the Green's function and the behavior of the kernel as the frequency parameter tends to infinity. Specifically, we establish that the operator is compact if and only if the kernel is square-integrable with respect to the Green's function. Our have significant implications for the study of wave propagation and scattering problems, as compactness is a crucial property for the application of spectral theory and the analysis of eigenvalue problems.

Text: This work focuses on the Ginzburg-Landau energy functional, a fundamental model in the theory of superconductivity, with an applied magnetic field. We derive Lorentz space estimates for the Ginzburg-Landau energy, establishing a connection between the energy's lower bound and the Jacobian of the gradient flow. Our main result is the convergence of the Jacobian as the applied magnetic field strength increases, demonstrating a key relationship between the energy's minimization and the magnetic field's influence on the system's behavior. Specifically, we show that the Jacobian converges to a constant as the magnetic field strength approaches a critical value, below which the system exhibits a phase transition from the superconducting to the normal state. Our findings have implications for understanding the effects of applied magnetic fields on superconducting materials and may be used to inform the development of novel superconducting devices and applications. The findings are rigorously established through a combination of variational techniques and functional assessment, providing a foundational framework for further research in this area.

Text: We theoretically investigate the ground state of trapped neutral fermions with population imbalance in the BCS-BEC crossover regime. On the basis of the single-channel Hamiltonian, we perform full numerical calculations of the Bogoliubov-de Gennes equation coupled with the regularized gap and number equations. The zero-temperature phase diagram in the crossover regime is presented, where the Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov (FFLO) pairing state governs the weak-coupling BCS region of a resonance. It is found that the FFLO oscillation vanishes in the BEC side, in which the system under population imbalance turns into a phase separation (PS) between locally binding superfluid and fully polarized spin domains. We also demonstrate numerical calculations with a large particle number O(10^5), comparable to that observed in recent experiments. The resulting density profile on a resonance yields the PS, which is in good agreement with the recent experiments, while the FFLO modulation exists in the pairing field. It is also proposed that the most favorable location for the detection of the FFLO oscillation is in the vicinity of the critical population imbalance in the weak coupling BCS regime, where the oscillation periodicity becomes much larger than the interparticle spacing. Finally, we analyze the radio-frequency (RF) spectroscopy in the imbalanced system. The clear difference in the RF spectroscopy between BCS and BEC sides reveals the structure of the pairing field and local ``magnetization''.

Text: Given a set of astrometric observations of the same object, the problem of orbit determination is to compute the orbit and to assess its uncertainty and reliability. We try on different personas, like worn jeans and faded band t-shirts, embracing some and discarding others as we search for the perfect fit. With each passing year, our sense of self becomes more nuanced, like the layers of a favorite book that's been read and reread, its pages dog-eared and worn. We carry the memories of loved ones, mentors, and friends who have shaped us, their influence seeping into our thoughts and actions like the sweet scent of old photographs. As we look back, we see the silhouettes of our former selves, like fading polaroids on a dusty shelf, reminders of the journeys we've undertaken and the dreams we've chased. And yet, even as we hold dear these memories of who we used to be, we're drawn to the horizon, where the promise of new experiences and untold stories beckons, inviting us to continue shaping, refining, and rediscovering our identity, a lifelong process of growth, exploration, and becoming. In this ever-unfolding narrative, we're both the authors and the characters, writing our own story, one chapter at a time.

Text: Theoretical models of supergravity have long been a subject of intense study, with significant implications for our understanding of the universe at the quantum gravity scale. Recent advances in the field have led to a renewed interest in non-geometric fluxes as potential s for supergravity theories. These exotic objects have been shown to possess unique properties that could potentially resolve long-standing issues in string theory, including the problem of moduli stabilization. In this work, we investigate the role of non-geometric fluxes in supergravity theories by employing a combination of mathematical and computational techniques. We utilize the framework of F-theory, which provides a powerful tool for studying the properties of fluxes in string theory. Our analysis focuses on the computation of the supergravity action, which is critical for understanding the dynamics of these theories. Our demonstrate that non-geometric fluxes can indeed serve as viable s for supergravity theories. We find that these fluxes can stabilize the moduli of the theory, leading to a consistent and predictive framework for string theory. Furthermore, our analysis reveals that non-geometric fluxes can also give rise to novel features, such as non-trivial topological invariants and non-geometric D-branes. These have significant implications for our understanding of the universe at the quantum gravity scale and highlight the importance of non-geometric fluxes in supergravity theories.

Text: The investigation of 4-quark components in light non-singlet scalar mesons is a crucial aspect of understanding the intricacies of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD). Utilizing QCD sum rules, we have examined the mixings of 4-quark components in these mesons, with a particular emphasis on the a0(980) and κ(800) states. Our analysis reveals that the 4-quark contributions to the scalar meson wave functions are substantial, with the tetraquark component playing a significant role in the composition of these states. The QCD sum rules are derived from the operator product expansion, and the resulting spectral densities are used to determine the masses and decay constants of the scalar mesons. By incorporating the 4-quark components into the analysis, we are able to improve the accuracy of the calculated masses and decay constants, and our are found to be in good agreement with experimental data. The of this study provide valuable insights into the structure and properties of light non-singlet scalar mesons, and have important implications for our understanding of the strong interaction and the behavior of hadrons in QCD. The also highlight the need for further investigation into the role of 4-quark components in other hadronic systems.

Text: The relativistic turducken phenomenon represents a paradigmatic exemplar of non-traditional, self-sustaining systems that defy conventional notions of excision and spatial boundary definition. Arising from the synergistic intersection of relativistic fusion principles and avian matter, this novel configuration involves the sequential, nested incorporation of avian species around a compact core of mass-energy, thereby creating a multi-layered, relativistic construct. Through rigorous application of numerical simulations and analytical models, we have elucidated the underlying dynamical processes governing the emergence and evolution of relativistic turduckens. Specifically, it has been discovered that the nested avian layers exhibit a singular form of spatially-resolved, relativistic confinement, wherein the core's relativistic energy density is effectively shielded from the surrounding environment. This phenomenon is predicated upon the coherent, non-linear interaction between the avian layers and the relativistic core, yielding a novel form of quantum entanglement-mediated stability that underwrites the overall system's integrity. Our investigation highlights the profound implications of the relativistic turducken phenomenon for the study of relativistic matter and energy, quantum confinement, and the emergence of complex, self-sustaining systems in extreme environments. By elucidating the intricate relationships between matter, energy, and space-time in the context of relativistic, multi-scale systems, this phenomenon presents a fertile area for continued research, inviting further exploration of the frontiers between relativistic, avian confinement, and quantum fluctuations.

Text: In this work, we investigate the role of nilpotent symmetry invariance in the superfield formulation of non-Abelian 1-form gauge theories. By employing a superfield formalism, we derive the nilpotent symmetry transformations that preserve the supersymmetric structure of these theories. Our analysis uncovers that the nilpotent symmetry invariance is closely tied to the gauge invariance of the theory, and we demonstrate that the two symmetries are intimately connected through the superfield formulation. We reveal that the nilpotent symmetry invariance imposes constraints on the form of the gauge field strength superfield and the supersymmetric covariant derivative, leading to a more stringent set of consistency conditions for the theory. We also investigate the implications of nilpotent symmetry invariance for the supersymmetric non-Abelian 1-form gauge theories, including the possibility of nilpotent symmetry breaking and its relation to the gauge hierarchy problem. Our results provide new insights into the supersymmetric formulation of non-Abelian 1-form gauge theories and have implications for the development of supersymmetric extensions of the standard model.

Text: This paper investigates the Leray numbers of projections in relation to a topological Helly type theorem, providing new insights into the topological properties of projections and their interconnections with Helly type theorems. We first establish a connection between the Leray numbers of a space and the Leray numbers of its projection, generalizing a known result for the case of dimension one. Our approach involves the use of a combination of techniques from algebraic topology, particularly the study of the cohomology of covers and the properties of the associated Alexander-Spanier cochain complex. We then utilize these to derive a topological Helly type theorem, which provides a characterization of the existence of a point in common to a family of sets in terms of the Leray numbers of their projections. This theorem has significant implications for the study of Helly type theorems and their connections to algebraic topology, and opens up new avenues for research in the field. Our also shed new light on the role of Leray numbers in the study of algebraic topology and their applications to geometric problems.

Text: Here, we focus on the development and assessment of dynamical Yang-Baxter maps that satisfy a specified invariance condition, thereby generalizing the traditional Yang-Baxter equation. A key aspect of our research lies in the identification of a broad class of dynamical Yang-Baxter maps that exhibit this invariance property, which is rooted in the presence of a Hopf algebraic structure. By leveraging the Hopf algebraic framework, we derive an explicit expression for the invariance condition in terms of the dynamical Yang-Baxter map and its associated Hopf algebra. Our analysis reveals that the invariance condition imposes a specific constraint on the dynamical Yang-Baxter map, enabling the derivation of a set of conserved quantities that provide a novel means of characterizing the behavior of these maps. Furthermore, our results establish that the invariance condition plays a crucial role in the classification of dynamical Yang-Baxter maps and their associated algebraic structures, thereby offering new insights into the underlying dynamics of these systems. The results of this research have significant implications for the analysis of integrable systems and their applications in physics and mathematics.

Text: In this investigation, we present a comprehensive analysis of charged particle production in high Q^2 deep-inelastic scattering (DIS) at the electron-proton collider HERA, with a focus on the underlying dynamics of the scattering process. Utilizing a dataset of 470,000 inclusive DIS events at √s = 318 GeV, we have extracted a comprehensive set of differential distributions for charged pions, kaons, and protons, as well as their combinations. Our reveal striking features in the azimuthal and pseudorapidity distributions of these particles, indicative of the complex interplay between partonic scattering and hadronization processes. Notably, we observe an enhancement of particle production in the forward region, which we attribute to the presence of gluon radiation and fragmentation processes. Furthermore, our analysis of the transverse momentum and rapidity dependence of charged particle yields provides valuable insights into the role of initial-state gluon recombination and final-state hadronization mechanisms. Our have important implications for understanding the structure of the proton and the dynamics of hadronic interactions, shedding new light on the underlying physics of high-energy DIS at HERA.

We adopt a systematic approach to renormalize the TPE potential, which involves the consistent treatment of the nucleon's mass and wave function corrections, as well as the inclusion of the pion mass corrections. Moreover, notably, our findings indicate that the renormalized TPE potential yields a significant improvement in the description of NN scattering data, particularly for the partial waves with higher orbital angular momenta, while we also observe that the renormalization of the TPE potential leads to a more accurate reproduction of the NN phase shifts and the deuteron binding energy. Our results demonstrate that the relativistic chiral TPE strategy provides a robust and reliable approach for the study of NN interactions, and can be used as a valuable tool for investigating the properties of nuclear systems.
