We adopt a microlocal analysis of the Kostant-Souriau prequantum line bundle over a compact Kähler manifold acted upon by a compact Lie group with possibly singular moment map level sets. By constructing a family of equivariant Toeplitz operators adapted to each stratum and employing the theory of symplectic implosion, we derive explicit asymptotic expansions for the Bergman kernels on both the unreduced and reduced spaces. The analysis is supplemented by a deformation-quantization framework that tracks the behavior of the star-product across singular loci. The study establishes a precise "singular unitarity" theorem: for each admissible weight, the natural map from the invariant subspace of the unreduced Hilbert space to the reduced Hilbert space extends to a unitary isomorphism after renormalization by a stratum-dependent density factor. Crucially, moreover, the failure of naïve unitarity is quantified by explicit correction terms localized on the singular strata, thereby resolving the longstanding ambiguity in QCR for singular symplectic quotients.

Text: The depletion of cold, star‑forming gas regulates galaxy evolution and dictates the transition from active star formation to quiescence. Cold‑gas proxies were derived using a calibrated combination of nebular emission‑line diagnostics (H α, [O II]), the Balmer decrement, and the Dₙ4000 index to estimate instantaneous gas‑to‑stellar mass ratios (μ₍gas₎). Environmental density was quantified via the projected 5th‑nearest‑neighbor metric, while stellar feedback strength was inferred from central velocity dispersion and AGN line ratios. Bayesian hierarchical models were employed to disentangle the relative contributions of external stripping versus internal consumption, incorporating measurement uncertainties and selection effects. The analysis reveals that ≈45 % of the observed μ₍gas₎ decline from the star‑forming main sequence to the green valley can be attributed to environment‑driven stripping in halos >10¹³ M⊙, whereas internal feedback accounts for ≈30 % of the depletion in isolated systems. A residual ≈25 % of gas loss appears consistent with secular consumption. These underscore the synergistic role of both external and internal mechanisms in governing the loss of star‑forming gas in SDSS galaxies.

Text: The Circular Economy represents an economic model that aims to systematically eliminate waste generation and pollution, maintain products and materials in productive use for extended periods, and regenerate natural systems, in deliberate contrast to the conventional linear economic model predicated on resource extraction, product manufacture, and disposal. Text: This study studies the meeting problem in the context of the quantum random walk, a quantum mechanical analogue of the classical random walk. Our results show that the quantum random walk exhibits a non-trivial meeting probability, which is influenced by the quantum coherence and entanglement between the particles. Text: The convergence of nanostructured architectures with magnetic semiconductor materials offers a versatile platform for advancing spin-electronics (spin-tronics). Structural and magnetic characterizations were performed with high-resolution transmission electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction, and SQUID magnetometry. Spin-dependent transport was probed via temperature-dependent Hall effect, non-local spin valve measurements, and ferromagnetic resonance spectroscopy. Complementary density-functional theory calculations incorporating Hubbard-U corrections elucidated the role of carrier-mediated exchange and defect states. Nanostructuring enhanced Curie temperatures by up to 30 K relative to bulk counterparts, attributed to strain-induced band-edge shifts and increased Mn/Co clustering control. Quantum confinement yielded a pronounced anisotropic magnetoresistance (up to 12 %) and spin diffusion lengths exceeding 200 nm at 10 K. Theoretical corroborated experimental trends, revealing that interface-engineered spin-orbit fields dominate spin relaxation. These insights establish design rules for integrating magnetic semiconductors into scalable spin-electronic architectures.

Text: We investigate the behavior of cold nuclear matter in the context of holographic QCD, a theoretical framework that seeks to describe the strong interactions using the principles of string theory. Text: The concept of a median, a robust central tendency measure in one dimension, does not extend uniquely to multivariate settings, where multiple notions (e.g., spatial, Tukey, and Oja medians) coexist. A persistent difficulty is the lack of a unifying geometric framework that captures both statistical robustness and measure-theoretic symmetry. Recent advances in measure-symmetrization-transformations that replace a probability measure by a centrally symmetric counterpart while preserving marginal distributions-suggest a promising avenue for reconciling these issues. We develop a rigorous analytical framework that links multivariate medians to the symmetrization of underlying probability measures. Using tools from convex geometry, optimal transport, and geometric measure theory, we (i) define a class of *symmetrically induced medians* via minimization of integrated gauge functions over symmetrized measures, (ii) prove existence and uniqueness under mild regularity conditions, and (iii) implement a stochastic approximation algorithm to compute these medians in high dimensions, validating convergence through empirical process theory. The proposed medians coincide with classical spatial medians for centrally symmetric distributions and interpolate between Tukey and Oja medians for asymmetric cases. Measure-symmetrization is shown to reduce median variability by a factor proportional to the degree of asymmetry, yielding enhanced robustness. Numerical experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate superior breakdown points and lower estimation bias compared with existing multivariate median estimators. These establish measure-symmetrization as a unifying principle for robust central location in multivariate analysis.

In the small‑sphere limit the leading term reproduces the matter energy density \(\frac{4\pi r^{3}}{3}T_{ab}u^{a}u^{b}\) and the next‑order correction encodes the Bel‑Robinson tensor, confirming agreement with the local energy‑momentum content. Conventional approaches to balanced truncation for LTP systems rely on the resolution of operator-valued Lyapunov equations to synthesize time-varying controllability and observability gramians, a process that becomes computationally infeasible for systems with high-dimensional state spaces. The proposed circumvents this limitation by harnessing temporally sampled data—specifically, input-output responses captured at discrete intervals across a single period—to numerically approximate these gramians. Through projection of the collected snapshots into a reduced subspace and subsequent resolution of a sequence of compact, time-varying Lyapunov-inspired equations, the method generates balanced realizations wherein states are hierarchically ranked by their contribution to system dynamics, enabling the selective elimination of less influential components. The framework ensures the preservation of asymptotic stability in the reduced-order model and formulates a priori error bounds contingent on the singular values of the balanced gramians, thereby providing quantifiable guarantees on the fidelity of the approximation. Empirical evaluations conducted on canonical LTP systems—such as a mechanically oscillating system subjected to periodic forcing and an electrical network with temporally modulated components—demonstrate significant computational efficiency compared to established techniques without compromising accuracy. The snapshot-driven approach is particularly efficacious for systems exhibiting rapidly evolving dynamics or expansive state representations, where direct gramian computation is impractical. This research establishes a conceptual bridge between data-centric model reduction paradigms and classical Lyapunov-based methodologies, offering a robust analytical tool for the analysis and control of complex time-periodic systems in domains including power grid networks, aerospace engineering, and vibrational isolation technologies.

Text: We find new decoupling limits of N=4 super Yang-Mills (SYM) on R x S3 with gauge group SU(N). These decoupling limits lead to decoupled theories that are much simpler than the full N=4 SYM but still contain many of its interesting features. The decoupling limits correspond to being in a near-critical region, near a point with zero temperature and critical chemical potentials. The new decoupling limits are found by generalizing the limits of hep-th/0605234 to include not only the chemical potentials for the SU(4) R-symmetry of N=4 SYM but also the chemical potentials corresponding to the SO(4) symmetry. In the decoupled theories it is possible to take a strong coupling limit in a controllable manner since the full effective Hamiltonian is known. For planar N=4 SYM on R x S3 all the decoupled theories correspond to fully integrable spin chains. We study the thermodynamics of the decoupled theories and find the Hagedorn temperature for small and large values of the effective coupling. We find an alternative formulation of the decoupling limits in the microcanonical ensemble. This leads to a characterization of certain regimes of weakly coupled N=4 SYM in which there are string-like states. Finally, we find a similar decoupling limit for pure Yang-Mills theory, which for the planar limit leads to a fully integrable decoupled theory.

Text: Circle configurations are central in Euclidean geometry, with classic such as the nine‑point circle, Apollonian packings, and the radical‑axis theorem. Recent interest in combinatorial geometry has highlighted the need for unified criteria governing incidence and tangency relations among multiple circles. We employ inversion geometry combined with algebraic elimination techniques to derive invariant relations for a set of *n* circles in general position. By mapping arbitrary configurations to a canonical model via Möbius transformations, we reduce the problem to solving a system of quadratic equations in the complex plane. Computational algebra systems verify the consistency of the derived constraints for *n* ≤ 6, and an inductive argument extends the result to arbitrary *n*. We prove that for any collection of *n* ≥ 3 circles whose pairwise radical axes are concurrent, the centers satisfy a single linear relation that can be expressed as a weighted sum of curvature‑centers equal to zero. This theorem generalizes the classical radical‑axis concurrency condition and yields immediate corollaries concerning Apollonian circle packings and Descartes’ circle theorem. Potential applications include circle‑packing algorithms and geometric design.

Text: The relaxation of a dewetting contact line is investigated theoretically in the so-called "Landau-Levich" geometry in which a vertical solid plate is withdrawn from a bath of partially wetting liquid. Text: A transcendental entire function f is called geometrically finite if the intersection of the set of singular values with the Fatou set is compact and the intersection of the postsingular set with the Julia set is finite. (In particular, this includes all entire functions with finite postsingular set.) If f is geometrically finite, then the Fatou set of f is either empty or consists of the basins of attraction of finitely many attracting or parabolic cycles. Let z_0 be a repelling or parabolic periodic point of such a map f. We show that, if f has finite order, then there exists an injective curve consisting of escaping points of f that connects z_0 to infinity. (This curve is called a dynamic ray.) In fact, the assumption of finite order can be weakened considerably; for example, it is sufficient to assume that f can be written as a finite composition of finite-order functions.

The resulting system of ordinary differential equations is cast into a compact, dimensionless dynamical-systems framework. Phase-space analysis, fixed-point classification, and numerical integrations are employed to explore the full solution space for a range of shear moduli and equation-of-state parameters. .** The elastic contribution generates new equilibrium points absent in perfect-fluid models, including a family of non-singular anisotropic attractors that persist for all finite times. Surface‑brightness profiles were deprojected to obtain radial temperature, density, and metallicity distributions, from which we derived entropy, pressure, and cooling‑time maps using a forward‑fitting Bayesian model that accounts for instrumental point‑spread functions and background uncertainties. The measured orbit lengths agree with theoretical predictions within 2 %, and the relative intensities follow the expected Fresnel leakage rates. The resulting coupled system is expressed in a single matrix-valued operator acting on the direct-product space ψ⊗φ. A Foldy-Wouthuysen transformation isolates the positive-energy sector, yielding an effective relativistic wave equation that includes spin-orbit, Darwin, and scalar-exchange terms up to order (1/c{2}). Numerical solutions are obtained for Coulomb-type and linear confinement potentials via a variational basis of correlated Gaussian functions. The derived equation is explicitly Lorentz-covariant and reduces to the Dirac equation for a free spin-½ particle and to the Klein-Gordon equation for a free spin-0 particle in the appropriate limits. For bound-state calculations, the spectrum reproduces known hydrogen-like levels with spin-dependent splittings and predicts novel fine-structure patterns for mixed-spin systems. Comparison with existing Bethe-Salpeter shows agreement within 2 % for low-lying states, confirming the accuracy of the reduction scheme and providing a practical tool for relativistic few-body analyses.

We set 95 % CL lower limits on the fundamental Planck scale of 5.2 TeV for a two-dimensional extra-dimensional scenario and 4.7 TeV for a six-dimensional case, excluding black-hole masses below 7.5 TeV. Furthermore, our framework is poised to revolutionize the understanding of laboratory plasmas for magnetic confinement and plasma-wall interactions, as well as ionized and partially ionized plasma turbulence. Ultimately, the proposed theoretical framework is a crucial step towards elucidating the dynamics of partially ionized plasmas, thereby paving the way for the development of more accurate models and simulations that are essential for advancing our knowledge of complex plasma behavior in the astrophysical and laboratory communities. Text: In type IIB/F-theory compactifications, Euclidean D-instantons generate crucial non-perturbative contributions to the four-dimensional effective superpotential. However, the presence of unlifted fermionic zero modes beyond the universal (theta{alpha}) pair typically obstructs such contributions. Recent studies suggest that instanton recombination and fluxes can modify the zero-mode spectrum, yet a systematic analysis of these mechanisms in realistic Calabi-Yau orientifolds is lacking. We employ a combined world-sheet and supergravity approach to analyse Euclidean D(p)-instantons on orientifolded Calabi-Yau threefolds with O3/O7 planes. The instanton zero-mode content is derived from the Dirac index on the wrapped cycle, incorporating the effects of world-volume gauge fluxes and bulk three-form flux (G_{3}). We then study multi-instanton configurations that undergo recombination via tachyon condensation, using the formalism of derived categories to track the resulting bound-state spectrum. The lifted modes are identified through flux-induced mass terms in the instanton effective action, obtained from the dimensional reduction of the DBI and Chern-Simons actions. We demonstrate that (i) recombination of two rigid O(1) instantons eliminates the extra (overline{tau}_{dotalpha}) modes by forming a single O(1) bound state, and (ii) supersymmetric ISD (G_{3}) flux generates bilinear couplings that give a universal mass to the remaining non-universal fermionic modes. Consequently, a broad class of instantons previously thought inert can contribute to the superpotential, provided the combined criteria of cycle rigidity, appropriate flux quanta, and compatible recombination channels are satisfied. Text: Charity and philanthropy, in their highest expressions, are not primarily about tax deductions or reputation management - they are expressions of a fundamental ethical commitment to the wellbeing of others and to the reduction of avoidable suffering in the world. The impulse to give is deeply rooted in human nature and affirmed by every major religious and ethical tradition: from the Islamic concept of Zakat to the Christian call to love your neighbor, from the Buddhist emphasis on compassion to the secular utilitarian argument for effective giving. Yet not all giving is equally effective, and one of the most important developments in contemporary philanthropy is the evidence-based movement that seeks to maximize the impact of charitable resources by rigorously evaluating which interventions actually work. Beyond the question of effectiveness lies the deeper question of justice: whether charity alone is an adequate response to systemic inequalities, or whether genuine philanthropy must also engage with the structures that produce need in the first place.

Text: For years, the idea that video games have become a legitimate art form has been discussed, yet its legitimacy remains a topic of contention. Those in favor of this notion point to games such as "The Last of Us" and "Red Dead Redemption 2", which they argue exhibit a richness of narrative and emotional impact comparable to that of literature and cinema. Nevertheless, the question remains as to whether these games can be regarded as art in the same way as the masterpieces of Picasso or Shakespeare. The response to this question is nuanced, much like the art form itself. The fact that video games are interactive allows players to connect with the story on a deeply personal level, which, when combined with the advanced graphics and sound design found in modern games, can result in a profoundly immersive experience. Nevertheless, when evaluating art, considerations extend beyond mere aesthetics and technical skill to encompass factors such as craftsmanship, innovation, and the willingness to confront and defy societal conventions. It is uncertain whether a game, whose primary function is entertainment, can be said to possess the same level of artistic value as a novel that explores complex themes and issues. Text: We present a study of the shapes, orientations, and alignments of Galactic dark matter subhalos in the ``Via Lactea'' simulation of a Milky Way-size LCDM host halo. Whereas isolated dark matter halos tend to be prolate, subhalos are predominantly triaxial. Overall subhalos are more spherical than the host halo, with minor to major and intermediate to major axis ratios of 0.68 and 0.83, respectively. Like isolated halos, subhalos tend to be less spherical in their central regions. The principal axis ratios are independent of subhalo mass, when the shapes are measured within a physical scale like r_Vmax, the radius of the peak of the circular velocity curve. Subhalos tend to be slightly more spherical closer to the host halo center. The spatial distribution of the subhalos traces the prolate shape of the host halo when they are selected by the largest V_max they ever had, i.e. before they experienced strong tidal mass loss. The subhalos' orientation is not random: the major axis tends to align with the direction towards the host halo center. This alignment disappears for halos beyond 3 r_200 and is more pronounced when the shapes are measured in the outer regions of the subhalos. The radial alignment is preserved during a subhalo's orbit and they become elongated during pericenter passage, indicating that the alignment is likely caused by the host halo's tidal forces. These tidal interactions with the host halo act to make subhalos rounder over time.

Text: We obtained H-band polarimetric data of IRAS 19312+1950 using the near-infrared camera (CIAO) on the 8 m Subaru telescope. The total intensity image shows a nearly spherical core with ~3" radius, an S-shaped arm extending ~10" in the northwest to southeast direction, and an extended lobe towards the southwest. The polarization map shows a centro-symmetric vector alignment in almost the entire nebula and low polarizations along the S-shaped arm. These suggest that the nebula is accompanied by a central star, and the S-shaped arm has a physically ring-like structure. From our radiative transfer modeling, we estimated the stellar temperature, the bolometric luminosity, and the current mass-loss rate to be 2800 K, 7000 L_sun, and 5.3x10^{-6} M_sun yr^{-1}, respectively. Taking into account previous observational , such as the detection of SiO maser emissions and silicate absorption feature in the 10 $\mu$m spectrum, our dust radiative transfer analysis based on our NIR imaging polarimetry suggests that (1) the central star of IRAS 19312+1950 is likely to be an oxygen-rich, dust-enshrouded AGB star and (2) most of the circumstellar material originates from other sources (e.g. ambient dark clouds) rather than as a result of mass loss from the central star.

Text: We consider a wireless sensors network scenario where two nodes detect correlated sources and deliver them to a central collector via a wireless link. Original data are instead independently encoded by means of low-complexity convolutional codes. The decoder performs joint decoding with the aim of exploiting the inherent correlation between the transmitted sources. Complexity at the decoder is kept low thanks to the use of an iterative joint decoding scheme, where the output of each decoder is fed to the other decoder's input as a-priori information. For such scheme, we derive a novel analytical framework for evaluating an upper bound of joint-detection packet error probability and for deriving the optimum coding scheme. Experimental confirm the validity of the analytical framework, and show that recursive codes allow a noticeable performance gain with respect to non-recursive coding schemes. The model incorporates (i) a thickness‑dependent depolarization field obtained from a self‑consistent Poisson–Schrödinger solver, (ii) elastic boundary conditions reflecting substrate clamping, and (iii) a phenomenological dead‑layer term calibrated against first‑principles calculations. Numerical simulations are performed for perovskite oxides (e.g., PbTiO₃, BaTiO₃) over thicknesses ranging from 0.5 nm to 50 nm, and the are validated against experimental hysteresis loops and piezoresponse force microscopy data. The model reproduces the experimentally observed critical thickness (~1.2 nm for PbTiO₃) and predicts a non‑monotonic scaling of coercive field with film thickness, arising from the competition between depolarization and elastic energy. Dielectric permittivity shows a pronounced enhancement near the critical thickness, consistent with a soft‑mode behavior. The framework provides quantitative guidance for engineering ferroelectric thin films with tailored functional responses across the nanoscale.

Building the full type hierarchy upon this interpretation of the base type gives a finite semantics for simply-typed lambda-trees. A calculus based on this semantics is proven sound and complete. In particular, for regular infinite lambda-trees it is decidable whether a given automaton has a run or not. As regular lambda-trees are precisely recursion schemes, this decidability result holds for arbitrary recursion schemes of arbitrary level, without any syntactical restriction.

Text: The Internet of Things, commonly abbreviated as IoT, refers to the expansive network of physical devices, vehicles, appliances, and other physical objects embedded with sensors, software applications, and connectivity capabilities that enable them to collect and exchange data over the internet. Ranging from smart home devices such as thermostats and security cameras to industrial sensors monitoring manufacturing equipment performance, IoT technology is creating a seamlessly interconnected digital environment. The proliferation of IoT-connected devices is generating unprecedented volumes of real-time operational data, which organizations can analyze to optimize processes, enhance user experiences, and develop innovative business models. However, the rapid expansion of IoT ecosystems also introduces substantial security vulnerabilities, as many devices lack robust built-in protective mechanisms. Standards development initiatives, edge computing architectures, and 5G connectivity infrastructure are recognized as key enabling factors driving the next wave of IoT innovation across agriculture, healthcare, transportation, and smart city domains.

Text: The progression of subcritical crack propagation in amorphous polymeric matrices is regulated by a multifaceted interplay among viscoelastic strain relaxation, incremental microstructural degradation, and thermally induced covalent bond scission. This investigation systematically examines the temporal evolution of tensile fracture mechanics in 200-micrometer-thick polycarbonate substrates subjected to sustained uniaxial loading conditions within a humidified environmental chamber. Utilizing a precision laser interferometric , the crack-length temporal dynamics are quantitatively documented across six orders of magnitude in crack velocity (10⁻¹⁰–10⁻⁴ m·s⁻¹), enabling the empirical derivation of a kinetic model. The observed crack velocity as a function of applied stress intensity factor (K) adheres to an Arrhenius-inspired formulation: v = v₀ exp[(K – K_c)/K₀], wherein the prefactor (v₀), critical threshold (K_c), and characteristic scaling parameter (K₀) are statistically optimized via nonlinear regression. This governing equation effectively captures the transition from a near-static to an accelerated propagation phase, with predictive accuracy for failure time estimation exhibiting a mean absolute deviation of less than 5%. Notably, the model incorporates environmental dependencies via its activation energy parameter, thereby establishing a universal scaling law that encapsulates the influence of thermal and hygral variables on viscoelastic crack evolution in polycarbonate. These furnish a robust theoretical framework for probabilistically assessing the long-term structural integrity of polymer-based components and inform the rational engineering of materials exhibiting enhanced damage tolerance.

Text: Our investigation into the anomalous X-ray pulsar 4U 0142+614 has been conducted through an extensive series of very deep X-ray observations by means of the Chandra X-ray Observatory. These observations, spanning a total exposure time of 1.2 million seconds, have provided unprecedented insight into the properties and behavior of this enigmatic object — our examination reveals a complex X-ray spectrum, which is well-described by a two-component model comprising a soft thermal component and a hard non-thermal component. The thermal component is consistent with emission from a neutron star cooling in a binary system, while the non-thermal component is indicative of magnetospheric emission from the neutron star's magnetic field. We also detect significant variability in the pulsar's X-ray flux, with a maximum observed variability amplitude of 25%. Our outcomes indicate that 4U 0142+614 is in a late stage of its evolution, with a spin-down torque that is significantly enhanced due to the interaction between its magnetic field and the surrounding interstellar medium. These findings provide new constraints on theoretical models of neutron star evolution and the physics of magnetospheric emission. At the same time, further evaluation of our data is ongoing, with the potential to shed new light on the properties and behavior of this fascinating object.

Text: This study investigates the integration of strings into the Yang-Mills-Higgs theory when coupled to gravity, an essential step towards a more comprehensive and unified description of fundamental forces in the universe. By incorporating the Nambu-Goto action into the Einstein-Hilbert action and coupling it with the Yang-Mills-Higgs action, we develop a novel framework that enables the quantization of both gravitational and gauge fields within a single theoretical framework. We demonstrate that the resulting theory yields a consistent and well-defined Lagrangian, which incorporates the key features of both string theory and general relativity. Our analysis reveals that the gravitational field exhibits a significant effect on the gauge boson dynamics, leading to the emergence of novel mass generations and the possibility of spontaneous symmetry breaking. Furthermore, we identify a class of string-like solutions that describe topological defects in the gravitational field, providing a new perspective on the interplay between gravity and gauge theory. The of this work have implications for our understanding of the fundamental forces and the structure of space-time, and pave the way for further investigations into the interplay between strings, gravity, and gauge fields.

Text: This article outlines a comprehensive framework for resolving the complexities associated with computing knot Floer homology, a topological invariant that encodes essential information about a knot's structure — building on the pioneering work of Ozsváth and Szabó, we establish a cubic hierarchy of resolutions, each corresponding to a distinct computational approach tailored to specific knot families. The first resolution, dubbed 'grid resolution', leverages the lattice structure underlying knot Floer homology to efficiently compute the invariant for torus knots. By contrast, the second resolution, 'chain resolution', employs a combinatorial approach to tackle a broader class of knots, including those with multiple crossings. In particular, the third resolution, 'triangulation resolution', combines insights from geometric and algebraic topology to provide a unified framework for computing knot Floer homology across a wide range of knot families. Our results demonstrate that each resolution offers a unique advantage in resolving computational bottlenecks, and that the cubic hierarchy offers a versatile toolkit for tackling the complexities of knot Floer homology — by consolidating these advances, we provide a robust and adaptable framework for computing this essential topological invariant.

Text: The study of nonequilibrium fluctuations in small systems has garnered significant attention in recent years, bridging the realms of physics and biology. In these systems, the inherent stochasticity induced by thermal fluctuations plays a crucial role in determining the dynamics and behavior, often leading to novel and counterintuitive phenomena. Our research delves into the theoretical and experimental aspects of nonequilibrium fluctuations, with a particular emphasis on their implications in biological systems. By employing a combination of analytical and numerical techniques, we investigate the statistical properties of fluctuations in systems far from equilibrium, including the breakdown of detailed balance and the emergence of non-Boltzmann distributions. Furthermore, we explore the relevance of these concepts to biological processes, such as molecular motors, protein folding, and cellular transport, where nonequilibrium fluctuations can significantly influence the functioning and efficiency of these systems. Our provide new insights into the complex interplay between stochasticity, nonequilibrium dynamics, and biological function, ultimately contributing to a deeper understanding of the intricate mechanisms governing the behavior of small systems in physics and biology. This knowledge can be leveraged to develop novel therapeutic strategies and biomimetic technologies that harness the unique properties of nonequilibrium fluctuations.

Text: Using recent CLEO III for the cross section for $e^+e^- \to {\rm hadrons}$ at seven centre-of-mass energies between 6.964 and 10.538 GeV, we derive a value for the strong coupling constant $\alpha_s(M_Z^2)=0.110_{-0.012}^{-0.010}{}_{-0.011}^{+0.010}$ where the uncertainties are uncorrelated and correlated, respectively. Our result differs significantly from the one derived by CLEO III, as a consequence of inclusion of quark mass effects and the proper matching between the effective theories with four and five flavours. Combining this new result with an analysis based on earlier cross section measurements in the energy region between 2 and 10.6 GeV, we obtain $\alpha_s(M_Z^2)=0.119^{+0.009}_{-0.011}$, well consistent with the current world average.

Text: The humble act of kindness - it's a stone cast into a still pond, sending ripples outward in unexpected ways. I recall a friend who, on a whim, bought coffee for the stranger behind her in the drive-thru line, simply because she could. The barista, charmed by this small gesture, decided to pay it forward and offered a free pastry to the next customer, who happened to be a harried young mother. As she bit into the warm croissant, her eyes lit up, and she felt a surge of gratitude that stayed with her throughout the day, influencing her interactions with her children, her coworkers, and even the gruff store clerk who helped her with a return. This is how kindness can spread, a gentle contagion that seeps into the crevices of our daily lives, often unnoticed but always felt. And it's not just the grand, showy acts that have this power - a held door, a sympathetic ear, a genuine compliment - these small, everyday kindnesses can be the catalyst for a chain reaction of good deeds and warm feelings that resonates far beyond the initial gesture. As my friend discovered, the ripple effect of kindness can be astonishing, a testament to the human capacity for empathy and connection, and a reminder that even the tiniest drop of goodwill can create a wave of compassion that washes over us all.

Text: Chandra ACIS-S observations of the galaxy cluster A3112 feature the presence of an excess of X-ray emission above the contribution from the diffuse hot gas, which can be equally well modeled with an additional non-thermal power-law model or with a low-temperature thermal model of low metal abundance. We show that the excess emission cannot be due to uncertainties in the subtraction or in the Galactic HI column density. Calibration uncertainties in the ACIS detector that may affect our are addressed by comparing the Chandra data to XMM MOS and PN spectra. While differences between the three instruments remain, all detect the excess in similar amounts, providing evidence against an instrumental nature of the excess. Given the presence of non-thermal radio emission near the center of A3112, we argue that the excess X-ray emission is of non-thermal nature and distributed throughout the entire X-ray bandpass, from soft to hard X-rays. The excess can be explained with the presence of a population of relativistic electrons with ~7% of the cluster's gas pressure. We also discuss a possible thermal nature of the excess, and examine the problems associated with such interpretation.

Text: The existence of sterile neutrinos, hypothetical particles that do not interact with normal matter via any fundamental force, has been a topic of interest in recent years due to their potential to resolve certain anomalies in short-baseline neutrino experiments. However, the presence of sterile neutrinos can also significantly impact various astrophysical phenomena, such as the formation and evolution of stars, the properties of supernovae, and the large-scale structure of the universe. In this study, we use a combination of astrophysical observations, including the cosmic microwave radiation, big bang nucleosynthesis, and the X-ray emission from galaxy clusters, to constrain the parameters of sterile neutrinos. Our analysis reveals that the mixing angle between active and sterile neutrinos is restricted to be less than 0.1, and the mass of the sterile neutrino is required to be greater than 1 eV, in order to be consistent with the observed astrophysical data. These restrictions provide valuable insights into the properties of sterile neutrinos and have important implications for our understanding of the neutrino sector and the evolution of the universe. The of this study can be used to inform future experimental searches for sterile neutrinos.

Text: This paper continues the investigation into the relationship between relative log convergent cohomology and relative rigid cohomology initiated in the first installment of this series. We establish a key result by demonstrating that the relative log convergent cohomology of a proper rigid analytic space (X, D) with respect to a divisor D can be canonically identified with the relative rigid cohomology of the pair (X, D). This identification enables us to derive a comparison theorem between these two cohomology theories, revealing that the relative log convergent cohomology is a deformation retract of the relative rigid cohomology. In particular, this result yields a new perspective on the relationship between these cohomology theories, with marked implications for the analysis of algebraic cycles and arithmetic geometry. Furthermore, we provide explicit examples to illustrate the application of our result to various geometric and arithmetic contexts, including the work of compactifications of algebraic varieties and the arithmetic geometry of curves over local fields.

Text: We outline a novel analysis of open charm meson production in deep-inelastic scattering (DIS) events at the COMPASS experiment, focusing on the determination of the delta G/G ratio from the charm quark fragmentation function. Our study utilizes a dataset of 2.5 million events, collected at a beam energy of 190 GeV and a scattering angle of 2.5 mrad, with the muon beam scattering off a liquid hydrogen target, and drawing on a custom-built algorithm to identify charm mesons, we reconstruct the invariant mass of D+ and D0 mesons, as well as their decay modes into various final states. By fitting the transverse momentum distributions of these mesons to a Monte Carlo simulation, we determine the charm quark fragmentation function and subsequently extract the delta G/G ratio. At the same time, notably, our results, obtained from a systematic fit to the data, yield a delta G/G ratio of 0.38 +/- 0.03 +/- 0.08, consistent with the predictions of the next-to-leading order (NLO) perturbative QCD calculations — this measurement provides valuable insights into the gluon distribution function of the nucleon and has implications for the grasp of of high-energy hadronic interactions.

Text: In this study we scrutinize the two-loop contributions to the pion mass within the SU(2) chiral perturbation theory framework, employing dimensional regularization in conjunction with the Gasser–Leutwyler effective Lagrangian expanded up to order \(p^{6}\); by systematically developing the effective action and meticulously evaluating the pertinent sunset and bubble topologies, we obtain closed analytic expressions for the mass shift \(\delta m_{\pi}^{2}\) that are explicitly expressed in terms of the leading-order parameters \(f_{\pi}\) and \(m_{\pi}\), the next-to-leading-order low‑energy constants \(L_{i}\), and the sixth‑order couplings \(C_{i}\), while the renormalization is carried out consistently at the two‑loop level, thereby ensuring the complete cancellation of ultraviolet divergences and the preservation of scale independence for physical observables; a subsequent numerical assessment, incorporating phenomenologically extracted values for the \(L_{i}\) and resonance‑saturation estimates for the \(C_{i}\), reveals a 1.5 % enhancement relative to the one‑loop result for \(m_{\pi}\) at the physical quark masses, and when juxtaposed with recent lattice QCD determinations of the pion mass dependence on the quark mass, the theoretical predictions exhibit excellent concordance within the quoted uncertainties, thereby furnishing a stringent benchmark for precision tests of chiral dynamics and furnishing refined inputs for the extrapolation of lattice data to the physical point.

Text: We investigate the local dynamics and gravitational collapse of a self-gravitating magnetized Fermi gas, a system relevant to the study of astrophysical objects such as neutron stars and white dwarfs. Utilizing a combination of numerical simulations and analytical calculations, we examine the interplay between magnetic fields, Fermi statistics, and gravitational collapse in a gas of fermions. Our approach involves solving the coupled equations of magnetohydrodynamics and the Poisson equation for the gravitational potential, taking into account the effects of magnetic field diffusion and fermionic interactions. We find that the presence of a strong magnetic field leads to an enhancement of the gas's gravitational collapse, accompanied by the formation of a central core and a magnetized halo. The Fermi statistics of the gas particles are found to play a crucial role in the collapse dynamics, leading to the emergence of a density singularity at the core. Our have implications for the formation and evolution of magnetized compact objects, highlighting the importance of considering the interplay between magnetic fields, gravity, and Fermi statistics in these systems. These shed new light on the complex dynamics governing the behavior of self-gravitating magnetized Fermi gases.

Text: This investigation examines the production of anticentauro events in ultra-relativistic heavy ion collisions, providing novel perspective into the dynamics of strongly interacting matter at the forefront of quantum chromodynamics. The anticentauro, a theoretical concept first suggested by the authors, refers to a hypothetical state of matter characterized by the absence of a color charge and the presence of a distinct parity inversion. Utilizing a Monte Carlo simulation structure, we have generated a thorough dataset of central Au-Au collisions at √sNN = 200 GeV, incorporating a range of hadronic and partonic interactions. Our outcomes demonstrate a statistically significant enhancement of anticentauro-like events in the energy range corresponding to the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) phase transition, suggesting a non-trivial interplay between color charge deconfinement and parity symmetry breaking. We also report a correlation analysis indicating that anticentauro formation is associated with anomalous multiplicity fluctuations and anisotropic flow patterns, underscoring the importance of examining the QGP phase space in pursuit of exotic states of matter. Our results have notable implications for the understanding of the strong interaction dynamics and the search for new physics beyond the Standard Model.

Text: We report a comprehensive experimental investigation into the phenomenon of back-action cancellation, a fundamental concept in the precision measurement of weak forces and interferometric sensing. Utilizing a sophisticated experimental setup that combines a high-finesse optical interferometer with a carefully calibrated measurement system, we demonstrate the ability to mitigate the deleterious effects of back-action noise on precision measurements. Our show that by carefully optimizing the interferometer's optical parameters and employing an adaptive feedback control scheme, we are able to effectively cancel the back-action noise, leading to a significant improvement in measurement sensitivity. Specifically, our data reveal a reduction in the measurement uncertainty by a factor of three, corresponding to an increase in precision by the same margin. These have far-reaching implications for the development of next-generation precision measurement instruments, including high-precision spectroscopy, gravitational wave detection, and force microscopy. Our work provides a valuable contribution to the ongoing effort to push the boundaries of precision measurement and shed light on the fundamental limits of sensing performance.

Text: Group testing is a sampling used to detect rare defective items in a large set. Traditional involve testing all possible combinations of items, resulting in exponential growth in the number of tests. Recent advances have focused on using random pools to reduce the number of tests, but optimal algorithms remain elusive. We propose a novel two-stage approach to group testing with random pools. In the first stage, we use a greedy algorithm to select the initial pool sizes and assign defective probabilities. In the second stage, we employ a dynamic programming approach to optimize the test sequence and minimize the expected number of tests. Our show that the proposed two-stage algorithm significantly outperforms existing in terms of the expected number of tests. We derive closed-form expressions for the optimal pool sizes and defective probabilities, and demonstrate their efficacy through extensive simulations. Our have important implications for applications in quality control, epidemiology, and machine learning, where group testing is a critical tool for efficiently identifying rare defects or anomalies.

Text: We report measurements of the optical gap in a GdN film at temperatures from 300 to 6K, covering both the paramagnetic and ferromagnetic phases. The gap is 1.31eV in the paramagnetic phase and red-shifts to 0.9eV in the spin-split bands below the Curie temperature. The paramagnetic gap is larger than was suggested by very early experiments, and has permitted us to refine a (LSDA+U)-computed band structure. The band structure was computed in the full translation symmetry of the ferromagnetic ground state, assigning the paramagnetic-state gap as the average of the majority- and minority-spin gaps in the ferromagnetic state. That procedure has been further tested by a band structure in a 32-atom supercell with randomly-oriented spins. After fitting only the paramagnetic gap the refined band structure then reproduces our measured gaps in both phases by direct transitions at the X point.

Text: Gene-editing technology has created the potential for new applications in both medicine and agriculture; the introduction of CRISPR allows scientists to precisely edit DNA. For instance, editing human embryos raises concerns about both the long-term impact on the individuals who undergo such procedures, as well as how they will be treated regarding consents to these procedures. Currently, there are fears of having "designer babies" and further increasing social inequality through the use of gene-editing technology; both of which require appropriate regulatory frameworks to manage any potential misuses of gene-editing biotechnology. Discussion of the impact of gene-editing technology should include participation from both the scientific community and the public. Text: This present investigation undertakes a meticulous and comprehensive examination of polynomials, a paradigmatic class of algebraic expressions endowed with far-reaching and multifaceted applications in mathematics, computer science, and engineering, thereby underscoring their fundamental significance in the aforementioned disciplines. Through an exhaustive mathematical analysis, the properties and comportment of polynomials, including their degree, coefficients, and roots, were thoroughly scrutinized, yielding valuable insights into the intrinsic mechanisms governing these algebraic expressions. A novel and systematic classification framework for polynomials was subsequently developed, predicated on their degree, which enables the expeditious identification and manipulation of polynomial expressions, thereby facilitating the efficient management of these mathematical constructs. The obtained in this research demonstrate that polynomials can be classified into discrete and distinct classes, comprising monic, non-monic, and bivariate polynomials, each exhibiting unique characteristics and applications that are intricately intertwined with the theoretical underpinnings of polynomial theory. Furthermore, a profound correlation between polynomial coefficients and roots was elucidated, revealing a hitherto understated yet fundamental nexus between these two pivotal concepts in algebraic expressions. The implications of this research are far-reaching, with significant repercussions for the development of polynomial-based algorithms in fields such as computer algebra, numerical analysis, and machine learning, thereby contributing to the progressive advancement of our understanding of polynomial theory and its diverse applications, thereby shedding new light on the rich and complex tapestry of algebraic expressions.

Text: The study of cosmological singularities remains a vital area of research in modern cosmology, particularly in the context of spatially-homogeneous models. These models provide a simplification of the complex dynamics of the universe, allowing for a deeper understanding of the behavior of the cosmos near singularities. Recent studies have highlighted the importance of the cosmological constant (Λ) in shaping the evolution of these models. However, the incorporation of a non-zero Λ into spatially-homogeneous models has been limited, and its impact on the formation of isotropic cosmological singularities remains poorly understood. In this study, we employ the Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) metric to investigate the evolution of spatially-homogeneous models with a non-zero cosmological constant. We utilize a numerical approach, integrating the Einstein field equations to simulate the dynamics of these models and identify the conditions under which isotropic cosmological singularities emerge. Our simulations reveal that the presence of a non-zero cosmological constant can significantly alter the evolution of spatially-homogeneous models, leading to the formation of isotropic cosmological singularities under specific conditions. Specifically, we find that a positive Λ can stabilize the expansion of the universe near the singularity, while a negative Λ can lead to an accelerated collapse. These have significant implications for our understanding of the behavior of the universe near singularities and the role of the cosmological constant in shaping its evolution.

Text: We present a comprehensive theoretical investigation into the vector-boson production of light Higgs pairs in the 2-Higgs Doublet Model (2HDM), a well-motivated extension of the Standard Model of particle physics. Our analysis focuses on the process pp → W+W- → hh, where two light Higgs bosons are produced in association with a dilepton pair, and pp → ZZ → hh, where two light Higgs bosons are produced in association with a dijet system. We calculate the production cross sections for these processes using state-of-the-art Monte Carlo simulations, taking into account the full range of possible 2HDM parameter space. Our show that the production rates for these processes are highly sensitive to the specific 2HDM parameters, particularly the masses and couplings of the additional Higgs bosons. We find that the light Higgs pair production cross sections can be significantly enhanced in the 2HDM, potentially leading to observable signals at the LHC. Our study provides a detailed understanding of the phenomenology of light Higgs pair production in the 2HDM and offers valuable insights for future experimental searches.

Text: As deep learning-based classifiers are increasingly adopted in real-world applications, the importance of understanding how a particular label is chosen grows. Single decision trees are an example of a simple, interpretable classifier, but are unsuitable for use with complex, high-dimensional data. On the other hand, the variational autoencoder (VAE) is designed to learn a factored, low-dimensional representation of data, but typically encodes high-likelihood data in an intrinsically non-separable way. We introduce the differentiable decision tree (DDT) as a modular component of deep networks and a simple, differentiable loss function that allows for end-to-end optimization of a deep network to compress high-dimensional data for classification by a single decision tree.

Text: Resilience is the capacity to absorb difficulty, adapt to adversity, and continue moving forward without being permanently broken by the experience. It is not the absence of pain or vulnerability - resilient people feel setbacks as acutely as anyone else. What distinguishes them is their relationship to those experiences and their ability to find a path forward even when none seems obvious. Resilience is partly temperamental, but it is also a set of learnable skills and cultivatable attitudes. Strong social connections, a sense of purpose, flexible thinking, and a history of having survived past difficulties all contribute to resilience. It also grows from the practice of meaning-making: the ability to construct a narrative around suffering that includes growth, learning, or contribution. Cultures and communities can foster or hinder resilience depending on how they respond to vulnerability and failure. At the individual level, building resilience is less about toughening yourself and more about deepening your resources - emotional, social, physical, and spiritual.

Text: Numerous models for grounded language understanding have been recently proposed, including (i) generic models that can be easily adapted to any given task and (ii) intuitively appealing modular models that require background knowledge to be instantiated. We compare both types of models in how much they lend themselves to a particular form of systematic generalization. Using a synthetic VQA test, we evaluate which models are capable of reasoning about all possible object pairs after training on only a small subset of them. Our findings show that the generalization of modular models is much more systematic and that it is highly sensitive to the module layout, i.e. to how exactly the modules are connected.

Text: This study presents an in-depth examination of the Kondo lattice model at half-filling, a configuration where the number of conduction electrons equals the number of localized spins. Our research focuses on the interplay between the Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) interaction and the Kondo screening, which arises due to the exchange coupling between the conduction electrons and the localized spins. Employing a combination of analytical and numerical techniques, including mean-field theory and density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) simulations, we investigate the phase diagram of the Kondo lattice model at half-filling. Our reveal a rich phase structure, comprising antiferromagnetic, ferromagnetic, and paramagnetic phases, which are determined by the strength of the RKKY interaction and the Kondo coupling. We also observe a quantum phase transition from the antiferromagnetic to the paramagnetic phase, which is characterized by a diverging susceptibility and a vanishing antiferromagnetic order parameter. Our provide insights into the behavior of heavy fermion systems and have implications for the understanding of the Kondo effect in real materials.

Text: The nulling of mid-infrared laser light, with wavelengths between 3-15 microns, is crucial for various astronomical and spectroscopic applications, including the direct imaging of exoplanets and the characterization of molecular compositions in planetary atmospheres. Currently, available nulling technologies face significant challenges in achieving high-contrast ratios and maintaining signal-to-noise ratios over extended periods. To address these issues, we propose an innovative approach using single-mode conductive waveguides. We designed and fabricated single-mode conductive waveguides with a specific diameter and metal coating to minimize losses and enhance the confinement of mid-infrared laser light. Our experiment employed a Mach-Zehnder interferometer configuration to demonstrate the waveguide's ability to null laser light. We controlled the phase shift of the input wavefront using a piezoelectric actuator and measured the output intensity using a sensitive thermopile detector. Our experiment successfully demonstrated the nulling of mid-infrared laser light using single-mode conductive waveguides, achieving a contrast ratio of 10^(-3) and maintaining a stable signal-to-noise ratio over 100 seconds. This proof-of-concept experiment paves the way for the development of high-contrast, mid-infrared nulling systems for advanced astronomical and spectroscopic applications.

Text: We present a theoretical and experimental investigation of the photodetachment of H$^{-}$ ions near a partial reflecting surface, which significantly alters the detachment dynamics compared to detachment in free space. Using a combination of quantum mechanical calculations and experimental measurements, we find that the presence of a partial reflector leads to a substantial increase in the detachment rate due to the enhancement of the incident photon flux. Moreover, the reflector-induced asymmetry in the detachment cross section reveals a complex interplay between the photon-matter interaction and the reflected electromagnetic fields — theoretical modeling, based on the time-dependent Schrödinger equation, shows that the partial reflector modifies the electron's wave function, thereby affecting the detachment probability, while experimental results, obtained via a custom-built setup, demonstrate a clear enhancement in the detachment rate in the presence of the partial reflector, in excellent agreement with theoretical predictions. As a result, our study provides new insights into the photodetachment process near a partial reflecting surface, with implications for grasp of various phenomena in atomic and molecular physics, as well as potential applications in quantum optics and nanotechnology.

Text: We report a thorough work of muon spin relaxation and hyperfine-enhanced 141Pr nuclear spin dynamics in the Pr(Os,Ru)4Sb12 and (Pr,La)Os4Sb12 compounds, which are members of the RT4Sb12 family with varying degrees of Pr-Os hybridization. Utilizing μ+SR spectroscopy, we explore the behavior of muon spins in these systems, uncovering distinct relaxation dynamics that reflect the impact of Pr-Os hybridization on the local magnetic moments and electronic properties. Specifically, our measurements reveal the presence of two distinct relaxation components in Pr(Os,Ru)4Sb12, corresponding to the Pr4+ and Os5+ moments, which exhibit a strong correlation with the 141Pr nuclear spin relaxation rate. In contrast, the (Pr,La)Os4Sb12 system displays a more complex relaxation behavior, likely arising from the mixed Pr-La valence state and the associated modification of the electronic structure. Our results not only provide insight into the spin dynamics in these compounds but also highlight the potential for μ+SR spectroscopy to probe the intricate relationships between local electronic moments and nuclear spin fluctuations in strongly correlated materials.

Text: This study investigates the fine-tuning problem in brane-antibrane inflationary models, specifically addressing the challenge of reconciling the small value of the cosmological constant with the large value of the fundamental Planck scale. We develop a novel approach to brane-antibrane inflation, incorporating a scalar field confined to a four-dimensional brane, which interacts with the four-dimensional graviton. Our framework allows for the dynamical stabilization of the brane separation, enabling the tuning of the fundamental parameters to achieve a steady inflationary scenario. We reveal that the fine-tuning problem can be mitigated through the introduction of a non-trivial potential for the scalar field, which arises from the interactions with the graviton. Our outcomes show that the introduced model can accommodate a wide range of inflationary scenarios, including both slow-roll and ultra-slow-roll inflation. Furthermore, we find that the model predicts a distinctive signature in the CMB power spectrum, which can be tested against future CMB observations. Our work provides a new perspective on the fine-tuning problem in brane-antibrane inflation, offering a potential solution to this long-standing issue in theoretical cosmology.

Text: In a peaceful town where life drifted by at an unhurried pace, an aging clockmaker spent his days bent over his bench, surrounded by the steady ticking of countless gears. Though the task promised no payment and fell outside his usual craft, the clockmaker welcomed him kindly. Setting aside his profitable repairs, he devoted hours to carefully shaping new joints and smoothing the wood until the toy looked finer than before. He returned it with a gentle smile, asking only to see the child happy. Years passed, and age began to weigh heavily on the craftsman. His hands trembled, his eyesight faded, and he feared he would soon have to close the shop he loved. Then one morning, an elegant carriage arrived at his door. From it stepped a confident young engineerâ€”the very boy whose toy he had once mended. The engineer presented him with an innovative machine he had created, designed to perform the delicate, demanding tasks of clock repair with flawless precision. Text: We present experimental evidence that the effective medium approximation (EMA), developed by D.C. Morse [Phys. Rev. E {\bf 63}, 031502, (2001)], provides the correct scaling law of the macroscopic plateau modulus $G^{0}\propto\rho^{4/3}L^{-1/3}_{p}$ (where $\rho$ is the contour length per unit volume and $L_{p}$ is the persistence length) of semi-flexible polymer solutions, in the highly entangled concentration regime. Competing theories, including a self-consistent binary collision approximation (BCA), have instead predicted $G^{0}\propto\rho^{7/5}L^{-1/5}_{p}$. Text: The purely affine, metric-affine and purely metric formulation of general relativity are dynamically equivalent and the relation between them is analogous to the Legendre relation between the Lagrangian and Hamiltonian dynamics. Specifically, we demonstrate that a strongly commuting CP_0-semigroup on a C*-algebra can be E_0-dilated if and only if its generator is affiliated with the C*-enveloping algebra of the C*-algebra. This result has significant implications for the study of ergodic theory, quantum information theory, and the structure of operator algebras, while furthermore, we derive a range of corollaries that elucidate the connection between E_0-dilation and the asymptotic behavior of strongly commuting CP_0-semigroups — the results presented in this article not only provide a crucial contribution to the existing literature on E_0-dilation but also open up new avenues for research in the field of operator algebras and quantum dynamics.

Text: We reveal that all CAT(0) boundaries of a group of the form HxK, where H is a hyperbolic group and K is a compact group, are CE (Conformal Dimension Equivalent) equivalent. Text: We consider the problem of estimating a density $f_X$ using a sample $Y_1,...,Y_n$ from $f_Y=f_X\star f_{\epsilon}$, where $f_{\epsilon}$ is an unknown density. Estimators of $f_X$ and its derivatives are constructed by using nonparametric estimators of $f_Y$ and $f_{\epsilon}$ and by applying a spectral cut-off in the Fourier domain. It is shown that the proposed estimators are asymptotically optimal in a minimax sense in the models with known or unknown error density, if the density $f_X$ belongs to a Sobolev space $H_{\mathbh p}$ and $f_{\epsilon}$ is ordinary smooth or supersmooth.

Text: We present a theoretical framework for plasma turbulence in astrophysical plasmas (solar wind, interstellar medium, galaxy clusters, accretion disks). The key assumptions are that the turbulence is anisotropic with respect to the mean magnetic field and frequencies are low compared to the ion cyclotron frequency. The energy injected at the outer scale scale has to be converted into heat, which ultimately cannot be done without collisions. A KINETIC CASCADE develops that brings the energy to collisional scales both in space and velocity. Its nature depends on the physics of plasma fluctuations. In each of the physically distinct scale ranges, the kinetic problem is systematically reduced to a more tractable set of equations. In the "inertial range" above the ion gyroscale, the kinetic cascade splits into a cascade of Alfvenic fluctuations, which are governed by the RMHD equations at both the collisional and collisionless scales, and a passive cascade of compressive fluctuations, which obey a linear kinetic equation along the moving field lines associated with the Alfvenic component. In the "dissipation range" between the ion and electron gyroscales, there are again two cascades: the kinetic-Alfven-wave (KAW) cascade governed by two fluid-like Electron RMHD equations and a passive phase-space cascade of ion entropy fluctuations. The latter cascade brings the energy of the inertial-range fluctuations that was damped by collisionless wave-particle interaction at the ion gyroscale to collisional scales in the phase space and leads to ion heating. The KAW energy is similarly damped at the electron gyroscale and converted into electron heat. Kolmogorov-style scaling relations are derived for these cascades. Astrophysical and space-physical applications are discussed in detail.

Text: In this paper we develop a refined transcendental framework for Kollár’s injectivity theorem, extending the introduced in the first part of this series to a broader class of singular hermitian line bundles and relative settings. By combining $L^{2}$-techniques for the $\bar\partial$-operator with a careful analysis of multiplier ideal sheaves associated to quasi‑plurisubharmonic potentials, we establish a new injectivity criterion that holds for higher direct images of adjoint bundles under proper Kähler morphisms, even when the underlying varieties possess log‑canonical singularities. The proof hinges on a novel curvature decomposition that isolates a semi‑positive component sufficient to invoke a twisted Bochner–Kodaira–Nakano identity, yielding $L^{2}$-estimates that are stable under base change. As a consequence, we obtain a unified vanishing theorem encompassing both Kollár’s original statement and its recent extensions by Fujino and Ambro, and we demonstrate applications to the deformation invariance of plurigenera and to the surjectivity of restriction maps for pluricanonical systems on varieties of general type. The illustrate the power of transcendental in birational geometry and suggest further avenues for exploiting analytic techniques in the study of higher direct image sheaves.

Text: The intracluster medium (ICM) is a vast, diffuse plasma that pervades galaxy clusters, providing a wealth of information on their physical properties and evolution. Our analysis reveals a strong correlation between the SZ temperature and the ICM's thermal energy, with a best-fit power-law index of 1.23 ± 0.15. We also find that the SZ temperature is a robust proxy for the ICM's entropy, with a correlation coefficient of 0.85 ± 0.12. Text: Spiritual growth is the deepening of a person's inner life - their relationship with meaning, purpose, the sacred, and the deepest dimensions of human experience. It is not confined to any particular religious tradition, though it is expressed through many of them. At its core, spiritual growth involves a movement from a self-centered orientation toward something larger - whether understood as God, the universe, compassion for all beings, or the call of ethical responsibility. This movement rarely follows a straight line; it typically involves periods of questioning, doubt, crisis, and apparent regression alongside periods of expansion and deepening clarity. The practices that support spiritual growth vary widely: prayer, meditation, service to others, study of sacred texts, time in nature, artistic creation, community life, and the confrontation of one's own mortality. What these practices share is a quality of serious engagement with the deepest questions of existence. Spiritual growth produces not certainty but increasing depth of character - a greater capacity for love, compassion, honesty, and the ability to hold life's complexity without being destroyed by it.

Text: This study investigates the critical delays that arise in polynomial eigenvalue problems (PEPs), which are fundamental to the analysis and design of linear time-invariant systems. We develop a novel framework for identifying and characterizing critical delays, which are defined as the time instances at which the system's stability properties undergo a discontinuous change. Our approach is based on the concept of delay-dependent stability, which requires the system's characteristic polynomial to be stable over a finite interval of time. We derive a set of necessary and sufficient conditions for critical delays, which are expressed in terms of the coefficients of the characteristic polynomial. These conditions are used to develop a delay-dependent stability criterion, which is shown to be equivalent to a classical stability criterion. Our are validated through numerical examples, including a polynomial matrix representation of a linear system with delayed feedback. The implications of our are far-reaching, as they provide new insights into the stability and performance of control systems subject to time delays, which are ubiquitous in engineering applications.

Detailed analysis of the data indicates a strong interference between the $s$-channel and $t$-channel production processes, providing insight into the underlying strong interaction dynamics governing this reaction. Text: We examine the phenomenon of Anderson localisation in the context of an interacting two-particle quantum system on a one-dimensional lattice ${\mathbb Z}$. We demonstrate that for weak interactions, the system exhibits a transition from delocalised to localised behaviour as the disorder strength increases. Furthermore, we identify a critical disorder strength below which the system remains delocalised, and above which localisation sets in. Our results offer new insights into the interplay between interactions and disorder in many-body quantum systems, and have implications for the understanding of Anderson localisation in systems with multiple degrees of freedom.

Text: We have carried out a comparative theoretical study of the electronic structure of the novel one-dimensional Ca$_3$CoRhO$_6$ and Ca$_3$FeRhO$_6$ systems. The insulating antiferromagnetic state for the Ca$_3$FeRhO$_6$ can be well explained by band structure calculations with the closed shell high-spin $d^5$ (Fe$^{3+}$) and low-spin $t_{2g}^{6}$ (Rh$^{3+}$) configurations. We found for the Ca$_3$CoRhO$_6$ that the Co has a strong tendency to be $d^7$ (Co$^{2+}$) rather than $d^6$ (Co$^{3+}$), and that there is an orbital degeneracy in the local Co electronic structure. Text: Entanglement quantification for bipartite qubit systems remains a central problem in quantum information theory. The negativity, defined as the sum of absolute values of the negative eigenvalues of the partially transposed density matrix, is a widely used computable entanglement monotone. However, evaluating negativity directly requires full spectral decomposition, which can be computationally demanding for mixed states. Recent advances suggest that the minimal principal minors of Hermitian matrices encode sufficient spectral information to bound or recover eigenvalue signs. We consider an arbitrary two‑qubit density operator ρ and its partial transpose ρ^{T_B}. By expressing ρ^{T_B} as a 4 × 4 Hermitian matrix, we derive analytic expressions for all principal minors of orders one, two, and three. Using Sylvester’s criterion and the interlacing properties of eigenvalues, we formulate a set of necessary and sufficient conditions under which the smallest principal minors guarantee the presence of negative eigenvalues. These conditions are then employed to construct an explicit formula for the negativity that depends only on a subset of principal minors, avoiding full diagonalisation. We demonstrate that the negativity of any bipartite qubit state can be exactly recovered from the three smallest principal minors of ρ^{T_B}. The resulting expression simplifies numerical evaluation and provides tight analytical bounds for mixed‑state entanglement. Moreover, the approach reveals a direct link between the geometry of Hermitian matrix minors and entanglement, offering a new tool for rapid entanglement assessment in experimental and theoretical studies.

The extracted critical exponents are consistent with those of two‑dimensional percolation, confirming that the clustering of color sources governs the fluctuation pattern. These provide quantitative support for string percolation as a viable mechanism for the emergence of collective behavior in relativistic heavy‑ion collisions.

The experimental apparatus comprises a beam of neutral atoms, which interact with the surface contaminants, resulting in a discernible deflection of the atomic trajectory that is directly proportional to the strength of the contaminant-induced electric field, thereby enabling the inference of the contaminant's presence and magnitude. Our empirical demonstrate the efficacy of this method in detecting electric fields generated by a diverse array of contaminants, including ions, free radicals, and organic molecules, thereby underscoring the potential applications of this technique in fields such as surface science, materials science, and environmental monitoring, where the detection of electric fields is essential for comprehending surface processes and phenomena. Consequently, the precision and sensitivity of this method render it a highly valuable instrument for researchers seeking to investigate the intricate interactions between surfaces and their surroundings.

Text: This exploration delves into the significance of Regge-mediated interactions within deeply virtual Compton scattering (DVCS), a critical phenomenon for unraveling nucleon architecture and the intricate mechanisms of quantum chromodynamics (QCD). A theoretical framework predicated on Regge parametrization is employed to dissect the contributions of principal Regge trajectories—specifically, the pomeron, f-trajectory, and A2-trajectory—to DVCS cross-sections in intermediate energy domains where perturbative QCD methodologies exhibit limited efficacy. This model is rigorously juxtaposed with the handbag approximation, which predominantly governs high-energy dynamics, to delineate their respective impacts across distinct kinematic configurations. Computational analyses reveal that Regge trajectories exert a pronounced influence on DVCS differential cross-sections within kinematic regions defined by intermediate Bjorken-x and minimal momentum transfer, where the handbag contribution wanes. This observation is substantiated through a comparative evaluation of predicted angular distributions and beam charge asymmetries, which exhibit enhanced concordance with empirical datasets upon integration of Regge exchanges. Furthermore, the synergy between Regge and handbag mechanisms is demonstrated to modulate the transverse-longitudinal structure of the DVCS amplitude, thereby illuminating the continuum between soft and hard QCD phenomena. These underscore the criticality of embedding Regge dynamics into DVCS investigations to advance comprehension of parton orbital angular momentum and nucleon spin structure, particularly in the energy regime where neither perturbative nor non-perturbative QCD models alone suffice.

Text: International Relations is the academic field of inquiry concerned with the interactions among sovereign states, international organizations, non-governmental organizations, multinational corporations, and other actors within the global arena. It encompasses the study of diplomacy and statecraft, the causes and management of war and peace, international law and norms, global governance architecture, foreign policy analysis, international economic relations, human rights promotion, and responses to transnational environmental challenges. Major theoretical frameworks in international relations include realism, which emphasizes state power, national interest, and the anarchic structure of the international system; liberalism, which highlights the constructive role of international institutions, economic interdependence, and democratic peace; and constructivism, which focuses on the constitutive role of ideas, norms, and collective identities in shaping international behavior. The post-Cold War international order has been marked by the rise of new powers, the growing influence of non-state actors, complex transnational challenges including climate change and terrorism, and ongoing debates about the future of sovereignty, multilateralism, and the international order.

Text: Here, we explore the intersection of operadic algebra and quantum mechanics through the lens of the harmonic oscillator, a fundamental model in physics. By interpreting the harmonic oscillator as a morphism in a suitable operad, we show a rich structure that underlies its classical and quantum behavior. Specifically, we define a new operad, denoted as HOS, whose algebraic properties are intimately connected with the solutions of the harmonic oscillator equation. Our results demonstrate that the operadic framework provides a unified framework for grasp of both the classical and quantum harmonic oscillators, shedding new light on the interplay between symmetries and physical observables. Furthermore, we show that the operadic harmonic oscillator framework generalizes to higher-dimensional systems, enabling the study of complex physical phenomena such as anharmonic oscillations and quantum field theories. Our research contributes to a deeper understanding of the algebraic foundations of quantum mechanics, with potential implications for the development of original mathematical tools and computational methods in physics. The operadic harmonic oscillator approach may also lead to new perspective into the nature of physical reality, including the role of symmetries and the emergence of quantum behavior.
