Text: This investigation introduces a pioneering method for determining the neutron-neutron scattering length via the gamma d --> pi^+ nn reaction, wherein chiral perturbation theory (ChPT) serves as the theoretical paradigm for elucidating the underlying dynamics. Text: Echolocation is a highly specialized biological sonar adaptation utilized by bats, cetaceans, and certain cave-dwelling birds to navigate and hunt in total darkness. To perceive their surroundings, these animals emit high-frequency sound pulses that travel through the air or water and bounce off nearby objects. By analyzing the returning echoes, the animal's brain can instantaneously calculate the distance, size, shape, and velocity of an object, including microscopic insects in mid-flight. This sophisticated acoustic mapping capability allows insectivorous bats to bypass visual limitations and dominate nocturnal ecological niches. Human engineers have successfully copied this natural technology to develop modern RADAR and SONAR systems for aviation and maritime navigation.

Text: We discuss the star-disk electric circuit for a young stellar object (YSO) and calculate the expected torques on the star and the disk. We show how a short circuit in the star-disk electric circuit may produce a magnetically-driven jet flow from the inner edge of a disk surrounding a young star. An unsteady bipolar jet flow is produced that flows perpendicular to the disk plane. Jet speeds of order hundreds of kilometres per second are possible, while the outflow mass loss rate is proportional to the mass accretion rate and is a function of the disk inner radius relative to the disk co-rotation radius.

Text: This study investigates the influence of phonon dimensionality on electron energy relaxation in metal-oxide nanostructures. Phonons play a pivotal role in the relaxation of electron energy, with their dimensionality significantly affecting the thermalization process. By employing a combination of first-principles calculations and molecular dynamics simulations, we investigated the impact of phonon confinement on electron-phonon interactions in nanostructured materials. Our results illustrate that the dimensionality of phonons significantly alters the energy relaxation rate of electrons, with reduced dimensionality leading to enhanced electron-phonon coupling and faster energy relaxation. Specifically, we found that in low-dimensional phonon systems, the energy relaxation rate is significantly faster than in three-dimensional phonon systems, attributed to the increased phonon density of states and the enhanced electron-phonon scattering events. These findings have important implications for the design and optimization of metal-oxide nanostructures for various electronic and optoelectronic applications, where efficient electron energy relaxation is essential for device performance.

Text: Here, we investigate the dynamic fluctuations of the chiral condensate and quasi-particle spectra in the vicinity of the QCD phase transition — utilizing lattice Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) simulations, we examined the behavior of these quantities as a function of temperature and quark chemical potential. Our results indicate that the chiral condensate exhibits significant fluctuations near the critical point, with a marked increase in its variance as the system approaches the transition temperature. By contrast, in particular, concurrently, the quasi-particle spectra undergo a substantial modification, characterized by a broadening of the spectral function and a reorganization of the quasi-particle peaks; these findings suggest that the chiral condensate and quasi-particle spectra are intimately connected, with the former serving as a proxy for the latter's behavior. Our analysis of the correlation between the chiral condensate fluctuations and quasi-particle spectra provides new insights into the dynamics of the QCD phase transition, shedding light on the underlying mechanisms governing the behavior of quark matter under extreme conditions. These results have far-reaching implications for our insight into of the strong interaction and the behavior of quark-gluon plasma.

Text: Dusty plasmas have generated a large amount of interest since the discovery of ordered structure (crystal) formation in experimentally generated complex plasmas in 1994. Dust particles within the plasma sheath generated in these complex plasmas can form vertical chains due to the streaming ion wakefield. For the simplest of these configurations (a two particle chain), the particle closest to the lower electrode will generally remain in the shadow of the particle farthest from the lower electrode. These in the two particles feeling differing ion drag forces: the top particle is acted on by the ion drag force directed from the plasma to the lower electrode, while the bottom particle is acted upon by the resulting wakefield produced by the interaction of the upper particle with the ion drag force. This dynamic situation currently provides the best known experimental environment for examining the physics behind the ion drag force and its interaction with the plasma sheath. An experimental method for investigating the interaction between pair-particle chains based on modulating the bias on the lower electrode employing a DC bias modulation technique will be presented.

Text: The dynamics of a quantum harmonic oscillator, situated in tandem with a dissipative environment, are thoroughly examined within the theoretical paradigm of the Lindblad theory. This framework affords a nuanced understanding of the decoherence-induced correlations between the oscillator's quantum state and its classical conjugate variables, thereby enabling an in-depth exploration of the interplay between quantum and classical phenomena. Employing a time-dependent density matrix formalism, we derive an exact solution for the reduced density matrix of the oscillator, which facilitates an investigation into the dynamics of quantum coherence and classical correlations. Notably, our disclose an incremental loss of quantum coherence, accompanied by the emergence of classical correlations with the environment, as quantitatively assessed by the linear entropy and the correlation entropy. Our analysis demonstrates that the Lindblad theory predicts a seamless transition from a quantum to a classical behavior, with the oscillator's dynamics exhibiting an irreversible trajectory towards a stable fixed-point solution, a phenomenon of critical significance in the context of open quantum systems. The implications of our extend to the realm of quantum foundations, where they contribute to an enhanced comprehension of the breakdown of quantum mechanics and the origins of classicality, as well as the burgeoning field of computational complexity.

Text: We report the observation of a resonance-like structure in the pi^+- ψ' mass distribution in exclusive B→K π^+- ψ' decays, through a dataset of 772 × 10^6 BB̅ pairs collected by the Belle II experiment. A significant peak is observed in the π^+- ψ' mass distribution, which is stable with a previously reported structure in this channel. The measured mass and width of the resonance are found to be (5.74 ± 0.04) GeV/c^2 and (3.2 ± 0.8) MeV, respectively. The measured branching fraction of the B→K π^+- ψ' decay is (4.9 ± 0.6 ± 1.1) × 10^-6. The observed structure is compared to various theoretical models, including those involving exotic states, meson-meson molecules, and glueballs. Our results offer new insights into the nature of this resonance and its implications for our insight into of the strong interaction. Text: This comprehensive investigation delves into the intricate interplay between the ratchet effect and transporting islands, a manifestation of chaotic sea dynamics with far-reaching implications for elucidating the behavior of complex systems and their propensity for directed transport. Text: A Bose-Einstein condensate in an external potential consisting of a superposition of a harmonic and a random potential is considered theoretically. This state is stable over a large range of particle numbers. The frequency of the breathing mode scales as $1/{\cal L}^2$. For negative scattering length a condensate of size ${\cal L}$ may exist as a metastable state. These finding are generalized to anisotropic traps.

Text: Phase synchronization (PS) of coupled oscillators is a fundamental phenomenon in nonlinear dynamics, yet its detection and characterization remain challenging, especially in high‑dimensional or experimentally noisy settings. Recent approaches based on recurrence and symbolic dynamics suggest that localized subsets of the phase space may encode the emergence of PS, but a unifying theoretical framework is lacking. We introduce a general framework that formalizes the concept of *localized sets*—subsets of the joint state space where the phase difference remains bounded over finite observation windows. By constructing a Poincaré‑type mapping on these sets and employing measure‑theoretic tools, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions for PS in terms of set invariance and contraction properties. The framework is validated analytically on prototypical models (e.g., coupled Rössler and Kuramoto–Sakaguchi systems) and numerically on networks of chaotic oscillators with heterogeneous coupling and noise. An algorithm for automated detection of localized sets from time‑series data is also presented. The proposed conditions accurately predict the onset of PS across all tested systems, revealing that PS corresponds to the emergence of invariant, low‑dimensional localized sets despite underlying chaos. The detection algorithm achieves >95 % true‑positive rates with minimal false alarms, even for noisy measurements. Moreover, the framework unifies previously disparate PS criteria and extends naturally to multiplex and time‑delayed networks, offering a robust tool for both theoretical analysis and experimental identification of phase‑synchronized states.

Text: As contrasted with physicists to idolize Bell's theorem and quantum nonlocality, we argue that quantum mechanics (QM), in reality, respects the principles of a macroscopic realism (PMRs). The current QM to tell us that "... the state of a system can be instantaneously changed by a distant measurement >..." cannot be treated as a physical theory. Its key statements - that the EPR-Bell experiments to violate Bell's inequality verify nonlocality, and nonlocal correlations respect special relativity - are false. Both the EPR-Bell experiments and theorems to support the "non-signalling principle" are based on the implicit assumption that all quantum postulates and, in particular, Born's averaging rule are fully applicable to Cat states. However, this is not the case. Introducing observables (e.g., correlations) for Cat states violates the correspondence principle. Pure (macro- and micro-)Cat states must be governed both by the PMRs and superposition principle. Our (macrorealistic) model of a one-dimensional completed scattering shows how these principles coexist with each other, in the case of a one-electron micro-Cat state.

Text: The projection of a bipartite network is a fundamental problem in network science, as it enables the analysis of complex systems comprising two distinct sets of nodes. A bipartite network, by definition, consists of two disjoint sets of nodes, where edges only connect nodes from different sets, and there are no edges between nodes within the same set. Projecting such a network involves transforming it into one or more unipartite networks, where edges connect nodes within the same set, thereby facilitating the application of various network analysis tools and techniques. Several projection have been proposed, including the widely used one-mode projection, which creates a weighted network where the weight of an edge between two nodes represents the number of common neighbors they share in the original bipartite network. Other , such as the bipartite local projection and the backbone projection, have also been developed to address specific challenges and applications, including community detection, node ranking, and network comparison, highlighting the importance of selecting an appropriate projection method to uncover meaningful insights into the structure and function of complex bipartite systems.

This equation, based on the Jarzynski equality, offers a direct link between the mechanical work performed during unzipping and the underlying DNA sequence. We show that, given a large-bandwidth dataset of mechanical unzipping events, it is possible to reconstruct the DNA sequence with high accuracy using this approach. Our method involves a maximum likelihood estimation of the sequence-dependent mechanical properties from the data, followed by a deconvolution of the sequence from the estimated properties. We show that, under idealized conditions, this approach can recover DNA sequences with an accuracy comparable to that of state-of-the-art sequencing technologies. Furthermore, we highlight the potential for this method to be used in conjunction with existing sequencing technologies, enabling the analysis of complex DNA sequences in regions that are currently difficult to access.

Text: We obtain static gauge field configurations for SU(2) Yang-Mills gauge theory in the absence of chromo-magnetic field. We also present a systematic way to obtain such configurations for SU(3) and SU(4) YM gauge theories by realizing their Lie algebras in terms of SU(2). Generalization of our method to SU(N) gauge theory with N>2 is straight forward. The gauge fields thus obtained are complex. We investigated the issue of uniform as well as real chromo-electric field with these configurations. Furthermore, we investigated the possible class of vacuum solutions for the gauge fields and found that they are gauge inequivalent to the usual vacuum configuration $Aa_{mu}=0$.

Text: We examine canonical quantization of relativistic field theories on the forward hyperboloid, a Lorentz-invariant surface of the form $x_mu xmu = tau2$. This choice of quantization surface implies that all components of the 4-momentum operator are affected by interactions (if present), whereas rotation and boost generators remain interaction free -- a feature characteristic of Dirac's `` point-formrqrq of relativistic dynamics. Unlike previous attempts to quantize fields on space-time hyperboloids, we keep the usual plane-wave expansion of the field operators and consider evolution of the system generated by the 4-momentum operator. We verify that the Fock-space representations of the Poincar'e generators for free scalar and spin-1/2 fields look the same as for equal-time quantization. Scattering is formulated for interacting fields in a covariant interaction picture and it is shown that the familiar perturbative expansion of the S-operator is recovered by our approach. An appendix analyzes special distributions, integrals over the forward hyperboloid, that are used repeatedly in the paper.

Text: A comprehensive investigation of the Coulomb blockade of field emission from nanoscale conductors has been conducted, elucidating the underlying physical mechanisms and their effects on the emission characteristics. Utilizing a combination of experimental techniques, including scanning tunneling microscopy and field emission spectroscopy, and theoretical modeling, we have examined the impact of electron-electron interactions and charging effects on the field emission process from individual nanowires and nanotubes. Our reveal that the Coulomb blockade, a phenomenon in which the emission of electrons from a conductor is suppressed due to the accumulation of charge, plays a crucial role in modulating the field emission current and stability. Specifically, we observe that the blockade effect leads to a significant reduction in the emission current and a corresponding increase in the turn-on field, while also influencing the emission spectrum and spatial distribution. These have important implications for the development of nanoscale field emission devices, highlighting the need for careful consideration of Coulomb blockade effects in the design and operation of such systems.

Text: In the realm of non-equilibrium statistical mechanics, the Totally Asymmetric Exclusion Process (TASEP) stands as a pioneering model, accurately describing the particle transport mechanism on a lattice. Building upon our previous work, this study successfully develops a determinant-based solution for the TASEP with parallel updates on a ring geometry, a configuration that generates correlations between the dynamics of adjacent particles, significantly increasing the model's analytical complexity. Employing an innovative blend of algebraic and combinatorial techniques, we derived an exact expression for the steady-state probability distribution of the TASEP, which relies heavily on the representation theory of the symmetric group and entails the computation of determinants of specially structured matrices. The resultant expression comprehensively characterizes the model's steady-state behavior, encompassing the density profile, current, and correlation functions, thus offering unparalleled insights into the TASEP's properties on ring geometries. These findings are anticipated to profoundly impact our understanding of non-equilibrium phenomena in diverse fields, including physics, biology, and traffic flow, while the determinant solution presented here serves as a foundation for further analytical and numerical investigations of the TASEP and related models.

Text: Gauge mediation in the theoretical context of string theory constitutes a paradigmatic framework for harmonizing the phenomenon of supersymmetry breaking with the stringent requirements of the Standard Model of particle physics. By positing that supersymmetry is spontaneously broken at a high-energy scale within a secluded, hidden sector of the string theory landscape, and that the resulting supersymmetry-breaking effects are transmitted to the observable sector via gauge interactions, this framework furnishes a novel mechanism for reconciling the disparate elements of supersymmetry breaking. A pivotal aspect of gauge mediation in string theory is the imperative of a hidden sector messenger sector, wherein the supersymmetry-breaking effects are mediated to the observable sector through the exchange of gauge bosons, thereby facilitating the transfer of supersymmetry-breaking information across the hidden sector boundary. Through a thorough investigation of the phenomenological implications of gauge mediation in string theory, our analysis focuses on the determination of the universal soft supersymmetry-breaking mass parameters and the prediction of supersymmetric particle masses, demonstrating that this framework can effectively reconcile the low-energy supersymmetry-breaking effects with the cosmological constraints, thus providing a well-motivated and experimentally testable paradigm for supersymmetry beyond the Standard Model. Consequently, the ensuing supersymmetric particle spectra are juxtaposed with the experimental constraints derived from the Large Hadron Collider, and the implications for future searches are systematically discussed and analyzed.

Text: In this investigation we present the outcomes of Spitzer spectral line mapping of six supernova remnants (SNRs), delivering a thorough dataset that underscores the varied nature of these astrophysical objects. Using the Infrared Spectrograph and Array Camera (IRAC) aboard the Spitzer Space Telescope, we acquired high‑resolution spectral line images of each remnant in the [O I], [O III], and [Si II] forbidden lines together with the underlying continuum. Principal‑component analysis (PCA) was then applied to the resulting data cubes to uncover the principal physical drivers behind the observed emission. The PCA‑derived eigenvectors explain the bulk of the variance in the spectral maps, enabling us to isolate the dominant spectral signatures of each remnant. These findings establish a basis for subsequent investigations of the remnants’ physical conditions—such as excitation mechanisms, ionisation sources, and elemental abundances—while also demonstrating that PCA serves as an efficient tool for reducing and interpreting large astronomical data sets, revealing subtle trends and patterns that would otherwise be obscured by conventional analysis techniques.

Text: Researchers have recently proposed a groundbreaking density-functional approach to investigate the behavior of fermionic systems at a Feshbach resonance, a phenomenon characterized by a profound increase in scattering length as the energy of a two-particle scattering state intersects that of a bound molecular state. By utilizing density-functional theory as a computational framework, a novel tool has been developed to describe the universal properties of fermionic systems near the resonance, encompassing energy, density profiles, and two-body correlation functions. Notably, the results demonstrate the density-functional's capacity to accurately capture the many-body physics of fermionic systems at Feshbach resonance, including the emergence of a pseudogap in the single-particle spectral function and the development of pairing correlations. Text: Research on very low-mass stars and brown dwarfs within resolved binary and multiple systems is pivotal in elucidating their formation and evolution processes, as well as the characteristics of their constituent elements. Text: This investigation discloses how two‑dimensional defect states emerge in photonic lattices that are optically induced, a behavior that stems from the intentional breakdown of the lattice’s inherent periodicity. By integrating analytical theory with laboratory tests, we show that 2‑D defect modes can be both produced and steered through deliberate geometric modifications of the lattice. The data reveal that inserting defects generates localized resonances possessing spectral and spatial signatures that differ markedly from those of the pristine structure. In particular, we detect a pronounced increase in defect‑mode intensity coupled with a contraction of the spectral linewidth when the defect’s size and location are finely tuned. Numerical experiments carried out with the finite‑difference time‑domain technique reproduce the measured trends with high precision, thereby corroborating the experimental observations. Our work supplies fresh perspectives on the dynamics of 2‑D defect excitations in optically induced photonic lattices and points to promising avenues for future photonic components, such as narrow‑band filters and high‑Q resonators. The outcomes presented here substantially enrich the current understanding of photonic crystals and optical metamaterials.

Moreover, this work bridges the gap between abstract operator algebra and quantum many-body systems, underscoring the utility of C*-algebras in advancing foundational research in quantum statistical mechanics and providing a foundation for designing robust quantum simulations in higher dimensions or non-translation-invariant lattices.
Label: AWP
Title: C^*-algebraic approach to the Bose-Hubbard model

Text: This study examines the genesis of magnetically-dominated interstellar clouds through shock-induced compression mechanisms, employing high-resolution computational simulations and analytical frameworks to dissect the synergistic interactions between shock-induced compression dynamics and magnetic field augmentation processes. By modeling compressive shocks with variable Mach numbers (≥10) and density ratios, we establish that intense shocks effectively condense and orient magnetic fields, resulting in magnetic field dominance surpassing thermal and turbulent contributions in post-shock regions, with magnetic energy density proportions exceeding thermal and kinetic energy components in ∼20% of modeled cases, even in initially subcritical magnetic field configurations. Post-shock strata demonstrate amplified density gradients and structured magnetic field configurations, wherein magnetic tension counteracts gravitational collapse while structural integrity is preserved through the interplay of shock-compressed interfaces and internal magnetic flux locking mechanisms. The findings underscore that shock-initiated formation mechanisms yield magnetic field architectures distinct from those generated via turbulent or gravity-driven processes, offering a mechanistic explanation for the ubiquity of magnetically-dominated dense structures in star-forming regions. This process elucidates the transformative role of shocks in interstellar medium organization, highlighting their capacity to transmute kinetic energy into magnetic field coherence, thereby modulating cloud stability, fragmentation thresholds, and the overarching efficiency of stellar birth in magnetized environments.
Label: AWP
Title: Shock-triggered formation of magnetically-dominated clouds

Text: This study examines the existence and moduli-theoretic characteristics of nodal curves situated on K3 surfaces, emphasizing configurations wherein the curves and their associated singularities demonstrate maximal generality within moduli. By synthesizing deformation-theoretic methodologies and lattice-theoretic classifications of K3 surfaces, the research delineates sufficient conditions for the emergence of nodal curves exhibiting predetermined nodal counts and occupying general positions within their respective linear systems. Through rigorous analysis of the interplay between the geometric properties of K3 surfaces and the combinatorial constraints imposed by nodal singularities, the paper demonstrates that such curves are prevalent in moduli when the underlying lattice structure adheres to specific primitiveness and ampleness criteria. Utilizing the Noether-Lefschetz theory and the deformation-invariance of Gromov-Witten invariants, the authors establish that the moduli space of these curves exhibits either general type or unirationality, contingent upon the selected polarization. Furthermore, the work characterizes the locus of nodal curves within the moduli space of stable maps, revealing intricate connections to the enumerative geometry of rational curves on K3 surfaces. These findings advance the comprehension of singularities in algebraic surfaces and elucidate the architecture of moduli spaces, which are pivotal to both algebraic geometry and mathematical physics. The research bridges classical inquiries in surface theory with contemporary frameworks in derived algebraic geometry, thereby providing a robust foundation for future investigations into the interplay between singularities and moduli.
Label: AWP
Title: Nodal curves with general moduli on K3 surfaces

Text: This investigation employs computational simulations and theoretical frameworks to elucidate the ramifications of accelerated growth kinetics on the developmental trajectories of weighted complex networks. By systematically modulating growth velocities within synthetic and empirical systems, our analysis reveals that heightened expansion rates induce significant modifications in degree distribution profiles, culminating in topologically heterogeneous configurations marked by an elevated density of high-degree nodes. Furthermore, the interplay between growth acceleration and weight heterogeneity engenders non-linear interdependencies, manifesting as augmented local clustering coefficients alongside diminished global modularity—a phenomenon attributed to the preferential reinforcement of localized connectivity at the expense of intermodular cohesion. Crucially, while accelerated growth enhances adaptive capacity in dynamic environments by fostering robustness to random perturbations, it concurrently exacerbates vulnerability to targeted disruptions through the emergence of structurally critical hubs. The universality of these evolutionary patterns is evidenced by cross-domain analyses spanning transportation infrastructures, biological interaction matrices, and technological communication networks, thereby establishing growth rate as a pivotal modulator of network resilience and functional efficiency. These findings not only delineate the mechanistic basis for growth-rate-dependent network evolution but also offer a theoretical foundation for optimizing the design of adaptive systems in contexts ranging from biological ecosystems to engineered infrastructure.
Label: AWP
Title:
Effects of accelerating growth on the evolution of weighted complex
  networks

Text: This research introduces an advanced methodology for the extraction of patterns characterized by a balanced interval distribution, a pioneering technique designed to surmount the constraints inherent in conventional pattern mining paradigms. Through the integration of an interval-based analytical framework, the proposed system effectively delineates significant and insightful patterns from extensive datasets, concurrently diminishing the perturbations induced by extraneous noise and anomalous data points. The balanced interval strategy not only ensures the mining process remains responsive to salient associations within the data but also fortifies it against the proliferation of spurious correlations, thereby enhancing the overall fidelity and relevance of the extracted pattern sets. The methodology harnesses an amalgamation of statistical inference and machine learning algorithms—including decision tree architectures and clustering mechanisms—to discern patterns that manifest uniform attribute distribution across designated intervals. The robustness and effectiveness of this approach are validated through empirical evaluations conducted on benchmark datasets, which consistently demonstrate marked enhancements in both the discriminative accuracy and representational quality of the identified patterns relative to contemporary state-of-the-art methodologies. These findings hold profound ramifications for multidisciplinary applications spanning data mining, knowledge discovery, and predictive analytics, where the precise identification of high-quality patterns is indispensable for optimizing data-driven decision-making processes.

Title: Mining Patterns with a Balanced Interval

Text: This investigation delves into the intrinsic topological configurations of spin glasses, a paradigmatic class of magnetically disordered materials, and elucidates the underlying network topography governing their inherent structural properties. By leveraging an advanced computational methodology, we generate and scrutinize large ensembles of inherent structures within the confines of the Edwards-Anderson spin glass model, thereby facilitating a comprehensive understanding of the intricate relationships between these structures. Notably, our findings reveal a resilient network of inherent structures, wherein each structural configuration is represented as a node, and the interconnectivities between them are calibrated to reflect the similarities in their energetic landscapes. Furthermore, we observe that this network exhibits scaling properties, with the degree distribution of the nodes adhering to a power-law scaling, indicative of a scale-free architecture, thereby underscoring the inherent complexity of these systems. Moreover, the network's clustering coefficient and shortest path length indicate a high level of connectivity and efficacious communication between structures, thereby substantiating the notion that the inherent structures of spin glasses are organized in a complex network, with far-reaching implications for our comprehension of the systems' thermodynamic and dynamic properties. These results not only provide novel insights into the emergent behavior of disordered systems but also shed light on the underlying mechanisms governing their structural and energetic organization, thereby expanding our understanding of these complex phenomena.
Label: AWP
Title:
Network of inherent structures in spin glasses: scaling and scale-free
  distributions

Text: This study undertakes an exhaustive magnetohydrostatic analysis of the equilibrium characteristics of solar prominence structures within coronal magnetic fields exhibiting minimal non-potentiality. Through the numerical resolution of the complete nonlinear system of magnetohydrostatic equations governing a gravitationally stratified, radiatively cooling plasma immersed in a three-dimensional magnetic topology extrapolated from potential-field models of photospheric magnetograms, we generate self-consistent prominence models incorporating empirically derived profiles of density, temperature, and pressure. The resulting equilibrium configurations demonstrate that infinitesimal deviations from potential magnetic field configurations, quantified by sub-kilogauss magnitude shear components, are adequate to produce magnetic dips capable of sustaining high-density prominence condensations in opposition to solar gravitational forces. A systematic parametric investigation is conducted to evaluate the geometric properties of magnetic dips as functions of the photospheric magnetic flux distribution, with quantitative characterization of the corresponding variations in prominence dimensions, including vertical extent, longitudinal span, and total mass. The stability characteristics of these quasi-potential equilibria are analyzed using linear perturbation theory, revealing marginal resistance to both interchange and torsional kink instabilities, with exponential amplification of perturbation growth rates observed beyond a critical shear threshold. These findings establish that significant magnetic helicity is not a prerequisite for prominence sustenance, thereby proposing a viable mechanism for prominence genesis in solar quiescent regions and providing observational constraints for forthcoming spectropolarimetric investigations of coronal magnetic field structures.
Label: AWP
Title:
Magnetohydrostatic solar prominences in near-potential coronal magnetic
  fields

Text: This investigation undertakes a multifaceted examination of the atmospheric muon charge ratio data amassed by the MINOS experiment at Fermilab, yielding novel theoretical insights into the fundamental physics underlying neutrino oscillations and the intrinsic properties of the neutrino sector. Through a detailed analysis of a dataset comprising 1.35x10^6 atmospheric neutrino events, we meticulously quantified the muon charge ratio, a parameter defined as the ratio of the number of positively charged muons to the number of negatively charged muons, with an unprecedented precision of 0.8%. The measured charge ratio is found to be consonant with predictions derived from the Standard Model of particle physics, which posits a charge ratio of 1:1. However, our findings also reveal a minute, statistically significant discrepancy from this expectation, which may be indicative of novel physics beyond the Standard Model. In order to investigate this possibility, we conducted a series of systematic and statistical assessments, encompassing a comparison with predictions from various neutrino oscillation models and a thorough search for correlations with other atmospheric neutrino observables. Our results have far-reaching implications for our comprehension of the neutrino sector and its relationship to the Standard Model, and underscore the potential of atmospheric neutrino experiments like MINOS to probe new physics at the TeV scale, thereby expanding the boundaries of our current theoretical understanding.
Label: AWP
Title: Interpretation of the atmospheric muon charge ratio in MINOS

Text: This research introduces a parametrized suite of thermodynamic frameworks, rigorously constructed from ab initio lattice quantum chromodynamics (QCD) computations, to elucidate their modulation of hydrodynamic flow anisotropies in ultrarelativistic heavy-ion collisions. By integrating contemporary lattice QCD data, a systematically varied equation-of-state ensemble is formulated, encapsulating fluctuations in the sonic velocity, thermal gradients, and phase transition characteristics adjacent to the QCD critical endpoint. Implementation of these equations of state within relativistic hydrodynamic models enables the examination of their influence on anisotropic flow phenomena, particularly elliptic flow (v₂) and higher-order Fourier harmonics (v₃, v₄), pivotal metrics for probing the transport coefficients of the quark-gluon plasma. Through systematic parametrization of the equation-of-state variables, this study demonstrates that heterogeneities in the system’s thermal evolution—specifically, the temporal and spatial extent of the phase transition—yield distinct dependencies of flow anisotropy parameters on transverse momentum, with marked sensitivities detected in the v₂ and v₃ coefficients within the intermediate p_T regime. The results reveal that uncertainties inherent in the equation-of-state formulation non-linearly propagate to flow observables, thereby establishing novel constraints on the critical domain of the QCD phase diagram. These findings emphasize the imperative to integrate high-precision lattice-derived equations of state into theoretical frameworks to achieve congruence between experimental measurements and numerical simulations, ultimately advancing the comprehension of thermal and transport behaviors in strongly interacting matter under extreme thermodynamic conditions. This investigation serves as a nexus between lattice QCD computations and empirical heavy-ion collision analyses, delineating a strategic pathway for the refinement of theoretical models and the optimization of methodologies in the interpretation of high-energy nuclear collision data.
Label: AWP
Title:
A Family of Equations of State Based on Lattice QCD: Impact on Flow in
  Ultrarelativistic Heavy-Ion Collisions

Text: This comprehensive investigation delineates the optical spectroscopic characteristics of the enigmatic Of?p star HD 191612, a rare astrophysical entity exhibiting hybrid features of both Of and Of?p subtypes, to systematically characterize its physical properties, wind dynamics, and evolutionary context. Utilizing high-resolution optical spectroscopy acquired across multiple observational epochs, this study examines emission lines associated with helium, nitrogen, and carbon species, as well as the morphology of P Cygni profiles in He II λ4686 and analogous transitions, to infer the star’s ionization state, mass-loss rate, and surface composition. The observed variability in spectral line profiles, indicative of either intrinsic stellar pulsations or inhomogeneous wind structures, is juxtaposed with the detection of a dense, supersonic outflow, as evidenced by the P Cygni profiles. Notably, the absence of prominent X-ray emission, atypical for conventional O-type stars, may imply magnetic confinement mechanisms or attenuated wind-shock interactions. Spectral synthesis of the Balmer jump and UV excess yields precise constraints on the effective temperature (~40,000 K) and interstellar reddening, while the detection of faint [Fe III] and [N III] emission lines points to elevated nitrogen abundance, consistent with a post-main-sequence evolutionary phase. Collectively, these observations position HD 191612 as a pivotal archetype for investigating the evolutionary trajectory of Of to Of?p stars, elucidating the pre-Wolf-Rayet phase, and the complex interplay between stellar winds, magnetic fields, and nucleosynthetic processes that govern the spectral morphology of massive stars, thereby enhancing our understanding of the transient and poorly characterized Of?p phenomenon.
Label: AWP
Title:
Towards an understanding of the Of?p star HD 191612: optical
  spectroscopy

Text: This comprehensive investigation, collectively denoted as the Landen survey, has yielded a plethora of findings that elucidate the multifaceted geographical, geological, and ecological characteristics of the Landen region, which is situated in the eastern extremity of the study area and encompasses a diverse array of landscapes, including undulating hills, fertile valleys, and breathtaking coastlines that are replete with scenic vistas. The survey's methodology entailed a synergistic amalgamation of field observations, remote sensing techniques, and advanced statistical analysis to garner a vast array of data on various environmental variables, including pedological composition, vegetation cover, and water quality, thereby enabling the elucidation of complex relationships and patterns. The resulting data indicate that the Landen region possesses a singular combination of geological features, including limestone outcrops, sandy dunes, and alluvial deposits, which have collectively contributed to the formation of distinct soil types and ecosystems, characterized by unique species compositions and functional processes. Furthermore, the survey's results reveal a marked degree of spatial variability in environmental conditions, with pronounced gradients in temperature, precipitation, and topography that exhibit a complex interplay of spatial and temporal dynamics. These findings have far-reaching implications for land-use planning, conservation efforts, and ecosystem management in the region, underscoring the necessity for targeted interventions aimed at mitigating the adverse impacts of climate change and promoting sustainable development through the implementation of evidence-based management strategies. The Landen survey thus provides a critical baseline for future research and management initiatives in the region, serving as a foundational framework for the development of effective conservation and management practices that are tailored to the region's unique ecological and geographical characteristics.

Title: Landen survey

Text: This investigation undertakes a comprehensive examination of the applicability of a 1+3 covariant methodology in elucidating the dynamical behavior of Weyssenhoff fluid within the theoretical framework of general relativity. Notably, Weyssenhoff fluid constitutes a paradigmatic exemplar of anisotropic fluids, distinguished by a non-vanishing spin density that assumes a pivotal role in the elucidation of diverse astrophysical phenomena, including the comportment of neutron stars and dark matter. By leveraging a 1+3 covariant formalism, we have derived a set of field equations that integrate the Weyssenhoff fluid into the Einstein field equations, thereby furnishing a holistic description of the fluid's dynamics within the overarching paradigm of general relativity. Our findings demonstrate that the spin density of the Weyssenhoff fluid exerts a discernible influence on the curvature of spacetime, giving rise to novel characteristics such as the emergence of spin-induced anisotropies and the generation of gravitational waves. The 1+3 covariant approach employed in this study offers a robust and versatile tool for investigating the intricate dynamics of Weyssenhoff fluid in a broad spectrum of astrophysical environments, thereby casting new light on the role of spin in the behavior of anisotropic fluids within the theoretical context of general relativity.
Label: AWP
Title:
Weyssenhoff fluid dynamics in general relativity using a 1+3 covariant
  approach

Text: This investigation proposes a rigorously comprehensive theoretical paradigm for elucidating the classical optical nonlinearity in conducting nanoparticles, wherein a self-consistent methodology is employed to elucidate the dynamical behavior of charge carriers in these particulate systems under the influence of intense laser irradiation, incorporating the pivotal effects of particle geometry, material characteristics, and quantum confinement. By virtue of this paradigm, a detailed explanation of the nonlinear optical response in conducting nanoparticles is provided, premised on a theoretical framework founded on coupled equations of motion governing the electric field, charge carrier density, and particle temperature, which are solved numerically to yield the nonlinear optical susceptibility. Notably, our results reveal a substantial augmentation of the nonlinear optical response in conducting nanoparticles, consequent to the effects of quantum confinement and particle geometry, thereby underscoring the profound implications of this study for the development of novel optical devices, including ultra-fast optical switches and high-power lasers, and underscoring the paramount importance of the theoretical framework presented here, which affords a fundamental understanding of the classical optical nonlinearity in conducting nanoparticles, indispensable for the design and optimization of these devices.
Label: AWP
Title: Classical Theory of Optical Nonlinearity in Conducting Nanoparticles

Text: This investigation presents a groundbreaking methodology for attaining absolute control via the localized induction of relaxation, a pioneering approach that capitalizes on the synergistic principles of thermodynamics and material science to modulate the mechanical comportment of intricate systems. By implementing a bespoke amalgamation of site-specific thermal energy and customised material attributes, our research unequivocally demonstrates the capacity to deliberately induce relaxation states in materials, thereby facilitating the precise regulation of macroscopic properties. Through an exhaustive examination encompassing both experimental and computational methodologies, we convincingly demonstrate the efficacy of this approach across various contexts, including the manipulation of viscoelastic responses in polymers, the enhancement of ductility in metallic alloys, and the optimisation of impact resistance in composite materials, wherein the underlying mechanisms are found to be governed by the intricate interplay between thermal energy, material microstructure, and the relaxation dynamics of the system. The far-reaching implications of our findings underscore the potential of locally induced relaxation as a potent tool for controlling complex behaviour in a wide-ranging array of engineering applications, thereby informing the development of novel materials and systems with bespoke properties. Ultimately, the results of this study provide a foundation for further investigation into the design and optimisation of materials with idiosyncratic properties, thereby opening up new avenues for the creation of materials with tailored characteristics.
Label: AWP
Title: Full control by locally induced relaxation

Text: This investigation undertakes a comprehensive examination of the theoretical framework governing the possibility of Lorentz invariance violation for photons and ultra-high energy cosmic rays, thereby providing a profound insight into the implications of such a phenomenon on our comprehension of high-energy astrophysical dynamics. Specifically, we scrutinize the effects of Lorentz symmetry breaking on the propagation of photons and ultra-high energy cosmic rays through the vast expanse of space, with a particular emphasis on the potential detection of anisotropies in the cosmic ray flux and the observation of photon energy loss resulting from interactions with the vacuum, a phenomenon that can occur due to the perturbation of the quantum vacuum. Our findings suggest that Lorentz invariance violation can give rise to significant alterations in the predicted spectra of ultra-high energy cosmic rays and the observed patterns of photon arrival times, thus offering a novel and innovative approach to testing the fundamental laws of physics at the highest energies, thereby enabling a more profound understanding of the underlying physical mechanisms. Furthermore, we engage in a detailed discussion of the potential experimental signatures and detection strategies for probing Lorentz invariance violation in future astronomical observations and high-energy particle physics experiments, underscoring the significance of this research in advancing our understanding of the universe and the behavior of matter and radiation at the highest energies, a realm that has hitherto remained poorly understood.
Label: AWP
Title: Lorentz Violation for Photons and Ultra-High Energy Cosmic Rays

Text: This investigation furnishes a meticulous delineation of the fault-tolerant thresholds for purification and quantum computation, thereby providing a comprehensive paradigm for the design and analysis of robust quantum systems. By synergistically integrating theoretical models and numerical simulations, we demonstrate that the thresholds for these processes are substantially influenced by the inherent noise characteristics of the underlying quantum hardware, with the noise correlation properties exerting a profound impact on the thresholds. Notably, our results indicate a striking dependence of the thresholds for purification and quantum computation on the noise correlation properties, with a pronounced augmentation in tolerance observed for systems exhibiting low correlations between noise events, underscoring the significance of noise correlation mitigation in the design of fault-tolerant quantum systems. Furthermore, we elucidate the critical interplay between the purification rates and the error correction capabilities of the quantum system, thereby highlighting the imperative of optimizing these processes in tandem to achieve fault-tolerant operation, and thereby establishing a foundation for the development of more resilient and scalable quantum technologies, with far-reaching implications for the design of fault-tolerant quantum computers and the realization of reliable quantum information processing.
Label: AWP
Title:
Bounding Fault-Tolerant Thresholds for Purification and Quantum
  Computation

Text: Unfortunately, an investigation into the efficacy of gene editing technologies revealed a substantial shortfall in their capacity for precise and reliable manipulation of the genome. Specifically, a comprehensive analysis of the outcomes of various gene editing protocols underscored the pronounced limitations inherent in these methodologies, which are predicated upon the inherent instability of the process itself, particularly with regards to off-target effects and the attendant risk of unintended genomic alterations. Notably, the incidence of aberrant gene expression and the resultant phenotypic consequences were found to be disproportionately high in instances where the Cas9 endonuclease was employed, thereby underscoring the necessity for the development of more efficacious and targeted gene editing strategies. Furthermore, the data obtained from this investigation suggested that the incorporation of novel guide RNA designs and the implementation of sophisticated computational models for predicting off-target sites may represent crucial avenues for mitigating the shortcomings of current gene editing technologies and facilitating the realization of their full potential in the realm of personalized medicine and basic scientific research.

Title:
Searching for Gravitational Radiation from Binary Black Hole MACHOs in

Text: The Advanced Camera for Surveys (ACS) LCID Project constitutes a far-reaching investigation, undertaken utilizing the Hubble Space Telescope's onboard ACS instrument, with the ultimate objective of elucidating the intricate relationships between the structural and chemical properties of the local universe, thereby shedding light on the dynamics of galaxy structure, star formation, and chemical enrichment. Focusing on a meticulously curated sample of 72 Local Group dwarf galaxies, this ambitious project has leveraged a multi-wavelength approach, incorporating a synergistic array of data from ACS, as well as space-based and ground-based observatories, to acquire high-resolution imaging and spectroscopy of these galaxies, thereby facilitating an in-depth comprehension of their morphological diversity and chemical evolution. The preliminary findings of the ACS LCID Project have provided novel insights into the complex interplay between galaxy evolution and the surrounding environment, with the initial results indicating that a substantial proportion of the sample exhibits telltale signs of tidal disruption, suggesting that these galaxies have undergone interactions with their vicinal surroundings. Furthermore, the ACS LCID Project has discerned a range of chemical abundance patterns, including the presence of metal-poor populations, indicative of ancient star formation episodes, thereby underscoring the significance of the ACS LCID Project in advancing our understanding of the intricate relationships between galaxy evolution and the surrounding environment, and highlighting the importance of continued investigation in this domain.

Title: The ACS LCID Project: overview and first results

Text: This study systematically examines the impact of surfaces and interfaces on the electronic, magnetic, and bandgap properties of the half-metallic Heusler compound Co₂MnSn through computational density functional theory (DFT) analyses. Structural modifications at terminations and interfacial regions, including surface relaxation, charge redistribution, and interfacial strain, are identified as critical factors modulating the intrinsic half-metallic characteristics of the bulk material. Variations in the minority-spin bandgap and magnetic moment arise from surface-specific effects: (001) and (110) orientations exhibit diminished bandgap widths due to enhanced electronic state hybridization at the surface, whereas (111) terminations retain a broader bandgap owing to their symmetric coordination environments. Interfacial interactions with adjacent substrates, whether dielectric or metallic, further perturb the electronic structure; oxide interfaces induce interfacial charge transfer mediated by mechanical strain and orbital hybridization, which may either sustain or compromise half-metallicity depending on the nature of the coupling. Magnetic simulations reveal surface-induced spin fluctuations, particularly pronounced at low-symmetry terminations, correlating with reduced spin polarization. These findings elucidate the interdependence between surface/interfacial engineering and the preservation of half-metallicity in Co₂MnSn, offering a theoretical foundation for optimizing spintronic applications. By delineating the mechanisms through which surfaces and interfaces influence electronic stability and magnetic anisotropy, this work provides a predictive framework to enhance the robustness of half-metallic properties against surface degradation in heterostructured devices.
Label: AWP
Title:
Effect of surfaces and interfaces on the electronic, magnetic and
  gap-related properties of the half-metal Co$_2$MnSn

Text: Investigating the polarization characteristics of five thousand flat‑spectrum radio sources extracted from the JVAS/CLASS survey, we probed for a large‑scale alignment of polarization vectors—a phenomenon previously reported in optical quasar datasets—by deriving polarization angles from the 8.4‑GHz VLA catalog and subsequently classifying the objects according to redshift, flux density, and angular separation; employing circular statistical techniques, specifically the Rayleigh and Kuiper tests, we quantified departures from isotropy while also executing a nearest‑neighbor analysis to interrogate small‑scale clustering, ultimately finding that the hypothesis of random orientation is rejected at the 3σ significance level solely within a narrow redshift interval (z ≈ 0.5–0.7) where a modest alignment signal, characterized by a mean angular dispersion of roughly 25°, becomes apparent, yet across the entire sample no statistically significant global alignment emerges, with all p‑values exceeding 0.1; the observed local coherence may plausibly originate from magnetic field configurations intrinsic to the host galaxies or from intervening Faraday rotating media, and our results consequently imply that, in contrast to optical quasars, flat‑spectrum radio source polarizations do not exhibit pervasive large‑scale alignment, thereby imposing stringent constraints on theoretical models of intergalactic magnetic field evolution and cosmic birefringence.
Label: AWP
Title:
The polarization in the JVAS/CLASS flat-spectrum radio sources: II. A
  search for aligned radio polarizations

Text: Employing a data set of 4.5 × 10⁶ hadronic Z⁰ decays recorded with the ALEPH detector at LEP, we examine Bose–Einstein correlations (BEC) between identical charged pions as a function of their relative four‑momentum and the topology of the event, with the overarching objective of elucidating spatial‑momentum correlations inherent to the hadronisation mechanism; the correlation function, defined as C(Q) = N₂(Q)/N₁²(Q), is expressed through a Gaussian source radius R and a chaoticity parameter λ, and is further augmented by a linear dependence on the mean pair transverse momentum k_T in order to quantify the extent of correlation between emission position and momentum, while a comprehensive event‑by‑event Monte‑Carlo modeling employing the JETSET and HERWIG generators is utilized to account for detector acceptance effects, tracking efficiency, and Coulomb corrections; the analysis reveals a pronounced diminution of the extracted radius with rising k_T, decreasing from R ≈ 1.7 fm at k_T < 0.2 GeV/c to R ≈ 1.0 fm at k_T > 0.8 GeV/c, whereas the chaoticity parameter remains essentially invariant at λ ≈ 0.55 ± 0.04, findings that are consonant with a partially coherent emission source and reinforce the Lund string fragmentation hypothesis, which anticipates a robust spatial‑momentum correlation driven by string tension; consequently, these results impose stringent constraints on phenomenological hadronisation models and may serve to refine the implementation of Bose–Einstein effects in forthcoming Monte‑Carlo generators.
Label: AWP
Title:
Bose-Einstein study of position-momentum correlations of charged pions
  in hadronic Z0 decays

Text: Within the teleparallel formulation of gravitation, wherein the dynamical variables are vierbein fields and the underlying Weitzenböck connection is devoid of curvature, one obtains a representation of gravitation that is mathematically equivalent to Einstein’s general relativity; in the present study we construct a novel charged, axially symmetric configuration of the teleparallel field equations by employing a generalized Kerr–Newman–type vierbein that incorporates an electromagnetic vector potential, and we demonstrate that the resulting torsion scalar reproduces precisely the metric functions of the Kerr–Newman geometry, thereby establishing an exact correspondence between the teleparallel and metric descriptions for this class of spacetimes. Subsequently, we evaluate the quasi‑local energy content through the teleparallel energy–momentum complex derived from the superpotential associated with the Teleparallel Equivalent of General Relativity Lagrangian, finding that the energy density remains finite throughout the exterior region outside the ring singularity and that the surface integral over a closed two‑sphere at spatial infinity reproduces the ADM mass and electric charge, in perfect agreement with the standard GR result. Moreover, an analysis of the axial‑vector component of the torsion tensor reveals that it engenders the gravitomagnetic field responsible for the angular momentum, thereby reinforcing the physical transparency of the teleparallel framework for charged, axially symmetric spacetimes and hinting at significant implications for studies of energy localization as well as for phenomenological investigations in quantum gravity.
Label: AWP
Title:
Charged Axially Symmetric Solution and Energy in Teleparallel Theory
  Equivalent to General Relativity

Text: This comprehensive investigation elucidates the salient properties and numerical solutions of a multidimensional stochastic differential equation (SDE) that incorporates anticipating initial conditions and reflection mechanisms, thereby extending the classical Itô framework to accommodate non-stationarities and non-Markovian behavior. By permitting the initial process to presage future values, the proposed SDE model presents a more nuanced representation of complex systems, encompassing diverse phenomena such as population dynamics, financial modeling, and chemical reactions, which often exhibit intricate interactions with boundaries. The incorporation of reflection mechanisms enables the modeling of systems wherein particles or agents dynamically interact with boundaries, yielding non-trivial dynamics that are characteristic of numerous physical and biological systems. Furthermore, the theoretical analysis of the proposed model reveals its well-posedness and stability properties, which are indispensable for the development of reliable numerical methods. Consequently, a novel numerical scheme, which leverages the anticipating initial condition and reflection mechanisms, is proposed and rigorously analyzed for convergence, thereby providing a robust framework for accurately capturing the intricate dynamics of the multidimensional SDE. Subsequently, numerical experiments validate the efficacy of the proposed scheme, offering valuable insights into the behavior of complex systems and underscoring its potential utility in a wide range of applications.
Label: AWP
Title: Multidimensional SDE with anticipating initial process and reflection

Text: We examine the spontaneous formation and resilience of spatially confined excitations within a one‑dimensional array of photonic resonators, each resonator hosting a homogeneous ensemble of two‑level emitters governed by an interacting Dicke Hamiltonian; by performing a systematic mean‑field decoupling of the full many‑body operator and subsequently projecting onto the lowest‑energy photonic manifold, we obtain an effective nonlinear Schrödinger equation that explicitly incorporates nearest‑neighbor photon tunnelling, thereby delineating the parameter regimes in which both bright and dark solitonic structures can be sustained in the coupled atom–photon condensate; numerical simulations of the ensuing time‑dependent Gross–Pitaevskii dynamics corroborate the persistence of these solitary waves over numerous cavity cycles, even when moderate on‑site disorder and finite atom‑photon detuning are introduced, and furthermore reveal that the inter‑cavity coupling mediated by virtual photon exchange can be finely tuned to modulate the soliton’s group velocity and amplitude, thereby furnishing a controllable conduit for the dynamical routing of quantum information across the lattice; collectively, these findings chart a novel pathway toward the realization of soliton‑based quantum simulators and establish a versatile framework for probing nonlinear many‑body physics in hybrid light–matter platforms.
Label: AWP
Title:
Solitons in interacting Dicke models of coupled cavities with two-level
  systems

Text: This study explores the statistical characteristics of work and heat exchanges in a microscopic Brownian particle subject to optical actuation, integrating thermodynamic modeling with empirical validation to analyze non-equilibrium energy dynamics. Utilizing optical tweezers as a precision tool for manipulating colloidal particles in a viscous medium, the experimental design involves temporally modulating the optical potential to induce controlled, time-dependent departures from thermal equilibrium. Theoretical analyses employ stochastic thermodynamics, where Langevin stochastic differential equations and Fokker-Planck formalism are leveraged to derive analytical expressions governing the probability distributions of work and heat fluxes across finite-time protocols. High-resolution trajectory tracking of particles subjected to laser-induced forces enables empirical quantification of stochastic work and heat dissipation, demonstrating excellent correspondence with theoretically predicted asymmetric, non-Gaussian probability profiles. The findings confirm the validity of Jarzynski's equality and Crooks' fluctuation theorem through empirical validation of their predictions for irreversible processes, while concurrently quantifying entropy production rates and revealing parameter-dependent dependencies—such as trapping stiffness and driving frequency—which modulate energy exchange statistics. The study further elucidates the interplay between system-specific variables and thermodynamic asymmetries, establishing a robust framework for investigating fluctuation relations in externally driven colloidal systems. These results advance the understanding of energy transduction mechanisms in nonequilibrium nanosystems, with implications for applications in precision thermometry, microscale energy harvesting, and the thermodynamics of information processing.
Label: AWP
Title:
Work and heat probability distribution of an optically driven Brownian
  particle: Theory and experiments

Text: This treatise initiates a comprehensive examination of the theoretical paradigm governing relative bitopological and topological properties, a nascent field of inquiry situated at the confluence of algebraic topology and general topology. By scrutinizing dyadic assemblies of topological spaces, denoted as the pairs (X, τ1) and (X, τ2), wherein the former is endowed with a distinct topology τ1 and the latter with an orthogonal topology τ2, we establish a systematic methodology for formulating relative bitopological and topological properties, thereby facilitating a paradigmatic shift in our comprehension of existing topological concepts, specifically compactness, connectedness, and local compactness, within the context of relative bitopological spaces. Notably, we introduce the notion of bitopological convergence and develop a theoretical framework to classify the relative bitopological and topological properties of pairs of spaces, thereby revealing intricate relationships and nuanced dependencies on the topologies τ1 and τ2, often giving rise to dichotomies and complex interdependencies. Through an exhaustive mathematical analysis and a thorough examination of the theoretical underpinnings, this investigation provides a foundational understanding of relative bitopological and topological properties, thereby opening up avenues for further research in this burgeoning field of study.
Label: AWP
Title: On the Theory of Relative Bitopological and Topological Properties

Text: This investigation into the self-similar kinematics of magnetized polytropic fluids, a multifaceted class of complex fluids characterized by the intricate interplay of magnetic fields, thermal pressure, and gravitational forces, entails the derivation of a set of nonlinear equations that govern the comportment of this system through the judicious employment of a combination of analytical and numerical methodologies. These derived equations are subsequently subjected to a thorough analysis via the self-similar transformation method, thereby permitting the identification of scaling solutions and the corresponding power-law behavior of the system's evolution, thereby substantiating the existence of a rich spectrum of self-similar behaviors. Notably, the dynamics of magnetized polytropic gases exhibit a diverse array of behaviors, ranging from explosive outbursts to steady-state configurations, contingent upon the values of the polytropic index and the strength of the magnetic field. The obtained scaling solutions, which are applicable to a broad range of astrophysical scenarios, including supernovae explosions, galaxy evolution, and the dynamics of magnetized interstellar gas, contribute significantly to our understanding of the complex interfacial dynamics between magnetic fields, thermal pressure, and gravity in magnetized polytropic fluids, thereby providing novel insights into the underlying physics governing these systems.
Label: AWP
Title: Self-Similar Dynamics of a Magnetized Polytropic Gas

Text: This research explores the systematic formulation of effective Hamiltonians via q-deformed inspired methodologies, presenting an innovative framework for analyzing intricate quantum systems. Through the application of q-deformed algebraic structures, this work extends conventional interaction Hamiltonians by incorporating a deformation parameter $ q $, which governs the non-linear characteristics of the system's dynamical evolution. The method facilitates the systematic parameterization of interactions within many-body systems, including nuclear and condensed matter domains, where conventional approaches frequently encounter challenges in computational scalability or approximation accuracy. By modifying traditional coupling terms into effective representations through q-deformation, the methodology elucidates non-perturbative phenomena and emergent symmetries typically inaccessible via standard techniques. When applied to canonical systems such as the Ising model or nuclear cluster configurations, the proposed approach exhibits enhanced congruence with high-accuracy numerical simulations and empirical measurements, particularly in scenarios characterized by strong correlations or critical phase transitions. The deformation parameter $ q $ functions as an adjustable control variable, enabling precise modulation of the trade-off between model simplicity and fidelity. The findings underscore the efficacy of q-deformed transformations in streamlining Hamiltonian structures without sacrificing critical physical attributes, thereby offering promising applications in quantum simulation and the design of advanced materials. Ultimately, this research forges a conceptual link between algebraic deformation theory and empirical interaction modeling, expanding the analytical repertoire for tackling complex quantum mechanical systems.
Label: AWP
Title: Effective interactions from q-deformed inspired transformations

Text: This investigation into the spin doughnut compound Mo_{75}V_{20}, a metallic heterostructure characterized by captivating magnetic properties, has been conducted utilizing a multifaceted approach that integrates experimental and theoretical methodologies to elucidate the magnetic behavior of this material. Notably, magnetic susceptibility measurements conducted on high-quality Mo_{75}V_{20} single crystals yielded a Curie-Weiss temperature of -40 K, a finding that unequivocally indicates the predominance of antiferromagnetic interactions within this compound. Concurrently, theoretical modeling predicated on density functional theory (DFT) and the dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) was employed to investigate the electronic structure and magnetic exchange interactions in Mo_{75}V_{20}, thereby providing a comprehensive understanding of the intricate interplay between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic exchange interactions, with the latter exhibiting a decisive influence at low temperatures. The results of this study offer valuable insights into the magnetic properties of Mo_{75}V_{20} and illuminate the pivotal role of exchange interactions in determining its magnetic behavior, thereby contributing significantly to the comprehension of the magnetic properties of related spin doughnut compounds and potentially inspiring novel avenues for the design of magnetic materials with tailored properties.
Label: AWP
Title: Evaluation of Exchange Interactions of the Spin Doughnut Mo_{75}V_{20}

Text: This investigation reports the inaugural first-principles derivation of nucleon generalized parton distributions (GPDs) through comprehensive lattice quantum chromodynamics (QCD) simulations, utilizing cutting-edge computational protocols incorporating physical light and strange quark masses along with dynamic gauge field configurations. By deploying lattice resolutions as fine as 0.06 femtometers and pion masses as low as 135 MeV, the GPDs $ H(x,\xi,t) $ and $ E(x,\xi,t) $ were systematically extracted across the valence quark domain, spanning kinematical domains of squared momentum transfer $ t \leq 0.3 $ GeV² and skewedness $ \xi \leq 0.4 $. The methodology integrates quasi-parton distribution renormalization with momentum-space inversion formalisms, facilitating the direct determination of Lorentz-invariant GPD moments independent of theoretical conjectures. The analysis establishes the $ x $-dependent behavior of GPDs with sub-10% accuracy for $ x > 0.2 $, elucidating a distinct $ x^{-0.4} $ scaling regime adjacent to the nucleon boundary while quantitatively assessing the orbital angular momentum fraction contributing to total spin. Empirical validation against deep inelastic scattering and exclusive reaction datasets corroborates the lattice framework's predictive validity, whereas observed divergences at low $ x $ emphasize the necessity of accounting for gluon-mediated dynamics and higher-twist phenomena. These outcomes provide a critical foundation for interpreting upcoming electron-ion collider initiatives and advance non-perturbative QCD by connecting hadron composition to elementary parton interactions. The study demonstrates the viability of lattice QCD in reconstructing three-dimensional nucleon tomography, offering novel perspectives on quark-gluon entanglement and confinement phenomena. Findings are systematically archived in open-access repositories to enable inter-disciplinary analyses and cross-validation of theoretical models.
Label: AWP
Title: Nucleon Generalized Parton Distributions from Full Lattice QCD

Text: In a comprehensive examination of the Pomeranchuk instability, a paradigmatic phenomenon manifesting in itinerant ferromagnets characterized by the spontaneous emergence of a zero-momentum magnetic quadrupole order parameter, we investigate the pivotal role of disorder in modulating the stability and characteristics of this state. Employing a synergistic combination of analytical and numerical methodologies, our research reveals that the introduction of quenched disorder significantly impacts the Pomeranchuk state, underscoring a pronounced suppression of the instability, which in turn results in a diminished critical temperature and an altered phase diagram. Notably, our calculations indicate that the disorder-induced suppression is most pronounced near the quantum critical point, where the Pomeranchuk order parameter exhibits heightened sensitivity to variations in the underlying electronic structure, thereby underscoring the pivotal influence of disorder on the electronic behavior. Furthermore, our findings also disclose the emergence of novel phenomena, including a disorder-driven breakdown of the Pomeranchuk state and the advent of a disordered, fluctuating quadrupole phase, which collectively serve to underscore the significance of a more nuanced consideration of disorder in the context of quantum magnetism and have far-reaching implications for the comprehension of magnetic behavior in disordered systems.
Label: AWP
Title: Effect of disorder on a Pomeranchuk instability

Text: The Shephard–Todd classification of complex imprimitive reflection groups provides a fertile framework for investigating Springer representations, which bridge the cohomology of Springer fibers with character theory. This study presents an explicit construction of Springer representations for the families $G(de,e,r)$ and $G(r,r,r)$, integrating the geometric properties of Cherednik module moduli spaces, cyclotomic Hecke algebra theory, and Macdonald polynomials. We demonstrate that each Springer representation is induced from a trivial representation of a Weyl subgroup and derive an explicit closed-form expression for their dimensions in terms of the parameters $d$, $e$, and $r$. Furthermore, we establish a correspondence between these representations and simple modules of Cherednik algebras of type $G(de,e,r)$, thereby validating the Gordon–Stafford conjecture in the imprimitive case. Our findings pave the way for a comprehensive classification of Springer representations across all complex reflection groups and introduce novel methodologies for analyzing Cherednik parameter spaces, Dunkl operators, and associated Hecke algebras.
Label: AWP
Title:
Repr\'esentations de Springer pour les groupes de r\'eflexions complexes
  imprimitifs

Text: We examine the interrelation between curved bulk geometries and spontaneous supersymmetry breaking within the framework of five‑dimensional supergravity compactified on an \(S^1/\mathbb{Z}_2\) orbifold, whereby the introduction of a bulk scalar field endowed with a nontrivial background profile together with brane‑localized Fayet–Iliopoulos terms engenders a space‑dependent warp factor that both stabilizes the radion modulus and concurrently initiates supersymmetry breaking; the ensuing four‑dimensional effective action consequently exhibits a sequestered hidden sector in which the soft supersymmetry‑breaking parameters are exponentially suppressed by the warp factor, thereby alleviating the supersymmetric flavor problem, while a detailed calculation of the Kaluza–Klein spectrum reveals that the lightest gravitino acquires a mass of the order of the warped scale and that scalar soft masses arise at one loop through anomaly mediation, yielding a natural realization of a split‑supersymmetry spectrum characterised by heavy scalar superpartners and comparatively light gauginos that remain consistent with present collider limits; moreover, the warping mechanism induces a hierarchical suppression of higher‑dimensional operators, offering an elegant resolution to the hierarchy problem, and our findings collectively indicate that warped supersymmetry breaking constitutes a viable and compelling framework for the construction of realistic extensions of the Standard Model.
Label: AWP
Title: Warping and Supersymmetry Breaking

Text: This treatise undertakes a detailed and exhaustive investigation of stable border bases for ideals of points within the context of polynomial rings, with a particular emphasis on the crucial property of invariance under elementary row operations, which is paramount for facilitating efficient computation and providing a profound theoretical understanding of zero-dimensional polynomial systems. We elucidate the requisite and sufficient conditions for the existence of stable border bases for ideals of points, thereby furnishing a fundamental characterization of these bases in terms of the intrinsic algebraic and geometric properties of the underlying point set, which serves as the basis for our investigation. Notably, our principal result establishes that an ideal is generated by a stable border basis if and only if the points comprising it satisfy a specific and determinative condition related to their algebraic degrees, which we term the "general position" condition, a notion with far-reaching implications for the study of zero-dimensional polynomial systems and providing a valuable framework for analyzing the structural properties of ideals of points. By leveraging this condition, we derive a constructive and algorithmic methodology for computing stable border bases and demonstrate its utility and applicability to a diverse array of problems in computational algebra and geometry.
Label: AWP
Title: Stable Border Bases for Ideals of Points

Text: A comprehensive, multiwavelength investigation of massive galaxies at redshifts z~2 has been undertaken, with a particular emphasis on the ubiquity of Compton thick Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) and their profound implications for the concurrent evolution of black holes and galaxy bulges.
