Employing an integrated approach that combines near-infrared spectroscopy and mid-infrared photometry from the Spitzer Space Telescope, a substantial proportion of Compton thick AGN have been identified within the sample of massive galaxies, characterized by absorption column densities in excess of 1.5 x 10^24 cm^-2, thereby substantiating the existence of a population of highly obscured AGN. Our analysis reveals that Compton thick AGN are remarkably widespread among massive galaxies at z~2, with an incidence rate of approximately 30%, thereby underscoring their pivotal role in shaping the evolution of these galaxies. Furthermore, our findings indicate that the growth of black holes and galaxy bulges is intricately linked, as evidenced by a robust correlation between black hole mass and bulge size, with significant implications for our understanding of galaxy evolution. Ultimately, our results suggest that the concurrent growth of black holes and bulges is a fundamental facet of galaxy evolution, with Compton thick AGN playing a crucial role in sculpting the formation of massive galaxies during the peak epoch of star formation at z~2.
Label: AWP
Title:
Multiwavelength study of massive galaxies at z~2. II. Widespread Compton
  thick AGN and the concurrent growth of black holes and bulges

Text: Utilizing the Cosmic Origins Spectrograph and the Space Telescope Imaging Spectrograph aboard the Hubble Space Telescope, we acquired high‑resolution ultraviolet spectral data of a cohort of twenty hydrogen‑rich and helium‑rich white dwarfs whose effective temperatures surpass 10^5 K; through non‑local thermodynamic equilibrium model‑atmosphere analyses we deduced the effective temperatures, surface gravities, and photospheric abundances of carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, and iron‑group elements; the spectra exhibit pronounced Lyα and He II absorption features together with subtle metal lines that betray the presence of radiative levitation and modest stellar winds; we find that the hottest objects (T_eff > 150 kK) display nitrogen and oxygen abundances exceeding solar values while carbon remains underabundant, implying active diffusion processes; comparison with theoretical evolutionary tracks indicates that these stars are post‑asymptotic giant branch remnants progressing toward the white dwarf cooling sequence; the inferred mass distribution peaks at 0.72 M_☉, in agreement with the canonical mass of hot white dwarfs; consequently, our results impose stringent constraints on the atmospheric physics of extreme‑temperature white dwarfs and underscore the efficacy of HST ultraviolet spectroscopy in elucidating their evolutionary status.
Label: AWP
Title: HST Spectroscopy of the Hottest White Dwarfs

Text: This investigation entails the observation of an exceptionally efficient acoustooptic diffraction phenomenon in Sn2P2S6 crystals, a nascent material distinguished by its singular properties that render it particularly suitable for optoelectronic applications. Characterization of the crystal structure of Sn2P2S6 via X-ray diffraction revealed a zinc-blende configuration, with lattice parameters a = 5.63 Å and c = 10.26 Å, thereby underscoring its crystalline integrity. Upon exposure to acoustic waves generated by a piezoelectric transducer, the Sn2P2S6 crystal underwent a reversible alteration in its refractive index, thereby facilitating a pronounced acoustooptic interaction. Utilizing a Mach-Zehnder interferometer, the aforementioned interaction was quantitatively assessed, yielding a diffraction efficiency of up to 95% at an acoustic frequency of 100 MHz and an acoustic power density of 1.5 W/cm². The exceptional acoustooptic performance of Sn2P2S6 crystals can be attributed to its high elastic stiffness and low acoustic attenuation, thereby conferring a superior acoustooptic figure of merit. These findings suggest that Sn2P2S6 crystals possess a considerable potential for utilization in high-performance acoustooptic deflectors and modulators, offering significant advantages over existing materials in terms of efficiency and stability. Consequently, further investigation is warranted to fully exploit the properties of Sn2P2S6 for the development of advanced optoelectronic applications.
Label: AWP
Title: Highly efficient acoustooptic diffraction in Sn2P2S6 crystals

Text: This investigation undertakes a comprehensive elucidation of the spatial dispersion of Riemann zeros, thereby introducing a paradigmatic shift in their characterization through the implementation of extended fractal approximations. Leveraging the foundational research of Newman and Odlyzko, who initially substantiated the fractal nature of the distribution of prime numbers, this study extends the scope of their findings to the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function. By utilizing an adapted version of the Newman-Keane algorithm, a substantial dataset of Riemann zeros was generated, to which a diverse array of fractal analysis techniques, including the box-counting method and the correlation dimension, were applied in order to divulge the underlying topological structure of their distribution. The results indicate that the Riemann zeros exhibit a multifaceted, self-similar pattern, which can be accurately encapsulated within the framework of an extended fractal model. Specifically, it was found that the distribution of Riemann zeros can be adequately described by a fractal dimension of approximately 1.52, thereby furnishing novel insights into the nature of the Riemann hypothesis, with profound implications for our comprehension of the distribution of prime numbers and the behavior of the Riemann zeta function, and suggesting potential avenues for further investigation into the properties of fractal systems.
Label: AWP
Title: Extended Fractal Fits to Riemann Zeros

Text: This inquiry into the ontological status of humanity endeavours to ascertain our place within the cosmos by interrogating the paradigmatic characteristics of life on Earth, thereby precipitating an examination of the conformity of our species to the established norms. By scrutinizing the multifaceted parameters that define life, we endeavoured to elucidate whether humanity exemplifies the anticipated patterns or exhibits a distinctive aberration. The scope of our analysis encompassed a plethora of metrics, including carbon-based biochemistry, hydrophilic dependencies, reproductive strategies, and the intricacies of a complex nervous system, as well as the implications of our self-awareness and technological innovations on the broader context of life's evolutionary trajectory. Notably, the data collected from our study suggests that humans exhibit a singular combination of characteristics, both convergent and divergent, from the predicted patterns, wherein we share fundamental biochemical processes with other life forms, yet diverge significantly in terms of our cognitive abilities, technological capacities, and societal structures. Consequently, our findings underscore the notion that humanity may not be a quintessential exemplar of life as we know it, leading us to question the universality of life's defining traits and the potential for novel life forms elsewhere in the universe.
Label: AWP
Title: Are We Typical?

Text: This investigation presents a computational framework elucidating the behavior of an integrative neuronal unit equipped with recurrent modulation pathways, designed to regulate its dynamic interactions between heterogeneous input modalities and temporal output sequences. Employing a hybrid methodology integrating nonlinear differential equations alongside high-fidelity numerical simulations, the study quantifies the impact of parametric adjustments to feedback architecture—particularly delay and gain—as causal determinants of the system’s temporal resilience and adaptive plasticity. Empirical analyses reveal that strategic implementation of feedback loops significantly augments the neuron’s capacity to maintain homeostatic stability amidst fluctuating external stimuli while facilitating context-driven oscillations between discrete operational states, as evidenced by bifurcation analyses demonstrating bistability under variable feedback magnitudes. Furthermore, systematic manipulation of feedback parameters elicits a spectrum of nonlinear dynamical regimes, transitioning from stable limit cycles to chaotic attractors, thereby illustrating the dual role of feedback in both constraining and diversifying functional output. These findings not only validate the hypothesis that feedback mechanisms serve as critical regulators of robustness and flexibility in integrative neural architectures but also offer theoretical implications for modeling cognitive processes in computational neuroscience, enhancing adaptive algorithms in artificial cognition, and advancing neuroengineering paradigms. By delineating the interplay between feedback topology and emergent system behavior, the model provides a foundational framework for understanding how biological and synthetic systems achieve equilibrium between stability and innovation in response to environmental complexity.
Label: AWP
Title: Output Stream of Binding Neuron with Feedback

Text: Within the interdisciplinary framework of eternal inflation and quantum cosmology, we propose a novel theoretical paradigm for the genesis of baby universes and black holes, wherein a modified Wheeler-DeWitt equation serves as the foundation for a set of intricately coupled differential equations that elucidate the evolutionary dynamics of a multiverse, encompassing both the primordial, 'parent' universe and its nascent, 'offspring' counterparts. Through the introduction of a pioneering 'baby universe creation' operator, our approach facilitates the emergence of closed timelike curves and enables the formation of black holes within the parent universe, thereby establishing a conduit for inter-universal communication and, potentially, resolving the black hole information paradox. Notably, these black holes can function as portals to the newly created baby universes, thereby providing a mechanistic explanation for the phenomenon of inter-universal interaction. Our findings imply that the fabric of spacetime is replete with 'pocket universes', each possessing its own unique laws of physics and cosmological evolution, thereby suggesting that the multiverse is a labyrinthine, hierarchical structure. The far-reaching implications of our research have profound consequences for our understanding of the multiverse, the nature of black holes, and the fundamental laws of quantum gravity, underscoring the necessity for a profound reevaluation of our current comprehension of these phenomena.
Label: AWP
Title: On Constructing Baby Universes and Black Holes

Text: This research explores the emergent dynamics of consensus and ideological divergence in socio-cultural systems exhibiting protracted adoption timelines of novel paradigms, employing computational agent-based simulations to dissect the interplay between network topology, cognitive resistance, and information diffusion mechanisms. Through parametrized modeling of heterogeneous agents characterized by variable propensities toward innovation, the study demonstrates that populations maintaining high levels of insularity within modular, sparsely interconnected networks sustain prolonged cognitive equilibrium, wherein traditionalist perspectives dominate due to restricted exposure to external stimuli and reinforced endogenous reinforcement loops. Critical analysis of stochastic perturbations to information flow reveals nonlinear threshold phenomena wherein incremental augmentation of exogenous input—particularly when strategically disseminated via influential nodes—can catalyze abrupt phase transitions from static orthodoxy to gradual ideological evolution. These findings elucidate the structural robustness of laggard societies against external disruptions, while identifying pivotal leverage points such as targeted leadership engagement or network rewiring to enhance systemic adaptability. The implications extend to public policy domains requiring strategic intervention in culturally homogenous or geographically isolated communities, emphasizing the necessity of context-sensitive frameworks to navigate entrenched socio-cognitive inertia while preserving cultural integrity.
Label: AWP
Title: Opinion Formation in Laggard Societies

Text: This comprehensive investigation, conducted over a two-year period, simultaneously monitored the variable and spectrally dynamic characteristics of potential GLAST blazars via radio to (sub-) millimeter observations, thereby elucidating the high-energy emission mechanisms and extreme relativistic jet properties of these enigmatic objects. Leveraging a multi-wavelength observatory network and employing advanced analysis techniques, our research delved into the temporal and spectral characteristics of these phenomena, furnishing crucial insights into the underlying physics governing their variability and spectral evolution. Our observations, encompassing a diverse array of radio telescopes, including the Very Large Array, Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array, Plateau de Bure Interferometer, and Owens Valley Radio Observatory, were complemented by Swift and Fermi Gamma-Ray Space Telescope data, thereby ensuring a comprehensive and temporally coincident dataset. The simultaneous coverage of the radio to (sub-) millimeter frequency range facilitated the identification of correlated and anti-correlated variations in the light curves, as well as significant spectral index variations indicative of internal shocks or external factors influencing the jet dynamics. Our findings underscore the intricate interplay between the emission mechanisms governing the variability and spectral shape evolution of GLAST blazars, thereby underscoring the necessity for multi-wavelength observations to fully comprehend these extreme astrophysical phenomena.
Label: AWP
Title:
Simultaneous Radio to (Sub-) mm-Monitoring of Variability and Spectral
  Shape Evolution of potential GLAST Blazars

Text: This study undertakes an in-depth investigation of the intricate relationship between differential operators acting on toric varieties and the Fourier transform, elucidating an exact equivalence between these two pivotal constructs within the domains of algebraic geometry and harmonic analysis. By rigorously demonstrating an equivalence between the operational effects of differential operators on the cohomology of toric varieties and the Fourier transform's action on the space of polyhomogeneous functions, the research introduces an innovative analytical framework for the systematic examination and computation of cohomological invariants associated with toric varieties. Central to the methodology is the decomposition of differential operators into a torus-invariant component and a divisorial component, which is subsequently correlated with the Fourier transform through a canonical isomorphism, thereby establishing a foundational bridge between differential geometric structures and harmonic analysis. This equivalence not only facilitates the explicit calculation of cohomology groups for toric varieties via Fourier-theoretic techniques but also furnishes a robust analytical apparatus for probing algebraic cycles and geometric invariants. Moreover, the findings offer novel insights into the topological and analytical characteristics of toric varieties, with ramifications extending to theoretical advancements in algebraic geometry, harmonic analysis, and mathematical physics, underscoring the interdisciplinary significance of the established correspondence.
Label: AWP
Title: Differential operators on toric varieties and Fourier transform

Text: The enigmatic phenomenon of dark energy, which precipitates the universe's accelerated expansion, constitutes a paradigmatic conundrum in modern cosmology, necessitating a comprehensive reevaluation of extant theoretical frameworks. This study endeavours to provide a unified theoretical paradigm that harmoniously integrates disparate insights from modified gravity theories, quantum field theory, and high-redshift cosmological surveys to reconcile discrepancies between observational data and prevailing models. By subjecting the cosmic microwave background anisotropies, baryon acoustic oscillations, and Type Ia supernova distance measurements to a rigorous analysis, we demonstrate that a dynamic dark energy component, characterized by a time-varying equation of state, offers a self-consistent explanation for the observed cosmic acceleration while addressing the cosmic coincidence problem and fine-tuning issue inherent in the standard ΛCDM model. The proposed framework incorporates a non-minimal coupling between dark energy and dark matter, mediated by a scalar field that dynamically adjusts to preserve energy-momentum conservation across cosmic epochs, thereby alleviating tensions between local and global measurements of the Hubble constant, as well as providing a natural mechanism for early dark energy, which aligns with constraints from Planck satellite data. Furthermore, this approach predicts a distinct signature in the matter power spectrum, which can be tested by upcoming large-scale structure surveys such as the Euclid mission, thereby laying the groundwork for a unified understanding of dark energy's role in shaping the universe's evolution and offering critical insights for future multi-messenger cosmology experiments.
Label: AWP
Title: Dark Energy: A Unifying View

Text: Through an in-depth examination of steady-state hydrodynamic instabilities in the context of active liquid crystals, our investigation employing hybrid lattice Boltzmann simulations elucidates the intricate dynamics of these complex fluids, characterized by spontaneous flow and the attendant breaking of symmetry, which arise from the reciprocal interplay between fluid motion and molecular order. By virtue of its judicious amalgamation of kinetic theory and lattice discretization, the lattice Boltzmann method offers a computationally efficient and numerically accurate framework for modeling these intricate systems, thereby facilitating a nuanced understanding of their behavior. Our simulations unequivocally demonstrate that the interplay between fluid flow, molecular order, and thermal fluctuations gives rise to a diverse array of hydrodynamic instabilities, marked by the formation of periodic patterns, including rolls and squares, which are hallmarks of complex fluid dynamics. A thorough analysis of the stability of these patterns reveals their marked dependence on the strength of activity, the molecular order parameter, and the level of thermal noise, underscoring the significance of considering the reciprocal relationship between fluid flow and molecular order in comprehending the behavior of active liquid crystals. Moreover, our findings offer novel insights into the underlying physics of these complex systems, with far-reaching implications for the understanding of various phenomena in soft matter and biological systems.
Label: AWP
Title:
Steady-state hydrodynamic instabilities of active liquid crystals:
  Hybrid lattice Boltzmann simulations

Text: This investigation proposes a paradigm-shifting analytical framework for substantiating the regularity of the minimal probability of ruin within the context of a solitary risk process governed by a compound Poisson model with exponentially distributed claim sizes. By conceiving the problem as a strategic game of optimal control and stopping, wherein a judiciously determined stopping time is utilized to minimize the probability of financial insolvency, we leverage stochastic control methodologies and exploit the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation to derive a partial differential equation that serves as a characterization of the minimal probability of ruin. Subsequently, this equation is resolved via a probabilistic approach involving the last-exit distribution, thereby yielding an explicit representation of the minimal probability of ruin. Our findings demonstrate that the minimal probability of ruin exhibits a tendency towards regular variation at infinity, a critical property for the evaluation of risk in insurance and finance, with profound implications for the development of risk management strategies and the design of reinsurance contracts. Notably, the analytical framework presented herein provides a rigorous and computationally tractable method for calculating the minimal probability of ruin, thereby facilitating more accurate risk assessments and informed decision-making under conditions of uncertainty.
Label: AWP
Title:
Proving Regularity of the Minimal Probability of Ruin via a Game of
  Stopping and Control

Text: This investigation delves into the relationship between Hamiltonian asymmetry and Tolman’s length, a pivotal parameter in surface thermodynamics that quantifies the curvature dependence of interfacial tension. Through a theoretical framework incorporating a controllable Hamiltonian asymmetry, we demonstrate that perturbations from symmetric energetic configurations induce substantial alterations in Tolman’s length, thereby challenging conventional paradigms that assume curvature independence. Utilizing a computational methodology integrating density functional theory and thermodynamic integration techniques, our analysis establishes a direct proportionality between the magnitude of Hamiltonian asymmetry and the emergence of non-linear variations in Tolman’s length. The findings elucidate that asymmetric Hamiltonian structures engender anisotropic stress gradients at material interfaces, which propagate to amplify surface curvature effects and modify the effective thickness of interfacial domains. Validation of these conclusions is achieved via comparative studies of systems governed by symmetric versus asymmetric Hamiltonian formalisms, underscoring the critical influence of energy landscape asymmetry on interfacial thermodynamics. These observations not only refine our understanding of curvature-driven surface phenomena but also provide foundational insights into the stability of colloidal dispersions, emulsions, and nanoscale material architectures. By demonstrating the feasibility of modulating Tolman’s length through Hamiltonian design, this work establishes a conceptual nexus between Hamiltonian mechanics and surface thermodynamics, while offering a mechanistic basis for the rational engineering of interfacial properties in advanced material systems. The results further advocate for the inclusion of Hamiltonian asymmetry as a fundamental variable in predictive models of interfacial behavior, thereby advancing the theoretical underpinnings of interfacial science.
Label: AWP
Title: Asymmetry of the Hamiltonian and the Tolman's length

Text: We present an innovative paradigm for the cultivation of high-quality decagonal quasicrystals through the employment of local rules-based deposition, thereby circumventing the traditional complexities and temporal constraints associated with their synthesis. Notably, quasicrystals, first identified in the 1980s, exhibit distinctive structural and physical properties that emanate from their manifestation of long-range order and short-range disorder, phenomena that have garnered significant attention in the scientific community. However, the conventional methods for synthesizing these materials often necessitate intricate and laborious procedures, underscoring the need for novel approaches to their growth. By leveraging a set of straightforward local rules, derived from a synergy of theoretical and numerical simulations, we have successfully guided the deposition of atoms on a substrate, thereby facilitating the formation of perfect decagonal quasicrystals characterized by well-defined structural and morphological properties. The local rules, which dictate the spatial arrangement of atoms in the burgeoning crystal, permit the realization of a perfectly ordered quasicrystalline structure, a phenomenon substantiated by high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) imaging, which reveal the ordered arrangement of atoms within the quasicrystal, thereby affirming its perfect decagonal symmetry. This breakthrough methodology enables the facile growth of perfect decagonal quasicrystals, thereby opening new avenues for the exploration of their unique properties and potential applications in advanced materials science and nanotechnology, with significant implications for the comprehension of quasicrystal growth mechanisms and the development of novel materials with tailored properties.
Label: AWP
Title: Growing Perfect Decagonal Quasicrystals by Local Rules

Text: Netsukuku constitutes a distributed, autonomous peer-to-peer networking framework engineered to facilitate scalable, infrastructure-independent communication across a heterogeneous array of nodes. By implementing an innovative routing methodology that employs a hierarchical geometric abstraction of network topology, the system enables nodes to dynamically self-organize via localized interactions, obviating the necessity for centralized control mechanisms. This architecture, which leverages a dual-layer routing strategy combining greedy forwarding with probabilistic flooding, optimizes path selection by dynamically adjusting to fluctuating node density and mobility, thereby enhancing robustness against node failures and minimizing latency. A critical distinction lies in its open-source, decentralized design, which not only mitigates the economic and logistical barriers of conventional infrastructure deployment but also fortifies security through end-to-end encryption and cryptographic authentication protocols. Comparative analyses highlight its superior adaptability in geographically dispersed or resource-constrained environments, such as disaster-affected regions, rural communities, and mobile ad-hoc networks, where traditional infrastructure-based systems often exhibit limitations. Furthermore, empirical evaluations underscore its capacity to sustain scalability with sublinear growth in computational overhead, even as node populations expand exponentially. These attributes position Netsukuku as a paradigm-shifting solution for next-generation decentralized communication ecosystems, addressing persistent challenges in connectivity equity and operational flexibility while advancing the feasibility of ubiquitous, low-cost digital access.
Label: AWP
Title: Overview of the Netsukuku network

Text: We hereby document the inaugural detection of WASP-1, an intriguing stellar entity characterized by a lithium- and metal-rich composition, coupled with an oversized planetary companion exhibiting marked deviations from typical celestial norms. As part of a comprehensive, ongoing survey aimed at elucidating the properties of transiting exoplanets, WASP-1 was initially identified as a paradigmatic candidate based on its distinctive transit-like signature and anomalous stellar attributes, which collectively suggested a unique evolutionary trajectory for this celestial body. A meticulous examination of the star's spectroscopic properties revealed an uncommonly high lithium abundance and an elevated metal content, indicative of a putative population II or A-type stellar ancestry, thus posing a conundrum vis-a-vis the conventional characteristics of stars hosting massive exoplanets, which are frequently found to be metal-poor. Conversely, the planetary companion, WASP-1b, orbits its parent star at a remarkably close distance, while exhibiting an inflated size, which may be indicative of intense stellar irradiation or tidal heating, thereby underscoring the intricate dynamical interplay between this star and its massive planetary companion. A thorough analysis of the system's properties reveals a complex interplay between the star's evolution and chemical composition, thereby underscoring the paramount importance of considering these factors in the context of exoplanetary science. Furthermore, a more in-depth examination of WASP-1 and its oversized planetary companion promises to yield valuable insights into the formation and evolution of massive exoplanets.
Label: AWP
Title: WASP-1: A lithium- and metal-rich star with an oversized planet

Text: NGC 1705‑1, a highly compact and exceptionally luminous super star cluster embedded within the proximate dwarf starburst galaxy NGC 1705, constitutes an optimal local analogue for the dense, metal‑poor star‑forming milieus that are postulated to give rise to long‑duration gamma‑ray bursts (GRBs); by exploiting a confluence of Hubble Space Telescope ultraviolet‑optical imaging, VLT/X‑shooter spectroscopy, and Chandra X‑ray observations, we determine an optimal age of 4.1 ± 0.5 Myr, a dynamical mass of (1.2 ± 0.3) × 10⁶ M⊙, and an ionized‑gas metallicity of 0.22 ± 0.03 Z⊙, all of which are consistent with the extreme conditions inferred for GRB progenitor sites; the cluster exhibits an exceptionally high ionizing photon production rate (Q₀ ≈ 10⁵⁰ s⁻¹) and harbours a pronounced Wolf–Rayet stellar population, as evidenced by broad He II λ4686 emission, thereby mirroring the stellar constituents deduced for GRB host galaxies; its star‑formation surface density exceeds 10 M⊙ yr⁻¹ kpc⁻², a value comparable to that measured in the cores of distant GRB host galaxies; moreover, the identification of a faint, hard X‑ray point source spatially coincident with the cluster intimates the presence of a compact remnant, possibly an incipient GRB progenitor; collectively, these observations confirm that NGC 1705‑1 satisfies the essential environmental prerequisites—subsolar metallicity, extreme stellar density, and potent stellar feedback—necessary for the production of long‑duration GRBs, thereby furnishing an unparalleled laboratory for probing the physical mechanisms that drive such catastrophic explosions.
Label: AWP
Title:
Super Star Cluster NGC1705-1: A Local Analogue to the Birthsite of
  Long-duration Gamma-ray Bursts

Text: In a comprehensive study, we have formulated a theoretical paradigm that facilitates an exhaustive examination of the vast string landscape, with particular emphasis on discerning the prohibited territories that emerge from the intricate interplay of compactification moduli and supersymmetry breaking. By integrating a distinctive amalgamation of techniques from Calabi-Yau manifold geometry and supergravity, we have demonstrated the existence of regions within the string landscape where supersymmetry is spontaneously broken at high energies, yet the resultant low-energy theory persists in exhibiting an unbroken discrete R-symmetry. The topological characteristics of these forbidden territories are distinguished by a non-trivial interplay between the complex structure moduli and the Kähler moduli, thereby giving rise to a multifaceted phenomenology comprising both supersymmetric and non-supersymmetric vacua. Our approach enables a systematic and thorough exploration of the string landscape, thereby facilitating the identification of regions that are not only phenomenologically viable but also theoretically well-motivated, thereby contributing significantly to our understanding of the string landscape and the origins of supersymmetry breaking, with far-reaching implications for the development of string theory beyond the minimal supersymmetric standard model.
Label: AWP
Title: Forbidden territories in the string landscape

Text: A comprehensive examination of the intricate magnetic phase transition in La{_{0.9}}Sr_{0.1}MnO{_3}, a perovskite manganite exhibiting a multifaceted phase diagram, has been undertaken to elucidate the complex interplay of magnetic phenomena underlying its behavior. Through a thorough temperature-dependent investigation, a paradigmatic shift from the glassy ferromagnetic behavior characteristic of the orbital domain state to long-range ferromagnetic ordering is revealed, as evidenced by the transformation observed in temperature-dependent magnetization curves, where a dichotomy exists between a disordered, glassy state prevailing at lower temperatures and a well-ordered ferromagnetic state emerging at higher temperatures. The glassy ferromagnetic state is distinguished by a broad maximum in the temperature-dependent magnetic susceptibility, which bespeaks spin-glass behavior, whereas the onset of long-range ferromagnetic ordering is corroborated by a sharp magnetization-temperature curve and a Curie-Weiss behavior in the inverse magnetic susceptibility, indicative of a well-defined magnetic ground state. These findings offer novel insights into the phase stability and magnetic properties of La{_{0.9}}Sr_{0.1}MnO{_3}, and underscore the pivotal role of orbital correlations in determining the magnetic ground state of this system, thereby underscoring the significance of these correlations in shaping its magnetic behavior.
Label: AWP
Title:
Changeover from Glassy ferromagnetism of the orbital domain state to
  long range ferromagnetic ordering in La{_{0.9}}Sr_{0.1}MnO{_3}

Text: This investigation into the confluence of shift systems and forbidden patterns constitutes a theoretical framework that amalgamates fundamental principles from coding theory and discrete mathematics, thereby facilitating a comprehensive examination of the intrinsic properties and behaviors of shift systems, which comprise sequences of symbols undergoing periodic permutations, and the emergent phenomenon of forbidden patterns within these systems. The latter are characterized by specific sequences that are inherently prohibited from occurring within a particular shift system, and the elucidation of their properties has profound implications for the understanding of information transmission and error-correcting codes, as well as the development of efficacious coding schemes. Utilizing a synergistic combination of algebraic and combinatorial methodologies, we derive novel conditions for the existence and non-existence of forbidden patterns in shift systems, thereby shedding luminescent insight into the intricate relationships between system parameters and pattern occurrence, and illuminating the fundamental constraints governing the transmission of information. Our results possess significant implications for the advancement of coding theory and discrete mathematics, contributing to the ongoing endeavor to elucidate the underlying dynamics governing shift systems and their associated forbidden patterns, and ultimately fostering a more profound comprehension of the intricate mechanisms governing information transmission.
Label: AWP
Title: Forbidden patterns and shift systems

Text: This comprehensive investigation elucidates the intricate interplay between dynamical tunneling, a quantum phenomenon wherein particles transcend potential barriers, and classical resonances, periodic motions of particles within the barrier, thereby providing a profound understanding of the relationship between these ostensibly disparate phenomena. Utilizing an innovative amalgamation of analytical and numerical methodologies, our research demonstrates that dynamical tunneling can precipitate classical resonances, characterized by a distinctive frequency spectrum that diverges from those of traditional classical resonances, thereby underscoring the symbiotic relationship between these ostensibly distinct phenomena. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the classical resonances thus engendered can be leveraged to efficaciously modulate the tunneling probability, thereby controlling the transmission of particles through the barrier, a finding with far-reaching implications for the comprehension of quantum-classical correspondence and potential applications in fields such as quantum mechanics, classical chaos, and nanotechnology, where the manipulation of complex systems is paramount. Our results, therefore, offer novel insights into the intricate interplay between dynamical tunneling and classical resonances, and highlight the potential for harnessing this synergy to manipulate the behavior of complex systems, thereby shedding new light on the dynamics of quantum-classical correspondence.
Label: AWP
Title: On dynamical tunneling and classical resonances

Text: Axion‑like particles (ALPs), compelling extensions of the Standard Model, can interact with photons via a dimension‑five coupling, thereby facilitating photon‑ALP oscillations within astrophysical magneto‑environments; in this study we evaluate the observability of such particles using both contemporary and forthcoming imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes (IACTs) as well as space‑borne gamma‑ray observatories by modeling the transport of ultra‑high‑energy photons originating from remote blazars and gamma‑ray bursts through the intergalactic medium, intracluster magnetic fields, and the Galactic magnetic field, employing a Monte‑Carlo framework that incorporates realistic turbulence spectra and attenuation by the extragalactic background light to produce synthetic spectra over a parameter grid spanning ALP masses between 10⁻⁹ and 10⁻⁶ eV and photon‑ALP couplings ranging from 10⁻¹² to 10⁻¹⁰ GeV⁻¹, upon which a likelihood‑ratio analysis is applied to identify energy‑dependent spectral irregularities, yielding projected sensitivity curves for the Cherenkov Telescope Array (CTA) and the Fermi Large Area Telescope (Fermi‑LAT), with results indicating that CTA will be capable of probing couplings as low as g_{aγ}≈5×10⁻¹² GeV⁻¹ for an ALP mass near 10⁻⁸ eV, thereby surpassing extant constraints from helioscopes and laboratory experiments, and consequently demonstrating that gamma‑ray telescopes constitute a powerful, complementary avenue for exploring the ALP parameter space and possess the potential to reveal evidence of physics beyond the Standard Model.
Label: AWP
Title: Detecting Axion-Like Particles With Gamma Ray Telescopes

Text: Within the Standard Model, the spontaneous breaking of gauge symmetry furnishes a dynamical mechanism for endowing elementary particles with mass, a process encapsulated by the Higgs mechanism in which a scalar field acquires a non‑vanishing vacuum expectation value, thereby reducing the electroweak symmetry group SU(2)×U(1) to the residual U(1) of electromagnetism; the consequent Goldstone modes are absorbed by the W± and Z⁰ vector bosons, conferring upon them longitudinal polarization states and masses that scale with the symmetry‑breaking vacuum expectation, while the orthogonal physical excitation persists as the Higgs boson. Fermionic masses arise through Yukawa interactions with the identical scalar, with the magnitudes of the Yukawa couplings encoding the observed mass hierarchy; this coherent schema successfully reproduces the experimentally measured masses of the gauge bosons and predicts the Higgs mass within current uncertainties, a prediction corroborated by precision electroweak data and the observation at the Large Hadron Collider of a 125 GeV scalar resonance. Furthermore, spontaneous symmetry breaking is instrumental in generating neutrino masses via various seesaw constructions and shapes the landscape of dynamical symmetry‑breaking scenarios such as technicolor; theoretical viability imposes the twin requisites of renormalizability and gauge‑anomaly cancellation, conditions that are fulfilled in the minimal Standard Model yet present formidable obstacles for many beyond‑the‑Standard‑Model proposals. Forthcoming high‑luminosity collider runs and advanced lattice gauge simulations will continue to interrogate the vacuum structure and assess the robustness of spontaneous symmetry breaking as the preeminent mechanism for mass generation.
Label: AWP
Title: Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking as a Basis of Particle Mass

Text: This treatise elucidates a comprehensive framework for extending the Tits representation to a diverse array of finitely generated groups, thereby encompassing Coxeter groups, Artin groups of finite and affine type, as well as certain classes of Kac-Moody groups, by virtue of their inherent root-system-like structures. Specifically, we introduce the notion of a weighted root datum, concurrently deforming the standard bilinear form, thereby facilitating the construction of a family of linear actions on a graded module over a commutative ring, which inherently preserve a generalized Coxeter form. Notably, we demonstrate that these representations are faithful under relatively mild nondegeneracy conditions, while also recovering the classical Tits representation when specialized to Coxeter groups. Furthermore, we establish a criterion for the existence of an invariant cone, thereby yielding a geometric model of the associated group action on a convex subset of a real vector space, which generalizes the Tits cone. The ensuing results not only provide novel insights into the linearity of Artin groups, the growth of Kac-Moody groups, and the construction of new reflection groups in higher dimensions, but also open up a new avenue for exploring the intricate interplay between the algebraic and geometric properties of generalized reflection groups.
Label: AWP
Title: Generalisations of the Tits representation

Text: This research systematically examines the emergence of $x \to 1$ singularities in quantum field theories, with a focus on their coordinate-space manifestations at fixed transverse momentum $k_\perp$. By dissecting the coordinate-space representation of parton distribution functions (PDFs) and structure functions, the study elucidates the intricate relationship between longitudinal momentum fractions ($x$) and transverse momentum dynamics in the $x \to 1$ regime. The singularities, which originate from the dominance of high-energy partonic configurations, are revealed to manifest as non-local quantum correlations in position space, thereby challenging conventional factorization frameworks. Employing a fixed-$k_\perp$ framework, the analysis isolates longitudinal dynamics, facilitating a rigorous examination of how these singularities influence the scaling behavior of PDFs and their experimental observables in high-energy processes. The formalism bridges the coordinate-space approach with the operator product expansion (OPE) and resummation methodologies, demonstrating that the $x \to 1$ limit necessitates a hybrid strategy integrating perturbative and non-perturbative analyses to accurately capture the divergent contributions. These findings have profound implications for precision phenomenology in collider experiments, as well as for the theoretical modeling of parton saturation and transverse momentum-dependent (TMD) factorization. By synthesizing insights from coordinate-space singularities and gauge-invariant constraints, this work provides a novel perspective on longitudinal momentum correlations in quantum field theories, underscoring the necessity of advanced coordinate-space techniques for addressing non-asymptotic QCD phenomena.
Label: AWP
Title: Coordinate-space picture and $x \to 1$ singularities at fixed $k_\perp$

Text: A confidence distribution (CD) constitutes a frequency-valued estimator of a scalar or vector parameter, serving as a nonparametric analogue to the Bayesian posterior while retaining exact frequency properties. Specifically, a CD is a family of cumulative distribution functions indexed by the sample, whose quantile functions generate confidence intervals with prescribed nominal levels, thereby inheriting invariance under reparameterization, asymptotic consistency, and the capacity to be derived from pivotal quantities, likelihood ratios, or resampling schemes. This framework enables a unified treatment of point estimation, interval estimation, and hypothesis testing within a singular distributional object, thereby facilitating the straightforward combination of independent evidence through the product of CDs or weighted averaging. Recent theoretical developments have demonstrated the asymptotic normality of CDs for models that satisfy regularity conditions, as well as established optimality properties analogous to those of likelihood-based procedures. Empirical studies have elucidated the utility of CDs in normal mean and variance inference, logistic regression, and meta-analysis, wherein they yield accurate confidence intervals and p-values without reliance on parametric assumptions. Notably, future research endeavors to extend CD theory to high-dimensional and non-regular settings, addressing computational challenges and exploring connections with empirical likelihood and Bayesian nonparametrics.
Label: AWP
Title: Confidence distribution (CD) -- distribution estimator of a parameter

Text: This investigation undertakes an exhaustive examination of the linear and nonlinear manifestations of the Rayleigh-Taylor instability under the auspices of a quasi-isobaric profile, thereby elucidating the multifaceted dynamics inherent to this phenomenon. The quasi-isobaric profile, characterized by a minuscule pressure gradient, serves as a paradigmatic model for atmospheric and oceanic flows, wherein the density variance is predominantly driven by temperature differences. Through a synergy of analytical and numerical methodologies, we scrutinize the growth rate and evolution of perturbations in both the linear and nonlinear regimes, with the objective of elucidating the underlying mechanisms governing the stability of the quasi-isobaric profile. Notably, our analytical treatment of the linear regime yields an expression for the growth rate of the instability, which is found to be consonant with previous theoretical studies, thereby validating the predictive efficacy of our analytical framework. Conversely, in the nonlinear regime, we employ a sophisticated numerical model to simulate the evolution of the instability, leading to the emergence of intricate structures and the eventual degradation of the quasi-isobaric profile, thus underscoring the profound impact of nonlinear processes on the dynamics of the Rayleigh-Taylor instability. Our results emphasize the imperative of incorporating nonlinear effects in modeling and predicting atmospheric and oceanic phenomena, thus contributing to a profounder comprehension of the underlying physics of the Rayleigh-Taylor instability and its pertinence to diverse geophysical flows.
Label: AWP
Title:
The linear and non linear Rayleigh-Taylor instability for the quasi
  isobaric profile

Text: In a seminal contribution to the interdisciplinary realm of algebraic geometry and integrable systems, a profound connection is elucidated between the recollement of deformed preprojective algebras and the Calogero-Moser correspondence, a paradigmatic relationship between these two ostensibly disparate fields. Specifically, it is demonstrated that the recollement of deformed preprojective algebras, which emanates from an in-depth examination of the derived categories of coherent sheaves on quiver varieties, gives rise to a family of Calogero-Moser spaces, whose topological characteristics are intimately connected with the Hamiltonian reduction of the cotangent bundle of a Lie group, and which are well-established as the phase spaces of integrable systems. Our findings provide a novel perspective on the geometric and algebraic underpinnings of the Calogero-Moser correspondence, thereby illuminating the intricate and multifaceted relationships that exist between quiver representations, derived categories, and integrable systems. Moreover, our research has far-reaching implications for the study of singularities, symplectic geometry, and representation theory, and sheds new light on the complex interplay between algebraic and geometric structures in the theory of integrable systems, thereby underscoring the recollement of deformed preprojective algebras as a potent tool for navigating the intricate and multifaceted landscape of integrable systems.
Label: AWP
Title:
Recollement of Deformed Preprojective Algebras and the Calogero-Moser
  Correspondence

Text: A novel candidate for a non-strangeness pentaquark, denoted as N*(1675), has been observed through a comprehensive examination of a substantial dataset amassed by the Belle II detector at the SuperKEKB electron-positron collider, wherein a likelihood-based analysis technique was employed to exploit the detector's distinctive characteristics. Specifically, the reconstruction of DsK-π+ and Dsπ+ππ final states, which are particularly sensitive to the decay modes of exotic hadrons, was undertaken, thereby facilitating the identification of a statistically significant excess in the mass spectrum of the DsK-π+ system, consistent with the presence of a new pentaquark state. The measured mass of the N*(1675) candidate, determined with an accuracy of 1675.4 ± 1.1 ± 1.3 MeV/c^2, and its estimated width, which is approximated to be 8.3 ± 1.7 ± 2.1 MeV/c^2, are commensurate with the properties of other established pentaquark states, thereby underscoring the significance of our findings. The implications of these results for our comprehension of exotic hadron spectroscopy are far-reaching, providing insight into the intricate dynamics of quark-antiquark-gluon interactions in hadronic systems, and thus illuminating the complex topography of non-strangeness pentaquarks.
Label: AWP
Title: A new candidate for non-strangeness pentaquarks: N*(1675)

Text: A comprehensive investigation into the phenomenon of very high energy (VHE) emission from gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) was conducted utilizing the Milagro gamma-ray observatory, a large area air Cherenkov detector situated in the southwestern United States, which operated from 2000 to 2008. Throughout this observational period, Milagro effectively monitored a substantial sector of the celestial expanse for gamma-ray emission exceeding 100 GeV, thereby leveraging an effective area of approximately 17 square kilometers. Consequently, the detector identified and triggered on 134 GRBs above a threshold of 1 GeV, which were subsequently analyzed for evidence of VHE emission surpassing 100 GeV, employing a synergistic amalgamation of data-driven and Monte Carlo-based methodologies to estimate the background and source flux. Notwithstanding these efforts, no significant VHE emission was discerned from any of the GRBs, resulting in upper limits ranging from 1.4 to 4.6 times the Crab Nebula flux, which provide valuable constraints on theoretical models of GRB emission, particularly those involving the acceleration of high-energy particles in relativistic shocks. These findings establish a new paradigm for the VHE emission from GRBs and significantly contribute to the elucidation of the underlying physics governing these enigmatic astrophysical events.
Label: AWP
Title: Search for Very High Energy Emission from Gamma-Ray Bursts using Milagro

Text: This investigation examines the dynamical behavior of open strings embedded within a uniform background B-field, employing a first-order mechanical framework to elucidate the emergence of noncommutative geometries and the unification of disparate theoretical constructs via soldering formalism. Through the incorporation of auxiliary variables into the phase space, the system's response to the B-field is systematically analyzed, revealing that spatial noncommutativity arises inherently from the Dirac quantization procedure applied to the string's boundary conditions. The soldering methodology, which facilitates the amalgamation of distinct contributions from the background flux and intrinsic string dynamics, is demonstrated to encode the resultant noncommutative geometric structure, thereby synthesizing the interplay between topological and algebraic properties of the open string. This approach not only clarifies the B-field's dual role as a modulator of geometric configurations and a mediator of noncommutative spacetime but also provides critical insights into the quantization processes of such systems. Furthermore, the formalism's capacity to reconcile dual worldsheet descriptions underscores its potential for extending these findings to higher-dimensional noncommutative field theories, while simultaneously highlighting the foundational implications for quantum gravitational phenomena and the exploration of string-theoretic duality. The study thus establishes a cohesive theoretical framework wherein the first-order mechanical treatment of open strings in B-field environments serves as a bridge between classical and quantum regimes, offering pathways to address unresolved questions in string theory and its geometric interpretations.
Label: AWP
Title:
Open string with a background B-field as the first order mechanics,
  noncommutativity and soldering formalism

Text: This investigation delves into the linearization of torsion classes within the Picard group of algebraic curves over finite fields, a longstanding enigma in algebraic geometry that has garnered considerable attention. By examining the behavior of Weil divisors under the Galois group's action on the finite field, we establish that the torsion classes in the Picard group can be effectively parameterized by the set of Weil divisors possessing distinct properties. Notably, for a given algebraic curve over a finite field, we demonstrate that the torsion classes in the Picard group can be linearly extended to form a vector space, which we term the "tangent space" of the Picard group, thereby providing a novel framework for understanding the geometric and algebraic properties of algebraic curves in this context. The far-reaching implications of our findings significantly advance the study of algebraic curves over finite fields, while also contributing to a deeper comprehension of the Picard group's structure, thereby shedding new light on the intricate relationships between algebraic and geometric properties. Furthermore, the application of techniques from Galois cohomology, in conjunction with the utilization of the Weil pairing, facilitates a more profound understanding of the curves' algebraic and geometric properties, laying the groundwork for future research in this area and underscoring the significance of our investigation to the broader field of algebraic geometry.
Label: AWP
Title:
Linearizing torsion classes in the Picard group of algebraic curves over
  finite fields

Text: This investigation delves into the fundamental problem of Diophantine approximation and algebraic number theory, specifically the simultaneous approximation of a real number α by all conjugates of an algebraic number β of degree n. The conjugates of β, denoted β₁, β₂, ..., βₙ, are examined in conjunction with the Diophantine inequalities that govern the approximation of α by each βᵢ, thereby elucidating the interplay between the simultaneous approximation of α by conjugates of β and the parameters that govern such approximations. It is demonstrated that, for any ε > 0, there exist infinitely many rational approximations q/p to α, such that the inequality |βᵢ - (α - q/p)| < ε/2^n holds for all i = 1, 2, ..., n, thereby extending the earlier result of Schmidt, who had previously considered the case n = 2. Furthermore, this investigation provides a quantitative estimate of the number of such approximations, expressed in terms of the height of β and the logarithm of ε, thereby furnishing a precise characterization of the approximability of α by conjugates of β. This study's methodology, which combines algebraic geometry and Diophantine approximation, has far-reaching implications for the study of Diophantine equations and algebraic curves, and its results possess potential applications in number theory, algebraic geometry, and cryptography.
Label: AWP
Title:
Simultaneous approximation of a real number by all conjugates of an
  algebraic number

Text: The emergence of phase transitions in large N gauge theories, precipitated by geometric considerations, is a phenomenon wherein the spatial dimensionality of the ambient space assumes a paramount significance in determining the thermodynamic comportment of the system, thereby exhibiting a nuanced interdependence with the underlying theory. Specifically, our investigation focuses on the geometrically induced phase transitions that arise in large N gauge theories as the spatial dimension is systematically varied, with particular emphasis on the intricate interplay between spatial curvature and the gauge theory's symmetry breaking patterns, which collectively serve to modulate the thermodynamic behavior of the system in a manner that is contingent upon the geometric attributes of the space on which the theory resides. Through a synergistic amalgamation of analytical and numerical methodologies, our research demonstrates that the geometric curvature can induce a sequence of phase transitions, characterized by the spontaneous breaking of the gauge symmetry and the concomitant formation of topological defects, thereby underscoring the critical role that geometry assumes in modulating the thermodynamic properties of the system. Notably, our findings indicate that the large N limit of the gauge theory constitutes a singularly propitious arena for the exploration of geometric phase transitions, wherein the reciprocal interplay between geometry and gauge symmetry can lead to a rich and varied assortment of thermodynamic behaviors with far-reaching implications for our comprehension of the interplay between geometry and gauge theories in the context of high-energy physics and quantum field theory.
Label: AWP
Title: Geometrically Induced Phase Transitions at Large N

Text: Our investigation delves into the intricate relationship between topological Markov shifts, a class of topological dynamical systems distinguished by their inherent shift-invariant measure-preserving properties and symbolic representation as shifts on a finite alphabet, and Cuntz-Krieger algebras, a class of operator algebras constructed from a finite set of generators and relations that encapsulate the algebraic structure of a topological dynamical system, thereby providing a paradigmatic framework for examining the intrinsic properties of such systems. By leveraging the prism of orbit equivalence, our research endeavors to establish a connection between these two ostensibly disparate frameworks by scrutinizing the conditions under which the crossed product algebras of a topological Markov shift and the Cuntz-Krieger algebra associated with a given shift exhibit isomorphism, a phenomenon that is contingent upon the conjugacy class of the shift map within the set of all shifts on a given alphabet. Notably, our findings have far-reaching implications for the study of topological dynamical systems and the classification of operator algebras, furnishing a novel heuristic tool for distinguishing between conjugate and non-conjugate shifts through the lens of their underlying algebraic structure, thereby offering a more nuanced understanding of the intricate relationships between these entities.
Label: AWP
Title:
Orbit equivalence of topological Markov shifts and Cuntz-Krieger
  algebras

Text: This study presents the experimental manifestation of a silicon spin field-effect transistor, a pivotal component in the development of spin-based quantum computing and spintronics applications, wherein the confluence of fundamental principles and technological advancements converges to facilitate the manipulation of spin and charge carriers. The device in question leverages a phosphorus-doped silicon-on-insulator substrate, thereby enabling the autonomous regulation of spin and charge carrier dynamics. Through the application of a vertical electric field, we have successfully demonstrated the control of spin orientation and the coherent precession of spins within the channel region, a phenomenon mediated by the spin-orbit interaction that is augmented by the presence of an oxidized silicon nitride interface. Notably, our measurements have yielded a spin lifetime of 10.5 microseconds and a spin coherence time of 1.2 microseconds, indicative of a high degree of spin control and coherence. These findings not only substantiate the feasibility of silicon-based spintronics but also serve as a pivotal stepping stone towards the realization of scalable and efficient spin-based quantum technologies, thereby empowering researchers to explore novel regimes in quantum information processing and storage, with far-reaching implications for the development of spin-based quantum computing and memory devices.
Label: AWP
Title: Experimental realization of a silicon spin field-effect transistor

Text: We present compelling evidence for the existence of a finite energy gap in the spin‑wave spectrum of the geometrically frustrated pyrochlore antiferromagnet Gd₂Sn₂O₇, as deduced from meticulous low‑temperature specific‑heat measurements; the compound, whose magnetic lattice is constituted by a network of corner‑sharing Gd³⁺ tetrahedra, exemplifies extreme frustration stemming from its pyrochlore geometry, and consequently lacks conventional long‑range magnetic order; the calorimetric data exhibit a pronounced anomaly at sub‑Kelvin temperatures that, upon rigorous analysis, can be quantitatively attributed to thermally activated spin‑wave excitations rather than to alternative degrees of freedom; by fitting the observed heat capacity to a theoretical model explicitly incorporating a gapped magnon dispersion, we achieve an excellent concordance between experimental observations and theoretical predictions, thereby substantiating the presence of a spin‑wave gap whose magnitude is extracted to be approximately 0.38 K, a value that underscores a significant energetic barrier impeding magnon propagation; this empirical determination aligns with contemporary theoretical frameworks for highly frustrated magnetic systems, wherein the absence of long‑range order is anticipated to engender a suppression of low‑energy excitations and the emergence of a finite gap; consequently, our findings enrich the thermodynamic understanding of Gd₂Sn₂O₇ and illuminate the fundamental nature of spin excitations in frustrated lattices, thereby contributing valuable insights to ongoing investigations of quantum phase transitions and unconventional magnetic phenomena.
Label: AWP
Title:
Evidence for gapped spin-wave excitations in the frustrated Gd2Sn2O7
  pyrochlore antiferromagnet from low-temperature specific heat measurements

Text: Notwithstanding the complexities inherent in elucidating the molecular constituents of astrophysical environments, recent investigations have endeavoured to identify and characterise hydrocarbon anions within the context of interstellar clouds and circumstellar envelopes, wherein these negatively charged species assume a pivotal role in governing the chemical and physical processes that underpin the formation of celestial bodies and planetary systems. Through the employment of cutting-edge spectroscopic methodologies and astronomical observations, we have successfully identified a suite of hydrocarbon anions, including C5H- and C7H-, within the interstellar clouds of the Orion Nebula and the circumstellar envelope of the asymptotic giant branch star, IRC+10216, thus underscoring the significance of these findings in understanding the molecular composition of these environments. Our results suggest that these anions are generated through the interaction of neutral gas and dust with intense radiation fields, which precipitates the fragmentation of molecular species and the subsequent liberation of free electrons, thereby providing valuable insights into the chemical and physical processes that govern the formation of complex organic molecules in these environments. Furthermore, the detection of these anions affords a unique opportunity to investigate the early stages of star formation and potential delivery of prebiotic molecules to planetary systems, thereby expanding our comprehension of the intricate relationships between molecular composition, stellar evolution, and planetary development.
Label: AWP
Title: Hydrocarbon anions in interstellar clouds and circumstellar envelopes

Text: This study presents a computational investigation into the emergence of (p,q) composite configurations through the interplay of p fundamental (F) strings and q Dirichlet (D) strings within a low-energy string theory paradigm. Utilizing lattice-discretized numerical models and dynamical system formulations, the research interrogates the stability and binding dynamics of these hybrid entities across multidimensional parameter spaces. Findings elucidate that (p,q) bound states materialize via a thermodynamic phase transition governed by topological charge conservation laws and renormalized string tension, wherein critical formation thresholds are contingent upon the ratio of p to q. The analyses demonstrate that when the effective coupling strength surpasses a spatially dependent critical threshold, the system undergoes a second-order phase transition, culminating in metastable (p,q) configurations distinguished by non-Abelian flux quantization and supersymmetric invariance. These results corroborate theoretical conjectures regarding enhanced supersymmetry in composite string states and provide empirical validation of moduli space stabilization mechanisms. Furthermore, the study establishes novel scaling relationships governing energy distribution within (p,q) systems, thereby forging a computational nexus between string theory and gauge/gravity dualities. Through rigorous simulation of F- and D-string dynamics, this work advances the comprehension of non-perturbative phenomena, offering novel insights into black hole entropy quantification and quantum gravitational frameworks.
Label: AWP
Title:
Numerical experiments with p F- and q D-strings: the formation of (p,q)
  bound states

Text: This investigation leverages the Boltzmann equation as a paradigmatic theoretical framework to scrutinize transport phenomena within finite, modular quantum systems, whose intricately interconnected components pose a paradigmatic challenge to extant approaches to quantum transport. By embracing a microscopic descriptive paradigm grounded in the Boltzmann equation, we derive a set of kinetic equations that comprehensively capture the essential attributes of quantum transport in these systems, thereby accounting for the effects of quantum coherence and correlations among the constituent units, as well as the modular structure's inherent complexity. Numerical solutions to the kinetic equations reveal distinct transport regimes characterized by the relative predominance of quantum effects versus classical diffusion, thereby underscoring the significant influence of the modular structure on determining the transport properties of these systems. Moreover, our findings substantiate the critical role of the modular structure in these systems and underscore the potential of the Boltzmann equation approach for elucidating the behavior of finite modular quantum systems across a broad spectrum of applications, including quantum computing and quantum simulation, thereby illuminating the theoretical underpinnings of these burgeoning fields.
Label: AWP
Title:
Boltzmann equation approach to transport in finite modular quantum
  systems

Text: This abstract delineates a systematic examination of the entanglement dynamics governed by non-Markovian noise processes within noisy continuous-variable quantum communication channels, elucidating the intricate temporal evolution of quantum correlations between two subsystems in such a framework. By employing a master equation formalism to model the system’s dynamical behavior, we formulate an analytical expression for the temporal decay rate of entanglement under non-Markovian perturbations, which manifests as oscillatory or non-monotonic temporal evolution. The findings reveal that non-Markovian noise dynamics not only induce an initial resurgence of entanglement subsequent to its initial decay but also engender a subsequent decline, contrasting starkly with the characteristic monotonic attenuation observed in systems subjected to Markovian noise environments. Furthermore, the study identifies specific parameter regimes wherein the revival of entanglement becomes markedly pronounced, underscoring the intricate interplay between the system-environment coupling strengths and the spectral characteristics of the noise. These results bear critical ramifications for the engineering of resilient quantum communication strategies in non-idealized, realistic environments, thereby emphasizing the imperative to account for non-Markovian noise effects in the theoretical and practical design of robust quantum information systems.
Label: AWP
Title:
Non-Markovian entanglement dynamics of noisy continuous variable quantum
  channels

Text: This study elaborates a refined statistical-mechanical paradigm for investigating extended-range correlations between bulk and boundary domains within black-hole geometries, thereby advancing the holographic correspondence beyond the dominant semiclassical regime. Through the formulation of an ensemble comprising quantum fields traversing a fixed asymptotically anti-de Sitter spacetime endowed with a dynamical horizon, the partition function is derived to explicitly encapsulate non-local coupling terms that interlink bulk curvature invariants with boundary conformal field operators. The emergent effective action exhibits a distinctive power-law attenuation of mutual information across spatially disjointed bulk-boundary subsystems, a characteristic that endures even at sub-Planckian length scales. Quantitative analysis of the entropy spectrum unveils a universal logarithmic correction to the Bekenstein–Hawking area law, a feature traceable to the entanglement entropy of bulk microstates with boundary field degrees of freedom. Furthermore, the statistical dynamics of horizon area fluctuations are demonstrated to conform to a generalized fluctuation–dissipation theorem, establishing a quantitative linkage between bulk thermodynamic heat capacity and boundary stress-energy tensor correlators. Collectively, these results establish a rigorous quantitative nexus between bulk quantum gravity dynamics and boundary conformal field theory, elucidating the microscopic genesis of holography and the entropy-theoretic foundations of black-hole thermodynamics.
Label: AWP
Title:
The Statistical Mechanics of Microscopic Long-Range Bulk-Boundary
  Dependence in Black-Hole Physics and Holography

Text: This investigation elucidates the notion of node similarity within subgraphs of protein interaction networks, thereby elucidating the intricate relationships between proteins and their functional implications, underscoring the significance of this paradigm in the field of molecular biology. By developing a novel computational framework, this study was able to quantify and compare the similarity of node attributes, including functional annotations and domain composition, within subgraphs of protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks, thereby harnessing the principles of graph theory and machine learning to identify clusters of nodes that exhibit high similarity in their attributes, thereby revealing functional modules and communities within the network. A comprehensive PPI network derived from the Human Protein Reference Database served as the test bed for this framework, yielding results that demonstrate the presence of distinct node similarity patterns within subgraphs, a phenomenon that was notably observed to be more pronounced in subgraphs comprising highly similar nodes, which in turn were found to be functionally related and share similar domain compositions, thereby suggesting a functional correlation between node attributes and network structure. The findings of this study have far-reaching implications for understanding protein function, predicting protein interactions, and identifying potential therapeutic targets in complex diseases, underscoring the potential of this framework to be broadly applied to other types of biological and complex networks.
Label: AWP
Title: Node similarity within subgraphs of protein interaction networks

Text: A unified framework describing diffractive deep inelastic scattering phenomena incorporating saturation effects is presented within this work. The proposed model integrates the color dipole formalism with nonlinear QCD evolution equations to capture the transition between dilute and dense partonic regimes. By systematically incorporating higher-twist corrections and employing the Balitsky-Kovchegov equation, we demonstrate remarkable agreement with experimental data from the Hadron-Electron Ring Accelerator and the Large Hadron Collider across a broad kinematic range. The saturation scale emerges naturally as the fundamental parameter governing the geometric scaling properties of the cross sections. Our findings provide compelling evidence that saturation phenomena are essential for a complete description of diffractive processes at high energies, offering new insights into the universal features of strong interactions in the Regge limit of quantum chromodynamics.
Label: AWP
Title:
A unified description of diffractive deep inelastic scattering with
  saturation

Text: This investigation undertakes a multifaceted factorization analysis of the fragmentation functions of hadrons comprising a heavy quark, with a primary emphasis on elucidating the underlying kinematical and dynamical mechanisms governing the transition from a heavy quark to a hadron. Employing a synergistic combination of perturbative Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) calculations and non-perturbative models, we derive a factorized form for the fragmentation function, thereby elucidating the intricate interplay between the initial-state fragmentation process and the final-state interactions, and thereby facilitating a comprehensive understanding of the hadronization phenomenon. Our analysis reveals that the fragmentation function can be decomposed into a product of the heavy-quark fragmentation function and a hadronization function, which encapsulates the effects of hadronization and final-state interactions, thus underscoring the importance of these dynamics in the hadronization process. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this factorized form enables a precise and accurate description of the fragmentation functions of hadrons containing a heavy quark, including the charm and bottom quark systems, thereby providing a robust framework for the interpretation of experimental data from hadron colliders, such as the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) and the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC). Our findings have significant implications for the extraction of valuable information on the strong interaction from hadronic final states, and by shedding light on the dynamics of heavy-quark hadronization, this study contributes to a deeper understanding of the strong interaction and the hadronization process, thereby expanding the knowledge base in this realm.
Label: AWP
Title:
Factorization analysis for the fragmentation functions of hadrons
  containing a heavy quark

Text: This investigation into the Comorosan phenomenon, wherein the incorporation of a minute quantity of a non-electrolyte into an electrolyte solution precipitates a substantial diminution in the solution's freezing point, thereby underscoring a discrepancy between the observed phenomenon and the theoretical expectations predicated by Raoult's Law, necessitates a rigorous thermodynamic analysis to elucidate the underlying mechanistic framework. In order to accomplish this, a multifaceted examination of the free energy of activation governing the process is undertaken, facilitated by a meticulously designed experimental protocol that entails the preparation of diverse electrolyte solutions featuring varying concentrations of non-electrolytes, followed by the measurement of their respective freezing points and the corresponding activation energies through differential scanning calorimetry. The resultant data indicate that the introduction of the non-electrolyte eventuates in a pronounced reduction in the activation energy required for crystal nucleation, thereby facilitating the inception of ice crystals and culminating in a lower observed freezing point. Through a comparative analysis of the experimentally derived data with theoretical models, it is conclusively demonstrated that the observed Comorosan effect can be attributed to the suppression of crystal growth inhibition exerted by the non-electrolyte, thereby leading to a diminution in the free energy of activation governing ice crystal formation, a finding with significant implications for an enhanced comprehension of the fundamental principles governing the behavior of complex solutions.
Label: AWP
Title: Free Energy of Activation for the Comorosan Effect

Text: This study probes the behavior of Bose-Einstein condensates in environments perturbed by arbitrarily strong random potentials, employing a synergy of analytical and numerical methodologies to elucidate the intricate interplay between quantum coherence and localization effects under conditions of varying potential strengths and spatial correlations, thereby extending the Gross-Pitaevskii formalism to accommodate disorder. Our investigation, conducted under the aegis of the Gross-Pitaevskii equation supplemented by a random potential term, reveals a critical threshold beyond which the condensate density undergoes a non-monotonic suppression, precipitating a phase transition from a delocalized superfluid state to a localized, fragmented state, wherein the emergence of Anderson-like localization is contingent upon the amplitude and correlation length of the disorder. By systematically varying these parameters, we establish a universal scaling relationship governing the onset of localization, distinct from regimes characterized by weak disorder, and attribute the breakdown of phase coherence and the emergence of substructures in the density profile at high disorder strengths to the formation of metastable excitations and enhanced quantum fluctuations. Consequently, our findings demonstrate that arbitrarily strong random potentials induce a qualitative transition from coherent to incoherent dynamics, with implications for the quantum simulation of disordered systems and the stability of superfluidity in heterogeneous environments, thereby providing a theoretical framework for the experimental exploration of Bose-Einstein condensates in disordered media and bridging fundamental studies of many-body localization with practical applications in quantum technologies.
Label: AWP
Title: Bose-Einstein-condensed gases in arbitrarily strong random potentials

Text: This investigation into the effectiveness of integrating a degree constraint (d-constraint) during Low-Density Parity-Check (LDPC) decoding within a Bliss framework, a paradigmatic approach that exploits the probabilistic nature of error correction, reveals a novel paradigm for decoding LDPC codes by synergistically combining message-passing algorithms and iterative refinement. However, the efficacy of the Bliss scheme is often compromised by the presence of cycles in the code's Tanner graph, which necessitates the implementation of a d-constraint, a restriction that confines the maximum degree of variable nodes in the Tanner graph to a predetermined value d.
