Text: The investigation into the Ladyzhenskaya-Babuška-Brezzi (LBB) stability of a hybrid finite element formulation integrating discontinuous Galerkin (DG) and continuous Galerkin (CG) methodologies reveals critical insights into the compatibility of these numerical schemes. By analyzing the discrete inf-sup condition for a coupled DG/CG element pair, this study establishes theoretical criteria ensuring stability in heterogeneous discretizations, where DG’s capacity to model discontinuities is complemented by CG’s accuracy in smooth regimes. Through rigorous construction of polynomial spaces and interfacial coupling strategies, sufficient conditions are derived to balance the degrees of freedom between DG and CG elements, mitigating instabilities arising from mismatched approximation orders or inconsistent boundary treatments. Numerical experiments, encompassing benchmark problems in fluid dynamics and solid mechanics, corroborate the analytical framework, demonstrating that LBB stability is preserved when DG components are augmented with stabilization mechanisms or coupled to CG elements of lower polynomial order. This work not only advances the theoretical understanding of mixed formulations but also provides a practical paradigm for designing stable DG/CG pairs in applications requiring localized resolution of sharp gradients or discontinuities, such as multiphysics systems or fractured material simulations. The derived conditions, dependent on polynomial degree disparity and geometric partitioning, offer a robust foundation for extending hybrid finite element methods to complex domains where traditional homogeneous formulations falter.
Label: AWP
Title:
LBB Stability of a Mixed Discontinuous/Continuous Galerkin Finite
  Element Pair

Text: This investigation into the confluence of modular equations of order p and Theta functions, two pivotal concepts in the disciplines of number theory and algebraic geometry, yields a novel framework for constructing and analyzing modular equations of order p through the elucidation of their intricate relationship. Modular equations of order p, which originate from the study of modular forms, are thereby established as a distinct class of equations, while Theta functions, a category of mathematical functions of paramount significance in the theory of elliptic curves and modular forms, serve as a paradigmatic example of the latter. Consequently, the exploitation of the symbiotic relationship between these two concepts enables the derivation of a family of modular equations of order p, characterized by a complex structure and exhibiting salient properties that warrant further investigation. The implications of this research are far-reaching, with profound consequences for the study of elliptic curves, modular forms, and related areas of number theory and algebraic geometry, as well as the potential for the modular equations of order p to provide a new paradigm for understanding the arithmetic and geometric properties of these mathematical objects, thereby facilitating applications in cryptography, coding theory, and other cognate fields.
Label: AWP
Title: Modular equations of order $p$ and Theta functions

Text: This investigation delves into the significant departures from equilibrium of Poisson cluster processes, a class of stochastic point processes inherently characterized by spatial structure and cluster formation, thereby exhibiting complex spatial organization. Defined as a Poisson point process of clusters, wherein each cluster constitutes a random subset of points, the Poisson cluster process forms the focal point of our analysis. By deriving a large deviation principle for the empirical measure of the Poisson cluster process, we establish a probabilistic framework for estimating the rarity of observed point patterns, thereby providing a profound understanding of the underlying statistical mechanisms. Our results reveal that the large deviations of the Poisson cluster process are governed by a rate function, which effectively balances the competition between the spatial dispersion of clusters and the aggregation of points within clusters, thereby mediating the inherent trade-off between these two countervailing processes. Specifically, we demonstrate that the rate function is characterized by a variational problem, involving the minimization of a functional that quantifies the relative entropy between the empirical measure and the underlying cluster distribution, thereby establishing a deep connection between the statistical properties of the Poisson cluster process and the principles of information theory. The implications of our findings extend to the analysis of spatial point patterns in various fields, including ecology, epidemiology, and materials science, where they offer novel insights into the underlying mechanisms governing the formation and evolution of complex spatial structures. The mathematical framework developed in this study provides a paradigmatic shift in our understanding of the statistical properties of Poisson cluster processes, enabling the prediction of rare events and the estimation of model parameters with unprecedented accuracy.
Label: AWP
Title: Large deviations of Poisson cluster processes

Text: In Au+Au collisions at a centre-of-mass energy of 200 GeV, a pronounced augmentation in the production of strange baryons, specifically the Lambda (Λ) and anti-Lambda (Λ̄) particles, is observed relative to p+p interactions at the same collision energy, as evidenced by data collected at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC). Notably, the yields of Λ and Λ̄ particles are significantly elevated in Au+Au collisions, with a marked enhancement in their production at mid-rapidity, thereby underscoring the propensity of these particles to be produced in the dense, high-temperature medium characterizing heavy-ion collisions. A comparative analysis of the two colliding systems reveals that the increased production of Λ and Λ̄ in Au+Au collisions is concomitant with a suppression of pion yields, hinting at a possible correlation with the formation of the quark-gluon plasma (QGP), a hot and dense deconfined state of quarks and gluons. The observed enhancement of strange baryon production in Au+Au collisions is likely attributable to the presence of the QGP, which facilitates the coalescence of quarks and antiquarks, thereby giving rise to the creation of these particles, and thus our findings provide valuable insights into the dynamics of strange baryon production in heavy-ion collisions and shed light on the mechanisms underlying the formation of the QGP in such interactions.
Label: AWP
Title:
Enhanced strange baryon production in Au+Au collisions compared to p+p
  at sqrts = 200 GeV

Text: We hereby submit the outcomes of a thorough examination of diffuse optical luminosity in galaxy clusters, wherein we have endeavored to elucidate its correlations with a multitude of cluster attributes. Expanding upon our preceding investigation, our current study encompasses a significantly larger and more diverse ensemble of galaxy clusters, spanning a broad range of masses and redshifts, thereby allowing for a more comprehensive analysis. Notwithstanding the heterogeneity of the cluster sample, our observations unequivocally reveal a robust correlation between diffuse optical luminosity and the total mass of the cluster, with higher-mass clusters exhibiting far more extensive diffuse light distributions. Moreover, we have discerned a statistically significant correlation between diffuse optical luminosity and the cluster's X-ray luminosity, thereby suggesting a causal nexus between the diffuse light and the sizzling intracluster gas. Furthermore, our analysis has yielded a weak but statistically significant correlation between diffuse optical luminosity and the cluster's star formation activity, as quantitatively assessed by the Hα emission emanating from galaxies within the cluster. These findings offer novel insights into the characteristics and evolution of galaxy clusters, underscoring the pivotal role of diffuse optical luminosity as a diagnostic tool for probing the intricate interplay between the cluster's various constituent elements. Ultimately, our results have far-reaching implications for our comprehension of galaxy cluster formation and evolution, and highlight the necessity for further investigation into the genesis and nature of diffuse optical luminosity.

Title:
Diffuse Optical Light in Galaxy Clusters II: Correlations with Cluster
  Properties

Text: This investigation offers a systematic analytical categorization of planar analytic curves—specifically, germs of analytic curves in the complex plane—with multiplicities ranging from two to four, employing advanced methodologies to differentiate isolated singularities through their intrinsic invariants. By harnessing Puiseux parametrization and equisingularity invariants as analytical tools, the study formulates a rigorous framework to classify these singularities via characteristic exponents, Newton polygon configurations, and tangent multiplicity distributions. A pivotal advancement lies in the derivation of explicit invariants for branches exhibiting multiplicities two through four, thereby expanding upon prior classifications that predominantly addressed lower complexities. The methodological framework integrates resolution techniques, including iterative blow-up procedures and normalization strategies, to deconstruct higher multiplicity scenarios into tractable combinatorial constructs. Central to this work are the formalized criteria for analytical equivalence and the algorithmic generation of distinguishing invariants, such as the semigroup of values and the dual graph representation of resolution trees, which are substantiated through computational case studies. These contributions not only resolve ambiguities inherent in topological invariant analyses but also establish a robust foundation for extrapolating classifications to higher multiplicities, with implications spanning algebraic geometry, singularity theory, and geometric modeling. By synthesizing classical algebraic approaches with contemporary computational paradigms, this research enhances the precision of analytic classification in complex planar curve singularities, offering a bridge between theoretical abstraction and practical algorithmic implementation.
Label: AWP
Title: Analytic classification of plane branches up to multiplicity 4

Text: In this comprehensive investigation, we undertake an in-depth examination of the spin-charge separation phenomenon within the context of two-component Bose-gases, a paradigmatic system comprising two disparate species of bosonic particles whose interactions give rise to intricate many-body dynamics. Through the employment of a mean-field approach and a variational ansatz, we derive an effective low-energy Hamiltonian that succinctly captures the quintessential features of this phenomenon, thereby enabling a profound understanding of the underlying physics. Our findings suggest that the spin-charge separation can be accomplished by judiciously adjusting the interaction strength between the two components, thereby inducing the emergence of a spin-liquid state characterized by the presence of two distinct types of excitations: spin excitations that are bereft of any charge and charge excitations that are devoid of spin. Notably, we discover that the spin-liquid state exhibits a non-trivial phase diagram, featuring a region of coexistence between the spin-liquid and a conventional superfluid phase, thereby underscoring the complexity of the system's behavior. The implications of our research are far-reaching, offering new insights into the behavior of strongly correlated Bose-gases and potentially shedding light on the study of ultracold atomic gases and other condensed matter systems, while also highlighting the relevance of the spin-charge separation phenomenon to certain quantum field theories, thereby underscoring the broader significance of our work.
Label: AWP
Title: Spin-charge separation in two-component Bose-gases

Text: This investigation into the utility of tree-structured regression in facilitating the differentiation of integrals, an operation of paramount importance in calculus, has led to the development of a novel approach for approximating the derivative of an integral function, which is particularly efficacious in scenarios where the underlying function is complex and lacks a closed-form analytical derivative. By capitalizing on the hierarchical structure of decision trees, a tree-structured regression model is constructed that approximates the integral function, and subsequently, the model's node-wise predictions are leveraged to compute the derivative in a computationally efficient manner. A series of theoretical and numerical experiments serves to substantiate the efficacy of this approach in accurately approximating the derivative of integrals, even in cases where traditional differentiation methods prove ineffectual. The results of this study suggest that tree-structured regression can serve as a viable alternative to traditional differentiation methods, particularly in high-dimensional and complex problem domains where the latter often fail to yield satisfactory results. Furthermore, the proposed method possesses the potential to not only expand the scope of applications for tree-structured regression in various fields, including computer science, engineering, and data analysis, but also to facilitate the extension of these applications to a broader spectrum of disciplines.
Label: AWP
Title: Tree-structured regression and the differentiation of integrals

Text: This study presents a theoretical framework elucidating the genesis of the early universe through a six-dimensional metastable vacuum state, wherein quantum fluctuations inherent to the higher-dimensional substrate catalyze the emergence of a temporally inverted singularity—interpreted as a white hole—that radiates energy and matter, thereby generating the astrophysical spectrum observed in contemporary cosmological data. By extending general relativity to encompass six spatial dimensions, the model posits that a phase transition within the vacuum's metastable configuration instigates a dynamic emission of spacetime curvature, culminating in the formation of a white hole whose event horizon, governed by higher-dimensional geodesic trajectories, orchestrates a redshifted energy distribution congruent with the cosmic microwave background and large-scale structure observations. Quantum gravitational effects intrinsic to the 6D framework are demonstrated to address the horizon and flatness problems without invoking ad hoc fine-tuning, while the residual entropy derived from the vacuum's decay may account for the dark matter and dark energy components observed in the universe. Numerical simulations of this paradigm replicate critical epochs of cosmic evolution, including baryon acoustic oscillations and the matter-radiation decoupling phase, thereby offering a unified explanation for the homogeneity, isotropy, and spectral characteristics of the universe. This model challenges conventional Big Bang narratives by proposing that the astrophysical spectrum arises from the decay of a multidimensional vacuum into a white hole, providing testable predictions for future gravitational wave astronomy and cosmological structure analyses, and establishing a novel paradigm for reconciling higher-dimensional physics with empirical cosmological phenomena.
Label: AWP
Title:
The bang of a white hole in the early universe from a 6D vacuum state:
  Origin of astrophysical spectrum

Text: This comprehensive investigation into the intricate process of stellar genesis within molecular clouds, a pivotal juncture in the galactic life cycle, has been facilitated by the integration of observational data from cutting-edge telescopes and intricate numerical simulations. Through a multidisciplinary approach, our research has yielded groundbreaking insights into the underlying physical mechanisms governing the complex dynamics of star formation within these dense, interstellar environments. Notably, our analysis has elucidated that the initial fragmentation of molecular clouds into prestellar cores is precipitated by a synergy of gravitational collapse and magnetic field-mediated processes, thereby providing a nuanced understanding of the initial stages of star formation. As these nascent cores continue to undergo a process of gravitational contraction, they eventually transition into a phase of accelerated accretion, ultimately culminating in the formation of protostellar objects. Furthermore, our findings suggest that the efficiency of star formation within molecular clouds is inextricably linked to the local gas density and turbulent state, with higher density regions exhibiting significantly enhanced star formation activity. Consequently, our results have far-reaching implications for our comprehension of the star formation process and the pivotal role that molecular clouds play in shaping the morphological and evolutionary trajectories of galaxies.
Label: AWP
Title: Star Formation in Molecular Clouds?

Text: A comprehensive investigation has been undertaken to elucidate the phenomenon of Coulomb blockade in graphene nanoribbons, a distinctive class of one-dimensional nanomaterials characterized by their singular electronic properties, which arise from the unique interplay between the material's intrinsic characteristics and the nanoscale dimensions of the ribbons. Through an integrated approach combining theoretical modeling and experimental methodologies, we have endeavored to scrutinize the transport characteristics of graphene nanoribbons at the nanoscale, wherein the confinement of electrons within the narrow channel of the nanoribbon precipitates a marked Coulomb blockade effect, wherein the flow of electrons is impeded by the repulsive Coulomb interaction between adjacent electrons, an effect that is further modulated by the introduction of defects and impurities, which alter the local electronic density of states and Coulomb coupling. Notably, our findings reveal a robust correlation between the Coulomb blockade behavior and the nanoribbon's width, edge termination, and doping level, underscoring the complex interplay between these variables and the electronic properties of the material. Furthermore, the observed Coulomb blockade effect is attributed to the quantized electronic states and the enhanced Coulomb interaction in the nanoribbon, which offer a promising platform for exploring quantum transport phenomena in graphene-based nanostructures, with significant implications for the development of graphene-based electronics and nanoscale devices.
Label: AWP
Title: Coulomb blockade in graphene nanoribbons

Text: In this investigation, we undertake a comprehensive examination of the non-Hermitian von Roos Hamiltonian, a quantum mechanical system characterized by $\eta$-weak-pseudo-Hermiticity, a distinctive property that enables the Hamiltonian's energy spectrum to remain real despite its non-Hermitian nature. This peculiarity arises from the introduction of an anti-Hermitian operator $\eta$, through which the von Roos Hamiltonian is derived and its $\eta$-weak-pseudo-Hermiticity is demonstrated, exemplified by the condition $\eta \hat{H} \eta^{-1} = \hat{H}^\dagger$, which serves as a defining characteristic of this phenomenon. Notably, we establish that the von Roos Hamiltonian exhibits isospectrality with its Hermitian counterpart, a consequence of which is that the energy spectra of the non-Hermitian and Hermitian systems coincide identically. Furthermore, by exploiting the isospectrality and $\eta$-weak-pseudo-Hermiticity of the von Roos Hamiltonian, we demonstrate its exact solvability, thereby facilitating the exact solution of the Schrödinger equation for this system and allowing us to obtain the eigenvalues and eigenstates, which are shown to be real and orthogonal. Our results provide a profound understanding of the properties of non-Hermitian Hamiltonians and underscore the importance of $\eta$-weak-pseudo-Hermiticity in ensuring the reality of the energy spectrum, thereby having significant implications for the study of quantum systems that exhibit non-Hermitian behavior.
Label: AWP
Title:
Non-Hermitian von Roos Hamiltonian's $\eta$-weak-pseudo-Hermiticity,
  isospectrality and exact solvability

Text: The development of precise theoretical frameworks for heavy quark jet dynamics represents a pivotal advancement in high-energy physics, enabling rigorous validation of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) and enhancing the discovery potential of novel phenomena at colliders. This study introduces a comprehensive approach that integrates higher-order perturbative QCD formalisms with refined parton shower algorithms and enhanced non-perturbative modeling techniques to simulate heavy quark jet production in high-energy proton-proton interactions. By incorporating next-to-next-to-leading-order (NNLO) QCD perturbation theory and advanced event generation methodologies, the model achieves a marked reduction in theoretical uncertainties—approximately 30%—across critical jet observables such as invariant mass, transverse momentum, and angular correlations. Experimental assessments using 13 TeV Large Hadron Collider (LHC) datasets demonstrate exceptional agreement between predicted distributions and empirical measurements from the ATLAS and CMS collaborations, with observed deviations within 5%, thereby affirming the robustness of the computational framework. The integration of resummation formalisms addressing collinear gluon radiation and improved parametrization of hadronization effects further fortifies the predictive power of the model, facilitating high-precision analyses of parton distribution functions and constraining potential anomalies in Standard Model predictions. These advancements not only augment the precision of heavy flavor physics investigations but also establish a foundational methodology for high-sensitivity searches targeting supersymmetric particles, dark matter mediators, and other exotic signatures, ensuring the framework's applicability to future collider experiments operating at elevated energy thresholds.
Label: AWP
Title: Accurate predictions for heavy quark jets

Text: The BeppoSAX Wide Field Cameras (WFC) X-ray source catalogue constitutes a meticulously assembled compilation of X-ray sources that have been detected by the WFC onboard the BeppoSAX mission, a joint Italian-Dutch X-ray astronomy satellite that was successfully launched in 1996. Through a systematic analysis of the WFC data, which encompasses a broad energy spectrum ranging from 2 to 10 keV and spans an approximate time period of eight years, this catalogue presents a comprehensive set of findings. The resulting dataset comprises a total of 1,144 X-ray sources, including point sources, extended sources, and variable sources, which were identified in multiple sky regions, predominantly concentrated in the Galactic plane and in directions corresponding to known X-ray emitting regions. Employing a synergy of automated and manual detection techniques, the source identification process was conducted, and the catalogue includes pertinent information on source position, flux, and variability, as well as associated errors and uncertainties. By virtue of its exhaustive character, the BeppoSAX WFC X-ray source catalogue represents a valuable resource for the X-ray astronomy community, facilitating the identification and in-depth study of newly discovered X-ray emitting objects, the characterization of previously known sources, and the exploration of the X-ray sky at an unprecedented level of detail, thereby making a substantial contribution to our comprehension of the X-ray universe.
Label: AWP
Title: The BeppoSAX WFC X-ray source catalogue

Text: This research presents novel integral formulations for convolutions involving non-central multivariate gamma distributions, addressing a critical void in the extant literature concerning their analytical tractability. By harnessing the operational properties of Laplace and Mellin transforms, coupled with the mathematical structure of generalized confluent hypergeometric functions, the study establishes a rigorous framework for expressing these convolutions as explicit integral identities. The derived expressions, which incorporate the interplay between shape, scale, and non-centrality parameters, are validated through convergence analysis and consistency with degenerate univariate cases. Notably, the formulations facilitate the evaluation of higher-order moments and tail behaviors, offering computational advantages over traditional numerical approaches in high-dimensional probabilistic modeling. The theoretical advancements are complemented by empirical demonstrations, illustrating their applicability in reliability engineering, multivariate signal processing, and statistical inference for correlated stochastic systems. Furthermore, the study elucidates how non-centrality parameters modulate the asymptotic characteristics of convolved distributions, thereby extending foundational results from univariate to multivariate settings. By synthesizing transform-based methodologies with special function theory, this work provides a robust analytical paradigm for addressing complex stochastic dependencies, with potential ramifications for predictive analytics and risk assessment in applied disciplines.
Label: AWP
Title:
Integral representations for convolutions of non-central multivariate
  gamma distributions

Text: This investigation explores the existence and properties of non-Abelian gravitational configurations within a five-dimensional spacetime framework (d=4+1) characterized by dual azimuthal symmetry, a symmetry manifesting as invariance under rotations in two orthogonal angular coordinates. Utilizing the coupled Einstein-Yang-Mills equations, the study formulates regular static solutions that transcend the constraints of classical Abelian gauge theories, integrating the intricate dynamics of non-Abelian SU(2) fields. Through analytical reduction of the field equations by leveraging the specified symmetry, the research unveils a novel class of topologically distinct geometries wherein gravitational and non-Abelian interactions coalesce to yield stable, singularity-free structures. Comparative analysis with four-dimensional analogs highlights enhanced moduli space complexity in higher dimensions, marked by divergent symmetry-breaking mechanisms and expanded solution multiplicity. Perturbative stability assessments reveal that these configurations resist destabilizing perturbations under stringent symmetry conditions, underscoring their robustness in extended dimensional contexts. By elucidating the geometric and topological attributes of these solutions, the work advances theoretical understanding of non-Abelian field interactions in higher-dimensional gravity, offering implications for holographic duality and the foundational architecture of unified field theories. The findings further illuminate the role of azimuthal symmetry in mediating structural stability, thereby contributing to the broader discourse on the interplay between gauge dynamics and spacetime geometry in multidimensional frameworks.
Label: AWP
Title: d=4+1 gravitating nonabelian solutions with bi-azimuthal symmetry

Text: This investigation probes the temporal evolution of a phantom scalar field within the formalism of loop quantum cosmology, with the explicit objective of clarifying how quantum‑geometric corrections influence the asymptotic dynamics of the cosmos; by invoking the effective Friedmann equation characteristic of loop quantum cosmology, a canonical phantom field endowed with a negative kinetic contribution and an exponential self‑interaction is incorporated, from which a fully autonomous system of nondimensional variables is systematically derived; subsequent numerical integration of these modified dynamical equations demonstrates that the classically inevitable big‑rip singularity, which typifies phantom‑driven scenarios, is supplanted by a non‑singular quantum bounce, after which the universe experiences a brief super‑inflationary epoch before ultimately converging onto a stable de Sitter attractor; a detailed phase‑space analysis reveals the presence of a critical point corresponding to a phantom‑dominated accelerated expansion, whose stability hinges critically upon the steepness parameter of the exponential potential; moreover, by computing the effective equation‑of‑state parameter, it is shown that this quantity asymptotically approaches the value −1, in stark contrast to the divergent behaviour encountered in classical general relativity; collectively, these results imply that loop quantum cosmology furnishes a plausible mechanism for resolving phantom‑driven singularities, thereby yielding a coherent, non‑singular cosmological model that remains in accord with observational constraints on the present‑day accelerated expansion.
Label: AWP
Title: Phantom field dynamics in loop quantum cosmology

Text: The investigation of photoinduced electrification (PIE) in dielectric and semiconducting solids has spanned a broad thermal spectrum in order to clarify the influence of thermally activated processes on charge segregation and the evolution of surface potentials; in the present third installment of this series, we carried out methodical photoemission and surface‑potential assessments on a curated ensemble of oxides and organic crystals under rigorously controlled illumination (λ = 365 nm, 10 mW cm⁻²) while systematically varying the specimen temperature between 80 K and 350 K, and found that the photoinduced surface potential exhibited a pronounced non‑monotonic temperature dependence, peaking near 200 K, which can be rationalized by the interplay between thermally activated detrapping of photo‑generated carriers and the concomitant diminution of surface recombination velocities; Arrhenius‑based kinetic analysis furnished activation energies of 0.45 eV for electron detrapping in TiO₂ and 0.32 eV for hole trapping in poly(3‑hexylthiophene), and moreover, temperature‑dependent photoconductivity investigations uncovered a transition from trap‑dominated to band‑limited transport regimes, thereby underscoring the pivotal role of temperature in modulating both the magnitude and the stability of PIE and furnishing indispensable insights for the engineering of optoelectronic devices intended to operate under diverse thermal conditions.
Label: AWP
Title: Photoinduced electrification of solids. III. Temperature dependences

Text: This investigation examines the physiological underpinnings of post-hatching parental care in a precocial avian species, elucidating the dynamic interplay between endocrine regulation and adaptive behavioral strategies in a taxon characterized by rapid post-natal development. Employing systematic observational methodologies and high-throughput hormone quantification techniques, we characterized the temporal dynamics of brooding, altricial feeding, and protective vigilance behaviors exhibited by parental carers toward their precocial offspring, alongside serum levels of prolactin, corticosterone, and testosterone. Robust associations emerged between elevated prolactin concentrations and heightened brooding frequency, suggesting a neuroendocrine mechanism that sustains parental attentiveness despite the ontogenetic independence of the young. Concurrently, elevated corticosterone levels correlated positively with increased vigilance and predator-response latency, implying a stress-axis mediated trade-off between parental engagement and environmental risk mitigation. Sex-based disparities in endocrine profiles were evident, with maternal individuals exhibiting significantly higher prolactin titers and more persistent care behaviors, whereas paternal subjects demonstrated testosterone-driven territoriality that indirectly enhanced offspring survival. These findings underscore the nuanced hormonal architecture governing parental care in precocial birds, wherein physiological states are calibrated to optimize investment in offspring while accommodating the reduced developmental dependency inherent to this life history strategy. By delineating these endocrine-behavioral linkages, the study contributes to a broader comprehension of the evolutionary compromises shaping avian parental strategies across diverse developmental paradigms.
Label: AWP
Title:
Post-hatching parental care behaviour and hormonal status in a precocial
  bird

Text: Borromean nuclei—defined by a tenuously bound valence cluster that loses its binding once any two‑body subsystem is excised—exhibit a markedly pronounced low‑energy dipole excitation spectrum that serves as a direct signature of their spatially extended halo configuration; in the present study we examine the interdependence between dipole excitation strength and the spatial arrangement of prototypical three‑body Borromean systems such as ^6He, ^11Li, and ^14Be by employing a fully microscopic hyperspherical harmonics approach in conjunction with a realistic nucleon–nucleon interaction, wherein the electric dipole operator is diagonalized within the continuum and the resulting matrix elements are subjected to the Lorentz integral transform technique to extract the B(E1) strength distribution, which is subsequently benchmarked against recent Coulomb breakup measurements; the calculations demonstrate that the observed soft dipole mode originates from a coherent oscillatory motion of valence neutrons relative to the core, and that its centroid energy displays an inverse proportionality to the root‑mean‑square matter radius, while the calculated dipole strength distribution exhibits pronounced sensitivity to the dineutron correlation length, thereby furnishing a quantitative correlation between the empirical B(E1) spectrum and the underlying three‑body geometry; these findings underscore the efficacy of dipole response as a diagnostic probe for elucidating the spatial structure of halo nuclei and for imposing stringent constraints on theoretical models of their many‑body dynamics.
Label: AWP
Title: Dipole excitation and geometry of borromean nuclei

Text: We propose the establishment of a novel observational classification, Beaming Binaries, to designate a distinct subset of photometric binary stars that exhibit periodic variability precipitated by relativistic beaming effects, which are a consequence of the interaction between the intense gravitational field of a compact object and the surrounding space-time. This subclass of binary systems comprises a compact object, such as a neutron star or black hole, in a tightly bound orbit with a companion star, and the periodic variability arises from the rotational modulation of the compact object's frame-dragged space-time, which induces a Doppler shift in the observed radiation, thereby resulting in a periodic modulation of the binary's apparent brightness. A specific class of binary systems, characterized by a compact object and a companion star with orbital periods spanning tens to hundreds of seconds, and a significant disparity in their luminosities, is identified as exhibiting pronounced beaming effects, which are substantiated through comprehensive multi-wavelength photometric monitoring and spectroscopic observations that reveal periodic variations in the binary's brightness and radial velocity curves. The introduction of the Beaming Binary category affords a new paradigm for the investigation of relativistic systems, thereby offering valuable insights into the properties of compact objects and the strong-field gravity regime; however, further in-depth investigations are requisite to fully elucidate the implications of this novel category and its potential applications in astrophysics.
Label: AWP
Title:
Beaming Binaries - a New Observational Category of Photometric Binary
  Stars

Text: This treatise undertakes a meticulous examination of the topological and geometric characteristics of double solid twistor spaces of variable signature, thereby expanding the parameters of extant research within the paradigm of twistor theory. Specifically, a double solid twistor space is conceptualized as a dyadic arrangement of complex vector spaces, each representing a singular solid twistor, with a precisely defined algebraic correspondence between them. The investigation is predicated on a nuanced understanding of the geometric and algebraic properties of these spaces, with a particular emphasis on the signature of the underlying metric tensor, which serves as the fundamental determinant of the spacetime manifold's curvature and topology. Through the introduction of an innovative framework that accommodates an arbitrary range of signatures, we derive a comprehensive set of necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of a double solid twistor space with a predetermined signature, thus elucidating the intricate relationships between the signature of the space and the algebraic properties of the associated twistor spaces. Our analysis discloses a multifaceted interplay between the signature of the space and the algebraic characteristics of the associated twistor spaces, thereby contributing significantly to our comprehension of the fundamental connections between geometry and algebra in this context, and has far-reaching implications for our understanding of the structure of twistor spaces, with potential repercussions for applications in theoretical physics, including the study of gravitational fields and the behavior of particles in curved spacetime.
Label: AWP
Title: Double solid twistor spaces: the case of arbitrary signature

Text: This investigation undertakes an exhaustive examination of the strong CP problem from a paradigmatic 5-dimensional perspective, thereby furnishing a novel, overarching framework for elucidating the ontogenesis of the CP-violating phase within the QCD sector. By embedding the Standard Model within a 5-dimensional spacetime replete with a warped extra dimension, we establish a compelling theoretical framework wherein the strong CP problem can be naturally resolved within the context of the Randall-Sundrum model. The introduction of a novel, 5-dimensional field, intimately connected with the axion mechanism, enables the generation of a minuscule CP-violating phase through the misalignment of the axion field with the background value, thereby establishing a causal relationship between these two entities. Notably, our analysis reveals that the observed CP-violating phase in QCD can be ascribed to the intricate interplay between the 5-dimensional axion field and the 4-dimensional SM fermions, thus affording a dynamical explanation for the strong CP problem. This 5-dimensional perspective offers a captivating, alternative solution to the traditional solutions, such as the Peccei-Quinn mechanism, and provides a novel, fertile ground for investigating the CP-violating phenomena in the QCD sector. Ultimately, the implications of this study hold significant promise for a profound, deeper comprehension of the fundamental laws governing the strong interactions.
Label: AWP
Title: Note on the strong CP problem from a 5-dimensional perspective

Text: This comprehensive examination of embedded star formation within the M16 Eagle Nebula, an illustrious H II region situated within the Serpens constellation, has been conducted using the extensive Spitzer/GLIMPSE dataset. This investigation, which encompasses the 3.6-24 μm wavelength range, has facilitated the identification and characterization of a diverse array of embedded sources, including young stellar objects (YSOs) and pre-main-sequence stars, thereby elucidating the complex interplay between these objects and the surrounding interstellar medium. Through the implementation of the c2d classification scheme, we have systematically categorized the YSOs and derived their spectral energy distributions (SEDs) using the Robitaille et al. model, thereby enabling the estimation of bolometric luminosities, effective temperatures, and masses for these objects. The resultant findings suggest that the embedded star formation processes within the M16 Eagle Nebula are significantly influenced by the prevailing conditions within the surrounding interstellar medium, with a considerable proportion of YSOs residing within dense, star-forming cores, thereby underscoring the pivotal role of these cores in the early stages of stellar evolution, and thereby contributing to a deeper comprehension of the complex, multifaceted processes governing star formation in molecular clouds.
Label: AWP
Title: Embedded Star Formation in the Eagle Nebula with Spitzer/GLIMPSE

Text: This investigation exploits density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) simulations to elucidate the electronic configuration and radical propensity of acenes, a paradigmatic series of linearly fused polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, characterized by a plethora of intriguing electronic properties, including augmented reactivity and conductivity, which are ostensibly attributed to the presence of unpaired electrons that arise from the perturbation of molecular symmetry. Notably, our DMRG calculations indicate that the highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) of acenes assumes a paramount role in the formation of radical character, with the unpaired electron predominantly localized on the end-capped rings. Furthermore, we observe that the magnitude of the radical character manifests a direct correlation with the length of the acene chain, thereby corroborating experimental observations of enhanced reactivity. Moreover, our findings suggest that the radical character of acenes is susceptible to variations in the degree of conjugation between the end-capped rings and the central polyene chain, thus underscoring the intricate relationship between molecular structure and electronic properties. Ultimately, this research provides a nuanced understanding of the electronic configuration and radical propensity of acenes, thereby casting light on their distinctive reactivity and potential applications in the realm of organic electronics and materials science.
Label: AWP
Title:
The radical character of the acenes: A density matrix renormalization
  group study

Text: This investigation elucidates the theoretical underpinnings for simulating quantum correlations via finite communication channels, thereby probing the intrinsic constraints of quantum information processing at its most fundamental level. By establishing a novel mathematical paradigm, we facilitate the simulation of quantum entanglement and non-locality, characteristic phenomena of quantum mechanics, through the utilization of classical communication protocols. Notably, our research scrutinizes the reciprocal relationship between the fidelity of the simulated quantum correlations and the requisite amount of communication to attain such fidelity, revealing a burgeoning exponential correlation between the two variables. Consequently, our analysis underscores the severe limitations imposed by finite communication resources on the scalability of quantum simulation, such that the number of parties involved dictates a precipitous increase in communication requirements. Furthermore, we substantiate that certain quantum protocols can be effectively simulated using finite communication resources, whereas others necessitate an impractically vast quantity of communication to achieve an acceptable level of fidelity. These findings have profound implications for the development of practical quantum information processing technologies and underscore the paramount importance of understanding the complex interplay between quantum correlations and finite communication resources. Ultimately, our results provide a foundational framework for future research into the characterization and optimization of quantum simulation protocols, thereby fostering a deeper comprehension of the intricate relationships governing quantum information processing.
Label: AWP
Title: Simulating Quantum Correlations with Finite Communication

Text: In the present investigation we establish a mathematically rigorous correspondence between driven, nonequilibrium lattice‑gas transport models and suitably engineered equilibrium systems, thereby permitting the application of equilibrium statistical‑mechanical techniques to the prediction of macroscopic fluctuation characteristics; by incorporating a time‑reversal invariant auxiliary dynamics and harnessing a detailed‑balance transformation, we obtain an effective Gibbsian weight that faithfully reproduces the stationary current statistics of both the asymmetric simple exclusion process and the zero‑range process in one spatial dimension; subsequently, we invoke macroscopic fluctuation theory to derive the large‑deviation functional associated with the empirical density and current, and we demonstrate that the equilibrium analogue produced by the aforementioned transformation yields cumulant generating functions that coincide to all orders with those of the original nonequilibrium systems; extensive numerical simulations corroborate that the likelihood of observing anomalous current fluctuations in the driven models is quantitatively replicated by the equilibrium counterpart over a spectrum of boundary‑driving intensities; these findings furnish a novel analytical apparatus for probing rare events in driven diffusive media and imply that the thermodynamic architecture of nonequilibrium steady states may be encapsulated within appropriately constructed equilibrium analogues.
Label: AWP
Title:
Mapping Nonequilibrium onto Equilibrium: The Macroscopic Fluctuations of
  Simple Transport Models

Text: This investigation furnishes a novel examination into the nascent epochs of the universe, specifically the emergence of fluctuations from a tachyonic Big Bang cosmological scenario. By integrating tachyonic fields into the paradigm of eternal inflation, we elucidate that the pre-inflationary era of the universe can be characterized by a regime of tachyonic instability, wherein tachyonic perturbations assume a pivotal role in the genesis of fluctuations, thereby precipitating the subsequent development of a complex network of causal domains that, in turn, give rise to the observed large-scale structure of the universe. Our research findings indicate that the tachyonic instability can provide a natural explanation for the observed homogeneity and isotropy of the universe, as well as the small but non-zero value of the cosmological constant, thus underscoring the tachyonic Big Bang scenario as a plausible cosmological framework. Furthermore, our results suggest that tachyonic fields may have played a crucial role in the emergence of fluctuations during the early universe, thereby providing a novel perspective on the origins of the universe and the formation of structure on large scales, with far-reaching implications that significantly impact our comprehension of the fundamental laws of physics governing the universe.
Label: AWP
Title: Emergence of Fluctuations from a Tachyonic Big Bang

Text: AMBER (Astronomical Multi‑BEam Recombiner) has furnished unparalleled near‑infrared interferometric observations for the VLTI, yet the extraction of trustworthy observables remains impeded by intricate instrumental artefacts and atmospheric disturbances; here we undertake an exhaustive re‑examination of an extensive archival AMBER corpus, concentrating on the ramifications of detector non‑linearity, the temporal evolution of defective pixels, and the steadiness of the wavelength calibration upon the extracted visibilities and closure phases, demonstrating that the conventional pipeline’s flat‑field correction, when executed without contemporaneous calibration exposures, engenders systematic biases reaching up to five per cent in visibility amplitudes, whereas the adoption of a pixel‑by‑pixel gain model mitigates this to sub‑percent levels, while additionally quantifying the influence of adaptive‑optics residuals on spectral‑channel cross‑talk and revealing that a recalibrated matrix incorporating real‑time fringe‑tracking data yields closure phases accurate to half a per cent; by implementing these refinements on a cohort of benchmark stars, we retrieve angular diameters that concur with independent interferometric determinations within two per cent, thereby underscoring the imperative of meticulous detector‑level calibration and continuous atmospheric monitoring to fully harness the scientific capabilities of AMBER on the VLTI.
Label: AWP
Title: AMBER on the VLTI: data processing and calibration issues

Text: This investigation delineates a high‑spectral‑resolution survey of quasar absorption lines within the low‑redshift regime, aimed at characterizing the statistical features and physical parameters of O VI absorbers; by exploiting observations of 149 quasars acquired with the Hubble Space Telescope’s Cosmic Origins Spectrograph and Space Telescope Imaging Spectrograph, we identified 79 distinct O VI systems spanning column densities of 10^13 ≤ N_O VI ≤ 10^15.5 cm^−2 across the redshift interval 0.01 ≤ z ≤ 0.6, thereby establishing a robust dataset for subsequent analysis. The application of spectral stacking combined with Voigt‑profile fitting reveals a column‑density distribution that peaks near N_O VI ≈ 10^14.5 cm^−2 and yields an incidence rate of dN/dX ≈ 0.15 per unit redshift, indicative of a relatively sparse but discernible population of absorbers. Cross‑correlation with ancillary ionic species—C IV, Si IV, and Ly α—demonstrates that 65 % of the systems exhibit multi‑phase gas signatures, implying turbulent, photoionized environments that depart from simple single‑phase models. By juxtaposing photoionization and collisional‑ionization equilibrium calculations, we constrain the temperature range to 10^5.5–10^6.5 K and the ionization parameter to log U ≈ –3 to –1, consistent with ionization by the metagalactic UV background; concomitant estimates of the median electron density (≈ 10^−3 cm^−3) and mass density (≈ 10^−4 cm^−3) further corroborate that these absorbers trace the warm–hot intergalactic medium or galactic haloes. Finally, the derived baryon mass density associated with O VI systems accounts for roughly 0.5 % of the cosmic baryon budget, thereby refining our comprehension of the intergalactic medium’s structure and the feedback processes that interlink galaxies with the cosmic web.
Label: AWP
Title:
A High-Resolution Survey of Low-Redshift QSO Absorption Lines:
  Statistics and Physical Conditions of O VI Absorbers

Text: This investigation examines relativistically mediated quantum tunneling, wherein particles transversing potential barriers under ultra-relativistic conditions exhibit transmission dynamics divergent from classical expectations. By integrating relativistic quantum mechanics with advanced formalisms, we demonstrate that the observed accelerated transmission phenomena emerge as a consequence of non-adiabatic dependencies inherent in the Dirac equation's eigenmodes relative to potential barrier characteristics. Utilizing a comprehensive relativistic formalism, our analysis reveals that ultra-high-energy fermions exhibit significantly diminished dwell times relative to sub-relativistic regimes, a manifestation of the Klein paradox phenomenon wherein relativistic massless Dirac particles achieve unitary transmission probabilities across symmetric potential configurations. Notably, while effective tunneling velocities may theoretically exceed the speed of light within specific energy domains, this observation remains consistent with causality preservation due to the non-local quantum entanglement effects and the absence of causality-violating information propagation. Furthermore, we formulate an analytical expression for the transmission coefficient that incorporates relativistic corrections, elucidating the critical spinor-dependent modulation of barrier transmissivity in high-energy contexts. These resolve apparent contradictions in relativistic tunneling phenomena while providing a robust theoretical foundation for understanding quantum transport in extreme relativistic regimes, with implications for next-generation quantum technologies operating at relativistic energy scales. The study underscores the imperative of relativistic corrections in quantum mechanical models to accurately characterize high-velocity particle dynamics.
Label: AWP

Text: Our investigation into the electrical properties of low-doped manganite single crystals has yielded the observation of anomalous non-equilibrium 1/f noise, a phenomenon intricately tied to the metal-insulator transition, wherein these crystals exhibit singular electrical characteristics. Through the utilization of a synergistic combination of DC and AC electrical measurements, we have exhaustively examined the noise characteristics of these crystals across a broad spectrum of temperatures and frequencies, thereby elucidating the underlying mechanisms governing these systems. The resultant data reveal that the noise power spectral density conformably exhibits a 1/f frequency dependence, indicative of non-equilibrium fluctuations within the electronic system, thereby underscoring the inherent non-stationarity of these systems. Notably, a substantial increase in noise amplitude is observed at temperatures proximal to the metal-insulator transition, thereby suggesting a strong correlation between the noise and the electronic phase segregation. Furthermore, our in-depth analysis has revealed that the 1/f noise is intimately linked to the thermal activation of charge carriers and the ensuing relaxation dynamics of the electronic system, thereby providing a nuanced understanding of the complex interplay between these variables. These not only contribute to the comprehension of the underlying mechanisms governing non-equilibrium behavior in manganite single crystals, but also possess far-reaching implications for the understanding of noise properties in correlated electron systems, thereby laying the groundwork for further research into the fundamental physics underlying these materials.
Label: AWP

Text: Emotional Intelligence, popularized by psychologist Daniel Goleman, refers to the capacity to recognize, accurately understand, effectively manage, and productively utilize both one's own emotions and the emotions of others in personal and professional interactions. The construct encompasses five core components: self-awareness, involving accurate recognition of one's own emotional states and their behavioral impact; self-regulation, involving the management of disruptive emotional impulses and maintenance of composure under pressure; intrinsic motivation, involving the application of emotional energy to pursue goals with persistence and optimism; empathy, involving the accurate sensing and understanding of others' emotions, needs, and concerns; and social skills, encompassing the abilities to build productive relationships, manage interpersonal conflict constructively, inspire and influence others, and work effectively within team contexts. Research consistently demonstrates that emotional intelligence represents a strong predictor of leadership effectiveness, occupational performance, relationship quality, and individual well-being, often more powerfully than cognitive intelligence or technical expertise alone. Unlike cognitive intelligence, emotional intelligence can be meaningfully developed and enhanced through self-reflection, mindfulness practice, professional coaching, behavioral feedback, and deliberate efforts to strengthen interpersonal awareness.
Label: AWP

Text:
An efficient, iterative semi-implicit (SI) numerical method for the time
integration of stiff wave systems is presented. Physics-based assumptions are
used to derive a convergent iterative formulation of the SI scheme which
enables the monitoring and control of the error introduced by the SI operator.
This iteration essentially turns a semi-implicit method into a fully implicit
method. Accuracy, rather than stability, determines the timestep. The scheme is
second-order accurate and shown to be equivalent to a simple preconditioning
method. We show how the diffusion operators can be handled so as to yield the
property of robust damping, i.e., dissipating the solution at all values of the
parameter $\mathcal D\dt$, where $\mathcal D$ is a diffusion operator and $\dt$
the timestep. The overall scheme remains second-order accurate even if the
advection and diffusion operators do not commute. In the limit of no physical
dissipation, and for a linear test wave problem, the method is shown to be
symplectic. The method is tested on the problem of Kinetic Alfv\'en wave
mediated magnetic reconnection. A Fourier (pseudo-spectral) representation is
used. A 2-field gyrofluid model is used and an efficacious k-space SI operator
for this problem is demonstrated. CPU speed-up factors over a CFL-limited
explicit algorithm ranging from $\sim20$ to several hundreds are obtained,
while accurately capturing the results of an explicit integration. Possible
extension of these results to a real-space (grid) discretization is discussed.
Label: HW
Title: An iterative semi-implicit scheme with robust damping

Text:
We propose a generalization of the Tonks-Girardeau model that describes a
coherent gas of cold two-level Bosons which interact with two external fields
in a Ramsey interferometer. They also interact among themselves by contact
collisions with interchange of momentum and internal state. We study the
corresponding Ramsey fringes and the quantum projection noise which,
essentially unaffected by the interactions, remains that for ideal Bosons. The
dual system of this gas, an ideal gas of two-level Fermions coupled by the
interaction with the separated fields, produces the same fringes and noise
fluctuations. The cases of time-separated and spatially-separated fields are
studied. For spatially separated fields the fringes may be broadened slightly
by increasing the number of particles, but only for large particle numbers far
from present experiments with Tonks-Girardeau gases. The uncertainty in the
determination of the atomic transition frequency diminishes, essentially with
the inverse root of the particle number.
Label: HW
Title: Ramsey interferometry with a two-level Tonks-Girardeau gas

Text:
We consider ``one-at-a-time'' coordinate-wise descent algorithms for a class
of convex optimization problems. An algorithm of this kind has been proposed
for the $L_1$-penalized regression (lasso) in the literature, but it seems to
have been largely ignored. Indeed, it seems that coordinate-wise algorithms are
not often used in convex optimization. We show that this algorithm is very
competitive with the well-known LARS (or homotopy) procedure in large lasso
problems, and that it can be applied to related methods such as the garotte and
elastic net. It turns out that coordinate-wise descent does not work in the
``fused lasso,'' however, so we derive a generalized algorithm that yields the
solution in much less time that a standard convex optimizer. Finally, we
generalize the procedure to the two-dimensional fused lasso, and demonstrate
its performance on some image smoothing problems.
Label: HW
Title: Pathwise coordinate optimization

Text:
Being motivated by John Tantalo's Planarity Game, we consider straight line
plane drawings of a planar graph $G$ with edge crossings and wonder how
obfuscated such drawings can be. We define $obf(G)$, the obfuscation complexity
of $G$, to be the maximum number of edge crossings in a drawing of $G$.
Relating $obf(G)$ to the distribution of vertex degrees in $G$, we show an
efficient way of constructing a drawing of $G$ with at least $obf(G)/3$ edge
crossings. We prove bounds $(\delta(G)^2/24-o(1))n^2 < \obf G <3 n^2$ for an
$n$-vertex planar graph $G$ with minimum vertex degree $\delta(G)\ge 2$.
  The shift complexity of $G$, denoted by $shift(G)$, is the minimum number of
vertex shifts sufficient to eliminate all edge crossings in an arbitrarily
obfuscated drawing of $G$ (after shifting a vertex, all incident edges are
supposed to be redrawn correspondingly). If $\delta(G)\ge 3$, then $shift(G)$
is linear in the number of vertices due to the known fact that the matching
number of $G$ is linear. However, in the case $\delta(G)\ge2$ we notice that
$shift(G)$ can be linear even if the matching number is bounded. As for
computational complexity, we show that, given a drawing $D$ of a planar graph,
it is NP-hard to find an optimum sequence of shifts making $D$ crossing-free.
Label: HW
Title: On the Obfuscation Complexity of Planar Graphs

Text:
The earliest phases of clustered star formation and the origin of the stellar
initial mass function (IMF) are currently much debated. In order to constrain
the origin of the IMF, we investigated the internal and relative motions of
starless condensations and protostars previously detected by us in the dust
continuum at 1.2mm in the L1688 protocluster of the Ophiuchus molecular cloud
complex. The starless condensations have a mass spectrum resembling the IMF and
are therefore likely representative of the initial stages of star formation in
the protocluster. We carried out detailed molecular line observations,
including some N2H+(1-0) mapping, of the Ophiuchus protocluster condensations
using the IRAM 30m telescope. We measured subsonic or at most transonic levels
of internal turbulence within the condensations, implying virial masses which
generally agree within a factor of ~ 2 with the masses derived from the 1.2mm
dust continuum. This supports the notion that most of the L1688 starless
condensations are gravitationally bound and prestellar in nature. We measured a
global one-dimensional velocity dispersion of less than 0.4 km/s between
condensations. This small relative velocity dispersion implies that, in
general, the condensations do not have time to interact with one another before
evolving into pre-main sequence objects. Our observations support the view that
the IMF is partly determined by cloud fragmentation at the prestellar stage.
Competitive accretion is unlikely to be the dominant mechanism at the
protostellar stage in the Ophiuchus protocluster, but it may possibly govern
the growth of starless, self-gravitating condensations initially produced by
gravoturbulent fragmentation toward an IMF, Salpeter-like mass spectrum.
Label: HW
Title:
The initial conditions of star formation in the Ophiuchus main cloud:
  Kinematics of the protocluster condensations

Text:
Distributed estimation based on measurements from multiple wireless sensors
is investigated. It is assumed that a group of sensors observe the same
quantity in independent additive observation noises with possibly different
variances. The observations are transmitted using amplify-and-forward (analog)
transmissions over non-ideal fading wireless channels from the sensors to a
fusion center, where they are combined to generate an estimate of the observed
quantity. Assuming that the Best Linear Unbiased Estimator (BLUE) is used by
the fusion center, the equal-power transmission strategy is first discussed,
where the system performance is analyzed by introducing the concept of
estimation outage and estimation diversity, and it is shown that there is an
achievable diversity gain on the order of the number of sensors. The optimal
power allocation strategies are then considered for two cases: minimum
distortion under power constraints; and minimum power under distortion
constraints. In the first case, it is shown that by turning off bad sensors,
i.e., sensors with bad channels and bad observation quality, adaptive power
gain can be achieved without sacrificing diversity gain. Here, the adaptive
power gain is similar to the array gain achieved in Multiple-Input
Single-Output (MISO) multi-antenna systems when channel conditions are known to
the transmitter. In the second case, the sum power is minimized under
zero-outage estimation distortion constraint, and some related energy
efficiency issues in sensor networks are discussed.
Label: HW
Title: Estimation Diversity and Energy Efficiency in Distributed Sensing

Text:
In this paper we compute the leading correction to the bipartite entanglement
entropy at large sub-system size, in integrable quantum field theories with
diagonal scattering matrices. We find a remarkably universal result, depending
only on the particle spectrum of the theory and not on the details of the
scattering matrix. We employ the "replica trick" whereby the entropy is
obtained as the derivative with respect to n of the trace of the n-th power of
the reduced density matrix of the sub-system, evaluated at n=1. The main
novelty of our work is the introduction of a particular type of twist fields in
quantum field theory that are naturally related to branch points in an
n-sheeted Riemann surface. Their two-point function directly gives the scaling
limit of the trace of the n-th power of the reduced density matrix. Taking
advantage of integrability, we use the expansion of this two-point function in
terms of form factors of the twist fields, in order to evaluate it at large
distances in the two-particle approximation. Although this is a well-known
technique, the new geometry of the problem implies a modification of the form
factor equations satisfied by standard local fields of integrable quantum field
theory. We derive the new form factor equations and provide solutions, which we
specialize both to the Ising and sinh-Gordon models.
Label: HW
Title:
Form factors of branch-point twist fields in quantum integrable models
  and entanglement entropy

Text:
Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) have proved effective at one dimensional
sequence learning tasks, such as speech and online handwriting recognition.
Some of the properties that make RNNs suitable for such tasks, for example
robustness to input warping, and the ability to access contextual information,
are also desirable in multidimensional domains. However, there has so far been
no direct way of applying RNNs to data with more than one spatio-temporal
dimension. This paper introduces multi-dimensional recurrent neural networks
(MDRNNs), thereby extending the potential applicability of RNNs to vision,
video processing, medical imaging and many other areas, while avoiding the
scaling problems that have plagued other multi-dimensional models. Experimental
results are provided for two image segmentation tasks.
Label: HW
Title: Multi-Dimensional Recurrent Neural Networks

Text:
Observational cosmology provides us with a large number of high precision
data which are used to derive models trying to reproduce ``on the mean'' our
observable patch of the Universe. Most of these attempts are achieved in the
framework of a Friedmann-Lema\^itre cosmology where large scale homogeneity is
assumed. However, we know, from the observation of structures at increasing
scales, that these models are only approximations of a smoothed or averaged
inhomogeneous underlying patern. Anyhow, when modelling the Universe, the usual
method is to use continuous functions representing the kinematical scalars of
the velocity field, implicitly assuming that they represent volume averages of
the corresponding fine-scale inhomogeneous quantities, then put them into the
Einstein equations which are solved to give the model and its dependance upon a
number of parameters arbitrarily defined. In General Relativity, such a method
is very much involved since the equations which determine the metric tensor and
the quantities calculated from it are highly nonlinear. The question raised by
the method consisting of determining the parameters of an a priori assumed FLRW
model from observational data is the ``fitting problem'' brought to general
attention by Ellis and Stoeger in the 80's. This problem has recently
experienced a reniewed attention due to the amount of available data and the
increase of the minimum scale at which homogeneity can be assumed. We propose a
discussion of this issue in the light of the latest developments of
observational and theoretical cosmology.
Label: HW
Title: Inhomogeneities in the Universe and the Fitting Problem

Text:
We study the kinematics of the barred spiral galaxy NGC 6946 by investigating
the velocity field from H-alpha Fabry-Perot observations, determined the
pattern speed of the bar by using the Tremaine-Weinberg method, and find a main
pattern speed of 21.7 (+4.0,-0.8) km/s/kpc. Our data clearly suggest the
presence of an additional pattern with a pattern speed more than twice that of
the large pattern in this galaxy. We use the epicycle approximation to deduce
the location of the resonance radii and subsequently determine the pattern
speed between the radii, and find that inside the inner Inner Lindblad
Resonance radius, a bar-like system has evolved.
Label: HW
Title: The pattern speeds of NGC 6946

Text:
This paper considers the problem of secure coding design for a type II
wiretap channel, where the main channel is noiseless and the eavesdropper
channel is a general binary-input symmetric-output memoryless channel. The
proposed secure error-correcting code has a nested code structure. Two secure
nested coding schemes are studied for a type II Gaussian wiretap channel. The
nesting is based on cosets of a good code sequence for the first scheme and on
cosets of the dual of a good code sequence for the second scheme. In each case,
the corresponding achievable rate-equivocation pair is derived based on the
threshold behavior of good code sequences. The two secure coding schemes
together establish an achievable rate-equivocation region, which almost covers
the secrecy capacity-equivocation region in this case study. The proposed
secure coding scheme is extended to a type II binary symmetric wiretap channel.
A new achievable perfect secrecy rate, which improves upon the previously
reported result by Thangaraj et al., is derived for this channel.
Label: HW
Title: Secure Nested Codes for Type II Wiretap Channels

Text:
In this article we study the thermal response functions for two
one-dimensional models, namely the Hubbard and spin-less fermion $t$-$V$
models. By exactly diagonalizing finite sized systems we calculate dynamical
electrical, thermoelectrical, and thermal conductivities via the Kubo
formalism. The thermopower (Seebeck coefficient), Lorenz number, and
dimensionless figure of merit are then constructed which are quantities of
great interest to the physics community both theoretically and experimentally.
We also geometrically frustrate these systems and destroy integrability by the
inclusion of a second neighbor hop. These frustrated systems are shown to have
enhanced thermopower and Lorenz number at intermediate and low temperatures.
Label: HW
Title:
Dynamical thermal response functions for strongly correlated
  one-dimensional systems

Text:
The isotropic-to-nematic transition in liquid crystals is studied in d=3
spatial dimensions. A simulation method is proposed to measure the angle
dependent interfacial tension g(theta), with theta the anchoring angle of the
nematic phase at the interface. In addition, an alternative liquid crystal
model is introduced, defined on a lattice. The advantage of the lattice model
is that accurate simulations of anchoring effects become possible. For the
lattice model, g(theta) depends sensitively on the nearest-neighbor pair
interaction, and both stable and metastable anchoring angles can be detected.
We also measure g(theta) for an off-lattice fluid of soft rods. For soft rods,
only one stable anchoring angle is found, corresponding to homogeneous
alignment of the nematic director in the plane of the interface. This finding
is in agreement with most theoretical predictions obtained for hard rods.
Label: HW
Title: Anchoring effects at the isotropic-nematic interface in liquid crystals

Text:
We describe a Cs atomic magnetometer operating in the spin-exchange
relaxation-free (SERF) regime. With a vapor cell temperature of
$103^\circ\rm{C}$ we achieve intrinsic magnetic resonance widths $\Delta B=17
{\rm \mu G}$ corresponding to an electron spin-relaxation rate of $300 {\rm
s^{-1}}$ when the spin-exchange rate is $\Gamma_{SE}=14000 {\rm s^{-1}}$. We
also observe an interesting narrowing effect due to diffusion. Signal-to-noise
measurements yield a sensitivity of about $400\thinspace{\rm pG/\sqrt{Hz}}$.
Based on photon shot noise, we project a sensitivity of $40 {\rm
pG/\sqrt{Hz}}$. A theoretical optimization of the magnetometer indicates
sensitivities on the order of $2 {\rm pG/\sqrt{Hz}}$ should be achievable in a
$1 {\rm cm^3}$ volume. Because Cs has a higher saturated vapor pressure than
other alkali metals, SERF magnetometers using Cs atoms are particularly
attractive in applications requiring lower temperatures.
Label: HW
Title: Spin-exchange relaxation free magnetometry with Cs vapor

Text:
Kination dominated quintessence models of dark energy have the intriguing
feature that the relic abundance of thermal cold dark matter can be
significantly enhanced compared to the predictions from standard cosmology.
Previous treatments of such models do not include a realistic embedding of
inflationary initial conditions. We remedy this situation by constructing a
viable inflationary model in which the inflaton and quintessence field are the
same scalar degree of freedom. Kination domination is achieved after inflation
through a strong push or "kick" of the inflaton, and sufficient reheating can
be achieved depending on model parameters. This allows us to explore both
model-dependent and model-independent cosmological predictions of this
scenario. We find that measurements of the B-mode CMB polarization can rule out
this class of scenarios almost model independently. We also discuss other
experimentally accessible signatures for this class of models.
Label: HW
Title: Inflationary Cosmology Connecting Dark Energy and Dark Matter

Text:
The organic metal \theta$-(BETS)$_4$HgBr$_4$(C$_6$H$_5$Cl) is known to
undergo a phase transition as the temperature is lowered down to about 240 K.
X-ray data obtained at 200 K indicate a corresponding modification of the
crystal structure, the symmetry of which is lowered from quadratic to
monoclinic. In addition, two different types of cation layers are observed in
the unit cell. The Fermi surface (FS), which can be regarded as a network of
compensated electron and hole orbits according to band structure calculations
at room temperature, turns to a set of two alternating linear chains of orbits
at low temperature. The field and temperature dependence of the Shubnikov-de
Haas oscillations spectrum have been studied up to 54 T. Eight frequencies are
observed which, in any case, points to a FS much more complex than predicted by
band structure calculations at room temperature, even though some of the
observed Fourier components might be ascribed to magnetic breakdown or
frequency mixing. The obtained spectrum could result from either an interaction
between the FS's linked to each of the two cation layers or to an eventual
additional phase transition in the temperature range below 200 K.
Label: HW
Title:
Crystal structure, Fermi surface calculations and Shubnikov-de Haas
  oscillations spectrum of the organic metal
  $\theta$-(BETS)$_4$HgBr$_4$(C$_6$H$_5$Cl) at low temperature

Text:
HESS J1616-508 is one of the brightest emitters in the TeV sky. Recent
observations with the IBIS/ISGRI telescope on board the INTEGRAL spacecraft
have revealed that a young, nearby and energetic pulsar, PSR J1617-5055, is a
powerful emitter of soft gamma-rays in the 20-100 keV domain. In this paper we
present an analysis of all available data from the INTEGRAL, Swift, BeppoSAX
and XMM-Newton telescopes with a view to assessing the most likely counterpart
to the HESS source. We find that the energy source that fuels the X/gamma-ray
emissions is derived from the pulsar, both on the basis of the positional
morphology, the timing evidence and the energetics of the system. Likewise, the
1.2% of the pulsar's spin down energy loss needed to power the 0.1-10 TeV
emission is also fully consistent with other HESS sources known to be
associated with pulsars. The relative sizes of the X/gamma-ray and VHE sources
are consistent with the expected lifetimes against synchrotron and Compton
losses for a single source of parent electrons emitted from the pulsar. We find
that no other known object in the vicinity could be reasonably considered as a
plausible counterpart to the HESS source. We conclude that there is good
evidence to assume that the HESS J1616-508 source is driven by PSR J1617-5055
in which a combination of synchrotron and inverse Compton processes combine to
create the observed morphology of a broad-band emitter from keV to TeV
energies.
Label: HW
Title: HESS J1616-508: likely powered by PSR J1617-5055

Text:
In an ambient space with rotational symmetry around an axis (which include
the Hyperbolic and Euclidean spaces), we study the evolution under the
volume-preserving mean curvature flow of a revolution hypersurface M generated
by a graph over the axis of revolution and with boundary in two totally
geodesic hypersurfaces (tgh for short). Requiring that, for each time t, the
evolving hypersurface M_t meets such tgh ortogonally, we prove that: a) the
flow exists while M_t does not touch the axis of rotation; b) throughout the
time interval of existence, b1) the generating curve of M_t remains a graph,
and b2) the averaged mean curvature is double side bounded by positive
constants; c) the singularity set (if non-empty) is finite and discrete along
the axis; d) under a suitable hypothesis relating the enclosed volume to the
n-volume of M, we achieve long time existence and convergence to a revolution
hypersurface of constant mean curvature.
Label: HW
Title:
Volume-preserving mean curvature flow of revolution hypersurfaces in a
  Rotationally Symmetric Space

Text:
In this paper we present a two channel model with the goal of reproducing the
soft scattering data available in the ISR-Tevatron energy range, and extend the
model results to LHC and Cosmic Rays energies. A characteristic feature of the
model is that we represent the sum of all diffractive final states at a vertex,
by a single diffractive state. Our two main results are: (i) The approach of
the elastic scattering amplitude to the black disc bound is very slow, reaching
it at energies far higher than the GZK ankle cutoff. (ii) Our predicted
survival probability for Higgs exclusive central diffractive production at the
LHC is 0.7%, which is considerably smaller than our previous estimate. The
above features are compatible with a parton-like model in which the traditional
soft Pomeron is replaced by an amplitude describing the partonic system, which
issaturated in the soft (long distance) limit.
Label: HW
Title:
A Soft Interaction Model at Ultra High Energies: Amplitudes, Cross
  Sections and Survival Probabilities

Text:
We list and analyze H I absorption lines at redshifts 2 < z < 4 with column
density (12 < log(N_HI) < 19) in 40 high-resolutional (FWHM = 8.0 km/s) quasar
spectra obtained with the Keck+HIRES. We de-blend and fit all H I lines within
1,000 km/s of 86 strong H I lines whose column densities are log(N_HI/[cm^-2])
> 15. Unlike most prior studies, we use not only Lya but also all visible
